## A button in the frame

InputGroupButton has four addon sizes: `xs`, `sm`, `icon-xs`, and `icon-sm`. These independent controls all clear their own domain. Pointer and keyboard activation keep the real button focus; the addon focus convenience steps aside for buttons. Use InputGroupButton inside an addon so sizing and button semantics agree.

<ComponentExample name="button" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { XIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, InputGroupButton, InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";

export function FrameButtons() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-4">
      {(["xs", "sm", "icon-xs", "icon-sm"] as const).map((size) => (
        <ClearDomain key={size} size={size} />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

function ClearDomain({ size }: { size: "xs" | "sm" | "icon-xs" | "icon-sm" }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState("cadence.dev");
  return (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroupInput aria-label={`Domain ${size}`} value={value} onChange={(event) => setValue(event.target.value)} />
      <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
        <InputGroupButton size={size} aria-label={`Clear domain ${size}`} onClick={() => setValue("")}>
          {size.startsWith("icon") ? <XIcon aria-hidden="true" /> : "Clear"}
        </InputGroupButton>
      </InputGroupAddon>
    </InputGroup>
  );
}
```

## A textarea with a footer

Use InputGroupTextarea for multiline content and `block-end` for the footer. The caller owns the draft, character limit and submission. Send clears only this draft and reports its submitted text; it is disabled while the draft is empty.

<ComponentExample name="textarea" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupAddon,
  InputGroupButton,
  InputGroupText,
  InputGroupTextarea,
} from "@/components/cadence/input-group";

export function NoteComposer() {
  const [note, setNote] = useState("");
  const [sent, setSent] = useState("");
  return (
    <form
      className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-3"
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        setSent(note);
        setNote("");
      }}
    >
      <InputGroup>
        <InputGroupTextarea
          aria-label="Note"
          rows={3}
          maxLength={280}
          value={note}
          onChange={(event) => setNote(event.target.value)}
          placeholder="Leave a note for the reviewer…"
        />
        <InputGroupAddon align="block-end">
          <InputGroupText>{note.length}/280</InputGroupText>
          <InputGroupButton type="submit" size="sm" variant="default" className="ml-auto" disabled={!note.trim()}>
            Send
          </InputGroupButton>
        </InputGroupAddon>
      </InputGroup>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {sent ? `Sent: ${sent}` : "No note sent."}
      </p>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Invalid

The application supplies `aria-invalid` and the error description. The group responds with a destructive border and never validates the value itself. Editing this field does not silently clear an application error.

<ComponentExample name="invalid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, InputGroupInput, InputGroupText } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";

export function InvalidEmail() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-2">
      <InputGroup>
        <InputGroupAddon>
          <InputGroupText>@</InputGroupText>
        </InputGroupAddon>
        <InputGroupInput
          type="email"
          aria-label="Email"
          defaultValue="unavailable@example.com"
          aria-invalid
          aria-describedby={id}
        />
      </InputGroup>
      <p id={id} className="text-sm text-destructive">
        This email address is unavailable.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A field with a fixed prefix or suffix: a currency symbol, `https://`, a unit, a
  domain.
- A control that needs one inline action: search with a shortcut hint, a chooser with
  a clear button, an invite field with a submit button.
- A textarea with a footer — a character count, a send button — where the footer must
  look attached to the field.

## When not to use

- A bare text field. Use `input`; the group would only re-create its border.
- A whole toolbar of actions. Use `button-group` beside the field, or a `form` layout:
  four buttons inside one field is a cramped target.
- A label. Use `field` and `FieldLabel`; an addon is not an accessible name.

## API

| Part                  | Props                    | Notes                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InputGroup`          | native div props         | The frame; `role="group"`, focus and invalid state via `:has()`. |
| `InputGroupAddon`     | `align`, native div      | `inline-start \| inline-end \| block-start \| block-end`, `data-align`. |
| `InputGroupButton`    | `size`, `variant`, `type`| `xs \| sm \| icon-xs \| icon-sm`; ghost by default.            |
| `InputGroupText`      | native span props        | Muted text or an icon; not a label.                            |
| `InputGroupInput`     | `input` props            | Control with the frame's chrome removed; `data-slot="input-group-control"`. |
| `InputGroupTextarea`  | `textarea` props         | Same, for multi-line.                                          |

The frame watches `[data-slot=input-group-control]` for `:focus-visible` and
`[aria-invalid=true]`, which is why the control can be borderless and the group still
shows the ring.

`InputGroupButton` preserves Button state callbacks for `className` and `style`, with caller classes last. The input and textarea wrappers keep their native props.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). The frame never animates. `transition-[color,box-shadow]` covers the
focus ring and the invalid border — state feedback that takes no space and does not
run on mount.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- The addon text is not a name. Give the control an `aria-label`, or put a `FieldLabel`
  around the group through `field`.
- `role="group"` on the frame and on each addon groups the pieces for assistive tech;
  add `aria-label` to the frame only if the group needs a name of its own.
- The addon focuses the input on click — a convenience for pointer users. Keyboard
  users tab straight into the control, which is already the shortest path.
- Buttons inside the frame keep their own names. An icon-only clear button needs
  `aria-label="Clear"`.
- `aria-invalid` must be on the control, not on the frame; the frame reacts to it.

## Validation and data ownership

P11: the group shows invalid state, it never decides it.

| `InputGroup` does                                        | You do                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Draws the destructive border when a control is invalid    | Deciding what is invalid                                 |
| Moves focus to the input when the addon is clicked        | Wiring `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`             |
| Renders the buttons you give it                           | Submit, retry, error mapping                             |

There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `resolver` prop, and no validation library is
imported. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsiveness and performance

The group fills its parent and permits shrinking. Block-start/end addons use column layout; inline
addons share the input row. The caller owns long addon labels, button wrapping and narrow-screen
composition.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Composed controls retain their
own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Never wrap `input` in this group to "add a border"; the input already has one.
- Put state on `InputGroupInput` (`aria-invalid`, `disabled`, `readOnly`) — the frame is
  chrome, and it inherits the appearance.
- Use `InputGroupButton`, not `Button`, inside the frame: the sizes are on the addon
  scale, and the addon's click handler recognises it as a button.

# Breadcrumb

Hierarchy navigation, from the root to the current page.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/breadcrumb
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge @base-ui/react lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| breadcrumb | `@components/cadence/breadcrumb/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/breadcrumb.json) |

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: breadcrumb](https://cadence.dev/r/breadcrumb.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

Copy both files in the target list, keeping `breadcrumb/index.tsx` beside the
shared `lib/` directory containing `cn.ts`. No motion runtime, provider or
additional item-specific CSS is required beyond the base theme and Tailwind
utilities. The trail stays static in full, reduced and none modes; the link's
colour transition is hover feedback. `lucide-react` is a component dependency
for the default chevron and ellipsis, even when an example uses a custom separator.

Keep the source's existing `"use client"` directive. In Next.js App Router, a
Server Component can compose the parts shown in Usage and the named examples
with serializable props, including the `render` element in “A router link”.
Event handlers or a function passed to `render` belong in a client module. The
preview already has a client boundary; copying its specimen does not require
the site's preview shell.

Only “A router link” needs `next/link` from an existing Next.js application; the
Breadcrumb source imports no framework router. In another router, use its link
element with `render` and keep the resulting anchor's destination. The caller
owns route destinations, ancestor order and which ancestors are hidden; Breadcrumb
does not derive a trail from the URL or navigate on its own.

“A deep trail that collapses” and the top preview use native `details`/`summary`,
so no extra registry item or npm package is needed. The disclosure keeps its
browser-owned state and supports Enter and Space without JavaScript.
`BreadcrumbEllipsis` is decorative; keep the summary's accessible name and make
hidden ancestors reachable. Use `BreadcrumbPage` for the current page and give
each navigation landmark a distinct label when rendering several trails.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@/components/cadence/breadcrumb";

export function Trail() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>plan.pdf</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

## A deep trail that collapses

`BreadcrumbEllipsis` is decorative, not a trigger. The caller chooses which ancestors to collapse.
Here a native `details` disclosure makes the hidden Documentation link reachable with Enter or Space,
including without JavaScript. Longer hierarchies can put multiple ancestor links in the disclosure.
Each trail owns its own open state; the component does not measure or truncate a route.

<ComponentExample name="collapsed" />

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbEllipsis,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@/components/cadence/breadcrumb";

export function CollapsedTrail() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb aria-label="Collapsed guide trail">
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <details className="relative">
            <summary aria-label="Show ancestors" className="cursor-pointer list-none rounded-sm focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring [&::-webkit-details-marker]:hidden">
              <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
            </summary>
            <div className="absolute top-full left-0 rounded-md border bg-popover p-3 text-popover-foreground shadow-md">
              <BreadcrumbLink href="/docs" className="whitespace-nowrap">Documentation</BreadcrumbLink>
            </div>
          </details>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Motion modes</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

## A custom separator

`BreadcrumbSeparator` accepts any child; its default is a chevron. A slash stays decorative: the
separator is hidden from assistive technology, while every ancestor remains a native link.
This choice changes the separator alone, without changing the trail or its destinations.

<ComponentExample name="separator" />

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@/components/cadence/breadcrumb";

export function CustomSeparator() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb aria-label="Slash trail">
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator>/</BreadcrumbSeparator>
        <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/components">Components</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator>/</BreadcrumbSeparator>
        <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Breadcrumb</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

## A router link

`BreadcrumbLink` accepts Base UI’s `render`. Pass the framework link to preserve client navigation
and prefetching; the rendered element is still an anchor with `data-slot="breadcrumb-link"`.
This Next.js example navigates to real Home and Components routes. The current page stays a
non-focusable `BreadcrumbPage`. In another router, replace only the `Link` import and element.

<ComponentExample name="router" />

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@/components/cadence/breadcrumb";

export function RouterTrail() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb aria-label="Router trail">
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink render={<Link href="/" />}>Home</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink render={<Link href="/components" />}>Components</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Breadcrumb</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A hierarchy deeper than two levels, where the user needs to know where they are and
  how to get back up: `Workspace / Projects / cadence-ui`.
- A page reached through a drill-down — a file inside a folder inside a drive.
- A trail that doubles as navigation: every ancestor is a link, the current page is
  not.

## When not to use

- Two levels of depth. The header already links home; a trail of two items adds noise.
- A wizard or a multi-step form. That is a progress indicator, and it must not let the
  user jump to a step they have not reached.
- A history of where the user came from ("back to search results"). That is a back
  link, and it should look like one.

## API

| Part                   | Props                 | Notes                                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`           | native nav props      | `aria-label="breadcrumb"`.                                    |
| `BreadcrumbList`       | native ol props       | Flex row that wraps; muted, small text.                       |
| `BreadcrumbItem`       | native li props       | Inline flex, one gap.                                         |
| `BreadcrumbLink`       | `render`, anchor props| Anchor by default; `data-slot="breadcrumb-link"`.             |
| `BreadcrumbPage`       | native span props     | The current page: `aria-current="page"`, not a link.          |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator`  | native li props       | `role="presentation"`, `aria-hidden`; chevron by default.     |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`   | native span props     | Hidden from assistive tech; contains `sr-only` "More".        |

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). Nothing in a trail animates. A navigation landmark that fades or
slides in is harder to find, and a trail that reflows on navigation makes the one
stable thing on the page move.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

`transition-colors` on the link is hover feedback on the text colour only.

## Accessibility

- The `nav` is labelled "breadcrumb" by default. Give each trail a distinct
  `aria-label` when several appear on one page, so readers can tell its landmarks apart.
- Order matters: `<ol>`/`<li>` gives the trail a length and a sequence, which is what
  a screen reader announces ("list, 3 items").
- The last item is `BreadcrumbPage`: `aria-current="page"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, and
  not focusable. It is where the user already is, so linking it is a no-op that costs a
  tab stop.
- Separators are decorative — `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden` — so the trail is
  read as names, not as "chevron".
- An ellipsis must not be the only way to reach hidden ancestors: pair it with an accessible
  disclosure or menu. The native disclosure above supports Enter and Space and works without JavaScript.

## Responsiveness and performance

The list wraps and increases its gap at sm. Collapsing a deep trail into an ellipsis is
caller-owned; the component does not measure width or choose hidden ancestors.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native
HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Composed controls retain their own dependencies and motion
contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript.
The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and
application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Do not wrap the current page in a link "for consistency". It is a `BreadcrumbPage`.
- Do not put the trail in a `Card` header as decoration; it is navigation and belongs
  near the top of the content region.
- If the hierarchy is generated from a route, derive the trail from the route's
  segments rather than hand-writing items — a trail that disagrees with the URL is
  worse than none.


Copy all ten files in the target list, keeping `pagination/index.tsx` and
`button/index.tsx` beside the shared `lib/` directory. Pagination imports
`buttonVariants` from the Button module for its anchor styles, so retain that
module's complete motion/provider dependency tree even though no `Button` is
rendered. The provider files are required imports; wrapping your application is
optional. Pagination itself stays static in full, reduced and none modes, with
only colour, border and shadow state feedback from the button styles. No
additional item-specific CSS is needed beyond the base theme and Tailwind utilities.

Keep the source's existing `"use client"` directives. In Next.js App Router,
Usage, the collapsed range, custom labels, sizes and boundary examples can be
composed in a Server Component with serializable props. “Without a page in the
URL” needs its own client module for `useState`, `useId` and the click handler.
The top preview has a client boundary already; copying its specimen does not
require the site's preview shell. All examples use the same installation files
and packages, including `lucide-react` for the component's chevrons and ellipsis;
none needs a framework router package.

Every page control is a native anchor. The caller supplies destinations, the
visible range, `isActive`, boundary states and result data; Pagination does not
read the URL, fetch records or calculate pages. Replace the sample query URLs
with destinations your application actually handles. The local-state example
preserves modified clicks, but its fragment fallback only reaches the results
region and cannot restore the selected page when shared or reloaded.

At a boundary, omit `href` and keep `role="link"` plus `aria-disabled="true"`;
`aria-disabled` alone does not stop an anchor with a destination. Ellipses remain
decorative. Give repeated navigation landmarks distinct labels, keep meaningful
previous/next accessible names when changing their text, and choose a compact
range that fits the parent on narrow screens.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from "@/components/cadence/pagination";

export function ResultPages() {
  return (
    <Pagination aria-label="Result pages">
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1#usage" />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=1#usage">1</PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=2#usage" isActive>
            2
          </PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=3#usage">3</PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext href="?page=3#usage" />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

## A collapsed range

The caller chooses the visible pages and supplies every destination. `PaginationEllipsis` is a
decorative skipped range, not a link or a range-expansion control. Here page 2 is current and the
last page stays reachable. The sample URLs retain `page` on this documentation route; your
application must read that query, fetch the results and derive `isActive` from its actual page.

<ComponentExample name="collapsed" />

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationEllipsis,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from "@/components/cadence/pagination";

export function CollapsedPages() {
  return (
    <Pagination aria-label="Collapsed result pages">
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1#usage" />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=1#usage">1</PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=2#usage" isActive>
            2
          </PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=3#usage">3</PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationEllipsis />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=12#usage">12</PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext href="?page=3#usage" />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

## Custom labels

`PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` accept `text`. Back and Forward are visible from `sm`
up; below it only the chevrons are visible. When changing the visible text, supply an
`aria-label` that includes that text: “Back to previous page” and “Forward to next page”
keep the direction clear at either width. The compact composition has its own real anchor destinations.

<ComponentExample name="labels" />

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from "@/components/cadence/pagination";

export function CustomLabels() {
  return (
    <Pagination aria-label="Custom-labelled result pages">
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1#usage" text="Back" aria-label="Back to previous page" />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=2#usage" isActive>
            2
          </PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext href="?page=3#usage" text="Forward" aria-label="Forward to next page" />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

## Without a page in the URL

This caller owns the current page and invoice records; Pagination does not fetch or slice data.
An ordinary click or Enter updates the results and `aria-current` without changing the URL.
Modified clicks retain the native anchor behavior, whose fragment points to the uniquely named
results region; that fallback only scrolls to the region, it cannot restore a local page. Use page
query URLs when opening, sharing or reloading must restore the selected results.

<ComponentExample name="local-state" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink } from "@/components/cadence/pagination";

const records = [
  ["Invoice 1001", "Invoice 1002"],
  ["Invoice 1003", "Invoice 1004"],
  ["Invoice 1005", "Invoice 1006"],
];

export function LocalPages() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  const resultsId = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-4">
      <section id={resultsId} aria-label="Invoice results" className="min-h-24 rounded-md border p-3">
        <p aria-live="polite" className="mb-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          Page {page} of 3
        </p>
        <ul className="text-sm">
          {records[page - 1]?.map((record) => (
            <li key={record}>{record}</li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </section>
      <Pagination aria-label="Invoice pages">
        <PaginationContent>
          {[1, 2, 3].map((value) => (
            <PaginationItem key={value}>
              <PaginationLink
                href={`#${resultsId}`}
                aria-controls={resultsId}
                isActive={value === page}
                onClick={(event) => {
                  if (event.button !== 0 || event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey || event.altKey) return;
                  event.preventDefault();
                  setPage(value);
                }}
              >
                {value}
              </PaginationLink>
            </PaginationItem>
          ))}
        </PaginationContent>
      </Pagination>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

`PaginationLink` reuses all eight button sizes, with `icon` as its default. Fixed active links
show the text and square shapes directly, without a shared size control. Previous and Next also
accept `size` but default to `default`; use text sizes when showing their written labels.
Sizes change the target geometry, not the page state. Allow enough touch space around small links.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink } from "@/components/cadence/pagination";

const sizes = ["default", "xs", "sm", "lg", "icon", "icon-xs", "icon-sm", "icon-lg"] as const;

export function PageSizes() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md grid-cols-2 gap-6 sm:grid-cols-4">
      {sizes.map((size) => (
        <div key={size} className="grid justify-items-center gap-2">
          <Pagination aria-label={`Pages sized ${size}`}>
            <PaginationContent>
              <PaginationItem>
                <PaginationLink size={size} href="?page=2#sizes" isActive>
                  2
                </PaginationLink>
              </PaginationItem>
            </PaginationContent>
          </Pagination>
          <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{size}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## At a boundary

At the first page, omit the previous control’s `href` and supply `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. Without an `href`, the explicit
role preserves the accessible label on the disabled anchor.
The anchor remains visible as context, is absent from the link tab order, and cannot navigate to
page zero. The caller owns this boundary decision; `aria-disabled` alone does not disable an
anchor that still has an `href`. Apply the same rule to Next at the last page.

<ComponentExample name="boundary" />

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from "@/components/cadence/pagination";

export function FirstPage() {
  return (
    <Pagination aria-label="First result page">
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious role="link" aria-disabled="true" />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=1#at-a-boundary" isActive>
            1
          </PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext href="?page=2#at-a-boundary" />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A result set that is paged for a reason: the total is unknown, the data is remote, or
  the URL should carry the page so it can be shared and reloaded.
- A list where the user needs to jump to a specific page, not only step forward.
- A table footer on the server, where the count lives in the response.

## When not to use

- A finite list that is already in memory. Render it, or a "load more" button — paging
  something you already have is a worse experience than scrolling.
- An infinite feed. There is no page to link to, so an anchor-based control lies.
- A carousel or a wizard. Those step through slides or steps, and their controls are
  buttons.

## API

| Part                  | Props                    | Notes                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Pagination`          | native nav props         | `aria-label="pagination"`, `role="navigation"`.                |
| `PaginationContent`   | native ul props          | Row with a one-unit gap.                                       |
| `PaginationItem`      | native li props          | One slot in the list.                                          |
| `PaginationLink`      | `isActive`, `size`, anchors | Always an `<a>`; `aria-current="page"` and `data-active` when active. |
| `PaginationPrevious`  | `text`, link props       | Chevron left; `aria-label="Go to previous page"`.              |
| `PaginationNext`      | `text`, link props       | Chevron right; `aria-label="Go to next page"`.                 |
| `PaginationEllipsis`  | native span props        | `aria-hidden`; contains `sr-only` "More pages".                |

`size` comes from the button variants (`icon` by default), so the shape matches a
button without becoming one.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A page change is a navigation: the content that changes is the list,
not the control. Animating the pagination would animate the one thing that stays the
same.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

If the new page's rows should arrive in sequence, that is `list.stagger` on the list.

## Accessibility

- `aria-label="pagination"` names the landmark, so it can be skipped or listed.
- The current page is `aria-current="page"`. Colour and the outline variant are the
  sighted half of the same signal — never the only one.
- Previous and next carry a written `aria-label`, because their visible text is hidden
  below `sm`. The chevron alone is not a name.
- A disabled end state (`page 1`, no previous) should render the control without an
  `href` and with `aria-disabled="true"`, not a link that 404s.
- The unordered list gives the count; the ellipsis is decorative and must not be
  focusable.

## Responsiveness and performance

Navigation fills its parent while the inner list remains a single row. The caller chooses the page
range and ellipses and may hide optional text on small screens; page counts are not computed by the
component.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Composed controls retain their
own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Every control is an anchor. Do not replace it with `Button` — the shape comes from
  `buttonVariants`, and Base UI's button would put `role="button"` on a link.
- Keep a real `href` when a click handler takes over. A fragment fallback keeps native
  navigation, but sharing the selected results requires a URL that encodes the page.
- Do not render more than about seven items; collapse the middle with
  `PaginationEllipsis`.

# Spinner

Short waits such as saving, sending, or publishing.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/spinner
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: spinner](https://cadence.dev/r/spinner.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine files in the target list, keeping `spinner/index.tsx` beside the
shared `lib/` directory and preserving relative imports and `"use client"`
directives. The glyph uses a CSS loop, but its `useCadenceMotion` import still
requires the provider files and their `motion` dependency. Copy every file from
the motion, utilities and provider payloads; wrapping the application in
`CadenceProvider` is optional. Without a wrapper, Spinner follows the system
motion preference.

Full and reduced both keep the single-glyph `animate-spin` rotation, the
animation system's specific reduced-motion exception. None uses `animate-none`
and leaves the named icon visible and still. Tailwind's `--animate-spin` theme
token owns the loop clock; provider `timeScale`, including zero, does not change
it. Use `mode="none"` on the included provider to stop the loop, as the explicit
`data-motion="none"` example does from its first render. No additional item-specific
CSS is required beyond the base theme and Tailwind utilities.

Inside a button also uses [Button](/components/button). Install it when copying
that example:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

For a manual Button installation, follow its Manual tab too; it adds
`button/index.tsx`, `@base-ui/react` and `class-variance-authority` alongside the
shared files and packages already listed here. Usage, Sized by the caller, A
specific label, `data-motion="none"` and the top specimen need no other registry items,
npm packages or assets. `lucide-react` is already an implementation dependency
for the loading glyph; the site's preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, all five body examples can be composed in a Server
Component with their shown serializable props, including the nested provider.
Keep the installed sources' client boundaries. A caller that adds React state,
event handlers or browser APIs needs its own client module. The examples are
fixed loading states: the caller starts and finishes requests, mounts or removes
Spinner, sets and clears the region's `aria-busy`, and exposes completion or error
feedback. Keep a meaningful status label; inside the pending button, keep its
written label, `disabled` and `aria-busy`, and hide the redundant glyph with
`aria-hidden`. Reserve any changing label width and choose icon sizes that fit
the surrounding layout.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner";

export function LoadingRegistry() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3 text-sm">
      <Spinner />
      <span className="text-muted-foreground">Loading the registry…</span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Inside a button

Keep the button’s written label and disable it while work is pending. `aria-busy` names the
button’s busy state; hide the redundant spinner glyph from assistive technology here so it does
not duplicate that label. This fixed pending state does not start a request or own its lifetime.
If switching from an idle label changes the width, reserve that width in the caller’s layout.

<ComponentExample name="button" />

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner";

export function SavingButton() {
  return (
    <Button disabled size="sm" aria-busy="true">
      <Spinner aria-hidden="true" />
      Saving
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## Sized by the caller

The icon is `size-4` by default and inherits `currentColor`. The fixed 12, 16, 24 and 32 pixel
specimens show caller classes rather than a finite `size` prop. Muted text colour belongs to the
first specimen only; each glyph keeps its own accessible loading status and inherits header motion.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner";

export function SpinnerSizes() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-4">
      <Spinner className="size-3 text-muted-foreground" />
      <Spinner />
      <Spinner className="size-6" />
      <Spinner className="size-8" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## A specific label

“Loading” is the default accessible name. Say what is loading when surrounding text does not: this
standalone status announces “Saving invoice” without adding a focus stop. The caller decides when
to mount it and must expose completion or an error through its own result UI.

<ComponentExample name="label" />

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner";

export function SavingInvoice() {
  return <Spinner aria-label="Saving invoice" />;
}
```

## Under `data-motion="none"`

This example explicitly fixes its provider to `none` from the first render, independently of the
header. The spinner stays visible and named, with no rotation or running animation; it is not a
post-mount mode switch. Other examples inherit the header. Both full and reduced keep Spinner’s
single-glyph rotation, the animation system’s specific reduced-motion exception.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner";

export function StaticSpinner() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        <Spinner aria-label="Static loading" data-testid="static-spinner" />
        Loading the registry…
      </span>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- An action the user just triggered: save, send, invite, publish. The spinner sits
  where the user is looking — inside the button, or immediately beside it.
- A wait with no measurable progress: a request that returns when it returns.
- A region that is loading and whose shape you cannot predict. When you *can* predict
  it, use `skeleton` instead: it keeps the layout stable.

## When not to use

- A wait under about 300 ms. The spinner appears and disappears before it can be read,
  which reads as a flicker. Keep the button's label and disable it.
- A known percentage. Use `progress`; a spinning wheel after "60%" is a regression.
- A page that is loading its first paint. There is nothing to spin inside yet — a
  skeleton or a server-rendered shell is better.
- A decorative "we're working on it" on a marketing page. Motion without a state
  change is decoration (P9).

## API

| Prop        | Type     | Default     | Description                                                    |
| ----------- | -------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | –           | Merged last — size and colour live here (`size-3`, `text-…`).   |
| `aria-label`| `string` | `"Loading"` | The accessible name; pass a specific one when it helps.         |

All native `svg` props are forwarded. `data-slot="spinner"` and `data-motion` are
always set, and `role="status"` with the label is the announcement.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `data.transition`, continuous form. The loop is CSS (`animate-spin`) rather
than Motion, for the same reason as `skeleton`: a spinner is by definition next to work
the user is waiting on, and it must not add a frame callback to it. Only `transform`
(rotation) changes, so the loop can never trigger layout.

| Phase   | Properties          | Token                         | Interruptible |
| ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------- |
| spin    | `rotate 0 → 360deg` | `data.transition` / `animate-spin` (theme timing) | yes (CSS)     |
| reduced | same rotation       | `animate-spin`                | yes (CSS)     |
| none    | none; icon static   | `animate-none`                | –             |

Reduced keeps the rotation on purpose: M5 removes travel and scale, and a rotation in
place is neither. A spinner that freezes under reduced motion would read as a frozen
app. `none` stops it completely, which is what a screenshot test or a print stylesheet
needs.

## Keyboard interactions

None. The spinner is not focusable and takes no input; focus stays on the control that
started the work, which is where the user's next action will be.

## Accessibility

- `role="status"` is a polite live region: the label is announced when the spinner
  appears, without interrupting. Do not wrap it in another `aria-live` region.
- The label must carry the meaning. The rotation is never the only signal, and under
  `data-motion="none"` it is not a signal at all.
- Give the busy region `aria-busy="true"` and remove it when the work finishes, so the
  state survives even if the spinner unmounts early.
- Do not replace a button's label with a spinner and nothing else. Keep the word, or
  add an `sr-only` copy, or the control loses its name mid-action.
- Do not stack spinners. One per action; a page with five is a page with no feedback.

## Responsive behavior

The spinner is an inline icon, so it follows the text it sits in. Inside a button it
keeps the button's height; inside a heading, size it down (`size-3`) or it will
dominate the line. On touch targets, keep the surrounding button at least 44×44 by
size, not by growing the icon.

## Performance

- One CSS animation per element, on `transform` only; no JS loop, no layout read.
- Compositor-friendly, but the animation-system budget still applies: fewer than
  twenty simultaneously animating elements. For a list of pending rows, render one
  spinner for the list, not one per row.
- No `will-change`: the browser promotes a transform animation on its own.

## Notes for AI

- Use `spinner` for an action, `skeleton` for a layout. Getting this backwards is the
  most common loading-state mistake: a skeleton in a button, or a spinner where the
  content shape was known all along.
- Keep the button's text; add the spinner in front of it and disable the button.
- Under `data-motion="none"` the icon stays visible. Do not hide it to "respect" the
  preference — the state still has to be visible.

files from the motion, utilities and provider payloads. The popup uses CSS
transitions, but its provider imports and the installed Button still require
`motion`; wrapping the application in `CadenceProvider` is optional.

Complete the base theme setup linked above, including Cadence's easing and scale
tokens, and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. There is no additional
Dialog-specific CSS. Each portalled overlay and panel resolves its own token
clock, including provider `timeScale`: full fades the overlay and fades/scales
the panel, reduced keeps opacity only, and none removes transitions and hidden
entry/exit opacity from the first frame. Without a wrapper, Dialog follows the
system motion preference. Use the included provider for explicit scopes; a
nested full scope still respects the system reduced-motion preference.

Usage, Editing a project and the top specimen also use [Field](/components/field)
and [Input](/components/input). Install them when copying the editing form:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/field @cadence/input
```

For manual installation, follow their Manual tabs too: add `field/index.tsx`,
`label/index.tsx`, `separator/index.tsx` and `input/index.tsx` alongside the shared
files already listed here. They add no npm packages beyond Dialog's complete
dependency command. The other examples' rendered controls need only Dialog,
the included Button and, for Explicit motion scopes, the included provider.
Several snippets retain unused Field/Input imports; install those items if you
copy the imports verbatim, or remove the unused imports. No example needs an
extra asset; `lucide-react` already supplies the built-in close icon. The site's
preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, keep the editing, controlled and footer export examples
in a client module because they own state and event handlers. Long content also
needs a client module for its focus ref. Without the built-in close button,
Modal and non-modal behavior, and Explicit motion scopes can be composed in a
Server Component with the shown JSX elements and serializable props; their
existing client directives may also be kept. `render={<Button />}` does not by
itself require a caller client boundary. A function-valued `render`,
`className(state)` or `style(state)`, event handler, or client-side hook such as
`useState` or `useRef` needs that boundary. Preserve the installed sources'
client directives in either case.

`DialogContent` already includes its portal and backdrop; do not add another
overlay around the standard composition. Give every panel a `DialogTitle` and
keep a visible close action when hiding the corner button. The default modal
traps focus and locks page scrolling; `modal={false}` and `"trap-focus"` change
that behavior but still keep DialogContent's backdrop. Base UI handles focus,
Escape and dismissal; the caller owns controlled open state, draft/saved data,
submission, validation and persistence. Cancel does not reset the editing
example's draft. For long content, supply the maximum height, scrolling and
initial focus target shown below so the heading and final close action remain
reachable. Hydrated interactions require JavaScript.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog";
import { Field, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function EditingDialog() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [name, setName] = useState("cadence-ui");
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState("cadence-ui");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Rename project</DialogTrigger>
        <DialogContent>
          <form
            className="grid gap-4"
            onSubmit={(event) => {
              event.preventDefault();
              setSaved(name);
              setOpen(false);
            }}
          >
            <DialogHeader>
              <DialogTitle>Rename project</DialogTitle>
              <DialogDescription>The URL stays the same. Existing links keep working.</DialogDescription>
            </DialogHeader>
            <Field>
              <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>Project name</FieldLabel>
              <Input id={id} value={name} onValueChange={setName} required />
            </Field>
            <DialogFooter>
              <DialogClose render={<Button type="button" variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
              <Button type="submit">Save name</Button>
            </DialogFooter>
          </form>
        </DialogContent>
      </Dialog>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" role="status">
        Project: {saved}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Editing a project

The form owns its draft and saved name. Save submits the form and closes it; Cancel dismisses without saving. Reopening keeps the caller-owned draft. Each instance uses its own ID and state.

<ComponentExample name="editing" />

## Controlled

An external application action can open the dialog without a DialogTrigger. The root reports Escape and outside dismissal through onOpenChange; the caller closes after finishing. Base UI restores focus to the previously focused opener when there is no trigger.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog";
import { Field, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function ControlledDialog() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Open from application state
      </Button>
      <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <DialogContent>
          <DialogHeader>
            <DialogTitle>Application-owned dialog</DialogTitle>
            <DialogDescription>
              The caller owns open. Escape and outside presses still report changes.
            </DialogDescription>
          </DialogHeader>
          <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Finish task</Button>
        </DialogContent>
      </Dialog>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Dialog {open ? "open" : "closed"}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Without the built-in close button

showCloseButton=false removes only the corner control. Supply a visible DialogClose; Escape and outside dismissal still work.

<ComponentExample name="without-close" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";

```

## Footer with a close action

DialogFooter showCloseButton adds a Close action. Preparing the export updates caller state and keeps the panel open; closing remains a separate action.

<ComponentExample name="footer-close" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog";

import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function FooterCloseDialog() {
  const [prepared, setPrepared] = useState(false);
  return (

      <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Export details</DialogTrigger>
```
