
## Long content

Constrain the panel height and enable overflow-y-auto when its body is long. The panel scrolls independently and the final Close action remains reachable. The component does not impose a scrolling height for every consumer. Initial focus targets the heading so opening a long panel starts at the top; Tab can then reach its close controls.

<ComponentExample name="long-content" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog";

export function LongContentDialog() {
  const titleRef = useRef<HTMLHeadingElement>(null);
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Read the changelog</DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent initialFocus={titleRef} className="max-h-[70vh] overflow-y-auto">
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle ref={titleRef} tabIndex={-1}>Release notes</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>Scroll this panel to read every change.</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <div className="grid gap-4 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          {Array.from({ length: 16 }, (_, index) => index + 1).map((change) => (
            <p key={change}>
              Change {change}: Components keep their native semantics, caller-owned data, and documented full, reduced,
              and none motion behavior.
            </p>
          ))}
        </div>
        <DialogFooter showCloseButton />
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

## Modal and non-modal behavior

The fixed triggers cover modal=true (the default), false, and trap-focus. True traps focus and locks page scrolling; false removes focus trapping and scroll locking; trap-focus retains the focus trap without locking page scrolling. DialogContent still renders its backdrop in every case, so an outside pointer press hits that backdrop and dismisses the panel; modal=false does not remove it. Use Popover for an anchored non-modal surface without this backdrop. Every panel still has a name and close action.

<ComponentExample name="modality" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog";
import { Field, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function DialogModality() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {([true, false, "trap-focus"] as const).map((modal) => (
        <Dialog key={String(modal)} modal={modal}>
          <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{String(modal)}</DialogTrigger>
          <DialogContent>
            <DialogHeader>
              <DialogTitle>Modal: {String(modal)}</DialogTitle>
              <DialogDescription>
                True traps focus and locks page scrolling; false removes the focus trap and scroll lock; trap-focus keeps the focus
                trap without scroll locking. DialogContent still renders a backdrop.
              </DialogDescription>
            </DialogHeader>
            <DialogFooter showCloseButton />
          </DialogContent>
        </Dialog>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

These are explicit overrides: the first dialog starts under none, so both its portal overlay and panel have zero duration from insertion. The second restores full inside that none scope; the system reduced-motion preference still wins. Ordinary examples inherit the site header instead.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog";
import { Field, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function DialogMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <Dialog>
          <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open without motion</DialogTrigger>
          <DialogContent data-testid="initial-none">
            <DialogHeader>
              <DialogTitle>Immediate dialog</DialogTitle>
              <DialogDescription>Both overlay and panel start with zero duration.</DialogDescription>
            </DialogHeader>
            <DialogFooter showCloseButton />
          </DialogContent>
        </Dialog>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Dialog>
            <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open nested full</DialogTrigger>
            <DialogContent data-testid="nested-full">
              <DialogHeader>
                <DialogTitle>Nested full dialog</DialogTitle>
                <DialogDescription>
                  This explicit scope restores timing; the system reduced preference still wins.
                </DialogDescription>
              </DialogHeader>
              <DialogFooter showCloseButton />
            </DialogContent>
          </Dialog>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A focused task that must interrupt the page: rename, invite, confirm.
- Content that needs a modal, a focus trap, and an obvious escape route.
- A short form whose result matters more than the page behind it.

## When not to use

- Non-blocking hints and menus; use `popover` or `tooltip`.
- Long multi-step flows; use a page or a wizard.
- Mobile sheets with drag gestures; use `drawer`.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI root; `modal` defaults to `true`, also accepts `false` or `"trap-focus"`. |
| `DialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `DialogContent` | `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `DialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DialogContent`. |
| `DialogClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the dialog. |
| `DialogHeader` / `DialogFooter` | `className`; footer `showCloseButton=false` | Layout; footer can add a Close action. |
| `DialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `DialogDescription` | `className` | Optional supporting text. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (overlay 96ms, panel 132ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so no transition runs | – | – |

The panel stays mounted while its exit transition runs; Base UI delays unmount until the
transition ends, so reopening mid-exit reverses cleanly.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. |
| Escape | Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`,
  focus trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling.
- The close button is a real button with a screen-reader-only label.
- `DialogTitle` is required; a dialog without an accessible name is invalid.
- Content is unmounted after the exit transition, so focus is never lost mid-flight.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred and capped at `max-w-lg`; on narrow viewports it keeps a 1rem gutter.
For long content, the caller adds a maximum height and `overflow-y-auto`, as in Long content above,
so the popup scrolls independently. Hydrated open/close interactions require JavaScript; no-JS retains the triggers and readable examples.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open.
- Animates opacity and scale only; no layout reads and no JavaScript animation loop.

## Notes for AI

- Always render a `DialogTitle`; it is the accessible name.
- Keep the confirming action specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- Do not animate height inside the dialog; mount content instead.

# Checkbox

Independent yes/no choices and multi-select lists.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/checkbox
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| checkbox | `@components/cadence/checkbox/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/checkbox.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: checkbox](https://cadence.dev/r/checkbox.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine files in the target list, including every file from the motion,
utilities and provider payloads. Keep `checkbox/index.tsx` beside the shared
`lib/` directory with the relative imports and `"use client"` directives intact.
The indicator uses `ControlSpan`, whose imports also reach `native-div.tsx` and
`press-button.tsx`; copying only `provider.tsx` is not enough. The provider files
and `motion` package are required even without an application wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied
files. There is no additional Checkbox-specific CSS or asset. `lucide-react`
supplies the tick and mixed-state icons. Only the indicator animates:
`state.morph` fades and scales it in full, keeps opacity with immediate full size
in reduced, and settles immediately in none, including an initially checked
control. Standalone checkboxes follow the system motion preference; the optional
`CadenceProvider` controls a subtree's mode and timing. A nested full scope still
respects the system reduced-motion preference.

Usage, the top specimen and the labelled examples also need
[Label](/components/label). Controlled and Native form submission additionally
use [Button](/components/button). Install the items needed by your example:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/label @cadence/button
```

For manual installation, follow their Manual tabs too: add `label/index.tsx`
and, when using Button, `button/index.tsx`. Their shared files are already in
Checkbox's target list. Label adds no npm package; Button also requires:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

Explicit motion scopes uses only Checkbox and the included provider. No example
needs another package or external asset. The site's preview shell is not consumer
setup.

In Next.js App Router, Controlled and Native form submission need a client
module for their state and event handlers. The other snippets can be composed
in a synchronous Server Component using the shown `useId` or stable unique IDs,
JSX and serializable props; their existing client directives may also be kept.
An event handler, a function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)`,
or a client-side hook such as `useState` or `useRef` needs a caller client
boundary. Preserve the installed sources' client directives in either case.

Give every control a visible label linked with `htmlFor` and a unique `id`, or
an `aria-label`. With the default renderer, the supplied `id` belongs to the
hidden native input; Base UI gives the visible checkbox its own accessible
name, focus and Space-key behavior. Use `defaultChecked` for an uncontrolled
initial value, or own `checked` with `onCheckedChange`. `indeterminate` announces
mixed state but does not set `checked` or derive a child selection for you.

Keep the default root as a flex or grid item, as Usage does. Inside a plain
block wrapper, give Checkbox `className="inline-flex"` so its `span` respects
the control's width and height, as the wrapped Static checkbox in Explicit
motion scopes demonstrates.

For native submission, supply `name` and `value`: a checked, enabled input
contributes that entry; an unchecked input is omitted unless you supply
`uncheckedValue`. Disabled inputs are omitted. A read-only choice stays
focusable and retains its checked submission value. `required` participates in
browser constraint validation, as the form example demonstrates. The caller
owns acceptance rules, controlled state, error text, submission, server-side
validation and persistence; Cadence renders `aria-invalid` and the described
error without deciding when either should clear.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function CheckboxSettings() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex items-start gap-3">
      <Checkbox id={id} aria-describedby={`${id}-help`} className="mt-0.5" />
      <div className="grid gap-1">
        <Label htmlFor={id}>Send the weekly digest</Label>
        <p id={`${id}-help`} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          Every Monday, 09:00.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`id` lands on the hidden input, so `htmlFor` on a `label` names the control and
clicking the label toggles it.

## Checked by default, and indeterminate

`defaultChecked` initializes an uncontrolled choice. `indeterminate` announces a mixed selection; it does not make the field checked for form submission. Both controls below own their state independently.

<ComponentExample name="states" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function CheckboxStates() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Checkbox id={`${id}-checked`} defaultChecked />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-checked`}>Checked by default</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Checkbox id={`${id}-mixed`} indeterminate />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-mixed`}>Some projects selected</Label>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

The caller owns acceptance and its status. Reset acceptance is an external update to this example alone; it does not change the top specimen or any other checkbox.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function ControlledCheckbox() {
  const id = useId();
  const [accepted, setAccepted] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Checkbox id={id} checked={accepted} onCheckedChange={setAccepted} />
        <Label htmlFor={id}>Accept the terms</Label>
      </div>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {accepted ? "Terms accepted" : "Terms not accepted"}
      </p>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setAccepted(false)}>
        Reset acceptance
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Invalid, with a described error

The caller supplies `aria-invalid` and the described error. Checking the box does not clear the error automatically: the application decides when it is resolved.

<ComponentExample name="invalid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function InvalidCheckbox() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Checkbox id={id} aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby={`${id}-error`} />
        <Label htmlFor={id}>Accept the terms</Label>
      </div>
      <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-destructive">
        You must accept the terms to continue.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## In a row of settings

Associate the visible label and help text with one unique control. The description remains available when the label wraps on a narrow screen.

<ComponentExample name="settings" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function CheckboxSettings() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex items-start gap-3">
      <Checkbox id={id} aria-describedby={`${id}-help`} className="mt-0.5" />
      <div className="grid gap-1">
        <Label htmlFor={id}>Send the weekly digest</Label>
        <p id={`${id}-help`} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          Every Monday, 09:00.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled and read-only

Disabled choices retain their checked or unchecked state and are skipped by keyboard navigation. A read-only choice stays focusable but cannot be changed. The group disabled marker also dims its label; Base UI does not use a native disabled button.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function DisabledCheckboxes() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="group flex items-center gap-3" data-disabled="true">
        <Checkbox id={`${id}-off`} disabled />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-off`}>Unavailable, unchecked</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="group flex items-center gap-3" data-disabled="true">
        <Checkbox id={`${id}-on`} disabled defaultChecked />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-on`}>Unavailable, checked</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Checkbox id={`${id}-readonly`} readOnly defaultChecked />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-readonly`}>Read-only preference</Label>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Native form submission

`name` and `value` define the native form entry. `required` uses browser constraint validation before this caller-owned submit handler runs. Server-side validation and persistence remain the application’s responsibility.

<ComponentExample name="form-submission" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function CheckboxForm() {
  const id = useId();
  const [result, setResult] = useState("Not submitted");
  return (
    <form
      className="grid gap-4"
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget);
        setResult(`Submitted consent: ${data.get("consent")}`);
      }}
    >
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Checkbox id={id} name="consent" value="accepted" required />
        <Label htmlFor={id}>Accept the terms (required)</Label>
      </div>
      <Button type="submit" size="sm">
        Submit consent
      </Button>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {result}
      </p>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The checked control is explicitly `none` from its first render, so its tick appears immediately and still toggles. Its neighbour explicitly restores `full` inside that scope; the system reduced-motion preference still takes precedence. These are deliberate local overrides. Ordinary examples follow the site header.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function StaticCheckbox() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <div data-testid="initial-none">
          <Checkbox aria-label="Static checkbox" className="inline-flex" defaultChecked />
        </div>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Checkbox aria-label="Explicit full checkbox" />
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- One independent yes/no choice: accept the terms, remember this device, include
  archived items.
- A set of choices where several can be true at once; use one checkbox per row.
- A parent row that summarises children: pass `indeterminate` while the children
  disagree.
- A table row selection, where each row is its own decision.

## When not to use

- Exactly one of several options; use `radio-group`, which also gives arrow-key
  navigation.
- An immediate setting that applies the moment it is flipped; use `switch`.
- A formatting command that acts on a selection; use `toggle`.

## API

| Prop               | Type                              | Default | Description                                          |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`          | `boolean`                         | –       | Controlled state.                                    |
| `defaultChecked`   | `boolean`                         | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state.                          |
| `onCheckedChange`  | `(checked, details) => void`      | –       | Fired on click and on Space.                         |
| `indeterminate`    | `boolean`                         | `false` | Mixed visual state for a parent row.                 |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                         | `false` | Ignores interaction and form submission.             |
| `readOnly`         | `boolean`                         | `false` | Focusable, submitted, not changeable.                |
| `required`         | `boolean`                         | `false` | Blocks form submission until checked.                |
| `name`, `value`    | `string`                          | –       | Form field identity and submitted value.             |
| `className`        | `string` / state callback                          | –       | Merged last.                                         |

All native attributes are forwarded, including `aria-invalid` and
`aria-describedby`.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. The tick is the protagonist — it fades in and settles from
0.96 to full size when the box is checked, and reverses when it is cleared.

| Phase   | Properties                    | Token          | Interruptible |
| ------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| check   | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes (re-click) |
| clear   | the same pair, reversed       | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| reduced | `opacity` only                | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| none    | no transition                 | –              | –             |

Only the indicator moves. The box itself keeps a `transition-shadow` for the focus
ring and the invalid ring, which is colour/shadow state feedback, not motion.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys          | Action                                     |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab`         | Moves focus to the checkbox.               |
| `Space`       | Toggles checked, unless `readOnly`.        |
| `Shift+Tab`   | Moves focus to the previous control.       |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders `role="checkbox"` on the visible element plus a hidden
  `<input type="checkbox">`, so the control is in the form and in the tab order.
- The tick is not the announcement: the state lives in `aria-checked`, which is
  why the reduced and `none` branches stay usable.
- Always pair the box with a `Label` (`htmlFor`) or an `aria-label`; a bare box
  has no accessible name.
- `indeterminate` announces as "mixed". Do not use it as a substitute for
  `checked` in a form.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                  | You do                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid` and forwards it to the input   | Deciding whether the box must be checked             |
| Forwards `required`, `name`, `value`, `disabled`     | Building the submitted payload                       |
| Announces `aria-checked` for all three states        | Mapping the error to the field with `aria-describedby` |

There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `rules` prop. [Field](/components/field) shows how the
invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

The control is fixed at 16px with a 44px touch target (the `after:` pseudo
element extends the hit area), so it behaves the same at every breakpoint. Put the
label beside it, not inside it; wrapping a checkbox in a label removes the
`aria-describedby` chain.

## Performance

No JS animation loop: one Motion element per box, animating only `opacity` and
`transform`. A list of 50 checkboxes is 50 short transitions on demand, never a
running loop.

## Notes for AI

- Use `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` for errors; there is no `error` prop.
- Do not add press animation to a checkbox; the tick is the only protagonist.
- For "one of N", use `radio-group`; for an instant setting, use `switch`.

# Radio Group

Choosing one option from a small, fixed set.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/radio-group
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| radio-group | `@components/cadence/radio-group/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/radio-group.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: radio-group](https://cadence.dev/r/radio-group.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine files in the target list, including every file from the motion,
utilities and provider payloads. Keep `radio-group/index.tsx` beside the shared
`lib/` directory with its relative imports and the sources' `"use client"`
directives intact. The dot uses `ControlSpan`, whose imports also reach
`native-div.tsx` and `press-button.tsx`; copying only `provider.tsx` is not enough.
The provider files and `motion` package are required even without an application
wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied
files. There is no additional Radio Group-specific CSS, icon package or external
asset. Only the dots animate: `state.morph` uses opacity and scale in
full, keeps opacity with immediate full size in reduced, and settles immediately
in none, including an initially selected item. Standalone groups follow the
system motion preference; the optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree's
mode and timing. A nested full scope still respects system reduced motion.

Usage, the top specimen and the labelled examples also need
[Label](/components/label). Controlled and Native form submission additionally
use [Button](/components/button). Install the items needed by your example:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/label @cadence/button
```

For manual installation, follow their Manual tabs too: add `label/index.tsx`
and, when using Button, `button/index.tsx`. Their shared files are already in
Radio Group's target list. Label adds no npm package; Button also requires:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

Explicit motion scopes uses only Radio Group and the included provider. No
example needs another package or external asset. The site's preview shell is
not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Controlled and Native form submission need a client
module for their state and event handlers. The other snippets can be composed
in a synchronous Server Component using the shown `useId` or stable unique IDs,
JSX and serializable props; their existing client directives may also be kept.
An event handler, a function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)`,
or a client-side hook such as `useState` or `useRef` needs a caller client
boundary. Preserve the installed sources' client directives in either case.

Name each group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Give every item a unique
`value` and a visible label linked by `htmlFor` and a unique `id`, or an
`aria-label`. With the default renderer, the item is a visible `span` with
`role="radio"` beside a hidden native radio input; the supplied item `id` belongs
to that input and Base UI connects the label to the visible control. Use
`defaultValue` for an uncontrolled initial selection, or own `value` with
`onValueChange` for a controlled group.

Tab enters at the selected item, or the first enabled item when none is selected.
Arrow keys move focus and selection, wrap, and skip disabled items; Space selects
the focused item. There is one tab stop per group. Group `disabled` disables all
items and removes them from the tab sequence. `readOnly` keeps the choices
focusable while preventing selection changes. Keep each default item in a flex
or grid layout, as the examples do; a horizontal layout changes the arrangement,
not the keyboard model.

For native submission, put `name` on the group and `value` on each item. Only the
selected, enabled input contributes the group's name/value entry; no selection
or a disabled selection contributes nothing. A read-only selected input retains
its submission value. `required` uses browser constraint validation to prevent
submission without a choice. The caller owns allowed values, controlled state,
error text, submission, server-side validation and persistence. Cadence renders
the supplied group error semantics; also pass `aria-invalid` to each item when
its ring should show the error. Selecting an option does not clear a caller's
error automatically.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/radio-group";

export function PlanChoices() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <RadioGroup defaultValue="team" aria-label="Plan" className="w-full max-w-xs gap-3">
      {["starter", "team", "scale"].map((plan) => (
        <div key={plan} className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-${plan}`} value={plan} />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-${plan}`}>{plan === "starter" ? "Starter" : plan === "team" ? "Team" : "Scale"}</Label>
        </div>
      ))}
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

Every item needs a `value`. The group is one form field: `name` goes on the
group, not on the items.

## Controlled

The caller owns the selected plan and status. Choose Team is an external update to this group only; choosing an item still uses the normal radio interaction.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/radio-group";

export function ControlledPlan() {
  const id = useId();
  const [plan, setPlan] = useState("team");
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <RadioGroup value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan} aria-label="Controlled plan">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-team`} value="team" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-team`}>Team</Label>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-scale`} value="scale" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-scale`}>Scale</Label>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Selected plan: {plan}
      </p>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setPlan("team")}>
        Choose Team
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Invalid

Put the error semantics on the group and connect its message with `aria-describedby`. Each item also receives `aria-invalid` for its destructive ring; the source does not infer an item’s invalid styling from an ancestor. The caller clears the error when appropriate.

<ComponentExample name="invalid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/radio-group";

export function InvalidPlan() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <RadioGroup aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby={`${id}-error`} aria-label="Required plan">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-team`} value="team" aria-invalid="true" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-team`}>Team</Label>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-scale`} value="scale" aria-invalid="true" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-scale`}>Scale</Label>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup>
      <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-destructive">
        Choose a plan to continue.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled item

The unavailable option stays visible and announced. Arrow keys skip it while keeping one selected item and one tab stop. The disabled group marker dims only that item’s label.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";

      </div>
      <div className="group flex items-center gap-3" data-disabled="true">
        <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-enterprise`} value="enterprise" disabled />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-enterprise`}>Enterprise (unavailable)</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-scale`} value="scale" />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-scale`}>Scale</Label>
      </div>
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

## Disabled and read-only groups

Group `disabled` disables every item and removes the group from the tab sequence. `readOnly` retains focus and the current selection while preventing changes. These are two independent groups.

<ComponentExample name="locked" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/radio-group";

export function LockedPlans() {

  return (
    <div className="grid gap-6">
      <RadioGroup defaultValue="team" disabled aria-label="Disabled plan">
        <div className="group flex items-center gap-3" data-disabled="true">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-disabled-team`} value="team" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-disabled-team`}>Team</Label>
        </div>
        <div className="group flex items-center gap-3" data-disabled="true">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-disabled-scale`} value="scale" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-disabled-scale`}>Scale</Label>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup>
      <RadioGroup defaultValue="team" readOnly aria-label="Read-only plan">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-readonly-team`} value="team" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-readonly-team`}>Team (read-only)</Label>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-readonly-scale`} value="scale" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-readonly-scale`}>Scale (read-only)</Label>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Horizontal layout

The default layout is a vertical grid. Short labels can use a wrapping flex row; layout classes belong to the caller and do not change the radio keyboard model.

<ComponentExample name="horizontal" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";

export function HorizontalPlans() {

    <RadioGroup defaultValue="daily" aria-label="Digest frequency" className="flex flex-wrap gap-6">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">

        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-daily`}>Daily</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-weekly`} value="weekly" />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-weekly`}>Weekly</Label>
      </div>
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

## Native form submission

The group owns one form name and submits the selected value. Native `required` prevents submission until a choice is made. This local handler displays the entry; the application still validates and saves it on the server.

<ComponentExample name="form-submission" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/radio-group";

export function ShippingForm() {
  const id = useId();
  const [result, setResult] = useState("Not submitted");
  return (
    <form
      className="grid gap-4"
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        setResult(`Shipping: ${new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("shipping")}`);
      }}
    >
      <RadioGroup name="shipping" required aria-label="Shipping method">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-standard`} value="standard" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-standard`}>Standard</Label>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <RadioGroupItem id={`${id}-express`} value="express" />
          <Label htmlFor={`${id}-express`}>Express</Label>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup>
      <Button type="submit" size="sm">
        Submit shipping
      </Button>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {result}
      </p>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The selected dot on the left is explicitly `none` from its first render. The independent group on the right explicitly restores `full` inside that scope, subject to system reduced-motion preferences. Ordinary groups inherit the site header; these overrides are fixed for this comparison.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/radio-group";

export function StaticRadio() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <div data-testid="initial-none">
          <RadioGroup defaultValue="static" aria-label="Static choice">
            <RadioGroupItem value="static" aria-label="Static radio" />
          </RadioGroup>
        </div>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <RadioGroup aria-label="Explicit full choice">
            <RadioGroupItem value="animated" aria-label="Explicit full radio" />
          </RadioGroup>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A small, fixed set of options where exactly one applies: a plan, a priority, a
  shipping method.
- Anywhere seeing all the options at once matters more than saving space.
- A setting that applies on submit, not immediately.

## When not to use

- Several answers can be true; use `checkbox`.
- The setting applies the moment it changes; use `switch`.
- More than about seven options, or a list that is filtered as you type; use
  `select` or `combobox`, which handle long lists and search.

## API

### `RadioGroup`

| Prop            | Type                                          | Default | Description                                     |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                                      | –       | Controlled selection.                           |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                                      | –       | Uncontrolled initial selection.                 |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details) => void`                    | –       | Fired when the selection changes.               |
| `name`          | `string`                                      | –       | Form field name, submitted with the selection.  |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                                     | `false` | Disables every item.                            |
| `required`      | `boolean`                                     | `false` | Blocks submit until something is selected.      |
| `className`     | `string` / state callback                                      | –       | Merged last; the default is `grid gap-3`.       |

### `RadioGroupItem`

| Prop        | Type      | Default | Description                              |
| ----------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `value`     | `string`  | –       | Required. Identifies this option.        |
| `disabled`  | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the option visible but unselectable.|
| `className` | `string` / state callback  | –       | Merged last.                             |

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. The dot of the newly selected item fades in and settles
from 0.96 to full size; the previously selected dot reverses. Nothing else in the
row moves, so the eye follows the choice.

| Phase     | Properties                        | Token          | Interruptible |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| select    | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| deselect  | the same pair, reversed           | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| reduced   | `opacity` only                    | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| none      | no transition                     | –              | –             |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                | Action                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`               | Enters the group at the selected item (or the first one).     |
| `Arrow Right/Down`  | Selects the next item and moves focus.                        |
| `Arrow Left/Up`     | Selects the previous item and moves focus.                    |
| `Space`             | Selects the focused item.                                     |

There is one tab stop for the whole group, not one per item: that is the roving
tabindex Base UI implements.

## Accessibility

- The group renders `role="radiogroup"`; each item renders `role="radio"` with a
  hidden input, so the form still submits a value.
- `aria-checked` carries the state on its own. The dot animation is never the only
  signal.
- Name the group with `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible heading, or with
  `aria-label` when a heading would be redundant.
- `aria-invalid` on the group describes the whole choice; pass it to each item too when its ring should show the supplied error.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                 | You do                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Forwards `aria-invalid` on the group and items   | Deciding that a choice is required                |
| Forwards `name`, `required`, and the selection      | Server-side validation of the submitted value     |
| Keeps arrow-key navigation within the group         | Focus policy after a failed submit                |

There is no `validate` or `schema` prop. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid
state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Items stack by default (`grid gap-3`). For a horizontal row of short labels, set
`className="flex flex-wrap gap-6"`; do not shorten the labels to fit — wrap them.

## Performance

One Motion element per item, each animating only `opacity` and `transform`, and
only when the selection changes. No layout thrash: the dot is absolutely sized by
CSS, so no measurement happens.

## Notes for AI

- Use `radio-group` for "one of N" and `checkbox` for "any of N".
- Put `name` on the group. Describe the group error with `aria-invalid` and pass it to items too when their rings should show the error.
- Do not build a radio group out of buttons with `aria-pressed`; the radio role
  is what gives arrow-key navigation and form submission.

# Switch

Settings that take effect immediately, such as alerts or visibility.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/switch
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — transitive registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| switch | `@components/cadence/switch/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/switch.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: switch](https://cadence.dev/r/switch.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine files in the target list, including every file from the motion,
utilities and provider payloads. Keep `switch/index.tsx` beside the shared `lib/`
directory with its relative imports and the sources' `"use client"` directives
intact. The thumb uses `ControlSpan`, whose imports also reach `native-div.tsx`
and `press-button.tsx`; copying only `provider.tsx` is not enough. The provider
files and `motion` package are required even without an application wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied
files. There is no additional Switch-specific CSS, icon package or external
asset. `state.morph` animates only the thumb's horizontal transform in full;
reduced and none jump to the checked endpoint without travel animation. The
track colour is state feedback. Both `default` and `sm` measure their own travel
with `ResizeObserver`; the first measured position settles immediately, including
an initially checked switch in none. Standalone switches follow the system
motion preference. The optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree's mode and
timing; a nested full scope still respects system reduced motion.

Usage, the top specimen and the labelled examples also need
[Label](/components/label). Controlled additionally uses [Button](/components/button).
Install the items needed by your example:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/label @cadence/button
```

For manual installation, follow their Manual tabs too: add `label/index.tsx`
and, when using Button, `button/index.tsx`. Their shared files are already in
Switch's target list. Label adds no npm package; Button also requires:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

Explicit motion scopes uses only Switch and the included provider. No example
needs another package or external asset. The site's preview shell is not
consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Controlled needs a client module for `useState`,
`onCheckedChange` and the external button's click handler. Usage, Sizes, In a
settings row, Disabled and read-only, and Explicit motion scopes can be composed
in a synchronous Server Component using the shown `useId` or stable unique IDs,
JSX and serializable props; their existing client directives may also be kept.
An event handler, a function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)`,
or a client-side hook such as `useState` or `useRef` needs a caller client
boundary. Preserve the installed sources' client directives in either case.

Give every switch a visible label linked by `htmlFor` and a unique `id`, or an
`aria-label`; connect help text with `aria-describedby`. With the default renderer,
the visible control is a `span` with `role="switch"` beside a hidden native
checkbox input. The supplied `id` belongs to that input and Base UI connects the
label to the visible control. Use `defaultChecked` for an uncontrolled initial
state, or own `checked` with `onCheckedChange` for a controlled switch.

Tab focuses an enabled switch; Space and Enter toggle it. `disabled` prevents
interaction and removes it from the tab sequence. `readOnly` keeps it focusable
while preventing changes. Keep the control from shrinking and let the surrounding
label and description wrap, as the settings row does.

For native submission, supply `name` and optionally `value` and `form`. A checked,
enabled switch contributes its name/value entry, with `"on"` as the default value.
An unchecked switch contributes nothing unless `uncheckedValue` supplies an
explicit off value. Disabled switches contribute neither value; a checked
read-only switch retains its entry. `required` uses browser constraint validation
to prevent submission while unchecked. The caller owns allowed state, error
messages, submission, server-side validation and persistence, including save
failures for immediate settings. Cadence forwards supplied `aria-invalid`;
provide a visible error message, as it adds no destructive track style.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Switch } from "@/components/cadence/switch";

export function SwitchSettings() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-md items-center justify-between gap-4">
      <div className="grid gap-1">
        <Label htmlFor={id}>Deploy alerts</Label>
        <p id={`${id}-help`} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          A notification for every failed build.
        </p>
      </div>
      <Switch id={id} aria-describedby={`${id}-help`} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

Both `default` and `sm` are fixed here, each initially off and on. Travel is measured from the track and thumb, so either size lands at its own endpoint. Each switch remains independently interactive.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Switch } from "@/components/cadence/switch";

export function SwitchSizes() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-6 gap-y-4">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Switch id={`${id}-off`} />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-off`}>Off</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Switch id={`${id}-on`} defaultChecked />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-on`}>On</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Switch id={`${id}-small-off`} size="sm" />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-small-off`}>Small</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Switch id={`${id}-small-on`} size="sm" defaultChecked />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-small-on`}>Small, on</Label>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

The caller owns this immediate preference and status. Turn alerts off demonstrates an external update, separate from the other examples. This example keeps state locally; a real application persists the preference and reports save failures.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Switch } from "@/components/cadence/switch";

export function ControlledSwitch() {
  const id = useId();
  const [on, setOn] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Switch id={id} checked={on} onCheckedChange={setOn} />
        <Label htmlFor={id}>Alerts</Label>
      </div>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Alerts {on ? "on" : "off"} in this example
      </p>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setOn(false)}>
        Turn alerts off
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## In a settings row

The label names the setting and the description explains its effect. The switch keeps its size while the caller’s row lets the text wrap.

<ComponentExample name="settings" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";

      <div className="grid gap-1">

        <p id={`${id}-help`} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          A notification for every failed build.
        </p>
      </div>

```

## Disabled and read-only

Disabled switches retain their state and leave the tab order. Read-only stays focusable but cannot change. The disabled row marker also dims the label; neither state is a substitute for explaining why a setting is unavailable.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Switch } from "@/components/cadence/switch";

export function DisabledSwitches() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="group flex items-center gap-3" data-disabled="true">
        <Switch id={`${id}-off`} disabled />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-off`}>Unavailable, off</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="group flex items-center gap-3" data-disabled="true">
        <Switch id={`${id}-on`} disabled defaultChecked />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-on`}>Unavailable, on</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Switch id={`${id}-readonly`} readOnly defaultChecked />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-readonly`}>Read-only setting</Label>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The checked switch is explicitly `none` from its first render. Its thumb still reaches the measured checked endpoint, then jumps immediately when toggled. The neighbour explicitly restores `full` inside that scope, subject to system reduced-motion preferences. Ordinary switches follow the site header.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Switch } from "@/components/cadence/switch";

export function StaticSwitch() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <div data-testid="initial-none">
          <Switch aria-label="Static switch" defaultChecked />
        </div>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Switch aria-label="Explicit full switch" />
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A setting that takes effect immediately: public/private, alerts on/off, a feature
  flag.
- A row in a settings list, where the label describes the thing and the switch
  describes its state.
- A preference with no submit button. Flipping it saves.

## When not to use

- The change is only applied on submit; use `checkbox`, which is the familiar form
  control for a pending decision.
- One of several options; use `radio-group`.
- A formatting command on a selection; use `toggle`.

## API

| Prop              | Type                        | Default     | Description                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`                   | –           | Controlled state.                              |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`                   | `false`     | Uncontrolled initial state.                    |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked, details) => void`| –           | Fired on click and on Space.                   |
| `size`            | `"sm" \| "default"`         | `"default"` | Track and thumb scale.                         |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`                   | `false`     | Ignores interaction and form submission.       |
| `readOnly`        | `boolean`                   | `false`     | Focusable, submitted, not changeable.          |
| `required`        | `boolean`                   | `false`     | Blocks submit until switched on.               |
| `name`, `value`   | `string`                    | –           | Form field identity and submitted value.       |
| `className`       | `string` / state callback                    | –           | Merged last.                                   |

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. The thumb travels from one end of the track to the other
while the track recolours. The travel distance is measured from the rendered track
and thumb — no hard-coded pixel value — so a custom size still lands flush.

| Phase   | Properties                         | Token          | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| on      | `translateX 0 → track − thumb`     | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| off     | the same distance, reversed        | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| reduced | no travel animation; the thumb jumps to the new end | – | –     |
| none    | no transition                      | –              | –             |

Under `reduced` the thumb still ends up in the right place: position is state, not
decoration. What is dropped is the animation, so the movement is instant.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys    | Action                                  |
| ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves focus to the switch.              |
| `Space` | Toggles the switch, unless `readOnly`.  |
| `Enter` | Toggles with the default Base UI keyboard handling, unless `readOnly`. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders `role="switch"` with `aria-checked` and a hidden input, so the
  value is submitted with the form.
- The state is not carried by colour alone: the thumb position, the track colour,
  and `aria-checked` change together.
- Give it a name with `Label htmlFor` or `aria-label`. "On" is a state, not a name.
- A switch that saves immediately should announce the outcome (a `toast` or an
  inline status), because there is no submit step to confirm it.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                              | You do                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Forwards `name`, `value`, `disabled`, `required` | Persisting the setting and handling failures     |
| Forwards supplied `aria-invalid`                   | Deciding whether the switch needs one at all     |
| Renders the on/off state                         | Announcing that the change was saved             |

Invalid semantics do not add a destructive track style; supply a visible error message when needed.
There is no `validate` or `schema` prop. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state
and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

The control is fixed-size at every breakpoint; the row around it is what changes.
In a narrow layout, let the label and description wrap above the switch instead of
shrinking the track.

## Performance

One `ResizeObserver` per switch measures the travel, so a font or layout change
does not desynchronise the thumb. The animation itself is a single `transform`
transition with no layout reads during interaction.

## Notes for AI

- Use `switch` only for immediate settings. If there is a Save button, use
  `checkbox`.
- Do not animate the track colour as motion; colour is state feedback.
- Keep the label outside the switch. A switch with no label has no accessible name.
