keep its scale at one with a zero clock. Pointer and keyboard values still
update immediately in every mode, and the fill has no authored transition.
Standalone sliders follow the system motion preference. The optional
`CadenceProvider` controls a subtree's mode and timing; nested full still
respects system reduced motion.

Usage, the top specimen, Range, Vertical, Disabled, Thumb collisions, Thumb
alignment and Explicit motion scopes use only Slider and its included helpers.
Controlled also needs [Button](/components/button):

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

For manual installation, follow Button's Manual tab too and add
`button/index.tsx`. Its shared files are already in Slider's target list; the
additional npm dependency is:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

No example needs another package or external asset. The site's preview shell is
not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Usage, Controlled and Range need a client module for
their `useState` and value-change handlers; Controlled also handles an external
button click. Vertical, Disabled, Thumb collisions, Thumb alignment and Explicit
motion scopes can be composed in a synchronous Server Component with the shown
JSX and serializable props; their existing client directives may also be kept.
An event handler, a function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)`,
or a client-side hook such as `useState` or `useRef` needs a caller client
boundary. Keep the installed sources' client directives in either case.

Supply an explicit numeric `defaultValue` for an uncontrolled single thumb, or
own `value` with `onValueChange` for a controlled slider. Arrays create one thumb
per entry; use ordered values within `min` and `max`, a positive `step` and a
valid `minStepsBetweenValues` for the available range. `onValueChange` reports
user changes; `onValueCommitted` reports a completed change. An external state
reset does not create a user commit. `format` and `locale` change the announced
value text, not the stored number.

Give each slider an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and show the current
value when precision matters. With two thumbs, `aria-label` gains minimum and
maximum suffixes; larger arrays gain numbered suffixes. A supplied
`aria-labelledby` is shared by the thumbs, so choose labels that make the range
understandable. Each thumb contains a native `input[type="range"]`; the root
`id` is not that input's id. Root `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` are not
automatically copied onto each native input. The caller owns error text and
native thumb associations; this wrapper exposes no per-thumb props.

Tab visits enabled thumbs. In left-to-right direction, Right/Up increase and
Left/Down decrease by `step`; Page Up/Down and Shift+arrows use `largeStep`.
Home/End move to the permitted endpoint, respecting neighbouring thumbs and
their minimum separation. `thumbCollisionBehavior` selects the pointer policy;
it does not remove keyboard bounds. Horizontal sliders fill their container;
give a vertical slider an explicit height, as Vertical does. Cadence defaults to
edge alignment. `edge-client-only` keeps its thumbs hidden until client
measurement, so use edge or center when thumbs must be visible before hydration.

For native submission, supply `name` and optionally `form`. Each enabled thumb's
range input contributes a numeric string under the same name; use
`FormData.getAll(name)` for a range. There is no extra hidden aggregate input.
Disabled sliders ignore interaction, leave the tab sequence and contribute no
entries. The caller owns acceptable values, parsing, error messages, submission,
server-side validation and persistence. Keep these rules outside the UI; native
range bounds are not business validation.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function VolumeSlider() {
  const [volume, setVolume] = useState(68);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-3">
      <p className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 text-sm">
        <span>Volume</span>
        <span className="text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">{volume}%</span>
      </p>
      <Slider aria-label="Volume" value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

`defaultValue` and `value` accept a number for one thumb, or an array with one entry per thumb. `aria-label`
on the slider is forwarded to every thumb's native range input, which is what a
screen reader announces. A range slider gets one accessible name per thumb —
`Price (minimum)` and `Price (maximum)` — because two inputs with the same name
are indistinguishable.

## Controlled

The caller owns the numeric value. `onValueChange` updates it during a gesture; `onValueCommitted` records the completed user change. Reset volume is an external value update, so it does not invent a new user commit or change any other example.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function ControlledSlider() {
  const [volume, setVolume] = useState(60);
  const [committed, setCommitted] = useState<number | null>(null);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-4">
      <Slider value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} onValueCommitted={setCommitted} aria-label="Controlled volume" />
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">
        Volume: {volume}%; last committed: {committed === null ? "not changed" : `${committed}%`}
      </p>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setVolume(60)}>
        Reset volume
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Range

An array creates one thumb per entry. This price band steps by 10 and keeps two steps between values. Each thumb gets a distinct accessible name; `format` and `locale` provide currency value text without changing the stored numbers.

<ComponentExample name="range" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function PriceRange() {
  const [price, setPrice] = useState([120, 480]);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-3">
      <p className="text-sm tabular-nums">
        Price: ${price[0]} – ${price[1]}
      </p>
      <Slider
        value={price}
        onValueChange={setPrice}
        min={0}
        max={600}
        step={10}
        minStepsBetweenValues={2}
        format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0 }}
        locale="en-US"
        aria-label="Price"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Vertical

Give a vertical slider a height. This independent slider starts at 64 and uses the same native keyboard steps as the horizontal control; its track fills the supplied 10rem height.

<ComponentExample name="vertical" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function VerticalSlider() {
  return <Slider orientation="vertical" defaultValue={64} className="h-40" aria-label="Level" />;
}
```

## Disabled

The disabled slider stays visible at 40, but ignores pointer and keyboard changes. Explain the unavailable setting in nearby text rather than relying on a dimmed track alone.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function DisabledSlider() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-3">
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Volume unavailable: 40%</p>
      <Slider defaultValue={40} disabled aria-label="Unavailable volume" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Thumb collisions

Each range has a fixed collision policy. While dragging, `push` moves the neighbouring thumb, `swap` hands the active thumb across the other value, and `none` clamps at the other thumb. These are independent ranges with the same starting values, not a policy selector. Keyboard bounds still respect the ordered values.

<ComponentExample name="collisions" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function SliderCollisions() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-6">
      {(["push", "swap", "none"] as const).map((behavior) => (
        <div key={behavior} className="grid gap-3">
          <p className="text-sm">{behavior === "none" ? "Clamped" : behavior === "push" ? "Push" : "Swap"}</p>
          <Slider defaultValue={[30, 60]} thumbCollisionBehavior={behavior} aria-label={`${behavior} range`} />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Thumb alignment

Cadence defaults to `edge`, placing the whole thumb inside the track endpoints. `center` places its centre on the endpoint. `edge-client-only` retains its thumb and native input in the server DOM, hidden until client measurement reveals them with edge geometry. Without JavaScript they stay hidden; the track and this explanation remain readable. Use `edge` or `center` when thumbs must be visible before hydration.

<ComponentExample name="alignment" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function SliderAlignment() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-6">
      {(["edge", "center", "edge-client-only"] as const).map((alignment) => (
        <div key={alignment} className="grid gap-3">
          <p className="text-sm">{alignment}</p>
          <Slider defaultValue={0} thumbAlignment={alignment} aria-label={`${alignment} alignment`} />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The first slider is explicitly `none` from its first render. Its value still follows pointer and keyboard input immediately, with no press scale. The second explicitly restores `full` inside that scope, subject to the system reduced-motion preference. Ordinary examples inherit the site header.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function StaticSlider() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-6">
        <div data-testid="initial-none">
          <Slider defaultValue={50} aria-label="Static slider" />
        </div>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Slider defaultValue={50} aria-label="Explicit full slider" />
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A value where the rough position matters more than the exact number: volume,
  brightness, zoom, opacity.
- A range (two thumbs): price between, time window, budget band.
- A filter where the user should feel the bounds instead of typing them.

## When not to use

- An exact number matters and the range is wide; pair a `slider` with an `input`,
  or use `input` alone.
- Fewer than about five discrete options; use `radio-group` or `toggle-group`.
- A value with no natural order, like picking a colour name.

## API

| Prop                 | Type                              | Default        | Description                                     |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `value`              | `number \| readonly number[]`     | –              | Controlled value, one entry per thumb.          |
| `defaultValue`       | same as `value`                   | –              | Uncontrolled initial value.                     |
| `onValueChange`      | `(value, details) => void`        | –              | Fired while dragging and on keyboard steps.     |
| `min`, `max`         | `number`                          | `0`, `100`     | Bounds.                                         |
| `step`               | `number`                          | `1`            | Snap increment.                                 |
| `orientation`        | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"`      | `"horizontal"` | Axis.                                           |
| `disabled`           | `boolean`                         | `false`        | Ignores pointer and keyboard.                   |
| `aria-label`         | `string`                          | –              | Forwarded to each thumb, suffixed per thumb.    |
| `className`          | `string` / state callback                          | –              | Merged last.                                    |

Base UI's `format`, `locale`, and `minStepsBetweenValues` are forwarded unchanged.

| Additional prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onValueCommitted` | `(value, details) => void` | – | Reports a completed user change. |
| `largeStep` | `number` | `10` | Page and Shift+arrow increment. |
| `minStepsBetweenValues` | `number` | `0` | Minimum separation, in steps. |
| `thumbCollisionBehavior` | `"push" \| "swap" \| "none"` | `"push"` | Pointer collision policy. |
| `thumbAlignment` | `"edge" \| "center" \| "edge-client-only"` | `"edge"` | Thumb position at endpoints. |
| `name`, `form` | `string` | – | Native form identity and owner. |

## Motion contract

Recipe: `feedback.press`. The dragged thumb compresses to 0.97 and springs back on
release — the same press language as `button` and `toggle`.

| Phase   | Properties              | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ----------------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| drag    | `scale 1 → 0.97`        | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1`        | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| reduced | no scale; the ring grows on focus/hover | – | –             |
| none    | no scale                | –                | –             |

The fill is deliberately not animated: it is glued to the pointer, and a
transition would make it trail the thumb by one frame per move.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                | Action                                  |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`               | Moves focus to the thumb.               |
| `Arrow Right/Up`    | Increases by one `step`.                |
| `Arrow Left/Down`   | Decreases by one `step`.                |
| `Page Up`/`Page Down` | Moves by a larger increment.           |
| `Home`/`End`        | Jumps to `min` / `max`.                 |

## Accessibility

- Every thumb contains a native `input[type=range]`, so the control works with
  assistive technology without a custom role.
- Always pass `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) — the fill has no text.
- Show the current value as text next to the slider when the number matters.
  Dragging is not a way to read a value.
- Supplied `aria-invalid` stays on the root; this wrapper does not add destructive colours or per-thumb error descriptions. The caller owns error text and native thumb associations (P11).

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                | You do                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Reports the value through `onValueChange`         | Deciding whether the range is acceptable            |
| Forwards supplied `aria-invalid` on the root                             | Writing the error text and its `aria-describedby` id |
| Steps and clamps the value to `min`/`max`         | Server-side bounds and business rules               |

[Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Horizontal sliders fill their container (`w-full`); vertical ones fill their
height. On touch screens the thumb keeps a 16px visual size but the range input
covers the whole control, so drag targets stay reachable.

## Performance

The value updates on pointer move without React re-rendering the whole form: Base
UI moves the thumb with a CSS custom property, and Motion animates only the press
scale. No `layout` animation, no measurement per frame.

## Notes for AI

- A numeric value renders one thumb; an array renders one thumb per entry. Omitting both values retains the upstream two-thumb default.
- Do not animate the fill. Motion here is press feedback only.
- Pair with an `input` when the exact number must be typeable.

# Toggle

Bold, italic, preview, and other on/off modes.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toggle
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |

| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| toggle | `@components/cadence/toggle/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: toggle](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, keeping `toggle/index.tsx` beside the shared `lib/`
directory and preserving the relative imports and `"use client"` directives.
The default renderer imports `press-button.tsx`, which reaches
`control-animation.tsx` and `native-div.tsx`; copy every file in the motion,
utilities and provider payloads. The provider files and `motion` package are
required imports even when you do not wrap the application in a provider.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied
files. Toggle needs no additional item-specific CSS or external asset. The
default renderer uses `feedback.press` for its press scale in full; reduced and
none keep scale at one with a zero clock. Pressed colours still communicate
state in every mode. Standalone toggles follow the system motion preference;
the optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree's mode and timing. A nested
full scope still respects system reduced motion.

Usage, the top specimen, With a label, Controlled and Inside a form use icons.
They need this example-only dependency; Toggle itself does not:

```package-manager
npm install lucide-react
```

Controlled and Inside a form also need [Button](/components/button):

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

For manual installation, follow Button's Manual tab and add `button/index.tsx`.
Its npm dependencies and shared files are already in Toggle's installation
graph. Variants, Sizes, Disabled and Explicit motion scopes need only Toggle
and the included helpers. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Controlled and Inside a form need a client module for
`useState`, change handlers and click or submit handlers. Usage, Variants,
Sizes, With a label, Disabled and Explicit motion scopes can be composed in a
synchronous Server Component with the shown JSX and serializable props. A
caller ref, event handler, function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or
`style(state)`, or a client-side hook such as `useState` or `useRef` needs a
caller client boundary. Keep the installed sources' client directives.

Use `defaultPressed` for initial uncontrolled state, or own `pressed` with
`onPressedChange` for controlled state. The callback receives the next boolean
and event details; `details.cancel()` vetoes the change. Give icon-only buttons
an `aria-label`; text children can supply the name. Enabled buttons are reached
with Tab and toggle with Space or Enter. `disabled` blocks activation and
removes the button from the tab order while retaining its pressed state.

The default element is a native `button` with `type="button"` and
`aria-pressed`. Toggle does not expose a submit-button `type` or `form`
association, generate a hidden input, or submit its pressed state through
`name`. Its `value` identifies an item in a Toggle Group, not a submitted
checked value. Inside a form explicitly maps caller state to a hidden input;
use Checkbox when you need a checked form control. The caller owns state,
persistence, validation, error text and any `aria-invalid` / `aria-describedby`
association.

Native animation and drag handlers, state-based classes/styles and refs pass
through the default renderer. A caller `render` replaces that renderer and
its press effect; spread the supplied props and preserve its ref and button
semantics. Keep `nativeButton` consistent with the rendered element.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Bold } from "lucide-react";
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function BoldToggle() {
  return (
    <Toggle aria-label="Bold" defaultPressed>
      <Bold />
    </Toggle>
  );
}
```

An icon-only toggle needs `aria-label`; the glyph is not a name.

## Variants

Default and outline each show an off and an initially pressed button. Outline adds a border on busy toolbar surfaces; every button still toggles independently.

<ComponentExample name="variants" />

```tsx
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function ToggleVariants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      <Toggle>Default</Toggle>
      <Toggle defaultPressed>Default on</Toggle>
      <Toggle variant="outline">Outline</Toggle>
      <Toggle variant="outline" defaultPressed>
        Outline on
      </Toggle>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

Small, default and large use fixed 32, 36 and 40px heights. Choose one for the surrounding toolbar rather than scaling its hit target.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function ToggleSizes() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Toggle variant="outline" size="sm">
        Small
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle variant="outline" size="default">
        Default
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle variant="outline" size="lg">
        Large
      </Toggle>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## With a label

Text supplies the accessible name; the icon is decorative. An icon-only toggle, as in Usage, needs its own aria-label.

<ComponentExample name="label" />

```tsx
import { BoldIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function LabelledToggle() {
  return (
    <Toggle variant="outline">
      <BoldIcon />
      Bold
    </Toggle>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

The caller owns the italic command. Clear italic updates this instance externally; it leaves all other examples alone.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { ItalicIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function ControlledToggle() {
  const [on, setOn] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
      <Toggle pressed={on} onPressedChange={setOn}>
        <ItalicIcon />
        Italic
      </Toggle>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {on ? "Italic enabled" : "Italic disabled"}
      </p>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setOn(false)}>
        Clear italic
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

Disabled off and on commands retain their pressed state and ignore pointer and keyboard input.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function DisabledToggles() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      <Toggle disabled>Unavailable off</Toggle>
      <Toggle disabled defaultPressed variant="outline">
        Unavailable on
      </Toggle>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Inside a form

Toggle renders a type="button", so its pressed state does not submit a form field. The caller explicitly maps state to a hidden input here; Save formatting reads real FormData. Use Checkbox for a native checked form value.

<ComponentExample name="form-submission" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { BoldIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function ToggleForm() {
  const [bold, setBold] = useState(false);
  const [result, setResult] = useState("Not submitted");
  return (
    <form
      className="grid justify-items-start gap-3"
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        setResult(`Submitted bold: ${new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("bold") ?? "absent"}`);
      }}
    >
      <Toggle pressed={bold} onPressedChange={setBold}>
        <BoldIcon />
        Bold
      </Toggle>
      {bold && <input type="hidden" name="bold" value="enabled" />}
      <Button type="submit" size="sm">
        Save formatting
      </Button>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {result}
      </p>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The first toggle is inside a fixed none provider from its first DOM appearance. The second explicitly overrides that outer scope with full; the system reduced-motion preference still wins. Ordinary examples inherit the site header.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function StaticToggle() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
        <div data-testid="initial-none">
          <Toggle aria-label="Static toggle On" defaultPressed>
            On
          </Toggle>
        </div>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <div data-testid="explicit-full">
            <Toggle aria-label="Explicit full toggle Press">Press</Toggle>
          </div>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A formatting or mode command that stays on until it is turned off: bold,
  italic, a preview pane, a grid/list switch.
- A compact toolbar button whose pressed state is visible next to its neighbours.
- A setting the user toggles repeatedly while working.

## When not to use

- The action is one-shot (save, delete, open); use `button`.
- A setting that takes effect immediately and permanently, like a preference; use
  `switch`.
- A group of related toggles that should read as one control; use `toggle-group`.

## API

| Prop               | Type                          | Default     | Description                              |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `pressed`          | `boolean`                     | –           | Controlled state.                        |
| `defaultPressed`   | `boolean`                     | `false`     | Uncontrolled initial state.              |
| `onPressedChange`  | `(pressed, details) => void`  | –           | Fired on click and on Space/Enter.       |
| `variant`          | `"default" \| "outline"`      | `"default"` | Visual weight.                           |
| `size`             | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`   | `"default"` | Height and minimum width.                |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                     | `false`     | Ignores interaction.                     |
| `className`        | `string` / state callback                      | –           | Merged last.                             |

`toggleVariants` is exported, so a custom part can share the same classes.

The default press button preserves native React `onAnimationStart`, `onDrag`,
`onDragStart` and `onDragEnd` events, including capture and cancellation. Callback
and object refs follow the same button; replacing a callback runs its React 19
cleanup before assigning the next ref. A caller `render` replaces the default
renderer and owns spreading its supplied props.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `feedback.press`. The button compresses to 0.97 while the pointer is down
and springs back on release.

| Phase   | Properties       | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| press   | `scale 1 → 0.97` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| reduced | no scale; the pressed background is the only change | – | – |
| none    | no scale         | –                | –             |

The pressed background is a colour transition, which is state feedback and stays
in every mode — otherwise a `none` user could not see the state.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys    | Action                          |
| ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves focus to the toggle.      |
| `Space` | Toggles the pressed state.      |
| `Enter` | Toggles the pressed state.      |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders a real `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed`, so assistive
  technology announces it as a toggle button, not a plain button.
- Icon-only toggles need `aria-label`; the pressed state is announced separately.
- The pressed state is never colour-only: the fill and `aria-pressed` change
  together, and the press scale is never the only feedback.
- Avoid toggles in a navigation bar; a link that changes style is still a link.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                            | You do                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Forwards native button props and `disabled`          | Deciding what a pressed toggle means       |
| Exposes `aria-invalid` styling                | Validation and error text                  |
| Keeps the pressed state in `aria-pressed`     | Persisting it                              |

[Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Sizes are fixed; in a toolbar that must shrink, drop to `size="sm"` rather than
scaling the button with a transform, which would blur the icon.

## Performance

One Motion element, pressing only on pointer down. No layout animation, no
measurement.

## Notes for AI

- Use `toggle` for a command that stays on; use `switch` for a preference that
  saves itself.
- Always provide `aria-label` for icon-only toggles.
- Do not add a `state.morph` label swap to a toggle; the press scale is the whole
  contract.

# Toggle Group

Text alignment, view density, and other mode sets.

## Installation


classes.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
```

Copy all ten target files, preserving the sibling `toggle/`, `toggle-group/`
and shared `lib/` directories, relative imports and `"use client"` directives.
The group imports Toggle's variant classes, and its default item renderer
reaches `press-button.tsx`, `control-animation.tsx` and `native-div.tsx`.
Copy every file in the listed payloads; the provider files and `motion` package
are required imports even without an application provider wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied
files. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is required. In full,
`feedback.press` scales item content, `layout.shared` moves a decorative fill
within each single-selection group, and `state.morph` fades/scales local fills
in multiple selection. Reduced drops press scale and shared travel but keeps
local opacity feedback; none settles all three immediately. Standalone groups
follow the system motion preference. The optional `CadenceProvider` controls
mode and timing; a nested full scope still respects system reduced motion.

Usage, the top specimen, Multiple and Vertical use icons. They need this
example-only package; Toggle Group itself does not:

```package-manager
npm install lucide-react
```

Controlled also needs [Button](/components/button):

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

For manual installation, follow Button's Manual tab and add `button/index.tsx`.
Its npm dependencies and shared files are already in this installation graph.
The other examples need only Toggle Group and its included helpers. The site's
preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Segmented with a required selection and Controlled need
client modules for `useState`, change handlers and the external button's click
handler. Usage, Visual variants, Multiple, Spacing, Vertical, Sizes, Disabled
and Explicit motion scopes can be composed in synchronous Server Components
with the shown JSX and serializable props. Caller refs, event handlers,
function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)`, and client hooks
such as `useState` or `useRef` need a caller client boundary. Keep the installed
sources' client directives.

Give each item a stable, nonempty `value`. The group owns pressed state through
an array: use `defaultValue` for uncontrolled initial values, or `value` with
`onValueChange` for controlled values. Single selection is the default and
allows an empty array when the selected item is pressed again; `multiple`
allows independent values. To require one selection, use the shown caller
policy that ignores empty requests. Group values take precedence over item
`pressed` / `defaultPressed`; `details.cancel()` in an item or group change
handler can veto a change.

The group renders `role="group"`, and items are native `type="button"` buttons
with `aria-pressed`. Name the group and every icon-only item. Tab enters the
enabled controls; horizontal arrows or vertical Up/Down move focus without
selecting, Home/End reach the ends, and Space/Enter toggle the focused item.
`loopFocus` defaults to true; false stops at either end. Disabled items are
skipped and cannot activate; disabling the group retains its values. For RTL
arrow navigation, use Base UI's `DirectionProvider` from
`@base-ui/react/direction-provider` with `direction="rtl"`, as well as RTL
document direction. Group size and variant are inherited by items; `spacing`
sets the gap, and zero joins adjacent pressed fills in multiple selection.
Nested groups have separate value, appearance and shared-fill scopes.

These buttons do not generate hidden inputs or submit the selected array
through `name` or item `value`, and do not expose a submit-button `type` or
`form` association. If a form needs these values, map caller-owned state to
explicit form fields and handle reset in the caller. The caller owns business
data, persistence, required-selection rules, validation, error text and any
`aria-invalid` / `aria-describedby` association.

Native animation and drag handlers, state-based classes/styles and refs pass
through the default renderer. A caller item `render` replaces its press
renderer while retaining the supplied decorative fill and content children;
spread the supplied props, including children, and preserve the ref and button
semantics. Keep `nativeButton` consistent with the rendered element.

## Usage

```tsx
import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight } from "lucide-react";
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function Alignment() {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup variant="outline" defaultValue={["left"]} aria-label="Text alignment">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left" aria-label="Align left">
        <AlignLeft />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center" aria-label="Align center">
        <AlignCenter />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right" aria-label="Align right">
        <AlignRight />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Visual variants

Default, outline and segmented are fixed, independent single-selection groups. Each starts on Week; clicking its selected item clears it.

<ComponentExample name="variants" />

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function GroupVariants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      {(["default", "outline", "segmented"] as const).map((variant) => (
        <ToggleGroup key={variant} variant={variant} defaultValue={["week"]} aria-label={`${variant} range`}>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="day">Day</ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="week">Week</ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="month">Month</ToggleGroupItem>
        </ToggleGroup>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Multiple

Multiple permits independent marks. Adjacent pressed fills join at zero spacing. Pressing Bold off does not change Italic.

<ComponentExample name="multiple" />

```tsx
import { BoldIcon, ItalicIcon, UnderlineIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function MultipleGroup() {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup multiple defaultValue={["bold"]} aria-label="Text style">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
        <BoldIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
        <ItalicIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline">
        <UnderlineIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Segmented with a required selection

The caller ignores empty arrays to require one selection. The pill style alone does not require a value or select a newly focused item.

<ComponentExample name="segmented" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function SegmentedGroup() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState(["week"]);
  return (
    <ToggleGroup
      variant="segmented"
      value={range}
      onValueChange={(next) => {
        if (next.length) setRange(next);
      }}
      aria-label="Time range"
    >
      <ToggleGroupItem value="day">Day</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="week">Week</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="month">Month</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Spacing

Zero spacing joins adjacent pressed fills; one spacing step separates them. Both groups retain independent multiple selection and an outer strip.

<ComponentExample name="spacing" />

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function GroupSpacing() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
      {[0, 1].map((spacing) => (
        <ToggleGroup
          key={spacing}
          variant="outline"
          multiple
          spacing={spacing}
          defaultValue={["bold", "italic"]}
          aria-label={`Spacing ${spacing}`}
        >
          <ToggleGroupItem value="bold">Bold</ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="italic">Italic</ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="underline">Underline</ToggleGroupItem>
        </ToggleGroup>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

The value is always an array, including for a single-selection group. The external alignment button changes only this caller-owned value; choosing the selected item can clear it.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function ControlledGroup() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(["center"]);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
      <ToggleGroup value={value} onValueChange={setValue} aria-label="Controlled alignment">
        <ToggleGroupItem value="left">Left</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="center">Center</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="right">Right</ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Selection: {value[0] ?? "none"}
      </p>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setValue(["left"])}>
        Align left externally
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

The first group skips a disabled middle item when moving focus and uses loopFocus={false} to stop at either end. The default is to wrap focus. The second disables the whole group and retains its selected Day.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function DisabledGroups() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
      <ToggleGroup defaultValue={["day"]} loopFocus={false} aria-label="Disabled item" variant="outline">
        <ToggleGroupItem value="day">Day</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="week" disabled>
          Week
        </ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="month">Month</ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
      <ToggleGroup disabled defaultValue={["day"]} aria-label="Disabled group" variant="outline">
        <ToggleGroupItem value="day">Day</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="week">Week</ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The first group is fixed to none from its first DOM appearance. A second provider explicitly selects full inside that outer none scope; the system reduced-motion preference still wins. All ordinary groups inherit the site header.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function StaticGroup() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
        <div data-testid="initial-none">
          <ToggleGroup value={["static"]} aria-label="Static group">
            <ToggleGroupItem value="static">On</ToggleGroupItem>
          </ToggleGroup>
        </div>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <div data-testid="explicit-full">
            <ToggleGroup defaultValue={["first"]} aria-label="Explicit full toggle-group">
              <ToggleGroupItem value="first">First</ToggleGroupItem>
              <ToggleGroupItem value="second">Second</ToggleGroupItem>
            </ToggleGroup>
          </div>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A small set of modes that belong to one control: text alignment, view density,
  a time range.
- A formatting toolbar where several marks can be active at once
  (`multiple`).
- Icon toolbars with a shared tinted fill (`default` or `outline`), or short text
  choices on a pill-shaped track (`segmented`).

## When not to use

- Exactly one option with a text label and a longer list; use `radio-group`, which
  exposes radio semantics rather than a row of toggle buttons.
- A single independent on/off command; use `toggle`.
- Navigation between pages; use `tabs`, which owns `role="tablist"`.

## API

### `ToggleGroup`

| Prop            | Type                                        | Default        | Description                              |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `readonly string[]`                         | –              | Controlled pressed values.               |
| `defaultValue`  | `readonly string[]`                         | `[]`           | Uncontrolled initial values.             |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[], details) => void`        | –              | Fired when any item changes.             |
| `disabled`      | `boolean` | `false` | Disables every item. |
| `loopFocus`     | `boolean` | `true` | Wrap arrow focus at either end. |
| `multiple`      | `boolean`                                   | `false`        | Allow more than one pressed item.        |
| `spacing`       | `number`                                    | `0`            | Gap in Tailwind spacing steps.           |
| `orientation`   | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"`                | `"horizontal"` | Axis, also drives arrow keys.            |
| `variant`       | `"default" \| "outline" \| "segmented"`     | `"default"`    | Shared strip, bordered strip, or pill track. |
| `size`          | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`                 | `"default"`    | Inherited by every item.                 |

### `ToggleGroupItem`

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                          |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `value`     | `string` | –       | Required. Identifies the item.       |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`| `false` | Keeps it visible but unpressable.    |
| `className` | `string` / state callback | –       | Merged last.                         |

The default press button preserves native React `onAnimationStart`, `onDrag`,
`onDragStart` and `onDragEnd` events, including capture and cancellation. Callback
and object refs follow the same button; replacing a callback runs its React 19
cleanup before assigning the next ref. A caller `render` replaces the default
renderer and owns spreading its supplied props.

## Motion contract

Single selection uses one shared decorative fill scoped to each group. Multiple
selection keeps one local fill per item. Neither changes the buttons' layout
boxes; corner changes that join neighboring fills are immediate state styling.

| Phase   | Properties       | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| press   | `scale 1 → 0.97` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| single selection | fill transform between items | `layout.shared` | yes |
| multiple selection | fill opacity and `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes |
| reduced | shared fill jumps; local fills fade; no press scale | – | – |
| none | immediate selection, opacity and press state; zero duration | – | – |

Press scale applies only to the content, keeping the button and decorative fill
in the group's common stacking context. A travelling fill stays below all labels
and icons, including the items it crosses and the focused destination.

Full mode uses the velocity-preserving shared spring. Reduced, none and a zero
recipe clock render a static single-selection fill, cancelling an in-flight
projection without replacing the focused button. Local fills keep opacity under
reduced and settle immediately under none. All animated parts expose
`data-motion`; every duration, scale and spring comes from Cadence tokens.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys               | Action                                        |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`              | Enters the group at the last pressed item.    |
| `Arrow Right/Down` | Moves focus to the next item.                 |
| `Arrow Left/Up`    | Moves focus to the previous item.             |
| `Space` / `Enter`  | Presses the focused item.                     |

With `loopFocus` (default) the arrows wrap around at the ends.

## Accessibility

- The group renders `role="group"`; each item is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`.
- Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` — a row of icon buttons
  with no group name is announced as unrelated buttons.
- Icon-only items need their own `aria-label`; the group name does not describe
  them.
- Do not use a toggle group where `role="tablist"` is correct; tabs imply a panel
  that is shown, a toggle group implies state.
- Selection fills are decorative (`aria-hidden`) and never receive focus.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                              | You do                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Forwards `disabled` and the pressed values      | Deciding whether a selection is required  |
| Renders the visual pressed state                | Persisting the choice                     |
| Exposes `aria-invalid` styling on items         | Validation and error text                 |

[Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Horizontal groups do not wrap; with more than about five items on a narrow screen,
switch to `orientation="vertical"` or replace the group with a `select`.

## Performance

One shared layout identity per single-selection group; Motion measures the fill
when selection changes. Multiple selection uses one local opacity/scale fill per
item. Press feedback stays on demand. No observers, timers or render-time layout
reads; use small option sets rather than long lists.

## Notes for AI

- `value` is an array in every mode, with or without `multiple`.
- Use `variant="segmented"` for a pill-shaped control; no separate component is needed.
- Use `multiple` for independent pressed fills; `spacing={0}` joins neighbors.
- To require a selection, control the value and ignore empty change requests.
- For "one of N" with text labels, prefer `radio-group`; for panels, `tabs`.

# Input OTP

Login codes, email verification, and device pairing.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input-otp
```

The component wraps [`input-otp`](https://github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp),
which owns the single hidden input, paste handling, and the caret position.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion input-otp lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, preserving the sibling `input-otp/` and shared
`lib/` directories, relative imports and `"use client"` directives. Copy every
file in the listed payloads, including the provider helpers. The provider files
and `motion` package are required imports even without a provider wrapper.
`lucide-react` is a component dependency: `InputOTPSeparator` imports its dash
icon even when your composition omits the separator.

Complete the linked base theme setup and ensure Tailwind scans the copied
files. No extra item-specific CSS or external asset is required. The
`input-otp` dependency supplies its transparent-input styling and no-JavaScript
CSS fallback; do not replace the real input with one input per slot. Its
`nonce` prop supports the injected runtime style tag when your CSP requires
one; review `noScriptCSSFallback` separately for your application's CSP.

Full mode plays `state.morph` when a character changes, with opacity and scale;
reduced keeps opacity at neutral scale; none shows characters immediately.
Deleting is instant, character nodes stay mounted, and mode changes cancel an
entry. The fake caret is static. Standalone inputs follow the system motion
preference. The optional `CadenceProvider` controls mode and timing; an explicit
nested full scope still respects system reduced motion.

Controlled needs [Button](/components/button) and [Label](/components/label).
Invalid, Disabled and read-only, and the top specimen also use Label:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button @cadence/label
```

For manual setup, follow their Manual tabs and add `button/index.tsx` and
`label/index.tsx`. Their shared files are already included above. Button adds
these npm dependencies; Label needs no additional npm package:

```package-manager
npm install @base-ui/react class-variance-authority
```

The other examples need only Input OTP and its included helpers. Numeric paste
imports `REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS` from the already required `input-otp` package.
The site's preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Controlled needs a caller client module for its state,
change/completion handlers and clear button. Grouped numeric codes and paste
needs one for its function-valued `pasteTransformer`. Usage, Without a
separator and Explicit motion scopes can use synchronous Server Components
with the shown serializable props. Invalid, Disabled and read-only, and the
top specimen use synchronous `useId` only; that hook alone does not require a
client boundary. Keep their shown client directives when copying the examples.
Caller refs, event handlers, function-valued `render`, `useState` or `useRef`
need a caller client boundary. Preserve the installed sources' directives.

Pass the required `maxLength` and render one slot for each index from zero
through `maxLength - 1`, inside the same InputOTP. Groups and separators only
arrange those slots; they do not create separate inputs. Keep codes as strings
to preserve leading zeros. Use `defaultValue` for an uncontrolled initial
value, or `value` with `onChange(nextString)` for editable controlled state.
`onComplete` reports a change from a shorter value to a full code; an initially
full value or replacing one full code with another is not a new completion.
The callback does not verify or submit the code by itself.

The default keyboard hint is `inputMode="numeric"`, not a character filter.
Set `pattern` explicitly when needed; `REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS` accepts digits.
A `pasteTransformer` normalizes the pasted text before the pattern check;
select all to replace a full code, otherwise paste uses the current selection
and truncates to `maxLength`. Selection, arrow keys and Backspace belong to
the single real input; slots mirror its active range and character state.
`containerClassName` styles the visible wrapper, while `className` styles
the transparent input. The default password-manager strategy is
`pushPasswordManagerStrategy="increase-width"`; `"none"` disables that
badge accommodation. Test actual autofill and password-manager integrations
in your target browsers.

Associate a visible Label with the InputOTP's `id`, or supply `aria-label`.
Put `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` on the real InputOTP, and
`aria-invalid` on each slot for its destructive border. Disabled blocks focus
and editing; read-only retains focus and selection for a fixed value. Native
`name`, `form` and `required` props belong to the real input: it contributes
one string under its name, disabled inputs are excluded, and read-only values
remain available to the form. Keep form reset explicit in caller state; do
not rely on native reset to synchronize the dependency's internal draft or
your completion message. The caller owns code delivery, normalization policy,
verification, submission, expiry/errors, retry limits and persistence.

## Usage

```tsx
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSeparator, InputOTPSlot } from "@/components/cadence/input-otp";

export function Code() {
  return (
    <InputOTP maxLength={6} aria-label="Verification code">
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
      <InputOTPSeparator />
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={4} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={5} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
    </InputOTP>
  );
}
```

`maxLength` must equal the number of slots. Each `InputOTPSlot` needs its `index`.

## Controlled, with completion

The caller owns the six-character draft and the completed-code message. Completion records a value; it does not authenticate it. Clear login code resets only this example and its message.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSlot } from "@/components/cadence/input-otp";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function ControlledCode() {
  const id = useId();
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
  const [completed, setCompleted] = useState("Not completed");
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Login code</Label>
      <InputOTP
        id={id}
        maxLength={6}
        value={code}
        onChange={setCode}
        onComplete={(value) => setCompleted(`Completed: ${value}`)}
      >
        <InputOTPGroup>
          {[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((index) => (
            <InputOTPSlot key={index} index={index} />
          ))}
        </InputOTPGroup>
      </InputOTP>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {completed}
      </p>
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        size="sm"
        onClick={() => {
          setCode("");
          setCompleted("Not completed");
        }}
      >
        Clear login code
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Invalid

The caller supplies the expired-code error and aria-describedby on the real input. Each visual slot also gets aria-invalid for its destructive border. Editing does not independently clear the server error.

<ComponentExample name="invalid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSlot } from "@/components/cadence/input-otp";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function InvalidCode() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Expired code</Label>
      <InputOTP id={id} maxLength={4} defaultValue="0000" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby={`${id}-error`}>
        <InputOTPGroup>
          {[0, 1, 2, 3].map((index) => (
            <InputOTPSlot key={index} index={index} aria-invalid />
          ))}
        </InputOTPGroup>
      </InputOTP>
      <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-destructive">
        This code has expired. Request another code.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled and read-only

Disabled prevents focus and editing. Read-only retains a focusable input and a copyable code, while rejecting edits. The values are fixed independently.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSlot } from "@/components/cadence/input-otp";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function DisabledCodes() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-disabled`}>Unavailable code</Label>
        <InputOTP id={`${id}-disabled`} maxLength={4} disabled value="1234">
          <InputOTPGroup>
            {[0, 1, 2, 3].map((index) => (
              <InputOTPSlot key={index} index={index} />
            ))}
          </InputOTPGroup>
        </InputOTP>
      </div>
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-readonly`}>Read-only code</Label>
        <InputOTP id={`${id}-readonly`} maxLength={4} readOnly value="5678">
          <InputOTPGroup>
            {[0, 1, 2, 3].map((index) => (
              <InputOTPSlot key={index} index={index} />
            ))}
          </InputOTPGroup>
        </InputOTP>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Without a separator

A four-character PIN needs one group and four indexed slots. maxLength must match the slot count; it is a code string and can retain leading zeros.

<ComponentExample name="without-separator" />

```tsx
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSlot } from "@/components/cadence/input-otp";

export function ShortCode() {
  return (
    <InputOTP maxLength={4} aria-label="PIN" containerClassName="justify-center">
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
    </InputOTP>
  );
}
```

## Grouped numeric codes and paste

Two three-slot groups share one real input. The numeric pattern accepts digits, while the caller strips hyphens from pasted codes such as 123-456. Paste replaces the current selection, so select all first when replacing a full code. Pattern checks characters, not server validity.

<ComponentExample name="paste" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS } from "input-otp";
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSeparator, InputOTPSlot } from "@/components/cadence/input-otp";

export function PasteCode() {
  return (
    <InputOTP
      maxLength={6}
      aria-label="Pasted numeric code"
      inputMode="numeric"
      pattern={REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS}
      pasteTransformer={(text) => text.replaceAll("-", "")}
    >
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
      <InputOTPSeparator />
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={4} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={5} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
    </InputOTP>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The filled first code is fixed to none from the moment its DOM appears. The second input explicitly requests full inside that none provider, subject to the system reduced-motion preference. Ordinary inputs inherit the header; the caret never blinks.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSlot } from "@/components/cadence/input-otp";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function StaticCode() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="grid gap-4">
        <div data-testid="initial-none">
          <InputOTP maxLength={1} value="1" aria-label="Static code">
            <InputOTPGroup>
              <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
            </InputOTPGroup>
          </InputOTP>
        </div>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <div data-testid="explicit-full">
            <InputOTP maxLength={1} aria-label="Explicit full input-otp">
              <InputOTPGroup>
                <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
              </InputOTPGroup>
            </InputOTP>
          </div>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A short code the user reads from another surface: a login code, an email
  verification, a device pairing code.
- Anywhere a single input would force the user to count characters.
- A code that arrives by SMS or authenticator app, where `autocomplete="one-time-code"`
  lets the OS offer it.

## When not to use

- A password the user chooses; use `input type="password"`.
- A long token that is pasted, not typed; use `input` with paste handling.
- A numeric field that is not a code, like a quantity; use `input type="number"`.

## API

### `InputOTP`

| Prop               | Type                        | Default | Description                                    |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `maxLength`        | `number`                    | –       | Required. Number of characters.                |
| `value`            | `string`                    | –       | Controlled value.                              |
| `defaultValue`     | `string`                    | –       | Uncontrolled initial value.                    |
| `onChange`         | `(value: string) => void`   | –       | Fired on every change, including paste.        |
| `onComplete`       | `(value: string) => void`   | –       | Fired when the code is full.                   |
| `readOnly`         | `boolean` | `false` | Allows focus and selection, rejects edits. |
| `pattern` | `string` | – | Accepted characters, not server verification. |
| `inputMode` | native input mode | `"numeric"` | Keyboard hint. |
| `pasteTransformer` | `(text: string) => string` | – | Caller normalization before paste filtering. |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                   | `false` | Ignores input.                                 |
| `containerClassName` | `string`                  | –       | Classes for the wrapper that positions the slots. |
| `className`        | `string`                    | –       | Classes for the input itself.                  |

### `InputOTPSlot`

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                          |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `index`     | `number` | –       | Required. Which character it shows.  |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last.                         |

`InputOTPGroup` and `InputOTPSeparator` are plain wrappers with `data-slot` values
`input-otp-group` and `input-otp-separator`.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. A character lands in its slot with a short fade and settles
from 0.96 to full size. Deleting a character is instant — an exit animation would
leave a ghost in a field the user is racing against.

| Phase   | Properties                        | Token         | Interruptible |
| ------- | --------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| type    | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes           |
| delete  | none (instant)                    | –             | –             |
| reduced | `opacity` only                    | `state.morph` | yes           |
| none    | no transition                     | –             | –             |

The character span stays mounted when its value changes; updates replay the recipe on that same node. Mode changes cancel the running entry, and `none` renders filled slots immediately, including on the first render.

The caret is drawn but does not blink. A blink is a continuous loop that would
have to be declared as `data.transition`; the active slot's ring already shows
where the next character goes, so the loop buys nothing.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys              | Action                                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Allowed character | Fills the active slot and advances.                       |
| `Backspace`       | Clears the current slot, then moves back.                 |
| `Arrow Left/Right`| Moves the active slot without changing the value.         |
| `Cmd/Ctrl + V`    | Pastes at the current selection; select all to replace a code. |

## Accessibility

- `input-otp` renders a single real input with `aria-label` and
  `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so assistive technology sees one field, not six.
- The slots are visual mirrors; they are not focusable and carry no role.
- `onComplete` reports a filled code for the caller to judge. The component never decides that a
  code is wrong.
- Keep the field visible while verifying and announce the result next to it, not
  through the slots' animation.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                  | You do                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid` on the slots                  | Deciding that the code is wrong or expired        |
| Reports every change and the completed value        | Verifying the code and mapping the server error   |
| Keeps the paste path working                        | Re-sending a code, throttling attempts            |

There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `rules` prop. [Field](/components/field) shows how the
invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Slots are 36px squares; six of them plus a separator fit a 320px viewport. For
longer codes, drop the separator group or reduce the gap in `containerClassName`
before shrinking the slots below 32px.

## Performance

One Motion element per slot, animating `opacity` and `transform` only when a
character changes. No per-keystroke layout read: the caret position comes from the
input, not from measurement.

## Notes for AI

- `maxLength` and the slot count must agree; a mismatch silently drops characters.
- Use `onComplete` to submit, not an effect that watches `value.length`.
- The caret does not blink on purpose. Do not re-add a `animate-caret-blink`
  loop without declaring the recipe.
