Copy all nine target files, keeping `progress/index.tsx` beside the shared
`lib/` directory, the relative imports intact and the sources' `"use client"`
directives. Progress imports `NativeControlDiv` from `control-animation.tsx`,
which also reaches `native-div.tsx` and `press-button.tsx`. Copy the complete
provider, motion and utilities payloads, even without a provider wrapper.
The provider files and `motion` package remain required imports.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied
files. Progress needs no additional item-specific CSS, icon package or external
asset. Its full-width indicator uses `scaleX` for determinate updates through
`data.transition`; reduced and none jump to the new fraction. A null value
uses the theme's opacity-only `animate-pulse` in full and reduced, and
`animate-none` in none. Continuous loops follow the theme animation token,
not the provider speed. Standalone bars follow the system motion preference;
an optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree, and nested full still respects
system reduced motion.

Usage, the top specimen, Labelled, Indeterminate, Complete, Custom range,
Composed track and Explicit motion scopes use only Progress and its included
helpers. Caller-owned progress also needs [Button](/components/button):

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

For manual installation, follow Button's Manual tab and add `button/index.tsx`.
Its shared files and Base UI package are already included above; its additional
npm dependency is:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

No example needs another package or external asset. The site's preview shell
is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Usage, Labelled, Indeterminate, Complete, Composed track
and the top specimen can be composed in synchronous Server Components with
the shown serializable props. Custom range needs a caller client module for
its function-valued `getAriaValueText`. Caller-owned progress and Explicit
motion scopes need one for `useState` and slider change handlers; the former
also handles a button click. Synchronous `useId` alone does not require a
client boundary. Caller refs, event handlers, function-valued `render`,
`className(state)`, `style(state)` or `ProgressValue` children also need a
caller client boundary. Preserve the installed sources' client directives.

Supply a finite numeric `value` within a finite `min`/`max` range with
`max > min`, or explicitly pass `null` for indeterminate work. The default
range is zero to 100; there is no `defaultValue` or automatic progress source.
The fill fraction is `(value - min) / (max - min)`, clamped to zero through one.
At the maximum, Base UI exposes the complete state. `ProgressValue` displays
the normalized percentage by default, so three of five displays 60%; `format`
and `locale` configure number formatting. `getAriaValueText(formatted, raw)`
customizes the accessible value text without changing the fill or visible
value. For null, Base UI omits `aria-valuenow` and the default visible value
is empty; provide meaningful loading text separately.

`Progress` appends its own track and indicator after its children. Put
`ProgressLabel` and `ProgressValue` inside the root. Adding a `ProgressTrack`
with `ProgressIndicator` creates an additional track sharing the same fraction,
as Composed track shows; it does not replace the default. Keep the indicator's
full width and transform ownership when styling it. A custom indicator `render`
replaces the animation adapter, so the caller must preserve its motion contract.

The root owns `role="progressbar"` and its range/value ARIA attributes, not
the track. Give it an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, or let the nested
`ProgressLabel` register its association after hydration. Use an explicit
root name when it must already be associated in server/no-JS markup.
`ProgressValue` is visible text with `aria-hidden`; the root supplies the
accessible value. The default bar has no tab stop, keyboard value editing,
hidden form input or submission value. Native props, refs and Base UI `render`
belong to their respective parts; retain the supplied props and ref when
replacing an element. Put cancellation or retry in separate controls.

The caller owns the real work, progress reports, range policy, loading/error
text, completion announcement, cancellation, retries and persistence. A value
of 100 in the default range only renders completion; it does not finish or
validate an upload, submit a form or announce a live status by itself.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@/components/cadence/progress";

export function Upload() {
  return <Progress value={40} aria-label="Uploading assets" />;
}
```

`value` is required and may be `null` for indeterminate work. `Progress` renders
its own track and indicator; `ProgressLabel` and `ProgressValue` go inside it as
children.

## Labelled, with the number

ProgressLabel supplies the accessible name and ProgressValue formats the same value as a percentage. The label and number remain readable above the default track. Pass format or locale to the root to configure number formatting.

<ComponentExample name="labelled" />

```tsx
import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressValue } from "@/components/cadence/progress";

export function LabelledProgress() {
  return (
    <Progress value={62} className="max-w-sm">
      <div className="flex w-full items-center justify-between">
        <ProgressLabel>Uploading assets</ProgressLabel>
        <ProgressValue />
      </div>
    </Progress>
  );
}
```

## Indeterminate

A null value omits aria-valuenow and pulses the full track using opacity. This loop remains under reduced motion, stops under none and follows the theme animation token rather than the provider speed.

<ComponentExample name="indeterminate" />

```tsx
import { Progress, ProgressLabel } from "@/components/cadence/progress";

export function IndeterminateProgress() {
  return (
    <Progress value={null} aria-label="Preparing preview" className="max-w-sm">
      <ProgressLabel>Preparing preview</ProgressLabel>
    </Progress>
  );
}
```

## Complete

A fixed completed task shows 100% and a separate status message. The caller supplies the completion announcement; a filled progressbar alone is not a live notification.

<ComponentExample name="complete" />

```tsx
import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressValue } from "@/components/cadence/progress";

export function CompleteProgress() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-3">
      <Progress value={100}>
        <div className="flex w-full items-center justify-between">
          <ProgressLabel>Upload complete</ProgressLabel>
          <ProgressValue />
        </div>
      </Progress>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        All files uploaded.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Custom range

Three completed steps in a five-step range render a 60% fill. The caller provides a more specific accessible value text without changing the numeric fraction.

<ComponentExample name="range" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Progress, ProgressValue } from "@/components/cadence/progress";

export function CustomProgressRange() {
  return (
    <Progress
      value={3}
      min={0}
      max={5}
      aria-label="Build steps"
      getAriaValueText={() => "Step 3 of 5"}
      className="max-w-sm"
    >
      <ProgressValue />
    </Progress>
  );
}
```

## Composed track

A custom track is added alongside the default track, matching the root composition. Both indicators read the same fraction. This example compares a six-pixel custom track with the default eight-pixel track; it does not replace the default.

<ComponentExample name="composed" />

```tsx
import { Progress, ProgressIndicator, ProgressTrack } from "@/components/cadence/progress";

export function ComposedProgress() {
  return (
    <Progress value={72} aria-label="Storage" className="max-w-sm">
      <ProgressTrack className="h-1.5 bg-muted">
        <ProgressIndicator className="bg-foreground" />
      </ProgressTrack>
    </Progress>
  );
}
```

## Caller-owned progress

The slider represents external upload reports; Complete upload supplies a final value. The caller owns updates and completion text. No timer invents progress, and none of these updates changes another example.

<ComponentExample name="caller-progress" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressValue } from "@/components/cadence/progress";

export function CallerProgress() {
  const id = useId();
  const [value, setValue] = useState(62);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-4">
      <label htmlFor={id} className="grid gap-2 text-sm">
        Upload progress
        <input
          id={id}
          type="range"
          min={0}
          max={100}
          value={value}
          onChange={(event) => setValue(Number(event.target.value))}
        />
      </label>
      <Progress value={value} aria-label="Uploading assets">
        <div className="flex w-full items-center justify-between">
          <ProgressLabel>Uploading assets</ProgressLabel>
          <ProgressValue />
        </div>
      </Progress>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {value === 100 ? "Upload complete" : `Uploaded ${value}%`}
      </p>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setValue(100)}>
        Complete upload
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The first indeterminate indicator is fixed to none from its first DOM appearance, with no opacity loop. The second bar explicitly requests full within that outer none scope; its external slider changes only that value, and system reduced motion still wins. Ordinary bars inherit the header.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Progress } from "@/components/cadence/progress";

export function StaticProgress() {
  const id = useId();
  const [value, setValue] = useState(20);
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-4">
        <div data-testid="initial-none">
          <Progress value={null} aria-label="Static progress" />
        </div>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <div data-testid="explicit-full" className="grid gap-3">
            <label htmlFor={id} className="grid gap-2 text-sm">
              Explicit full progress
              <input
                id={id}
                type="range"
                min={0}
                max={100}
                value={value}
                onChange={(event) => setValue(Number(event.target.value))}
              />
            </label>
            <Progress value={value} aria-label="Explicit full progress" />
          </div>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Work with a measurable end: an upload, an import, a multi-step build.
- Work long enough that the user would otherwise wonder whether anything is
  happening, and short enough that they will watch the bar.
- A determinate value next to other numbers, where the bar is a second reading of
  the same fact.

## When not to use

- Work of unknown duration. Pass `value={null}` for an indeterminate bar, or use
  `spinner` when there is no bar to fill.
- A page that is simply loading its own content; use `skeleton`.
- A value that is not progressing toward an end, like a score. Render the number.

## API

### `Progress`

| Prop              | Type                                  | Default | Description                                  |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `value`           | `number \| null`                      | –       | Required. `null` means indeterminate.        |
| `min`, `max`      | `number`                              | `0`, `100` | Range.                                    |
| `format`          | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`            | –       | How `ProgressValue` formats the number.      |
| `getAriaValueText`| `(formatted: string, raw: number \| null) => string`              | –       | Human-readable value for assistive tech.     |
| `className`       | `string` / state callback                              | –       | Merged last; the default is a wrap layout.   |

### `ProgressTrack`, `ProgressIndicator`, `ProgressLabel`, `ProgressValue`

Plain wrappers over Base UI's parts; each forwards `className` and native props.
`ProgressIndicator` carries the motion.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `data.transition`, in both of its documented forms.

| Phase         | Properties                     | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------- |
| value change  | `scaleX old → new` (one-shot)  | `data.transition`| yes           |
| indeterminate | `opacity` pulse (continuous)   | `data.transition`| yes           |
| reduced       | value jumps; pulse kept, opacity only | `data.transition` | yes     |
| none          | no transition, `animate-none`  | –                | –             |

The fill is a `scaleX` transform on an element that keeps the full track width, so
a value change never triggers layout. Under `reduced` the fill jumps to the new
value — position is information, the animation is not — while the indeterminate
pulse survives, because opacity-only loading feedback is what M5 keeps.

## Keyboard interactions

No keyboard interaction: the progress bar is not focusable. If the user can cancel
the work, put a `button` next to it.

## Accessibility

- Base UI puts `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and
  `aria-valuenow` on the root; `value={null}` omits `aria-valuenow`.
- Give it a name with `aria-label`, or render `ProgressLabel` inside the root and
  let Base UI wire it.
- Announce completion outside the bar (text or `toast`); a full bar is not
  announced by a screen reader on its own.
- Never hide the percentage behind the animation: `ProgressValue` is the readable
  copy of the same fact.

## Responsive behavior

The bar fills its container and stays 8px tall at every breakpoint. When it sits in
a card header, keep the label and value on one line and let the bar take the next
line — the default `flex-wrap` layout does this without extra classes.

## Performance

One animated indicator per track. A determinate update uses a native transform animation; an indeterminate bar runs a CSS opacity loop. These do not animate layout, but whole-page frame performance still needs measurement. Avoid driving `value` from `requestAnimationFrame`
yourself; pass the real value and let the transition smooth it.

## Notes for AI

- `value` is required; pass `null` for indeterminate, never `undefined`.
- Use `scaleX`, not width. A width transition relayouts the track every frame.
- For work with no measurable end and no bar, use `spinner`, not a fake percentage.

# Alert Dialog

Destructive or irreversible actions that need confirmation.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/alert-dialog
```

This also installs `button`, which the two actions render through.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| button | `@components/cadence/button/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) |
| alert-dialog | `@components/cadence/alert-dialog/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/alert-dialog.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json)

[Source files: alert-dialog](https://cadence.dev/r/alert-dialog.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all ten target files, keeping `alert-dialog/index.tsx`, `button/index.tsx`
and the shared `lib/` directory in the same `cadence/` tree. Preserve the
relative imports and the sources' `"use client"` directives. Button reaches
`press-button.tsx`, which imports `control-animation.tsx` and in turn
`native-div.tsx`; copy every file in the provider, motion and utilities
payloads. The provider files and `motion` package remain required imports
even when you omit the optional provider wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the
copied files. Include the Cadence easing and motion-scale tokens used by the
popup classes. There is no additional item-specific CSS or external asset.
The overlay fades and the panel fades and scales in full; reduced keeps
opacity only, and none removes the transitions and hidden entry styles.
Each portalled surface resolves its own provider clock. Standalone components
follow the system motion preference; an optional `CadenceProvider` controls
a subtree, and nested full still respects system reduced motion. The included
Button retains its own press-feedback contract.

Usage, Confirmation sizes and With an icon import `Trash2Icon`; the top
specimen uses it too. To copy those snippets unchanged, also install:

```package-manager
npm install lucide-react
```

An icon is optional for the component. Controlled, A confirmation that is
still working and Explicit motion scopes need no additional package or
registry item. Button and `CadenceProvider` are already included above.
The site's preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Usage, Confirmation sizes, With an icon, Controlled,
the pending example and the top specimen need a caller client module for
their `useState` and event handlers. Explicit motion scopes contains only
serializable JSX and element-valued `render` props, so it can be composed in
a synchronous Server Component. Caller refs, event handlers, function-valued
`render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)` also need a caller client
boundary. Synchronous `useId` alone does not require one. Preserve the
installed sources' client directives.

Place the trigger and content within the same `AlertDialog` root. The root
supports uncontrolled `defaultOpen`, or controlled `open` / `onOpenChange`;
it remains modal and ignores outside pointer presses. `AlertDialogContent`
already renders its portal, overlay and popup, so do not add another portal
or overlay around it. It accepts popup props such as `initialFocus` and
`finalFocus`; `size` defaults to `"default"`, with `"sm"` for the compact
layout. The separately exported Portal and Overlay are for custom composition.

Always include `AlertDialogTitle` for the accessible name and use
`AlertDialogDescription` for the consequence. Base UI associates them with
the alert dialog and manages focus trapping, scroll locking and Escape.
Keep Cancel first in DOM order so keyboard and mouse opening initially focus
the safe choice; touch opening can focus the popup itself. Default focus return
uses the trigger; when opening from an
external control, keep a suitable return target or supply `finalFocus`.
Mark a decorative media icon `aria-hidden="true"`. Custom Base UI `render`
elements must preserve the supplied props and ref; `render={<Button />}`
does not need an extra wrapper or `asChild`.

`AlertDialogCancel` renders Base UI Close through Button and closes
automatically; its defaults are `variant="outline"` and `size="default"`.
`AlertDialogAction` renders Button and leaves the dialog open. Use controlled
state to close after the caller's operation succeeds. Neither button performs
the destructive operation for you. In the pending example, the caller disables
both decision buttons, sets `aria-busy`, and rejects close requests while
pending; Complete request only resolves a local simulation. The caller owns
authorization, request execution, pending/error/retry UI, dismissal policy,
result announcements and persistence. The component adds no validation or
automatic form submission.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { Trash2Icon } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogMedia,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/alert-dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Confirmation({ size = "default", withIcon = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; withIcon?: boolean }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [deleted, setDeleted] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
          {size === "sm" ? "Archive" : "Delete project"}
        </AlertDialogTrigger>
        <AlertDialogContent size={size}>
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            {withIcon && (
              <AlertDialogMedia>
                <Trash2Icon aria-hidden="true" />
              </AlertDialogMedia>
            )}
            <AlertDialogTitle>{size === "sm" ? "Archive this project?" : "Delete this project?"}</AlertDialogTitle>
            <AlertDialogDescription>
              {size === "sm"
                ? "It stops deploying. You can unarchive it later."
                : "Every deployment and its logs go with it. This cannot be undone."}
            </AlertDialogDescription>
          </AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogFooter>
            <AlertDialogCancel>{size === "sm" ? "Cancel" : "Keep project"}</AlertDialogCancel>
            <AlertDialogAction
              variant={size === "sm" ? "default" : "destructive"}
              onClick={() => {
                setDeleted(true);
                setOpen(false);
              }}
            >
              {size === "sm" ? "Archive" : "Delete project"}
            </AlertDialogAction>
          </AlertDialogFooter>
        </AlertDialogContent>
      </AlertDialog>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {deleted ? (size === "sm" ? "Project archived locally" : "Project deleted locally") : "No changes"}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

The external opener sets caller-owned open state. Revoke key records a local result and closes explicitly. A production caller would close when its own operation completes; AlertDialogAction does not close automatically.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/alert-dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function ControlledConfirmation() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [confirmed, setConfirmed] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Request key revocation
      </Button>
      <AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <AlertDialogContent>
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogTitle>Revoke this key?</AlertDialogTitle>
            <AlertDialogDescription>Services using it lose access. Create a replacement first.</AlertDialogDescription>
          </AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogFooter>
            <AlertDialogCancel>Keep key</AlertDialogCancel>
            <AlertDialogAction
              variant="destructive"
              onClick={() => {
                setConfirmed(true);
                setOpen(false);
              }}
            >
              Revoke key
            </AlertDialogAction>
          </AlertDialogFooter>
        </AlertDialogContent>
      </AlertDialog>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {confirmed ? "Key revoked locally" : "Key active"}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## A confirmation that is still working

The caller owns pending and disables both decision buttons while working. This example deliberately has no request: Complete request resolves the local simulation. The controlled root rejects Escape while pending; before pending, Escape and Cancel work normally. Keep this policy and an error/retry path in application code.

<ComponentExample name="pending" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/alert-dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function PendingConfirmation() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [pending, setPending] = useState(false);
  const [complete, setComplete] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <AlertDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={(next) => {
          if (!pending) setOpen(next);
        }}
      >
        <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Delete draft</AlertDialogTrigger>
        <AlertDialogContent>
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this draft?</AlertDialogTitle>
            <AlertDialogDescription>
              This local example models a caller-owned request. Complete request resolves it without sending data.
            </AlertDialogDescription>
          </AlertDialogHeader>
          <p role="status" className="text-sm">
            {pending ? "Deletion pending" : "Ready to delete"}
          </p>
          <AlertDialogFooter>
            <AlertDialogCancel disabled={pending}>Keep draft</AlertDialogCancel>
            <AlertDialogAction
              variant="destructive"
              disabled={pending}
              aria-busy={pending}
              onClick={() => setPending(true)}
            >
              {pending ? "Deleting…" : "Delete draft"}
            </AlertDialogAction>
          </AlertDialogFooter>
          {pending && (
            <Button
              variant="outline"
              onClick={() => {
                setPending(false);
                setComplete(true);
                setOpen(false);
              }}
            >
              Complete request
            </Button>
          )}
        </AlertDialogContent>
      </AlertDialog>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {complete ? "Draft deleted locally" : "Draft retained"}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

These fixed overrides demonstrate none from portal insertion and explicit full nested within none. The OS reduced preference still wins over full. Request deletion deliberately leaves these uncontrolled panels open, matching AlertDialogAction; use Cancel or Escape to dismiss. Ordinary examples inherit the site header.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/alert-dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function AlertMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <AlertDialog>
          <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open without motion</AlertDialogTrigger>
          <AlertDialogContent data-testid="initial-none">
            <AlertDialogHeader>
              <AlertDialogTitle>Immediate confirmation</AlertDialogTitle>
              <AlertDialogDescription>No transition runs on this panel or its overlay.</AlertDialogDescription>
            </AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogFooter>
              <AlertDialogCancel>Keep project</AlertDialogCancel>
              <AlertDialogAction>Request deletion</AlertDialogAction>
            </AlertDialogFooter>
          </AlertDialogContent>
        </AlertDialog>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <AlertDialog>
            <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open nested full</AlertDialogTrigger>
            <AlertDialogContent data-testid="nested-full">
              <AlertDialogHeader>
                <AlertDialogTitle>Nested full confirmation</AlertDialogTitle>
                <AlertDialogDescription>
                  The OS preference can still reduce this explicit full scope.
                </AlertDialogDescription>
              </AlertDialogHeader>
              <AlertDialogFooter>
                <AlertDialogCancel>Keep project</AlertDialogCancel>
                <AlertDialogAction>Request deletion</AlertDialogAction>
              </AlertDialogFooter>
            </AlertDialogContent>
          </AlertDialog>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A destructive or irreversible action — deleting a project, revoking a key, overwriting a draft — that the
  user must confirm on purpose.
- A decision the page cannot make for the user: move the workspace, leave without saving, end the session.
- A step that must be acknowledged before anything else continues, where an accidental dismissal would be
  the bug.

## When not to use

- A task with more than one decision or a form to fill in. Use `dialog`: it can be dismissed, and it should be.
- A message that does not block anything. Use `alert` where it belongs on the page, or `toast` for a moment.
- A hint attached to a control. Use `tooltip`.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AlertDialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpenChangeComplete` | Base UI root. Always modal; pointer dismissal is fixed off. |
| `AlertDialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `AlertDialogContent` | `size` (`"default" \| "sm"`), `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `AlertDialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `AlertDialogContent`. |
| `AlertDialogHeader` / `AlertDialogFooter` | `className` | Layout only. |
| `AlertDialogMedia` | `className` | Icon slot; changes the header layout. |
| `AlertDialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `AlertDialogDescription` | `className` | Supporting text; wire it to the decision, not the product. |
| `AlertDialogAction` | `variant`, `size`, `onClick`, `render` | Confirming Button. The caller owns closing via the root’s controlled `open` value. |
| `AlertDialogCancel` | `variant` (`outline`), `size`, `onClick`, `render` | Dismissing button. Also closes the dialog. |

`AlertDialogCancel` renders Base UI’s Close. `AlertDialogAction` matches the pinned upstream
Button: clicking it invokes the caller’s handler and leaves the popup open. Use controlled
`open` / `onOpenChange` to close when the caller decides the action is complete.

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (overlay 96ms, panel 132ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so no transition runs | – | – |

The entrance is the dialog's, because this is the same popup: a fade under a 0.96-scale settle. The
motion is CSS-only — Base UI toggles `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style` and the class list
reads the duration tokens — so there is no JavaScript animation loop and nothing to interrupt by hand.
Reopening during the exit reverses the fade rather than restarting it.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. Focus never reaches the page behind it. |
| Escape | Cancels: the dialog closes and focus returns to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused button — confirm or cancel, whichever has focus. |

The outside press is the one path that is deliberately missing: clicking the overlay does nothing,
which is the difference between this component and `dialog`.

## Accessibility

The destructive action uses foreground text on a tinted destructive background. This preserves the warning colour while meeting text contrast in both themes.

- Base UI provides `role="alertdialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and the Escape path.
- `AlertDialogTitle` is required: an alert dialog without an accessible name is invalid, and it is
  announced as the first thing inside the popup. `AlertDialogDescription` becomes the description, so
  put the consequence there, not in a second paragraph.
- Focus lands on the cancel control, the first tabbable element inside the popup, not on the destructive
  action — so a stray Enter cancels rather than confirms. Put `AlertDialogCancel` first in the footer for
  that reason; the footer's column-reverse layout still shows the confirming action on top.
- Destructive styling is colour plus a specific verb ("Delete project", not "OK"). Never rely on the
  red alone; the label has to carry the meaning in greyscale and in a screen reader.
- `AlertDialogMedia` is decorative when the title already says what happened. Mark the icon
  `aria-hidden="true"` unless it is the only signal.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred with a 1rem gutter on narrow viewports: `max-w-lg` for the default size and
`max-w-xs` for `size="sm"`. The footer stacks its buttons in reverse DOM order (the confirming action
on top) below `sm`, and becomes a row that ends on the right above it. With `size="sm"` the two
buttons split the width instead of stacking, so the two answers stay side by side at every size.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the overlay and panel unmount after the exit transition.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only: no layout reads, no `width`/`height` transition, and no
  JavaScript animation running while the dialog sits open.
- `AlertDialogAction` and `AlertDialogCancel` are ordinary `Button`s, so the press feedback is the
  button's (a 0.97 scale that the same motion mode can drop).

## Notes for AI

- Reach for `alert-dialog` only when the answer must be deliberate. A form, a longer task, or anything
  the user may want to dismiss belongs in `dialog`.
- Always render `AlertDialogTitle`; it is the accessible name. Use `AlertDialogDescription` for the
  consequence of the action, in one sentence.
- Name the confirming button after its effect ("Delete project", "Leave without saving"), never "OK".
- Cancel closes automatically. The confirming Action stays open; use the root’s controlled `open` value when the caller decides to close.
- Use `AlertDialogMedia` for an icon, not for an illustration: the slot is a 4rem square that changes
  the header layout.

# Popover

Filters, share links, and other controls tied to a trigger.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/popover
```

The examples compose `@cadence/button`, `@cadence/checkbox`, `@cadence/label`, `@cadence/field`,
and `@cadence/input` as needed. Install those items when copying their corresponding examples.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| popover | `@components/cadence/popover/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/popover.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: popover](https://cadence.dev/r/popover.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, keeping `popover/index.tsx` and the shared `lib/`
directory in the same `cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and the
sources' `"use client"` directives. Copy every file in the motion, utilities
and provider payloads, including helpers not imported by Popover directly.
The provider files and `motion` package are required imports even when you
omit the optional provider wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the
copied files. Include the Cadence easing and motion-scale tokens used by the
popup classes. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is required.
Full fades and scales the panel from its anchor; reduced keeps opacity only;
none removes the transitions and hidden entry/exit styles. The portalled popup
resolves its own mode and token clock. Standalone components follow the system
motion preference; an optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree, and nested
full still respects system reduced motion.

The examples need additional registry items. Copy each item's complete Manual
setup, including its npm dependencies and shared files:

- [Button](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation) is used by Usage,
  the top specimen and every body example.
- [Checkbox](https://cadence.dev/components/checkbox#installation) and
  [Label](https://cadence.dev/components/label#installation) are used by Usage,
  the top specimen and Column visibility. Checkbox also requires `lucide-react`.
- [Field](https://cadence.dev/components/field#installation) and
  [Input](https://cadence.dev/components/input#installation) are used by With a form.

Logical sides and RTL imports Base UI `DirectionProvider`, and Modal when it
has to be imports Base UI `Popover.Close`; both come from the already required
`@base-ui/react` package. Explicit motion scopes uses the included provider.
The site's preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Usage, Column visibility, With a form, Controlled and
the top specimen need a caller client module for their state and handlers.
Positioned by side, Aligned to the trigger, Logical sides and RTL, Modal when
it has to be and Explicit motion scopes contain serializable JSX and
element-valued `render` props, so they can be composed in synchronous Server
Components. Caller refs, event handlers, function-valued `render`,
`className(state)` or `style(state)` also need a caller client boundary.
Synchronous `useId` alone does not require one. Keep the installed client
directives and the snippets' existing directives when copying them unchanged.

Place the trigger and content within the same `Popover` root. Use
`defaultOpen` for uncontrolled opening, or `open` / `onOpenChange` for caller
control. For an external opener, use a unique `triggerId` matching the trigger's
`id` so the panel stays anchored. `PopoverTrigger` renders a button by default;
`render={<Button />}` merges the trigger onto that button. Custom render
elements must preserve supplied props and refs.

`PopoverContent` already owns the portal, positioner and popup. Its positioning
defaults are `side="bottom"`, `align="center"`, `sideOffset={4}` and
`alignOffset={0}`; offsets control geometry, not animation. Base UI can flip
or shift the panel to avoid collisions. Logical sides need Base UI
`DirectionProvider` as well as DOM `dir`, as shown in the RTL example.
Cadence exports no separate Portal, Positioner, Anchor, Arrow or Close part.
Include `PopoverTitle` for an accessible name and `PopoverDescription` for
supporting context. Popup props such as `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` pass
through; Base UI manages ARIA associations and focus return.

The root is non-modal by default. Enter or Space opens from the trigger;
Escape and outside presses dismiss, and Tab can leave the non-modal panel.
`modal={true}` blocks outside interaction and locks desktop page scrolling;
`modal="trap-focus"` avoids that scroll lock. Both modal settings need a
registered Base UI `Popover.Close` inside the content to activate focus
trapping, as in Modal when it has to be. Modal popovers still allow dismissal;
provide the close control for touch screen readers, and account for Base UI's
touch scrolling behavior.

The caller owns column selection, form drafts, saved values, requests,
validation, errors, persistence and controlled closing. In With a form, Save
handles submission and closes explicitly; dismissing does not save, and the
draft survives in caller state. Native `required` belongs to that example's
input. Popover performs no validation or automatic saving; render supplied
invalid state on the relevant controls with `aria-invalid` / `data-invalid`.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";

import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";

export function ColumnPopover() {
  const id = useId();
  const [columns, setColumns] = useState(["Name", "Status", "Owner"]);
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Visible columns</PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverContent align="start">
        <PopoverHeader>
          <PopoverTitle>Visible columns</PopoverTitle>
          <PopoverDescription>{columns.length} of four columns are shown.</PopoverDescription>
        </PopoverHeader>
        <div className="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-2">
          {["Name", "Status", "Owner", "Updated"].map((column) => (
            <div key={column} className="flex items-center gap-2">
              <Checkbox
                id={`${id}-${column}`}
                checked={columns.includes(column)}
                onCheckedChange={(checked) =>
                  setColumns((previous) =>
                    checked ? [...previous, column] : previous.filter((value) => value !== column),
                  )
                }
              />
              <Label htmlFor={`${id}-${column}`} className="font-normal">
                {column}
              </Label>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```
