## Positioned by side

The four physical sides are separate fixed instances. Base UI flips a panel when space is insufficient, so the requested side is a preference rather than a guarantee. sideOffset controls the gap, not an animation distance.

<ComponentExample name="sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";

export function PopoverSides() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["top", "right", "bottom", "left"] as const).map((side) => (
        <Popover key={side}>
          <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{side}</PopoverTrigger>
          <PopoverContent side={side} sideOffset={8} className="w-48">
            <PopoverHeader>
              <PopoverTitle>{side} placement</PopoverTitle>
              <PopoverDescription>Base UI can flip this panel to avoid a collision.</PopoverDescription>
            </PopoverHeader>
          </PopoverContent>
        </Popover>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Aligned to the trigger

Start, center, and end alignments are fixed instances on the bottom side. alignOffset is zero here; the caller can change the numeric offset without changing the motion recipe. Collision handling can shift the final position.

<ComponentExample name="alignments" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";

export function PopoverAlignments() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["start", "center", "end"] as const).map((align) => (
        <Popover key={align}>
          <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{align}</PopoverTrigger>
          <PopoverContent align={align} alignOffset={0} className="w-48">
            <PopoverHeader>
              <PopoverTitle>{align} alignment</PopoverTitle>
              <PopoverDescription>Aligned to this trigger along the cross axis.</PopoverDescription>
            </PopoverHeader>
          </PopoverContent>
        </Popover>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Logical sides and RTL

inline-start and inline-end follow reading direction. This RTL example supplies Base UI DirectionProvider as well as the DOM dir attribute; setting DOM direction alone does not configure Base UI positioning. Each logical side has its own trigger.

<ComponentExample name="logical-sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DirectionProvider } from "@base-ui/react/direction-provider";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";

export function LogicalPopovers() {
  return (
    <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">
      <div dir="rtl" className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        {(["inline-start", "inline-end"] as const).map((side) => (
          <Popover key={side}>
            <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{side}</PopoverTrigger>
            <PopoverContent side={side} className="w-48">
              <PopoverHeader>
                <PopoverTitle>{side}</PopoverTitle>
                <PopoverDescription>Logical placement follows right-to-left direction.</PopoverDescription>
              </PopoverHeader>
            </PopoverContent>
          </Popover>
        ))}
      </div>
    </DirectionProvider>
  );
}
```

## With a form

This form owns its draft and saved name. Save submits and explicitly closes; dismissing does not save. Reopening retains the draft in caller state. The non-modal default allows focus to leave the panel.

<ComponentExample name="form" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import { Field, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";

import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";

export function FormPopover() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [name, setName] = useState("Open PRs");
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState("Open PRs");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <Popover open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Rename view</PopoverTrigger>
        <PopoverContent>
          <form
            className="grid gap-4"
            onSubmit={(event) => {
              event.preventDefault();
              setSaved(name);
              setOpen(false);
            }}
          >
            <PopoverHeader>
              <PopoverTitle>Rename this view</PopoverTitle>
              <PopoverDescription>The caller owns this draft and the saved name.</PopoverDescription>
            </PopoverHeader>
            <Field>
              <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>View name</FieldLabel>
              <Input id={id} value={name} onValueChange={setName} required />
            </Field>
            <Button type="submit">Save view</Button>
          </form>
        </PopoverContent>
      </Popover>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        View: {saved}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

The external application opener changes open without clicking the trigger. A unique triggerId and matching trigger id keep that controlled update anchored. Finish editing closes explicitly; the trigger and Escape also report open changes.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";

export function ControlledPopover() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Open from application state
      </Button>
      <Popover open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} triggerId={id}>
        <PopoverTrigger id={id} render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
          View options
        </PopoverTrigger>
        <PopoverContent>
          <PopoverHeader>
            <PopoverTitle>Application-owned panel</PopoverTitle>
            <PopoverDescription>The trigger ID anchors external open updates to the same trigger.</PopoverDescription>
          </PopoverHeader>
          <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
            Finish editing
          </Button>
        </PopoverContent>
      </Popover>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Modal when it has to be

False, true, and trap-focus are fixed instances. True blocks outside interactions and locks desktop page scrolling; trap-focus keeps focus inside without scroll locking. On touch devices Base UI may keep the page scrollable. Cadence does not export PopoverClose: compose Base UI Popover.Close through Button so Base UI registers the close part and enables the modal=true focus trap. It also gives touch screen readers an exit.

<ComponentExample name="modal" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Popover as PopoverPrimitive } from "@base-ui/react/popover";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";

export function ModalPopovers() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {([false, true, "trap-focus"] as const).map((modal) => (
        <Popover key={String(modal)} modal={modal}>
          <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{String(modal)}</PopoverTrigger>
          <PopoverContent>
            <PopoverHeader>
              <PopoverTitle>Modal: {String(modal)}</PopoverTitle>
              <PopoverDescription>
                False allows page interaction. True blocks outside interaction and locks desktop page scrolling.
                Trap-focus keeps focus inside without scroll locking.
              </PopoverDescription>
            </PopoverHeader>
            <PopoverPrimitive.Close render={<Button variant="outline" className="mt-3" />}>
              Close options
            </PopoverPrimitive.Close>
          </PopoverContent>
        </Popover>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

The first fixed scope uses none from portal insertion. The second restores full within that none provider; the OS reduced preference still wins. These explicit mode examples are separate from ordinary instances that inherit the header.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";

export function PopoverMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <Popover>
          <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open without motion</PopoverTrigger>
          <PopoverContent data-testid="initial-none">
            <PopoverHeader>
              <PopoverTitle>Immediate popover</PopoverTitle>
              <PopoverDescription>This portal starts at zero duration.</PopoverDescription>
            </PopoverHeader>
          </PopoverContent>
        </Popover>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Popover>
            <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open nested full</PopoverTrigger>
            <PopoverContent data-testid="nested-full">
              <PopoverHeader>
                <PopoverTitle>Nested full popover</PopoverTitle>
                <PopoverDescription>The OS preference still wins over explicit full.</PopoverDescription>
              </PopoverHeader>
            </PopoverContent>
          </Popover>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A small set of controls that belongs to the thing it is attached to: column visibility, a filter, a
  share link, a colour picker.
- Context that would crowd the page if it were always visible, but that the user opens on demand.
- An edit that is scoped to one trigger and can be dismissed without losing the page.

## When not to use

- A confirmation that must be answered. Use `alert-dialog`: a popover can be dismissed by clicking away.
- A task that needs the whole screen or a focus trap. Use `dialog` or `sheet`.
- A one- or two-word hint on a control. Use `tooltip`, which cannot hold interactive content.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Popover` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `triggerId`, `modal` | Base UI root; `modal=false` by default, also accepts `true` and `"trap-focus"`. |
| `PopoverTrigger` | native button props, `render` | The anchor and the toggle. |
| `PopoverContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Portal and positioner; side=`bottom`, align=`center`, sideOffset=`4`, alignOffset=`0`. Sides include physical and logical values. |
| `PopoverHeader` | `className` | Stacked title and description. |
| `PopoverTitle` | `className` | Base UI heading; the panel's accessible name. |
| `PopoverDescription` | `className` | Muted supporting text; becomes `aria-describedby`. |

`PopoverContent` positions itself; there is no `PopoverAnchor` export, because Base UI anchors to the
trigger and upstream's Base UI surface has no anchor part.

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel appears on the first frame | – | – |

The panel grows out of its anchor rather than sliding towards it. A slide would need a distance token
and four per-side classes, and it moves the edge the positioner just lined up away from the trigger;
`--transform-origin` says the same thing with one transform. The scale reads `--motion-scale-in`, so
the class list carries a token and not a number.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Opens the popover from its trigger. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the panel's controls and then out; modal focus trapping also needs a registered Base UI Close part, as in the modal example. |
| Escape | Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger. |

Pressing outside closes it, which is the difference between a popover and an alert dialog.

## Accessibility

- Base UI gives the popup `role="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` on the trigger, `aria-controls`, and focus
  return on close. The panel is labelled by `PopoverTitle` and described by `PopoverDescription` when
  both are rendered.
- The trigger keeps `aria-expanded` in step, so assistive technology announces "collapsed" / "expanded"
  rather than a dialog appearing out of nowhere.
- `PopoverTitle` is optional for an interactive panel, but any popover that opens a region of controls
  should have one: an unnamed dialog is announced as just "dialog".
- Interactive controls inside the panel are reachable: the popover is non-modal, so Tab leaves it and
  the trigger's focus ring stays where the user left it.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is `w-72` wide and flips sides when the trigger has no room above or below; Base UI also
shifts it along the cross axis to stay inside the viewport. On a narrow screen it can fill most of the
width — pass `className="w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]"` or a max width when the content is wider than the
default.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the portal unmounts after the exit transition.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no `top`/`left` transition, no JavaScript
  animation loop. Reopening during the exit reverses the fade.

## Notes for AI

- Use `popover` for anchored, dismissible content; use `alert-dialog` for a deliberate confirmation.
- Pass the trigger through `render`, not a wrapper: the trigger is what the positioner anchors to and
  what gets `aria-expanded`.
- Modal popovers still dismiss on Escape and outside presses. Alert Dialog blocks outside dismissal;
  Escape can still cancel that confirmation.

Popover resolves its local token clock inside the portal, including timeScale and
reducedDurationScale. Callback classes/styles are evaluated with Base UI state and
merged last. Live reduced removes scale transitions; none cancels transitions and
renders without hidden starting/ending opacity, including nested provider overrides.

# Tooltip

Hints for icon buttons, shortcuts, and truncated values.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/tooltip
```

Optionally wrap the app in `TooltipProvider` once to set one delay for every tooltip; Base UI does not
require it.
These examples also use `@cadence/button`; the icon example uses `lucide-react`.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| tooltip | `@components/cadence/tooltip/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/tooltip.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: tooltip](https://cadence.dev/r/tooltip.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, keeping `tooltip/index.tsx` and the shared `lib/`
directory in the same `cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and the
sources' `"use client"` directives. Copy every file in the motion, utilities
and provider payloads, including helpers not imported by Tooltip directly.
The provider files and `motion` package are required imports even without
the optional `CadenceProvider` wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the
copied files. Include the Cadence easing and motion-scale tokens used by the
popup classes. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is required.
Full fades and scales the label from its anchor; reduced keeps opacity only;
none removes transitions and hidden entry/exit styles. The portalled popup
resolves its own mode and token clock. Standalone components follow the system
motion preference; an optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree, and nested
full still respects system reduced motion.

[Button](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation) is used by Usage,
the top specimen and every body example. Copy its complete Manual setup,
including its npm dependencies and shared files. Usage and the top specimen
also import an icon:

```package-manager
npm install lucide-react
```

Logical sides and RTL imports Base UI `DirectionProvider` from the already
required `@base-ui/react` package. Explicit motion scopes uses the included
Cadence provider. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Controlled needs a caller client module for its state
and event handlers. The other examples and top specimen contain serializable
JSX and element-valued `render` props, so they can be composed in synchronous
Server Components. Caller refs, event handlers, function-valued `render`,
`className(state)` or `style(state)` also need a caller client boundary.
Synchronous `useId` alone does not require one. Keep the installed client
directives and the snippets' existing directives when copying them unchanged.

Place `TooltipTrigger` and `TooltipContent` within the same `Tooltip` root.
Use `defaultOpen` for uncontrolled opening, or `open` / `onOpenChange` for
caller control. External opening needs a unique `triggerId` matching the
trigger's `id`, as in Controlled, to keep the popup anchored. The trigger
renders a button by default; `render={<Button />}` merges onto that button.
Custom render elements must preserve supplied props and refs.

`TooltipContent` already owns the portal, positioner, popup and arrow. Its
positioning defaults are `side="top"`, `align="center"`, `sideOffset={4}` and
`alignOffset={0}`. Offsets control geometry, and Base UI can flip or shift the
label to avoid collisions. Logical sides need Base UI `DirectionProvider`
as well as DOM `dir`, as shown in the RTL example. Cadence exports no separate
Portal, Positioner, Arrow or Anchor part.

`TooltipProvider` is optional and groups adjacent hints under one hover delay;
its Cadence default is `delay={0}`. Without a provider or trigger override,
Base UI uses 600ms. A trigger's `delay` overrides the initial delay; an active
provider group can show adjacent hints immediately. Keyboard focus opens
immediately. Trigger `closeDelay` controls hover closing. These interaction
delays are independent of motion mode, including none.

Give icon-only triggers an accessible name such as `aria-label`. Cadence adds
`role="tooltip"` and links the open popup through `aria-describedby`; the hint
supplements the control's name. Hover or keyboard focus reveals the label,
leaving hides it, and Escape dismisses without moving focus. Enter and Space
still activate the trigger. Keep essential instructions visible and use
Popover for interactive content.

Root or trigger `disabled` suppresses the hint; disable the rendered Button
separately to block its action. A native disabled button cannot receive focus.
Disabled controls therefore uses a focusable, disabled Button rendered as a
span around the truly disabled native button, with `pointer-events-none` on
the inner button so hover targets the wrapper. Preserve that composition for
both pointer and keyboard access.

The caller owns action availability, business data, shortcut behavior, requests
and controlled open state. Tooltip only presents explanatory UI; it does not
implement those actions or validate form data. JavaScript is required for
hover, focus, delayed opening and controlled updates.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { BoldIcon } from "lucide-react";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function BoldTooltip() {
  return (
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" />} aria-label="Bold">
        <BoldIcon aria-hidden="true" />
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>Bold (⌘B)</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

## Positioned by side

The four physical sides have separate fixed triggers. Base UI flips and shifts the label when space runs out. sideOffset changes the gap; the scale still grows from the anchor origin.

<ComponentExample name="sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function TooltipSides() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["top", "right", "bottom", "left"] as const).map((side) => (
        <Tooltip key={side}>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{side}</TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent side={side} sideOffset={8}>
            {side} placement
          </TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Aligned to the trigger

Start, center, and end are fixed cross-axis alignments on the default top side. alignOffset is zero here; numeric offsets remain caller choices. The content and arrow follow collision handling.

<ComponentExample name="alignments" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function TooltipAlignments() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["start", "center", "end"] as const).map((align) => (
        <Tooltip key={align}>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{align}</TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent align={align} alignOffset={0}>
            {align} alignment with this trigger
          </TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Logical sides and RTL

inline-start and inline-end follow Base UI DirectionProvider. This example also sets DOM dir=rtl for text. The two independent triggers cover logical placement without a side selector.

<ComponentExample name="logical-sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DirectionProvider } from "@base-ui/react/direction-provider";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function LogicalTooltips() {
  return (
    <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">
      <div dir="rtl" className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        {(["inline-start", "inline-end"] as const).map((side) => (
          <Tooltip key={side}>
            <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{side}</TooltipTrigger>
            <TooltipContent side={side}>{side} follows RTL</TooltipContent>
          </Tooltip>
        ))}
      </div>
    </DirectionProvider>
  );
}
```

## A delay for the whole app

Place TooltipProvider around the application once to give all its tooltips the same 300ms hover delay. These two hints stand in for that application scope. Adjacent hints can open instantly while the provider group is active. Keyboard focus opens immediately. Without a provider or trigger override, Base UI uses its default 600ms; Cadence TooltipProvider itself defaults delay to zero.

<ComponentExample name="delay" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function AppTooltipDelay() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider delay={300}>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <Tooltip>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Upload help</TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent>Upload files up to 10 MB</TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
        <Tooltip>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Share help</TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent>Only invited people can read this project</TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
      </div>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Disabled controls

A native disabled button cannot receive keyboard focus. The outer Button renders a span through nativeButton=false and uses disabled plus focusableWhenDisabled: it provides button semantics, a focus ring, and blocked activation while remaining focusable. It wraps the truly disabled native Deploy button. pointer-events-none sends pointer targeting to the wrapper, so both hover and keyboard focus reveal the explanation.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function DisabledControlTooltip() {
  return (
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger
        render={
          <Button
            render={<span />}
            nativeButton={false}
            disabled
            focusableWhenDisabled
            variant="ghost"
            className="h-auto p-0"
          />
        }
        aria-label="Why Deploy is unavailable"
      >
        <Button disabled className="pointer-events-none">
          Deploy
        </Button>
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>Finish the required fields first</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

The external Show shortcut action owns open state. A unique triggerId anchors that update to Keyboard help; normal focus, hover, and Escape still report changes through onOpenChange. The popup carries only explanatory text.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function ControlledTooltip() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen((value) => !value)}>
        {open ? "Hide shortcut" : "Show shortcut"}
      </Button>
      <Tooltip open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} triggerId={id}>
        <TooltipTrigger id={id} render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
          Keyboard help
        </TooltipTrigger>
        <TooltipContent>Press ⌘K to search</TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

These explicit overrides show none from insertion and full restored within that none scope, subject to OS reduction. Other examples inherit the site header. The tooltip delay is interaction timing and is independent of its motion mode.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function TooltipMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <Tooltip>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open without motion</TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent data-testid="initial-none">Immediate tooltip</TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Tooltip>
            <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open nested full</TooltipTrigger>
            <TooltipContent data-testid="nested-full">The OS preference still wins</TooltipContent>
          </Tooltip>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- An icon-only control whose meaning is not obvious from the icon alone.
- The full value behind a truncated label, or a keyboard shortcut next to an action.
- A hint that helps the first use of a dense control and is useless once learned.

## When not to use

- Anything the user must read to act: a tooltip disappears on scroll, touch, and Escape. If the content
  matters, put it on the page or in a `popover`.
- Interactive content. A tooltip cannot hold a button or a link; use `popover`.
- The accessible name of a button that already has text. Two labels that disagree is worse than one.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TooltipProvider` | `delay` | Optional. One delay for every tooltip inside. |
| `Tooltip` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `triggerId`, `disabled` | Base UI root; `triggerId` anchors external open updates. |
| `TooltipTrigger` | native button props, `render`, `delay`, `closeDelay`, `disabled` | Hover/focus target; carries `aria-describedby`. Trigger `disabled` suppresses the hint; disable the rendered Button separately to block its action. |
| `TooltipContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, popup, and arrow. `side` defaults to `top`, `sideOffset` to `4`. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | label `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | label `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the label appears on the first frame | – | – |

A tooltip is small enough that `duration.fast` is already at the edge of readable: nothing here waits
for an exit to finish. The arrow is part of the popup and moves with it, so it is never animated
separately.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focus shows the label; leaving hides it. |
| Escape | Hides the label and leaves focus on the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the trigger. The tooltip does not swallow the press. |

Keyboard focus provides an additional route to the same explanation. Keep essential instructions
visible on the page, including for touch users.

## Accessibility

- Base UI's own tooltip adds neither `role="tooltip"` nor `aria-describedby`; Cadence wires both. The
  trigger points at the popup only while it is open — a closed popup would otherwise leave a dangling
  id, which axe reports — and the popup is `role="tooltip"`.
- The tooltip must not be the only name of a control. Give an icon button a real `aria-label`; the
  tooltip is the extra sentence, not the name.
- Text stays readable in both themes: `bg-foreground` / `text-background` invert, so the label keeps
  contrast against whatever surface it floats over.
- Escape dismisses it without moving focus, so a tooltip never traps a keyboard user.

## Responsive behavior

The label is `w-fit` with a `max-w-xs` cap and wraps at word boundaries (`text-balance`) instead of
running off screen. Base UI flips the side and shifts the alignment when the viewport cannot fit it.

## Performance

- The popup tree is mounted only while the label is open; a page can carry dozens of tooltips without
  paying for them all.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no measuring loop, no JavaScript animation.
  Hover is not a state the component polls.

## Notes for AI

- Use a tooltip to name or explain a control, never to deliver information the user needs to proceed.
- Do not put a link, button, or form inside it; use `popover`.
- Give every icon-only trigger an `aria-label`: the tooltip complements the name, it does not replace it.

# Hover Card

Previews of links, profiles, and repositories.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/hover-card
```

The action, placement and scope examples compose `@cadence/button`. Install that item when copying those examples.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: hover-card](https://cadence.dev/r/hover-card.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, keeping `hover-card/index.tsx` and the shared
`lib/` directory in the same `cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and
the sources' `"use client"` directives. Copy every file in the motion,
utilities and provider payloads, including helpers not imported by Hover
Card directly. The provider files and `motion` package are required imports
even without the optional `CadenceProvider` wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the
copied files. Include the Cadence easing and motion-scale tokens used by the
popup classes. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is required.
Full fades and scales the card from its anchor; reduced keeps opacity only;
none removes transitions and hidden entry/exit styles. The portalled popup
resolves its own mode and token clock. Standalone components follow the system
motion preference; an optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree, and nested
full still respects system reduced motion.

Usage, the top specimen and Trigger delay use only Hover Card. With an action
inside, Placement, Alignment, Logical placement, Controlled preview and
Explicit motion scopes also use
[Button](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation). Copy its complete
Manual setup, including its npm dependencies and shared files. Logical
placement imports Base UI `DirectionProvider` from the already required
`@base-ui/react` package. Explicit motion scopes uses the included Cadence
provider. Beyond Button's dependencies, the examples need no additional npm
package. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, With an action inside needs a caller client module for
its ref, state and keyboard/click handlers; Controlled preview needs one for
its state and event handlers. The other examples and top specimen contain
serializable JSX and element-valued `render` props, so they can be composed
in synchronous Server Components. Caller refs, event handlers,
function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)` also need a
caller client boundary. Synchronous `useId` alone does not require one. Keep
the installed client directives and the snippets' existing directives when
copying them unchanged.

Place `HoverCardTrigger` and `HoverCardContent` within the same `HoverCard`
root. Use `defaultOpen` for uncontrolled opening, or `open` / `onOpenChange`
for caller control. External opening needs a unique `triggerId` matching the
trigger's `id`, as in Controlled preview, to keep the card anchored. The
trigger renders an anchor by default: give it a useful `href` and visible
link text. `render={<Button />}` merges onto a button; custom render elements
must preserve supplied props and refs.

`HoverCardContent` already owns the portal, positioner and popup. Its
positioning defaults are `side="bottom"`, `align="center"`, `sideOffset={4}`
and `alignOffset={4}`. Offsets control geometry, and Base UI can flip or shift
the card to avoid collisions. Logical sides need Base UI `DirectionProvider`
as well as DOM `dir`, as shown in Logical placement. Cadence exports no
separate Portal, Positioner, Arrow or Anchor part.

Trigger `delay` and `closeDelay` default to 600ms and 300ms. Pointer entry and
keyboard focus can open the card; focus opening also uses `delay`. Pointer
crossing into the popup keeps it open, and leaving uses the closing delay.
These interaction delays are independent of motion mode, including none.
Escape dismisses the card; Enter on a link keeps its normal navigation.
The action example supplies its own ArrowDown ref bridge to Follow because
the portal does not place that action immediately after the trigger in page
Tab order. Preserve that bridge when copying the example.

Keep the trigger's accessible name and destination useful on their own.
The popup has no dialog role and is not the trigger's accessible description.
All previewed information must also be available at the destination or in
visible page content: touch activation may follow the link without revealing
the preview. Use Popover for an intentionally opened task or essential action.
The caller owns navigation, profile data, Follow state, requests and errors;
the example's Follow action changes local state only.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";

export function ReviewerCard() {
  return (
    <p className="text-sm">
      Reviewed by{" "}
      <HoverCard>
        <HoverCardTrigger render={<a className="underline underline-offset-4" href="/docs/changelog" />}>@linruoxin</HoverCardTrigger>
        <HoverCardContent>
          <p className="text-sm font-medium">Lin Ruoxin</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Maintains the motion layer and the registry.</p>
        </HoverCardContent>
      </HoverCard>
    </p>
  );
}
```

## With an action inside

A real local Follow action belongs to this example alone. The supplementary card stays open while its pointer or focus is inside; the profile link remains useful without opening it. Nothing is sent to a server. Once keyboard focus opens this card, ArrowDown moves to Follow using a caller-owned ref. The portal does not itself insert that action immediately after the trigger in the page Tab order.

<ComponentExample name="action" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";

export function FollowReviewer() {
  const follow = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const [following, setFollowing] = useState(false);
  return (
    <HoverCard>
      <HoverCardTrigger onKeyDown={(event) => { if (event.key === "ArrowDown") { event.preventDefault(); follow.current?.focus(); } }} render={<a href="/docs/changelog" className="text-sm underline" />}>Reviewer profile</HoverCardTrigger>
      <HoverCardContent>
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Lin Ruoxin</p>
        <p className="mb-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Maintains the motion layer.</p>
        <Button size="xs" variant="secondary" ref={follow} aria-pressed={following} onClick={() => setFollowing((value) => !value)}>
          {following ? "Following" : "Follow"}
        </Button>
      </HoverCardContent>
    </HoverCard>
  );
}
```

## Placement

The preferred side defaults to bottom. Each trigger has its own fixed side and portal. Base UI can flip or shift a card near the viewport edge; these are placement preferences, not a promise to overflow.

<ComponentExample name="sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";

export function HoverCardSides() {
  return (<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["top","right","bottom","left"] as const).map((value) => (
        <HoverCard key={value}>
          <HoverCardTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{value}</HoverCardTrigger>
          <HoverCardContent side={value} alignOffset={0}>Preview: {value}</HoverCardContent>
        </HoverCard>
      ))}
    </div>);
}
```

## Alignment

Compare all three alignments below their triggers. This example sets alignOffset to zero so the edge or centre is visible; the component default remains 4px.

<ComponentExample name="alignments" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";

export function HoverCardAlignments() {
  return (<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["start","center","end"] as const).map((value) => (
        <HoverCard key={value}>
          <HoverCardTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{value}</HoverCardTrigger>
          <HoverCardContent align={value} alignOffset={0}>Preview: {value}</HoverCardContent>
        </HoverCard>
      ))}
    </div>);
}
```

## Logical placement

Logical sides follow the direction provider. In RTL, inline-start prefers the right and inline-end prefers the left; physical sides keep their meaning.

<ComponentExample name="logical-sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DirectionProvider } from "@base-ui/react/direction-provider";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";

export function LogicalHoverCards() {
  return (<DirectionProvider direction="rtl"><div dir="rtl"><div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["inline-start","inline-end"] as const).map((value) => (
        <HoverCard key={value}>
          <HoverCardTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{value}</HoverCardTrigger>
          <HoverCardContent side={value} alignOffset={0}>Preview: {value}</HoverCardContent>
        </HoverCard>
      ))}
    </div></div></DirectionProvider>);
}
```

## Trigger delay

The trigger owns delay and closeDelay. This card waits 400ms on pointer entry and 300ms on pointer leave, giving time to cross into the card. The installed Base UI defaults are 600ms and 300ms. Focus also makes the preview reachable.

<ComponentExample name="delay" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";

export function DelayedReviewer() {
  return (
    <HoverCard>
      <HoverCardTrigger delay={400} closeDelay={300} render={<a href="/docs/changelog" className="text-sm underline" />}>Delayed profile</HoverCardTrigger>
      <HoverCardContent>Preview after a short pointer pause.</HoverCardContent>
    </HoverCard>
  );
}
```

## Controlled preview

The caller owns open state. The external action targets a unique triggerId so the preview has a real anchor even when opened externally. It remains supplementary and can still close through the normal pointer, focus and Escape paths.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";

export function ControlledReviewer() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen((value) => !value)}>{open ? "Hide preview" : "Show preview"}</Button>
      <HoverCard open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} triggerId={id}>
        <HoverCardTrigger id={id} render={<a href="/docs/changelog" className="text-sm underline" />}>Controlled profile</HoverCardTrigger>
        <HoverCardContent>Caller-owned profile preview.</HoverCardContent>
      </HoverCard>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

Ordinary examples inherit the site header. Only this comparison sets a fixed none provider, with a nested full override. The system reduced-motion preference still takes precedence over full.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function HoverCardMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <HoverCard>
          <HoverCardTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open without motion</HoverCardTrigger>
          <HoverCardContent data-testid="initial-none">Immediate preview</HoverCardContent>
        </HoverCard>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <HoverCard>
            <HoverCardTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open nested full</HoverCardTrigger>
            <HoverCardContent data-testid="nested-full">The OS preference still wins</HoverCardContent>
          </HoverCard>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A preview of what a link leads to: a profile, a repository, a document — enough to decide whether to
  click.
- Context that helps a name make sense — the person behind an `@handle`, the project behind a package.
- A short panel with one or two actions that should not interrupt the page.

## When not to use

- A label for an icon. Use `tooltip`: it is smaller, quicker, and announced as a description.
- Content the user opened on purpose. Use `popover`: hover cards close when the pointer moves on, and
  anything with a task in it deserves a deliberate open.
- Information the user needs to answer a question. Nothing that appears and disappears on hover can be
  the only place it lives.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HoverCard` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | Base UI root; owns open state. |
| `HoverCardTrigger` | native anchor props, `render`, `delay`, `closeDelay` | The link or button the card describes. |
| `HoverCardContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, and popup. `side` defaults to `bottom`, `sideOffset` to `4`, `alignOffset` to `4`. |

The portal renders `data-slot="hover-card-portal"`; the popup is `data-slot="hover-card-content"`. There
is no `HoverCardArrow`: upstream's Base UI surface has none, and the card is a surface rather than a
pointer.

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel appears on the first frame | – | – |

Same anchored motion as `popover` and `tooltip`: the scale starts at `--transform-origin`, which Base UI
points at the trigger. Hover cards close when the pointer leaves, so the exit has to be short; `fast` is
the anchored-surface duration the three share.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focusing the trigger opens the card. In the action example, ArrowDown moves to Follow; Tab otherwise follows the page order. |
| Escape | Closes the card and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter | Follows the trigger link, or activates the focused button. |
| Space | Activates a focused button; native links keep their normal Space scrolling behavior. |
| ArrowDown | In the action example, moves from the open trigger to Follow through the caller-owned ref. |

Keyboard focus opens the card for the same reason it does in a tooltip: without it, the content would
exist only for pointer users.

## Accessibility

- The trigger carries the accessible name; the card is supplementary. That is why Cadence does not give
  the popup `role="dialog"` or wire it as the trigger's description: a panel that may hold several
  paragraphs and a button is neither a name nor a description, and a screen reader reading it on every
  focus would be noise.
- The action example supplies an explicit ArrowDown focus bridge into its portal. Do not assume the
  portal puts actions directly after the trigger in page Tab order; use a popover for a deliberate task.
- Hover is never the only path: focus opens it too, and Escape closes it, so the card never traps a
  keyboard user.
- If the card is the only place a piece of information exists, it is in the wrong component — move it
  into the page or into a `popover`.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is `w-64` with `p-4`; Base UI flips it to another side and shifts the alignment when the
viewport cannot fit it. On touch devices there is no hover: tapping the trigger link may navigate
directly without revealing the preview. All previewed information must also be available at the
destination or in visible page content.

## Performance

- Mounted only while open, so a page of links carries no extra popup trees.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only: no layout reads, no `top`/`left` transition, no JavaScript
  animation loop. The card follows the anchor through the positioner, not through React state.

## Notes for AI

- Use `hover-card` only for a preview of the linked thing; use `popover` for anything the user opens to
  act, and `tooltip` for a label.
- The trigger must have its own text or `aria-label`; the card is not its name.
- Keep the card small: a person, a repository, a document summary, one action. If it needs scrolling, it
  wants to be a `popover` or a page.

The site's preview shell is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Usage, the top filter specimen and Controlled form need
a client module for their state and event handlers. A long list needs one for
