`useState`, `useRef`, function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)`
does require that boundary. Preserve the installed sources' client directives.

`SheetContent` already includes its portal and backdrop; do not duplicate them
in the standard composition. It defaults to the right edge with the corner
close button visible. Use `side` for the four physical edges, and keep a visible
close action when setting `showCloseButton={false}`. Give every panel a
`SheetTitle` and meaningful supporting text through `SheetDescription`. Default
modal behavior traps focus and locks page scrolling; `modal={false}` and
`modal="trap-focus"` change those behaviors but still keep SheetContent's
backdrop. Base UI handles focus, Escape, outside dismissal and focus return.
The caller owns controlled open state, filter application, draft/saved values,
submission, validation and persistence. Cancel preserves the controlled
example's draft. For long content, keep the header and footer outside the
`min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto` body and supply the initial focus target shown
below. Top and bottom panels size to content, so constrain tall content for
your viewport. Hydrated interactions require JavaScript.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox";
import { Field, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/sheet";

export function FiltersSheet() {
  const id = useId();
  const [openOnly, setOpenOnly] = useState(true);
  const [applied, setApplied] = useState("Open only");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Sheet>
        <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open filters</SheetTrigger>
        <SheetContent>
          <SheetHeader>
            <SheetTitle>Filters</SheetTitle>
            <SheetDescription>Choose filters for this local view.</SheetDescription>
          </SheetHeader>
          <FieldGroup className="px-4">
            <Field orientation="horizontal">
              <Checkbox id={id} checked={openOnly} onCheckedChange={setOpenOnly} />
              <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>Open only</FieldLabel>
            </Field>
          </FieldGroup>
          <SheetFooter>
            <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpenOnly(false)}>
              Clear selection
            </Button>
            <SheetClose render={<Button onClick={() => setApplied(openOnly ? "Open only" : "All items")} />}>
              Apply filters
            </SheetClose>
          </SheetFooter>
        </SheetContent>
      </Sheet>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {applied}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## The four edges

Each trigger opens an independent sheet at a fixed edge. Right is the default. Side panels use three quarters of the viewport with a desktop width cap; top and bottom panels span the width and size to content.

<ComponentExample name="edges" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/sheet";

export function SheetEdges() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["right", "left", "top", "bottom"] as const).map((side) => (
        <Sheet key={side}>
          <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{side}</SheetTrigger>
          <SheetContent side={side}>
            <SheetHeader>
              <SheetTitle>{side} sheet</SheetTitle>
              <SheetDescription>A fixed {side} edge.</SheetDescription>
            </SheetHeader>
            <SheetFooter>
              <SheetClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Done</SheetClose>
            </SheetFooter>
          </SheetContent>
        </Sheet>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Without the built-in close button

showCloseButton=false removes only the corner control. Keep a clear footer close action, Escape and outside dismissal. This example provides an explicit Done action.

<ComponentExample name="footer-close" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/sheet";

export function FooterCloseSheet() {
  return (
    <Sheet>
      <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open footer close</SheetTrigger>
      <SheetContent showCloseButton={false}>
        <SheetHeader>
          <SheetTitle>View details</SheetTitle>
          <SheetDescription>The footer provides the visible close action.</SheetDescription>
        </SheetHeader>
        <p className="px-4 text-sm">A short details panel.</p>
        <SheetFooter>
          <SheetClose render={<Button />}>Done</SheetClose>
        </SheetFooter>
      </SheetContent>
    </Sheet>
  );
}
```

## A long list

Keep the header, close button and footer outside the scrolling body. A min-height of zero lets the middle flex child shrink. Initial focus on the title opens the list at its beginning without jumping to a footer control. The entries link to the changelog, so Tab reaches the scrolling body and PageDown scrolls it without requiring a pointer.

<ComponentExample name="long-list" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/sheet";

export function LongSheet() {
  const title = useRef<HTMLHeadingElement>(null);
  return (
    <Sheet>
      <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Browse activity</SheetTrigger>
      <SheetContent initialFocus={title}>
        <SheetHeader>
          <SheetTitle ref={title} tabIndex={-1}>
            Activity
          </SheetTitle>
          <SheetDescription>Scroll the list while the footer stays in view.</SheetDescription>
        </SheetHeader>
        <section aria-label="Activity entries"  className="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-4 outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring"><ol className="flex flex-col gap-4">
          {Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, index) => (
            <li key={index.toString()} className="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">
              <a href="/docs/changelog" className="underline underline-offset-4">Activity {index + 1}: documentation updated.</a>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ol></section>
        <SheetFooter>
          <SheetClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Done</SheetClose>
        </SheetFooter>
      </SheetContent>
    </Sheet>
  );
}
```

## Controlled form

The caller owns open, draft and saved values. Save updates local state and closes; Cancel leaves the saved value unchanged and preserves the draft for reopening. No request or validation is performed. Each form owns its label ID.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Field, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/sheet";

export function ControlledSheet() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("Weekly digest");
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState("Weekly digest");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Sheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit title</SheetTrigger>
        <SheetContent>
          <SheetHeader>
            <SheetTitle>Edit title</SheetTitle>
            <SheetDescription>Save changes to this local example.</SheetDescription>
          </SheetHeader>
          <form
            className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col"
            onSubmit={(event) => {
              event.preventDefault();
              setSaved(draft);
              setOpen(false);
            }}
          >
            <FieldGroup className="px-4">
              <Field>
                <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>Title draft</FieldLabel>
                <Input id={id} value={draft} onValueChange={setDraft} />
              </Field>
            </FieldGroup>
            <SheetFooter>
              <SheetClose render={<Button type="button" variant="outline" />}>Cancel</SheetClose>
              <Button type="submit">Save title</Button>
            </SheetFooter>
          </form>
        </SheetContent>
      </Sheet>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        Saved: {saved}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Modal behavior

Compare modal=true (scroll lock and focus trap), false (page interaction remains available), and trap-focus (focus trap without scroll lock). SheetContent always renders its backdrop, including false and trap-focus; use a suitable composition when the page must remain visually unobscured.

<ComponentExample name="modality" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/sheet";

export function SheetModality() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {([true, false, "trap-focus"] as const).map((modal) => (
        <Sheet key={String(modal)} modal={modal}>
          <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{String(modal)}</SheetTrigger>
          <SheetContent>
            <SheetHeader>
              <SheetTitle>Mode: {String(modal)}</SheetTitle>
              <SheetDescription>Focus and scrolling follow the root modal setting.</SheetDescription>
            </SheetHeader>
            <SheetFooter>
              <SheetClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Done</SheetClose>
            </SheetFooter>
          </SheetContent>
        </Sheet>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

Ordinary sheets inherit the header clock. This comparison alone fixes none and then restores full in a nested scope. The OS reduced-motion preference still wins. Both the panel and its backdrop resolve the local clock.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/sheet";

export function SheetMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <Sheet>
          <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open without motion</SheetTrigger>
          <SheetContent data-testid="initial-none">
            <SheetHeader>
              <SheetTitle>Immediate sheet</SheetTitle>
              <SheetDescription>No entering motion.</SheetDescription>
            </SheetHeader>
          </SheetContent>
        </Sheet>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Sheet>
            <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open nested full</SheetTrigger>
            <SheetContent data-testid="nested-full">
              <SheetHeader>
                <SheetTitle>Nested full sheet</SheetTitle>
                <SheetDescription>The OS preference still wins.</SheetDescription>
              </SheetHeader>
            </SheetContent>
          </Sheet>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A task that should keep the page in view: filters, a details panel, settings for the thing behind it.
- A form too tall or too wide for a `popover`, opened on purpose and dismissed on purpose.
- Mobile navigation or a secondary menu, where a full dialog would feel heavy.

## When not to use

- A confirmation that must be answered before anything continues. Use `alert-dialog`.
- A hint about a control. Use `tooltip` or `hover-card`.
- A flow with its own steps and URL. That is a page, not an overlay.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Sheet` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI dialog root. |
| `SheetTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the sheet. |
| `SheetContent` | `side` (`"right" \| "left" \| "top" \| "bottom"`), `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `SheetOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `SheetContent`. |
| `SheetPortal` | `container` | Available for a custom portal target. |
| `SheetClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the sheet. |
| `SheetHeader` / `SheetFooter` | `className` | Padding and stacking only. |
| `SheetTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `SheetDescription` | `className` | Supporting text. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `translate` from its own size; backdrop `opacity 0 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.base` / `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `translate` back off its edge; backdrop `opacity → 0` | `exit.fade` · panel `duration.base` / backdrop `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no translate; at `timeScale={1}`, default duration tokens run at 0.6×: panel 132ms / backdrop 96ms | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel is in place on the first frame | – | – |

The slide is `translate-*-full`, the panel's own width or height, not a fixed distance: a side panel
should enter from off its edge at every size, and a distance token would need one value per side. The
transition list names `translate` rather than `transform` because Tailwind v4's `translate-*` utilities
write the property individually — the same reason the dialogs transition `scale`.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the sheet; focus never reaches the page behind it. |
| Escape | Closes the sheet and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

The panel and backdrop resolve local token clocks from the effective mode and time scale, including
full inside a parent none scope. None also removes starting/ending opacity classes, so no hidden
starting frame remains. Caller state callback classes/styles still merge last.

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling.
- `SheetTitle` is required: a sheet without an accessible name is invalid. `SheetDescription` becomes
  the description, so put the consequence there, not in a second paragraph.
- The built-in close control is a button with a screen-reader-only "Close" label; it sits in the
  top-right corner at every side and never traps the focus ring.
- A destructive footer action uses `variant="destructive"` plus a specific verb; the colour is never the
  only signal.

## Responsive behavior

A right or left sheet is `w-3/4` capped at `sm:max-w-sm`; a top or bottom sheet spans the width with an
auto height. Long content should scroll inside a wrapper (see "A long list"), so the footer stays
reachable and the page behind does not move.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the overlay and panel unmount after the exit.
- Animates `opacity` and `translate` only: the panel is `fixed` at its edge, so nothing reflows and the
  page behind never reads layout.
- The close control is a `Button`, so its press feedback obeys the same motion mode as the sheet.

## Notes for AI

- Use `sheet` for a task beside the page; use `alert-dialog` when the answer must be deliberate, and
  `popover` when the content is small and anchored to a control.
- Always render `SheetTitle`; put the side effect of closing (reset, discard) in the footer, not in the
  title.
- Name the footer action after its effect ("Apply filters"), not "OK".
- If the sheet opens a form, remember P11: the sheet renders invalid state from `aria-invalid` but never
  validates anything itself.

# Drawer

Quick tasks on touch screens, such as share or move.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/drawer
```

The examples compose `@cadence/button`, `@cadence/field` and `@cadence/input` as needed.
Install those items when copying their corresponding examples.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| drawer | `@components/cadence/drawer/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/drawer.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: drawer](https://cadence.dev/r/drawer.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine files in the target list, including every shared `lib/` file.
Keep the mirrored `cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives
intact. The popup and backdrop use CSS transitions, but the provider imports
still require `motion`. The provider files are required; wrapping your
application in `CadenceProvider` is optional.

Complete the base theme setup linked above, including Cadence's easing tokens,
and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. There is no additional
Drawer-specific CSS or asset in these payloads. Each portalled popup and
backdrop resolves its own motion clock, including provider `timeScale`: full
slides and fades the popup, reduced keeps the fade and drops the closed-state
slide, and none removes authored transitions and hidden entry/exit opacity
from the first frame. Direct finger tracking remains in all three modes.
Without a wrapper, Drawer follows the system motion preference; a nested full
scope still respects the system reduced-motion preference.

Usage, the top Move conversation specimen and every body example additionally
use [Button](/components/button). Controlled draft also needs
[Field](/components/field) and [Input](/components/input). Install the items
used by the example you copy:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button @cadence/field @cadence/input
```

For manual installation, follow those pages' Manual tabs too. Button adds
`button/index.tsx`; Controlled draft additionally adds `field/index.tsx`,
`label/index.tsx`, `separator/index.tsx` and `input/index.tsx`. Reuse the shared
files already listed here. Button and Field require this extra npm package;
Input adds none beyond Drawer's complete dependency command:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

Explicit motion scopes uses the included provider. The site's preview shell
is not consumer setup.

In Next.js App Router, Usage, the top Move conversation specimen, Snap points
and Controlled draft need a client module for their state and event handlers.
A visible swipe handle, Swiping from another edge, Non-modal and focus-only
drawers, and Explicit motion scopes can be composed in a synchronous Server
Component with their shown JSX elements and serializable props; their existing
client directives may also be kept. `render={<Button />}` and synchronous
`useId` alone do not require a caller client boundary. A ref, event handler,
`useState`, function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)` does
require that boundary. Preserve the installed sources' client directives.

`DrawerContent` already includes its portal, viewport, popup and scrollable
content region, plus a backdrop only when `modal={true}`. Do not duplicate
these parts in the standard composition. Drawer defaults to `swipeDirection="down"`,
`modal={true}` and no handle. Direction selects both the edge and the outward
dismissal gesture: down/up are vertical, left/right are horizontal. The optional
handle is an aria-hidden visual cue; retain a real `DrawerClose` and a
`DrawerTitle`, with meaningful supporting text through `DrawerDescription`.
Trigger and Close use native buttons by default; `render` composes another
element with Base UI's props and ref.

Default modal behavior traps focus and locks page scrolling. `modal={false}`
allows interaction with the page; `modal="trap-focus"` traps focus without
scroll lock. Those two modes have no backdrop in this composition. Base UI
owns focus, Escape, outside dismissal, focus return and swipe recognition.
Vertical snap points are Base UI positions; the Snap points example controls
`snapPoint` through `onSnapPointChange`, Expand and Peek. The caller owns open
and snap state when controlled, action data, draft/saved values, submission,
validation and persistence. Move conversation and Save only update local
example state; Cancel preserves the draft without updating the saved value.
The content region scrolls inside the popup, including its header and footer;
constrain tall content to your viewport. Hydrated interactions require JavaScript.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";

export function MoveConversation() {
  const [destination, setDestination] = useState("Not moved");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Drawer showSwipeHandle>
        <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Move conversation</DrawerTrigger>
        <DrawerContent>
          <DrawerHeader>
            <DrawerTitle>Move conversation</DrawerTitle>
            <DrawerDescription>Drag down to dismiss, or choose a local destination.</DrawerDescription>
          </DrawerHeader>
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-1 py-4">
            {["Inbox", "Archive", "Read later"].map((value) => (
              <DrawerClose
                key={value}
                render={<Button variant="ghost" className="justify-start" onClick={() => setDestination(value)} />}
              >
                {value}
              </DrawerClose>
            ))}
          </div>
          <DrawerFooter>
            <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DrawerClose>
          </DrawerFooter>
        </DrawerContent>
      </Drawer>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {destination}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## A visible swipe handle

The handle is a visual gesture cue, aria-hidden rather than a focusable close button. Compare the default without a handle and showSwipeHandle=true. Both retain a real Close action and Escape.

<ComponentExample name="handle" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";

export function DrawerHandles() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {[false, true].map((handle) => (
        <Drawer key={String(handle)} showSwipeHandle={handle}>
          <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
            {handle ? "With handle" : "Without handle"}
          </DrawerTrigger>
          <DrawerContent>
            <DrawerHeader>
              <DrawerTitle>Swipe cue</DrawerTitle>
              <DrawerDescription>Drag down or use the close action.</DrawerDescription>
            </DrawerHeader>
            <DrawerFooter className="pt-4">
              <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DrawerClose>
            </DrawerFooter>
          </DrawerContent>
        </Drawer>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Swiping from another edge

Every direction has its own fixed trigger. down/up use the vertical axis; left/right use the horizontal axis. The direction is the dismissal gesture as well as the edge placement. Try an outward touch swipe or use Close.

<ComponentExample name="directions" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";

export function DrawerDirections() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["down", "up", "left", "right"] as const).map((direction) => (
        <Drawer key={direction} swipeDirection={direction} showSwipeHandle>
          <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{direction}</DrawerTrigger>
          <DrawerContent>
            <DrawerHeader>
              <DrawerTitle>{direction} drawer</DrawerTitle>
              <DrawerDescription>Swipe {direction} to dismiss.</DrawerDescription>
            </DrawerHeader>
            <DrawerFooter className="pt-4">
              <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DrawerClose>
            </DrawerFooter>
          </DrawerContent>
        </Drawer>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Snap points

This tall drawer rests at half or full height. The caller owns snapPoint, so Expand and Peek demonstrate external updates of the same panel, not a generic placement selector. Touch dragging still follows Base UI snap behavior. The backdrop follows swipe progress.

<ComponentExample name="snap-points" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";

export function SnappingDrawer() {
  const [snap, setSnap] = useState<number | string | null>(0.5);
  return (
    <Drawer showSwipeHandle snapPoints={[0.5, 1]} snapPoint={snap} onSnapPointChange={setSnap}>
      <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open snap points</DrawerTrigger>
      <DrawerContent className="h-[80dvh]">
        <DrawerHeader>
          <DrawerTitle>Reading queue</DrawerTitle>
          <DrawerDescription>Expand to read more, or drag between snap points.</DrawerDescription>
        </DrawerHeader>
        <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2 py-4">
          <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setSnap(1)}>
            Expand
          </Button>
          <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setSnap(0.5)}>
            Peek
          </Button>
        </div>
        <p role="status" className="text-sm">
          Snap: {String(snap)}
        </p>
        <ol className="flex flex-col gap-4 py-4">
          {Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, index) => (
            <li key={index.toString()} className="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">
              Reading item {index + 1}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ol>
        <DrawerFooter>
          <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DrawerClose>
        </DrawerFooter>
      </DrawerContent>
    </Drawer>
  );
}
```

## Non-modal and focus-only drawers

Compare true, false and trap-focus. Only true renders a backdrop and locks page scrolling. false allows page focus; trap-focus keeps focus inside without scroll lock. Close controls remain available in every mode.

<ComponentExample name="modality" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,

  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";

export function DrawerModality() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {([true, false, "trap-focus"] as const).map((modal) => (
        <Drawer key={String(modal)} modal={modal} showSwipeHandle>
          <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{String(modal)}</DrawerTrigger>
          <DrawerContent>
            <DrawerHeader>
              <DrawerTitle>Mode: {String(modal)}</DrawerTitle>
              <DrawerDescription>Focus and scrolling follow this mode.</DrawerDescription>
            </DrawerHeader>
            <DrawerFooter className="pt-4">
              <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DrawerClose>
            </DrawerFooter>
          </DrawerContent>
        </Drawer>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled draft

The caller owns open and draft state. Save records only local example state and closes. Cancel preserves the draft for reopening without changing the saved value. No network request or validation is implied.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";
import { Field, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";

export function ControlledDrawer() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("Read later");
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState("Read later");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Drawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} showSwipeHandle>
        <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit destination</DrawerTrigger>
        <DrawerContent>
          <DrawerHeader>
            <DrawerTitle>Destination label</DrawerTitle>
            <DrawerDescription>Rename this local example destination.</DrawerDescription>
          </DrawerHeader>
          <form
            className="flex flex-col gap-4 pt-4"
            onSubmit={(event) => {
              event.preventDefault();
              setSaved(draft);
              setOpen(false);
            }}
          >
            <FieldGroup>
              <Field>
                <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>Destination draft</FieldLabel>
                <Input id={id} value={draft} onValueChange={setDraft} />
              </Field>
            </FieldGroup>
            <DrawerFooter>
              <DrawerClose render={<Button type="button" variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DrawerClose>
              <Button type="submit">Save destination</Button>
            </DrawerFooter>
          </form>
        </DrawerContent>
      </Drawer>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        Saved: {saved}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

Ordinary drawers inherit the header. This example alone fixes none and nests a full override, subject to the OS preference. Direct finger tracking remains in every mode; none removes the authored enter, exit and release duration.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function DrawerMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <Drawer showSwipeHandle>
          <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open without motion</DrawerTrigger>
          <DrawerContent data-testid="initial-none">
            <DrawerHeader>
              <DrawerTitle>Immediate drawer</DrawerTitle>
              <DrawerDescription>No authored transition.</DrawerDescription>
            </DrawerHeader>
            <DrawerFooter>
              <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DrawerClose>
            </DrawerFooter>
          </DrawerContent>
        </Drawer>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Drawer showSwipeHandle>
            <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open nested full</DrawerTrigger>
            <DrawerContent data-testid="nested-full">
              <DrawerHeader>
                <DrawerTitle>Nested full drawer</DrawerTitle>
                <DrawerDescription>The OS preference still wins.</DrawerDescription>
              </DrawerHeader>
              <DrawerFooter>
                <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DrawerClose>
              </DrawerFooter>
            </DrawerContent>
          </Drawer>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A short task opened from the bottom of the screen, where the thumb is: move to, share, quick actions.
- A list or explanation that the page behind should stay visible for — a bottom sheet covers the bottom,
  not the context.
- A panel the user expects to swipe away, because that is how sheets behave on touch devices.

## When not to use

- A decision that must be answered. Use `alert-dialog`; a drawer can be dragged shut.
- A hint on a control. Use `tooltip` or `hover-card`.
- A long multi-step flow. Use a page or a `sheet` with a footer; dragging half-way through a form is a
  worse experience than a full surface.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Drawer` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`, `snapPoints`, `swipeDirection`, `showSwipeHandle` | `showSwipeHandle` is additive; `swipeDirection` defaults to `"down"` and `modal` to `true`. |
| `DrawerTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the drawer. |
| `DrawerContent` | `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay (when modal), viewport, popup, and content. |
| `DrawerOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DrawerContent`. |
| `DrawerSwipeHandle` | `className` | The handle; rendered for you when `showSwipeHandle` is set. |
| `DrawerClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the drawer. |
| `DrawerHeader` / `DrawerFooter` | `className` | Stacking and spacing only. |
| `DrawerTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `DrawerDescription` | `className` | Supporting text. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | sheet `opacity 0 → 1` + `transform` from `--closed-transform`; backdrop `opacity 0 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.slow` / `duration.fast` | yes |
| drag | `transform` follows `--drawer-swipe-movement-*`; backdrop opacity is `1 - --drawer-swipe-progress` | Base UI gesture (no authored recipe) | yes (it is the gesture) |
| exit | sheet back to `--closed-transform` + `opacity → 0`; backdrop `opacity → 0` | `exit.fade` · `duration.slow` / `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | fade only: the closed-state slide is dropped, so the sheet appears and disappears in place | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the sheet is in place on the first frame | – | – |

The drag keeps tracking the finger under `reduced`: that movement is the user's own, not authored motion,
and a sheet that ignored the drag would be worse than one that follows it. The release animation uses the
token duration rather than a velocity-scaled one — the swipe physics decide *where* the sheet settles,
the token decides how long the settle takes.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside a modal drawer. |
| Escape | Closes the drawer and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling while the drawer is modal.
- `DrawerTitle` is required: a drawer without an accessible name is invalid.
- The swipe handle is `aria-hidden="true"` and is never the only way out. A user who cannot drag gets
  the close controls, Escape, and the overlay press (for a modal drawer).
- The content region scrolls on its own (`overflow-y-auto`), so a long list inside the sheet does not
  move the page behind it.

## Responsive behavior

The default sheet sits at the bottom, spans the width, and caps its height at `calc(100dvh - 3rem)` so a
strip of the page stays visible. `swipeDirection="left"` / `"right"` becomes a side panel at `w-3/4`,
capped at `max-w-sm` from `sm` up. Snap points change the resting height without changing any of that
geometry.

## Performance

- The drag writes CSS variables and a `transform`; it never touches layout or React state per frame.
- The backdrop opacity is a `calc()` on the same variable, so the page behind dims as the sheet moves
  without a second animation.
- Entry and exit animate `transform` and `opacity` only. Nothing is measured during render.

## Notes for AI

- Use `drawer` for a short touch-first task from the bottom edge; use `sheet` for a side panel that
  holds a form, and `alert-dialog` when the answer must be deliberate.
- Always render `DrawerTitle`. `DrawerDescription` is the second line of the announcement.
- Never make the swipe the only dismissal: keep a `DrawerClose`, and let Escape work.
- For a list of actions, each row is a `DrawerClose` so choosing one closes the sheet.

# Select

Choosing one value from a short list of options.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/select
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |

| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: select](https://cadence.dev/r/select.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine files in the target list, including every shared `lib/` file.
Keep the mirrored `cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives
intact. The provider files and `motion` are required imports even though the
popup itself uses CSS transitions; wrapping your application in
`CadenceProvider` is optional.

Complete the base theme setup linked above, including Cadence's easing tokens,
and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. These payloads contain no additional
Select-specific CSS or assets. Full mode animates the measured value-slot width,
the pointer label handoff, the check and the popup. Reduced makes width changes
instant, skips the handoff and removes scale while retaining opacity; none
removes authored transitions from the first frame. Standalone Select follows
the system motion preference; a nested full scope still respects system
reduced motion.

Usage, Sizes, Groups and labels, Disabled and invalid, Multiple values, Panel
placement and the top specimen need only this dependency graph. Controlled
value and Form submission additionally use [Button](/components/button):

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

For manual installation, follow Button's Manual tab too. Add
`button/index.tsx`, reuse the shared files listed here, and install its one
extra npm dependency:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

In Next.js App Router, Controlled value and Form submission need a client
module for their state and event handlers. Keep the original Usage composition
in a client module too: its automatic child-label lookup requires the client
`SelectItem` identity. For a Server Component composition of Usage, supply an
explicit `items` value-to-label map; without it, the trigger displays raw values
such as `next` and `remix`. The other shown examples already supply `items` and
can be composed in synchronous Server Components with their serializable JSX
and props; synchronous `useId` alone does not require a caller client boundary.
Existing client directives may be kept. A ref, event handler, function-valued
`SelectValue` children, `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)` does need
that boundary. Preserve the installed sources' client directives. The site's
preview shell is not consumer setup; hydrated interactions require JavaScript.

`SelectContent` already includes its portal, positioner, popup, list and scroll
arrows. The default `alignItemWithTrigger={true}` overlays the selected item
on the trigger when space and the input method permit it; touch uses anchored
placement. Set it to false when requesting `side`, `align` or their offsets,
as Panel placement does. Base UI handles collision fallback, list scrolling,
keyboard navigation, focus return and dismissal. Name every trigger with a
visible associated label or `aria-label`.

The caller owns the option data and labels, controlled `value`/`onValueChange`
and `open`/`onOpenChange` when supplied, validation, error text, submission and
remote loading. `defaultValue` initializes an uncontrolled selection; use an
array with `multiple`. `items` maps values to display labels, as in the top
specimen and body examples. Without it, Cadence derives labels from directly
composed `SelectItem` children, including nested groups; it cannot inspect
items hidden inside a custom component wrapper. Supply `items` for those
wrappers, and provide explicit labels in `items` for object values. Object
values may also need Base UI's `itemToStringLabel`,
`itemToStringValue` and `isItemEqualToValue`; keep object identity stable or
provide a comparator. Function props require a client caller.

`name` enables native form submission through Base UI's visually hidden input;
multiple values produce repeated entries under that name. `required` uses
browser constraint validation, `disabled` prevents interaction and omits the
value from FormData, and `readOnly` prevents choosing a different value.
Pass `aria-invalid` and associated error text to the trigger for caller-owned
invalid state. The Form submission example reads FormData into local state;
it does not persist or send data. No validation or form-state package is needed.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "@/components/cadence/select";

export function FrameworkSelect() {
  return (
    <Select defaultValue="next">
      <SelectTrigger className="w-48" aria-label="Framework">
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectItem value="next">Next.js</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="remix">Remix</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="astro">Astro</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

The default trigger is for forms; `size="sm"` fits dense rows. The empty control uses a placeholder without adding an empty option. Each select owns its value.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

function FrameworkSelect({ size = "default", empty = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; empty?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue={empty ? undefined : "next"}>
      <SelectTrigger size={size} aria-label={empty ? "Framework, empty" : size === "sm" ? "Framework, small" : "Framework"}>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}

export function Sizes() {
  return <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3"><FrameworkSelect /><FrameworkSelect size="sm" /><FrameworkSelect empty /></div>;
}
```

## Controlled value

The caller owns `value` and `onValueChange`. The external action chooses Astro in this example only; selections in other cards stay independent.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

function FrameworkSelect({ size = "default", empty = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; empty?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue={empty ? undefined : "next"}>
      <SelectTrigger size={size} aria-label={empty ? "Framework, empty" : size === "sm" ? "Framework, small" : "Framework"}>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}

export function Controlled() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>("next");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col items-center gap-5">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        <Select items={frameworks} value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
          <SelectTrigger aria-label="Controlled framework"><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
          <SelectContent>{frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}</SelectContent>
        </Select>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setValue("astro")}>Choose Astro externally</Button>
      </div>
      <output className="text-sm" aria-live="polite">Value: {value}</output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Form submission

`name` supplies the hidden input for FormData. `required` delegates empty-value checks to the browser; select a framework, then submit to read the caller-owned result.

<ComponentExample name="form-submission" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

function FrameworkSelect({ size = "default", empty = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; empty?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue={empty ? undefined : "next"}>
      <SelectTrigger size={size} aria-label={empty ? "Framework, empty" : size === "sm" ? "Framework, small" : "Framework"}>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}

export function FormSubmission() {
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState<string>();
  return (
    <form className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3" onSubmit={(event) => {
      event.preventDefault();
      setSubmitted(String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("framework")));
    }}>
      <Select items={frameworks} name="framework" required>
        <SelectTrigger aria-label="Framework to submit"><SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" /></SelectTrigger>
        <SelectContent>{frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}</SelectContent>
      </Select>
      <Button type="submit">Submit framework</Button>
      <output className="w-full text-sm" aria-live="polite">{submitted ? `Submitted: ${submitted}` : "No submission yet"}</output>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Disabled and invalid

Disabled prevents selection. Invalid is a supplied visual and accessible state, with an independently identified error; the caller decides when to clear it.

<ComponentExample name="disabled-invalid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

function FrameworkSelect({ size = "default", empty = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; empty?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue={empty ? undefined : "next"}>
      <SelectTrigger size={size} aria-label={empty ? "Framework, empty" : size === "sm" ? "Framework, small" : "Framework"}>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}

export function DisabledInvalid() {
  const errorId = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col items-center gap-5">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        <Select items={frameworks} disabled defaultValue="next">
          <SelectTrigger aria-label="Framework, disabled"><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
          <SelectContent><SelectItem value="next">Next.js</SelectItem></SelectContent>
        </Select>
        <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue="astro">
          <SelectTrigger aria-label="Framework, invalid" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby={errorId}><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
          <SelectContent>{frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}</SelectContent>
        </Select>
      </div>
      <p id={errorId} className="text-sm text-destructive">This framework is unavailable for your project.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Multiple values

`multiple` keeps an array of values and leaves the list open while options are toggled. The trigger lists the selected labels; Escape closes the list and restores focus. Use Combobox for a searchable multi-select or chips.

<ComponentExample name="multiple" />

```tsx
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

export function Multiple() {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} multiple defaultValue={["next", "astro"]}>
      <SelectTrigger aria-label="Multiple frameworks">
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose frameworks" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => (
          <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>
            {label}
          </SelectItem>
        ))}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}
```

## Panel placement

The first row fixes the four sides; the second fixes start, center and end alignment. These examples disable `alignItemWithTrigger` so the popup uses the requested anchored placement instead of overlaying the selected item. Viewport collision handling may flip the effective side. Each trigger keeps its own value and associated label.

<ComponentExample name="placement" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

export function Placement() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col items-center gap-5">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        {(["top", "right", "bottom", "left"] as const).map((side) => (
          <div key={side} className="grid gap-2">
            <label htmlFor={`${id}-${side}`} className="text-xs capitalize">
              {side} panel
            </label>
            <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue="next">
              <SelectTrigger id={`${id}-${side}`} aria-label={`Framework, ${side} panel`}>
                <SelectValue />
              </SelectTrigger>
              <SelectContent side={side} alignItemWithTrigger={false}>
                {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => (
                  <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>
                    {label}
                  </SelectItem>
                ))}
              </SelectContent>
            </Select>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        {(["start", "center", "end"] as const).map((align) => (
          <div key={align} className="grid gap-2">
            <label htmlFor={`${id}-${align}`} className="text-xs capitalize">
              {align} alignment
            </label>
            <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue="next">
              <SelectTrigger id={`${id}-${align}`} aria-label={`Framework, ${align} alignment`}>
                <SelectValue />
              </SelectTrigger>
              <SelectContent align={align} alignItemWithTrigger={false}>
                {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => (
                  <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>
                    {label}
                  </SelectItem>
                ))}
              </SelectContent>
            </Select>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Choosing one value from a list that is too long for radios but too short to need search.
- A compact form control where the current value should stay visible in the trigger.
- A setting that changes the surface around it, so the value and its width should move together.

## When not to use

- Free-text or type-to-filter input. Use `combobox` once it ships, or an `input` with a datalist.
- Two or three mutually exclusive options that should stay visible. Use `radio-group`.
- Navigation between routes. Use a menu or links; a select submits a value, it does not navigate.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Select` | `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `disabled`, `required`, `name`, `multiple`, `items` | Base UI root; `items` lets `SelectValue` render labels from data. |
| `SelectTrigger` | `size` (`"sm" \| "default"`), native button props | Contains `SelectValue`; the chevron is rendered for you. |
| `SelectValue` | `placeholder` | The selected label, or the placeholder when empty. |
| `SelectContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `alignItemWithTrigger` | Portals, positions, and sizes to `--anchor-width`. |
| `SelectItem` | `value`, `disabled` | Renders the label and the check indicator. |
| `SelectGroup` / `SelectLabel` | group props | Purely structural. |
| `SelectSeparator` | separator props | A single hairline. |
| `SelectScrollUpButton` / `SelectScrollDownButton` | scroll-arrow props | Appear only when the list overflows. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pointer selection | value slot width | `geometry.resize` | yes (physics-defined, clamped) |
| pointer selection | label `x`/`y` from the item to the trigger | `handoff` | yes |
| pointer selection | check `scale` / `opacity` | `state.morph` | yes |
| open / close | popup `opacity` / `scale` | `popup.anchored` | yes |
| reduced | width jumps, no flight, no scale; opacity stays | – | – |
| none | every duration is zero | – | – |

The trigger's label is laid out at its final width inside a clipped slot. Animating that slot's width
folds the surface without re-wrapping the label. The portalled label follows the live destination
as the trigger resizes, including shifts in centered or right-aligned rows, so the flight and real
label meet at the same position. Keyboard selection has no origin, so it changes the width and lets the label swap
without a flight; the pointer keeps the spatial handoff.
The portalled flight label uses its natural text width, so a longer selection stays fully visible
even if Base UI has not yet committed the destination label when its position is measured.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The site header changes the inherited motion mode on the same component tree, including each named example. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive. A cancelled selection
does not fly the pointer label over the current value. Natural text width is observed
separately from the animated outer slot, including content and viewport changes.

## Keyboard interactions

- `Enter` / `Space` / `ArrowDown` opens the list and focuses the selected item.
- `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` moves the highlight; `Home` / `End` jump to the ends.
- Typeahead letters move the highlight to the next matching label.
- `Enter` selects; `Escape` closes without changing the value.
- `Tab` closes the list and moves focus to the next control.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders the trigger as a combobox and the list as a listbox, wired with
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; keyboard navigation moves focus to the options.
- Name the control with `aria-label` or a visible external label associated with the trigger; the value alone is not a name.
- The selected item keeps `aria-selected="true"`; the check is a visual duplicate, not the only signal.
- Under reduced motion the value still changes and the check still appears; nothing is conveyed by
  the flight alone.
- The handoff clone is `aria-hidden`: screen readers hear the value once, from the trigger.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller owns selection values, validation, error text, submission and any remote
loading/filtering. Render supplied aria-invalid/data-invalid and associate described
errors; this component does not validate or install a form-state library.

## Responsive behavior

The popup is at least `--anchor-width` wide and caps at `--available-height`, so it flips and scrolls
inside the viewport. `alignItemWithTrigger` keeps the selected item over the trigger when space permits;
touch opening disables this alignment and uses anchored placement. The width animation is short and only touches the
trigger, so a select in a toolbar does not reflow the page beyond its own row.

## Performance

- One measured width animation and, on pointer selection, one absolutely positioned label for the
  duration of the handoff. No blur and no shadow animation.
- Width is a layout property; it is allowed only on this T3 component and only through
  `geometry.resize`, which jumps under reduced and none.
- The list renders every supplied item without virtualisation; the component adds no per-item animation beyond the check
  indicator.
- Budget: T3 (12 KB gzip). If a page animates several selects at once, only the open one moves.

## Notes for AI

- Prefer `SelectValue placeholder="…"` over an empty first item; an empty item is a selectable value.
- Keep item labels short and distinct; typeahead matches their text.
- Do not add a separate "selected" class to the trigger; the value already carries the state.
- For invalid state, pass `aria-invalid`; the trigger styles it from the attribute.

# Combobox

Picking from a long list you can filter by typing.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/combobox
```

Combobox examples that use external actions also require `@cadence/button`.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — transitive registry dependency.
- [@cadence/input](https://cadence.dev/r/input.json) — transitive registry dependency.
- [@cadence/textarea](https://cadence.dev/r/textarea.json) — transitive registry dependency.
- [@cadence/input-group](https://cadence.dev/r/input-group.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.
