4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all thirteen target files, including every shared `lib/` file and the
Button, Input, Textarea and Input Group sources. Keep the mirrored `cadence/`
tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives intact. Input Group imports
all three controls even when this composition only renders its input and button.
The provider files and `motion` are required imports; wrapping your application
in `CadenceProvider` is optional.

Complete the base theme setup linked above, including Cadence's easing tokens,
and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. These payloads contain no additional
Combobox-specific CSS or assets. Full mode scales and fades the popup and animates
the selection tick. Reduced keeps opacity and removes scale; none disables those
transitions from the first frame. Filtering and list placement update immediately
in every mode. Standalone components respect the system motion preference, as
does a nested full provider.

Usage, the top specimen and every body example use only this dependency graph.
Button for Controlled values and submission is already included transitively
through Input Group; no extra file or npm package is needed. Logical sides also
uses `DirectionProvider` from the already required `@base-ui/react`; pair its
direction with the DOM `dir` attribute, as shown.

In Next.js App Router, keep all fifteen shown Usage/example compositions in
client modules. Each passes a function to `ComboboxList`; Groups and separators
also uses a `ComboboxCollection` callback. Multiple values uses
`useComboboxAnchor` and function-valued `ComboboxValue` children. Controlled
values and submission, Object values and Caller-owned results additionally own
state, handlers or effects. Synchronous `useId` alone does not require a client
caller, but the list callbacks in Disabled, read-only and invalid do. Function
props such as `filter`, label/value converters, equality comparators, `render`,
`className(state)` and `style(state)`, and refs or event handlers also need that
boundary. A Server Component can render one of these client compositions with
serializable data props. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup;
hydrated filtering, selection and dismissal require JavaScript.

`ComboboxInput` includes the input-group frame, native input, optional trigger
and optional clear control. Name the input with a visible associated label or
`aria-label`; name a separate trigger too. `ComboboxContent` includes the portal,
positioner and popup; compose `ComboboxEmpty` and `ComboboxList` inside it.
The default placement is bottom/start with a side offset of 6. Base UI handles
collision fallback, highlighting, keyboard navigation and dismissal. The list
scrolls within the available popup height. On narrow screens, prefer top/bottom
placement: the default minimum popup width can override the available width in
inline-side layouts. If using inline sides, explicitly reduce the content's
minimum width and verify the result. In a multiple-value composition, use
an array selection, render chips with `ComboboxValue`, attach
`useComboboxAnchor` to `ComboboxChips`, and pass the same ref to the content.
Hiding chip remove buttons does not prevent Backspace removal; use root
`readOnly` when changes must be forbidden.

The caller owns the catalogue, selected `value`, input query and `open` state
when controlled, labels, validation, error text, submission and remote results.
Pass `items` for the render-function lists shown here; `defaultValue` initializes
an uncontrolled selection. Object values use `itemToStringLabel`,
`itemToStringValue` and a stable identity or `isItemEqualToValue` comparator.
For externally filtered results, pass `filter={null}` and keep cancellation,
loading/error feedback and result ordering in the caller. `ComboboxEmpty`
represents no matches, not a pending request.

`name` supplies the selected value to native FormData; multiple selections
produce repeated entries. Typing a query alone does not commit a selection.
`required` enables native constraint validation, `disabled` prevents editing and
omits the value from FormData, and `readOnly` preserves the selection while still
allowing the popup to be browsed. Supply `aria-invalid` on the input and associate
caller-owned error text. Controlled values and submission uses `noValidate` and
only records the submission in local state. No validation or form-state package
is needed.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

const frameworks = ["Next.js", "SvelteKit", "Nuxt.js", "Remix", "Astro"];
export function FrameworkPicker() {
  return (
    <Combobox items={frameworks}>
      <ComboboxInput aria-label="Framework" placeholder="Select a framework" />
      <ComboboxContent>
        <ComboboxEmpty>No framework found.</ComboboxEmpty>
        <ComboboxList>
          {(item: string) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
              {item}
            </ComboboxItem>
          )}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
```

`items` is the catalogue. Typing filters it; selection commits a catalogue value.

## Groups and separators

Pass each group its own items so filtering can remove empty groups. Collection renders the filtered children; the separator belongs between the two catalogues, not between every row.

<ComponentExample name="groups" />

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxCollection,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxGroup,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxLabel,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxSeparator,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

export function GroupedPicker() {
  const groups = [
    { value: "Frontend", items: ["React", "Vue", "Svelte"] },
    { value: "Backend", items: ["Go", "Rust", "Elixir"] },
  ];
  return (
    <Combobox items={groups}>
      <ComboboxInput className="w-56 max-w-full" aria-label="Stack" placeholder="Choose a stack" />
      <ComboboxContent>
        <ComboboxEmpty>No stack found.</ComboboxEmpty>
        <ComboboxList>
          {(group: (typeof groups)[number], index: number) => (
            <React.Fragment key={group.value}>
              {index > 0 && <ComboboxSeparator />}
              <ComboboxGroup items={group.items}>
                <ComboboxLabel>{group.value}</ComboboxLabel>
                <ComboboxCollection>
                  {(item: string) => (
                    <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
                      {item}
                    </ComboboxItem>
                  )}
                </ComboboxCollection>
              </ComboboxGroup>
            </React.Fragment>
          )}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
```

## Clear and trigger controls

The four fixed fields compare both flags independently. Clear removes a selected value; its presence hides the built-in chevron. Hiding the trigger does not disable keyboard opening or turn Enter into form submission.

<ComponentExample name="controls" />

```tsx
"use client";

import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

const frameworks = ["Next.js", "SvelteKit", "Nuxt.js", "Remix", "Astro"];
function Options() {
  return (
    <>
      <ComboboxEmpty>No framework found.</ComboboxEmpty>
      <ComboboxList>
        {(item: string) => (
          <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
            {item}
          </ComboboxItem>
        )}
      </ComboboxList>
    </>
  );
}
function _Picker({
  label,
  side = "bottom",
  align = "start",
}: {
  label: string;
  side?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" | "inline-start" | "inline-end";
  align?: "start" | "center" | "end";
}) {
  return (
    <Combobox items={frameworks}>
      <ComboboxInput className="w-56 max-w-full" aria-label={label} placeholder={label} />
      <ComboboxContent side={side} align={align}>
        <Options />
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}

export function PickerControls() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
      {[
        { label: "Trigger only", showTrigger: true, showClear: false },
        { label: "Clear and trigger", showTrigger: true, showClear: true },
        { label: "Clear only", showTrigger: false, showClear: true },
        { label: "Input only", showTrigger: false, showClear: false },
      ].map((props) => (
        <Combobox key={props.label} items={frameworks} defaultValue="Astro">
          <ComboboxInput
            className="w-48 max-w-full"
            aria-label={props.label}
            showTrigger={props.showTrigger}
            showClear={props.showClear}
          />
          <ComboboxContent>
            <Options />
          </ComboboxContent>
        </Combobox>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Multiple values

Each editor owns its selection and anchor. The first allows chip removal; the second hides remove buttons with showRemove=false. This is an affordance choice: Backspace can still remove a value. Use readOnly on the root when editing must be forbidden.

<ComponentExample name="multiple" />

```tsx
"use client";
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxChip,
  ComboboxChips,
  ComboboxChipsInput,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxValue,
  useComboboxAnchor,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

function TopicEditor({ removable }: { removable: boolean }) {
  const anchor = useComboboxAnchor();
  const topics = ["Design", "Docs", "Testing", "Release"];
  return (
    <Combobox multiple items={topics} defaultValue={["Design", "Docs"]}>
      <ComboboxChips ref={anchor} className="w-64 max-w-full">
        <ComboboxValue>
          {(value: string[]) => (
            <>
              {value.map((topic) => (
                <ComboboxChip key={topic} showRemove={removable}>
                  {topic}
                </ComboboxChip>
              ))}
              <ComboboxChipsInput
                aria-label={removable ? "Editable topics" : "Topics without remove buttons"}
                placeholder="Add topic"
              />
            </>
          )}
        </ComboboxValue>
      </ComboboxChips>
      <ComboboxContent anchor={anchor}>
        <ComboboxEmpty>No topic found.</ComboboxEmpty>
        <ComboboxList>
          {(item: string) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
              {item}
            </ComboboxItem>
          )}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
export function TopicPickers() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
      <TopicEditor removable />
      <TopicEditor removable={false} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled, read-only and invalid

Disabled fields cannot be edited or opened. Read-only keeps a selected value available for focus and submission; the popup can still be opened and browsed, but choosing another row does not change that value. The caller supplies the invalid attribute and associated error; an unavailable item stays visible but cannot be selected.

<ComponentExample name="states" />

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

const frameworks = ["Next.js", "SvelteKit", "Nuxt.js", "Remix", "Astro"];
function Options() {
  return (
    <>
      <ComboboxEmpty>No framework found.</ComboboxEmpty>
      <ComboboxList>
        {(item: string) => (
          <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
            {item}
          </ComboboxItem>
        )}
      </ComboboxList>
    </>
  );
}
function _Picker({
  label,
  side = "bottom",
  align = "start",
}: {
  label: string;
  side?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" | "inline-start" | "inline-end";
  align?: "start" | "center" | "end";
}) {
  return (
    <Combobox items={frameworks}>
      <ComboboxInput className="w-56 max-w-full" aria-label={label} placeholder={label} />
      <ComboboxContent side={side} align={align}>
        <Options />
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}

export function PickerStates() {
  const error = React.useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
      <Combobox items={frameworks} disabled defaultValue="Remix">
        <ComboboxInput className="w-48 max-w-full" disabled aria-label="Disabled framework" />
        <ComboboxContent>
          <Options />
        </ComboboxContent>
      </Combobox>
      <Combobox items={frameworks} readOnly defaultValue="Astro">
        <ComboboxInput className="w-48 max-w-full" aria-label="Read-only framework" />
        <ComboboxContent>
          <Options />
        </ComboboxContent>
      </Combobox>
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Combobox items={frameworks}>
          <ComboboxInput
            className="w-56 max-w-full"
            aria-label="Required framework"
            aria-invalid="true"
            aria-describedby={error}
            placeholder="Choose an available framework"
          />
          <ComboboxContent>
            <ComboboxEmpty>No framework found.</ComboboxEmpty>
            <ComboboxList>
              {(item: string) => (
                <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item} disabled={item === "Nuxt.js"}>
                  {item}
                </ComboboxItem>
              )}
            </ComboboxList>
          </ComboboxContent>
        </Combobox>
        <p id={error} className="text-sm text-destructive">
          Choose an available framework.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled values and submission

The caller owns the selected value, input query, open state and submitted result. Use the external action to set Astro, then edit independently. The native FormData entry comes from name; typing a query alone does not commit it as a selection. This example uses noValidate so validation remains with the caller.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

const frameworks = ["Next.js", "SvelteKit", "Nuxt.js", "Remix", "Astro"];
function Options() {
  return (
    <>
      <ComboboxEmpty>No framework found.</ComboboxEmpty>
      <ComboboxList>
        {(item: string) => (
          <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
            {item}
          </ComboboxItem>
        )}
      </ComboboxList>
    </>
  );
}
function _Picker({
  label,
  side = "bottom",
  align = "start",
}: {
  label: string;
  side?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" | "inline-start" | "inline-end";
  align?: "start" | "center" | "end";
}) {
  return (
    <Combobox items={frameworks}>
      <ComboboxInput className="w-56 max-w-full" aria-label={label} placeholder={label} />
      <ComboboxContent side={side} align={align}>
        <Options />
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}

export function ControlledPicker() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState<string | null>("Remix");
  const [query, setQuery] = React.useState("Remix");
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = React.useState("Not submitted");
  return (
    <form
      noValidate
      className="grid justify-items-start gap-3"
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        setSubmitted(String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("framework") ?? ""));
      }}
    >
      <Combobox
        items={frameworks}
        name="framework"
        value={value}
        onValueChange={setValue}
        inputValue={query}
        onInputValueChange={setQuery}
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
      >
        <ComboboxInput className="w-56 max-w-full" aria-label="Controlled framework" showClear />
        <ComboboxContent>
          <Options />
        </ComboboxContent>
      </Combobox>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button
          type="button"
          variant="outline"
          onClick={() => {
            setValue("Astro");
            setQuery("Astro");
          }}
        >
          Set Astro externally
        </Button>
        <Button type="submit">Submit selection</Button>
      </div>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Selected: {value ?? "none"}; submitted: {submitted}
      </p>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Object values

Convert object labels and submitted values explicitly. Compare stable ids when an application recreates option objects; object identity need not be the selection identity.

<ComponentExample name="objects" />

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

export function ObjectPicker() {
  const people = [
    { id: "ada", name: "Ada Lovelace" },
    { id: "grace", name: "Grace Hopper" },
    { id: "margaret", name: "Margaret Hamilton" },
  ];
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState<(typeof people)[number] | null>({ id: "ada", name: "Ada Lovelace" });
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <Combobox
        items={people}
        value={value}
        onValueChange={setValue}
        itemToStringLabel={(person) => person.name}
        itemToStringValue={(person) => person.id}
        isItemEqualToValue={(a, b) => a.id === b.id}
      >
        <ComboboxInput className="w-64 max-w-full" aria-label="Assignee" showClear />
        <ComboboxContent>
          <ComboboxEmpty>No person found.</ComboboxEmpty>
          <ComboboxList>
            {(person: (typeof people)[number]) => (
              <ComboboxItem key={person.id} value={person}>
                {person.name}
              </ComboboxItem>
            )}
          </ComboboxList>
        </ComboboxContent>
      </Combobox>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Assignee id: {value?.id ?? "none"}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Caller-owned results

The caller filters this local catalogue asynchronously and passes filter=null to avoid a second client filter. The microtask stands in for an application search function, not a network request. Replace it with your own service; keep cancellation, pending/error feedback and result ordering in the caller. Cleanup rejects stale completions; an empty result and a pending request are different states.

<ComponentExample name="results" />

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

export function ResultPicker() {
  const [query, setQuery] = React.useState("");
  const [results, setResults] = React.useState<string[]>(["London", "Paris", "Tokyo"]);
  const [pending, setPending] = React.useState(false);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    let active = true;
    setPending(true);
    Promise.resolve(
      ["London", "Paris", "Tokyo"].filter((city) => city.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())),
    ).then((next) => {
      if (active) {
        setResults(next);
        setPending(false);
      }
    });
    return () => {
      active = false;
    };
  }, [query]);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Combobox items={results} filter={null} onInputValueChange={setQuery}>
        <ComboboxInput className="w-56 max-w-full" aria-label="City" placeholder="Search a city" />
        <ComboboxContent>
          {pending ? (
            <p role="status" className="p-2 text-sm">
              Searching cities…
            </p>
          ) : (
            <ComboboxEmpty>No city found.</ComboboxEmpty>
          )}
          <ComboboxList>
            {(city: string) => (
              <ComboboxItem key={city} value={city}>
                {city}
              </ComboboxItem>
            )}
          </ComboboxList>
        </ComboboxContent>
      </Combobox>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {pending ? "Searching" : `${results.length} cities returned`}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Highlight and loop boundaries

## Without motion

## When to use

- Choosing one value from a list too long to scan: countries, assignees, repositories.
- A search field that filters a catalogue while keeping typed queries separate from committed values.
- Several values from the same catalogue, where each choice should stay visible as a chip.
- A picker whose options arrive from a search endpoint rather than from a constant.

## When not to use

- Fewer than about eight fixed options. Use `select`; a popup that has to be opened to show three items is
  slower than three radios.
- Commands rather than values — navigation, actions, "go to file". Use `command`.
- Free text with no catalogue behind it. Use `input`.
- A control that must not accept typing, such as a language picker in a settings form. Use `select`.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Combobox` | `items`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `multiple`, `disabled`, `name`, `required`, `onInputValueChange`, `itemToStringLabel` | Base UI root. `items` drives what the popup filters and what the render callbacks receive. |
| `ComboboxInput` | `showTrigger` (`true`), `showClear` (`false`), `disabled`, native input props | The field: a bare input inside an input-group frame, with the chevron and the optional clear button. |
| `ComboboxTrigger` | native button props | The chevron on its own, for a field built by hand. |
| `ComboboxValue` | render callback or children | The selected label; in the chips layout it renders the chips. |
| `ComboboxContent` | `side` (`"bottom"`), `sideOffset` (`6`), `align` (`"start"`), `alignOffset` (`0`), `anchor` | Portals, positions, and sizes to `--anchor-width`. |
| `ComboboxList` | children or render function `(item, index) => ReactNode` | Scrolls, and takes the height the popup has left. |
| `ComboboxItem` | `value`, `disabled` | Renders the label and the tick. |
| `ComboboxGroup` / `ComboboxLabel` | `items` on the group | Structural; the group's `items` let filtering drop it whole. |
| `ComboboxEmpty` | children | Shown when the filter matches nothing. |
| `ComboboxSeparator` | separator props | A hairline between unrelated groups. |
| `ComboboxChips` / `ComboboxChip` / `ComboboxChipsInput` | `showRemove` (`true`) on the chip | The multi-value layout. |
| `ComboboxCollection` | collection props | Escape hatch for virtualised lists. |
| `useComboboxAnchor` | – | A ref to anchor the popup to the chips frame. |

`ComboboxClear` is internal on purpose: it belongs to `ComboboxInput`'s layout, and a component that owns
an undo affordance should not also hand out half of one.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | popup `opacity` 0→1, `scale` `--motion-scale-in`→1 | `popup.anchored` | yes: a CSS transition, so reopening reverses it |
| close | popup `opacity` 1→0, `scale` 1→`--motion-scale-in` | `exit.fade` | yes |
| select | tick `scale` `0.96`→1, `opacity` 0→1 | `state.morph` | yes: a spring, retargeted from the current value |
| filter | none — rows are replaced, not moved | – | – |
| reduced | popup and tick fade without scaling; tick stays at full size | – | – |
| none | every duration is zero | – | – |

The scale grows out of `--transform-origin`, which Base UI writes from the positioner, so the panel opens
from the field rather than from its own centre. The list itself never animates: a filter runs on every
keystroke, and a row that is still travelling when the next character arrives is a list the reader has to
chase.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. Ordinary examples inherit the site header on the same component tree; the named Without motion example demonstrates explicit local overrides. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive. Base UI 1.9's typeable focus manager hides background
nodes from assistive technology while leaving their tab stops enabled. Cadence adds native
temporary negative tab indices only to newly hidden focus stops, preserving outside pointer activation; Tab releases them before normal focus navigation and
Base UI's blur dismissal. Existing hidden/inert nodes and parent dialogs keep their owners; cleanup preserves caller tabindex changes. `ComboboxInput` string classes style the field frame;
state callback classes style the native input with its real Base UI input state.

## Keyboard interactions

- `ArrowDown` or `Alt+ArrowDown` opens the popup; with it open, `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the highlight.
- Typing filters the list. `autoHighlight` (default `false`) optionally highlights the first match.
- `Enter` selects the highlighted item and closes the popup.
- With the popup open, `Escape` dismisses it. With it already closed, `Escape` clears the query and selected values.
- `Tab` closes the popup and moves focus to the next control.
- `Backspace` in the chips layout deletes the last chip when the input is empty.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders the input as a `combobox` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and
  `aria-activedescendant`, and the list as a `listbox` whose rows are `option`s.
- Name the field: `aria-label` on `ComboboxInput`, or a `Field`/`Label` pair around it. The placeholder is
  not a name.
- The selected row keeps `aria-selected="true"`; the tick is a visual duplicate, never the only signal.
- The empty state is a sibling of the list inside the popup; it is readable feedback, not a selectable option.
- Under reduced motion nothing is conveyed by the panel's scale: the list is there, the tick is at full
  size, and `aria-selected` carries the state.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller owns selection values, validation, error text, submission and any remote
loading/filtering. Render supplied aria-invalid/data-invalid and associate described
errors; this component does not validate or install a form-state library.

## Responsive behavior

The single-value popup anchors to the native input, not the input-group frame, and has a minimum width
`--spacing(7)` larger than that input. Its maximum width follows available space, but the minimum can
override it in narrow inline-side placements and let the popup extend outside the viewport. Prefer
top/bottom placement there, or explicitly reduce the content's minimum width and check the result. It flips above the field near the viewport edge, and the list — not the
popup — scrolls inside `--available-height`. In the chips layout the frame wraps to a second line instead
of scrolling horizontally, and the popup widens to the chips container.

## Performance

- One CSS transition on `opacity` and `scale` per open and per close; no JS animation loop, and no layout
  read.
- Each mounted row keeps its indicator and uses the token spring for selection changes. Filtering replaces
  rendered rows immediately instead of animating the list layout.
- The filter is synchronous over whatever `items` holds; a remote list is a debounce in the caller, not a
  behaviour of this component.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip).

## Notes for AI

- Always pass `items` to `Combobox`; it drives filtering and is what the `ComboboxList` render callback
  receives. Without it the list renders nothing.
- Use `value`/`onValueChange` for a controlled picker, `defaultValue` otherwise — same contract as `select`.
- `multiple` requires the chips layout; do not pair `multiple` with a plain `ComboboxInput`.
- Do not add a "loading" prop: async feedback is the caller's state, and `ComboboxEmpty` is for an empty
  result, not for a pending one.
- For invalid state pass `aria-invalid` on `ComboboxInput`; the frame styles the border and the ring from
  the attribute.

# Dropdown Menu

Row actions, filters, and view settings behind one button.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/dropdown-menu
```

The examples compose `@cadence/button`; install that item alongside the menu when copying them.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, including every shared `lib/` file. Keep the mirrored
`cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives intact. The provider
files and `motion` are required imports; wrapping your application in
`CadenceProvider` is optional. Complete the base theme setup linked above,
including Cadence's easing tokens, and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files.
These payloads contain no additional menu-specific CSS or assets.

Usage, the top specimen and every body example also compose Button. Follow
[Button's manual installation](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation)
and copy its full [payload source](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json), adding
`@components/cadence/button/index.tsx` alongside the shared files already listed.
Its only additional npm dependency is:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

Logical placement uses `DirectionProvider` from the already required
`@base-ui/react`; pair its direction with the DOM `dir` attribute, as shown.

In Next.js App Router, keep Usage, Items, shortcuts, and destructive actions,
Checkbox and radio items, Submenus, Grouping and Controlled open in client
modules: they own state and handlers. Disabled controls, Placement, Alignment,
Logical placement, Non-modal menu and Explicit motion scopes are static
compositions and can be rendered by a Server Component using serializable props,
including the JSX element passed to `render`. Adding event handlers, refs or
function-valued `render`, `className` or `style` props requires a client caller.
Synchronous `useId` alone does not require one. The site's preview shell is not
consumer setup; hydrated opening, navigation, selection and dismissal require
JavaScript.

Compose a root, trigger and content. Pass Button through the trigger's `render`
prop so the primitive's accessible name, expanded state and events reach the
actual button. Content already includes its portal, positioner and popup; do
not add a second portal around it. Its defaults are bottom/start with a 4px
side offset and zero alignment offset. Submenus use Sub, SubTrigger and
SubContent; their defaults are right/start, zero side offset and -3px alignment
offset. Base UI owns collision handling, item focus, typeahead, submenu
navigation and dismissal. Cap caller-defined widths for narrow viewports and
verify the actual open panel bounds. In Placement, the fixed `w-52` can overflow
a narrow side placement; add `max-w-(--available-width)` and check the minimum
width too.

The caller owns commands and their effects, permissions, controlled `open`,
checkbox `checked` and radio-group `value`, persistence and error feedback.
Use `defaultOpen`, `defaultChecked` and `defaultValue` for uncontrolled initial
state. For external opening, Controlled open pairs a unique root `triggerId`
with the trigger's `id` to preserve the anchor. Put actions on `onClick`;
ordinary items close by default, `closeOnClick={false}` keeps them open, and
checkbox/radio items stay open by default. Disabled items expose their state
and remain discoverable with arrow keys but cannot activate. Shortcut text
does not register a key binding. Group labels name a DropdownMenuGroup;
ungrouped labels are captions. This menu supplies no form-state or validation
package, and the examples only update local status text.

Full mode scales and fades the popup and animates the checkbox/radio mark.
Reduced keeps opacity and removes scale; none disables those transitions from
the first mounted frame. A nested provider can restore full inside none,
subject to the system reduced-motion preference. Keep native menu focus and
dismissal behavior when supplying custom render elements or handlers; use
ordinary links or Navigation Menu for a navigation list and Popover for a task
form.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubContent,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function RowActions() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No action yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuContent>
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setResult("Renamed locally")}>Rename</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setResult("Duplicated locally")}>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuSub>
              <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Move to</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
              <DropdownMenuSubContent>
                <DropdownMenuGroup>
                  {["Backlog", "In review", "Done"].map((value) => (
                    <DropdownMenuItem key={value} onClick={() => setResult(`Moved to ${value}`)}>
                      {value}
                    </DropdownMenuItem>
                  ))}
                </DropdownMenuGroup>
              </DropdownMenuSubContent>
            </DropdownMenuSub>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
          <DropdownMenuSeparator />
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => setResult("Deleted locally")}>
              Delete
            </DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {result}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Items, shortcuts, and destructive actions

Default and destructive items are directly visible in one menu. inset aligns text with state indicators. Shortcut text is a visual hint, not a registered binding. closeOnClick=false keeps the local Keep open action available; other commands record a local result and close. No resource is deleted.

<ComponentExample name="items" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuShortcut,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function MenuCommands() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No command yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Commands</DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuContent className="w-56">
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setResult("Edit selected")}>
              Edit<DropdownMenuShortcut>⌘E</DropdownMenuShortcut>
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem inset closeOnClick={false} onClick={() => setResult("Still open")}>
              Keep open
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => setResult("Delete selected locally")}>
              Delete<DropdownMenuShortcut>⌘⌫</DropdownMenuShortcut>
            </DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        {result}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Checkbox and radio items

The caller owns Comments and Density; Description is an independent uncontrolled item. Choosing these keeps the menu open so several settings can change in one visit. Their indicators expose aria-checked and inherit the header mode. The status reads back local values only.

<ComponentExample name="selection" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuRadioGroup,
  DropdownMenuRadioItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function ViewMenu() {
  const [comments, setComments] = useState(false);
  const [density, setDensity] = useState("comfortable");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>View</DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuContent className="w-52">
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuLabel inset>Show</DropdownMenuLabel>
            <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem defaultChecked inset>
              Description
            </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
            <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem checked={comments} onCheckedChange={setComments}>
              Comments
            </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
          <DropdownMenuSeparator />
          <DropdownMenuRadioGroup aria-label="Density" value={density} onValueChange={setDensity}>
            <DropdownMenuLabel>Density</DropdownMenuLabel>
            <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="compact" inset>
              Compact
            </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
            <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="comfortable">Comfortable</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
          </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        Comments: {comments ? "shown" : "hidden"}; density: {density}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Submenus

The submenu has its own portal and shares the surface motion contract. ArrowRight opens it and ArrowLeft returns to the parent trigger; hover also opens it. The parent also offers a direct Keep here command. The inset submenu records a different local destination when an item runs.

<ComponentExample name="submenus" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubContent,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function MoveMenu() {
  const [destination, setDestination] = useState("Not moved");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Move item</DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuContent>
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setDestination("Current group")}>Keep here</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuSub>
              <DropdownMenuSubTrigger inset>Move to</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
              <DropdownMenuSubContent>
                <DropdownMenuGroup>
                  {["Backlog", "Review"].map((value) => (
                    <DropdownMenuItem key={value} onClick={() => setDestination(value)}>
                      {value}
                    </DropdownMenuItem>
                  ))}
                </DropdownMenuGroup>
              </DropdownMenuSubContent>
            </DropdownMenuSub>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        {destination}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Grouping

A label inside DropdownMenuGroup gives that group its accessible name. A label outside a group is only a visible caption, as Density is in the preceding radio example. Use separators between distinct command groups.

<ComponentExample name="grouping" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function GroupedMenu() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No grouped action yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Grouped actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuContent>
          <DropdownMenuLabel>Project commands</DropdownMenuLabel>
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuLabel inset>Pull request</DropdownMenuLabel>
            <DropdownMenuItem inset onClick={() => setResult("Review selected locally")}>
              Review
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem inset onClick={() => setResult("Summary selected locally")}>
              Copy summary
            </DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
          <DropdownMenuSeparator />
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuLabel>History</DropdownMenuLabel>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setResult("Activity selected locally")}>View activity</DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        {result}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled open

The external action opens the same controlled menu. A unique triggerId preserves the actual anchor. The caller owns the open flag and records local actions; native Escape and outside dismissal still work.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function ControlledMenu() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No action");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Open externally
      </Button>
      <DropdownMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} triggerId={id}>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger id={id} render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
          Controlled actions
        </DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuContent>
          <DropdownMenuGroup>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setResult("Copied locally")}>Copy</DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuGroup>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        {result}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled controls

The disabled trigger cannot open a menu. In the second menu, disabled commands, checkbox, radio and submenu triggers stay visible but cannot run. Base UI keeps disabled items keyboard-focusable so their unavailable state can be discovered. The enabled Done item remains available.

## Placement

Each menu prefers a fixed physical side. Collision detection may flip or shift it inside the viewport. The default is bottom with a 4px gap.

<ComponentExample name="sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function MenuSides() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["top", "right", "bottom", "left"] as const).map((value) => (
        <DropdownMenu key={value}>
          <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{value}</DropdownMenuTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuContent side={value} className="w-52">
            <DropdownMenuGroup>
              <DropdownMenuItem>Close menu</DropdownMenuItem>
              <DropdownMenuItem>Done</DropdownMenuItem>
            </DropdownMenuGroup>
          </DropdownMenuContent>
        </DropdownMenu>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Logical placement

Logical placement follows the direction provider: RTL inline-start prefers right and inline-end prefers left. Physical sides remain physical. The width cap follows Base UI's available-width variable so the panel fits the chosen side on a narrow viewport.

<ComponentExample name="logical-sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DirectionProvider } from "@base-ui/react/direction-provider";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function LogicalMenus() {
  return (
    <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">
      <div dir="rtl">
        <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
          {(["inline-start", "inline-end"] as const).map((value) => (
            <DropdownMenu key={value}>
              <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{value}</DropdownMenuTrigger>
              <DropdownMenuContent side={value} className="w-52 max-w-(--available-width)">
                <DropdownMenuGroup>
                  <DropdownMenuItem>Close menu</DropdownMenuItem>
                  <DropdownMenuItem>Done</DropdownMenuItem>
                </DropdownMenuGroup>
              </DropdownMenuContent>
            </DropdownMenu>
          ))}
        </div>
      </div>
    </DirectionProvider>
  );
}
```

## Non-modal menu

Compare modal true and false. Both keep the usual command keyboard path and dismiss on Escape; false permits outside pointer interaction while the menu is open. Use a popover when the panel contains a task form.

<ComponentExample name="modality" />

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

  DropdownMenuTrigger,

  return (

          <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>{String(modal)}</DropdownMenuTrigger>

            <DropdownMenuGroup>
              <DropdownMenuItem>Copy</DropdownMenuItem>
              <DropdownMenuItem>Done</DropdownMenuItem>
            </DropdownMenuGroup>
          </DropdownMenuContent>
        </DropdownMenu>
      ))}
    </div>
  );

## Explicit motion scopes

Ordinary menus inherit the header. Only this example sets none and restores full in a nested provider; the OS reduced preference still wins. Popup and checkbox indicator both use that local clock.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function MenuMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <DropdownMenu>
          <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open without motion</DropdownMenuTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuContent data-testid="initial-none">
            <DropdownMenuGroup>
              <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>Comments</DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
            </DropdownMenuGroup>
          </DropdownMenuContent>
        </DropdownMenu>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <DropdownMenu>
            <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open nested full</DropdownMenuTrigger>
            <DropdownMenuContent data-testid="nested-full">
              <DropdownMenuGroup>
                <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>Comments</DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
              </DropdownMenuGroup>
            </DropdownMenuContent>
          </DropdownMenu>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A row of actions behind one trigger: a table row, a card, a file.
- A filter or view setting where the panel stays open while several options change.
- A command list too long for a toolbar and too short to need search.

## When not to use

- A list of links for ordinary site navigation. Use a `navigation-menu` or plain links;
  a navigational command in a menu retains the menu's keyboard behavior.
- A value you select and read back. Use `select`, which keeps the chosen value in the trigger.
- A destructive answer that must be confirmed. Use `alert-dialog`; a menu item is a
  one-keystroke action and closes immediately.
- More than about a dozen entries, or entries the user has to search. Use `command`.

## API

### `DropdownMenu`

| Prop           | Type                       | Default | Description                                     |
| -------------- | -------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                  | –       | Controlled open state.                          |
| `defaultOpen`  | `boolean`                  | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state.                     |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`  | –       | Fires on every open and close, including Escape. |
| `modal`        | `boolean`                  | `true`  | Limits outside pointer interaction and locks desktop scrolling. Tab dismisses the menu. |

### `DropdownMenuTrigger`

Native button props and `render`. The trigger owns `aria-haspopup="menu"` and
`aria-expanded`; pass a `Button` through `render` rather than wrapping one, so those land on
the element the user presses.

### `DropdownMenuContent`

| Prop          | Type                                          | Default    | Description                                    |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"`      | `"bottom"` | Preferred side; flips when there is no room.   |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                 | `"start"`  | Alignment along the trigger's edge.            |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                      | `4`        | Gap between trigger and panel, in pixels.       |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                      | `0`        | Shift along the alignment axis.                 |
| `className`   | string or Base UI state callback                                      | –          | Merged last.                                    |

### `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`

| Part                     | Props                                                              | Notes                                             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `DropdownMenuItem`       | `onClick`, `disabled`, `inset`, `variant`, `closeOnClick`            | `variant`: `"default" \| "destructive"`.          |
| `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` | `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `inset`            | Keeps the menu open.                              |
| `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` | `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`                            | One selection for the group.                      |
| `DropdownMenuRadioItem`  | `value` (required), `disabled`, `inset`                             | Keeps the menu open.                              |
| `DropdownMenuSub`        | –                                                                  | Groups a submenu trigger and its content.         |
| `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` | `disabled`, `inset`                                                | Renders the chevron.                              |
| `DropdownMenuSubContent` | Same as `DropdownMenuContent`                                      | `side="right"`, `alignOffset={-3}` by default.    |

### `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`

`DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`,
`DropdownMenuShortcut`, `DropdownMenuPortal`.

## Motion contract

| Phase         | Properties                                        | Token             | Interruptible                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------- |
| open          | panel `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` from the trigger origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| close         | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.96`               | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes                |
| check / radio | mark `opacity` + `scale`                          | `state.morph`     | yes                          |
| reduced       | panel fades, no scale; the mark cross-fades at full size | `exit.fade` | yes                         |
| none          | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`; the mark jumps | –      | –                            |

Opening and closing are one CSS transition on `opacity` and `scale`, driven by Base UI's
`data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`, so an interrupted close reverses rather than
restarts. The panel grows out of `--transform-origin`, which Base UI points at the trigger;
a submenu grows out of its item the same way, because both levels render the same panel.

The highlighted row is a colour change, not motion: `data-highlighted` switches the item's
background. A travelling highlight would be a shared element across items — `layout.move`,
which belongs to `tabs` and `toggle-group`, not to a menu that can be entered at any row.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The site header changes the inherited mode on the same component tree; the named
Explicit motion scopes example demonstrates fixed local overrides. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                      | Action                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` / `Space` / `ArrowDown` | Opens the menu and highlights the first item.                 |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp`   | Moves the highlight; it wraps at the ends.                          |
| `Home` / `End`            | First and last item.                                                |
| Typeahead letters         | Highlights the next item whose label starts with them.              |
| `Enter` / `Space`         | Runs the highlighted item and closes the menu.                      |
| `ArrowRight`              | Opens the highlighted submenu; `ArrowLeft` closes it.               |
| `Escape`                  | Closes the menu, returns focus to the trigger, runs nothing.        |
| `Tab`                     | Closes the menu and moves to the next control in the page.          |

## Accessibility

- Base UI wires the trigger with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and renders the
  panel as `role="menu"` with `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, and `menuitemradio` parts.
- For a navigational command, use `DropdownMenuItem render={<a href="…" />}`. The anchor
  keeps its `href` and receives `role="menuitem"` and Base UI's focus and activation behavior.
  Do not nest a second interactive link inside an item.
- `DropdownMenuLabel` inside a `DropdownMenuGroup` is the group's accessible name. Outside a
  group it is a caption: visible to sighted users, not announced as a label.
- `DropdownMenuShortcut` is text, not a binding. Announce the shortcut in the item's label
  only when it is registered, or the reader is told about a key that does nothing.
- The default modal mode limits outside pointer interaction and locks desktop scrolling. `Tab`
  still dismisses the menu and continues the page order; this is not a dialog focus trap.

## Responsive behavior

The panel caps at `--available-height` and scrolls. The positioner can flip the side and
shift along the cross axis, but caller-defined widths can still exceed the available space
in side placements. Cap them with `max-w-(--available-width)` and verify open bounds;
reduce the `min-w-[8rem]` minimum too if the available space is narrower.
On touch, the menu opens on tap and
the highlighted item follows the tap; there is no hover state to design around. `min-w-[8rem]`
keeps short menus readable, and the panel does not stretch to the trigger's width — a menu
is as wide as its widest item.

## Performance

- One portal per open menu; closing unmounts it after the exit transition.
- The panel animates `opacity` and `scale` only, on one element. Nothing measures layout, and
  no JavaScript runs per frame.
- Items carry no per-item motion: the only animated state is the check mark, and it animates
  two properties on a 14px span.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip). A page with a dozen closed menus pays for one component's source,
  no mounted popups, and no timers.

## Notes for AI

- Put the action on `onClick`. Base UI's menu item has no `onSelect`; a handler that only
  exists on `onSelect` never fires.
- Pass the trigger through `render` so `aria-haspopup` lands on the button, not on a wrapper.
- Group items before labelling them: a `DropdownMenuLabel` outside a `DropdownMenuGroup` is a
  caption, and a group without a label is announced as an unnamed group.
- Do not put a form with validation inside a menu. A menu is a list of commands; `popover`
  is the surface for controls.

The popup owns its `duration.fast` clock, including provider timeScale and the
reduced duration multiplier. An explicit full provider restores the clock inside
an outer none scope. In none mode the popup removes starting/ending opacity and
uses zero duration on the first frame. Function-valued popup `className` and
`style` receive Base UI state and merge after the component defaults.

# Context Menu

Right-click actions on a file, row, or canvas.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/context-menu
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
