4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, including every shared `lib/` file. Keep the mirrored
`cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives intact. The provider
files and `motion` are required imports; wrapping your application in
`CadenceProvider` is optional. Complete the base theme setup linked above,
including Cadence's easing tokens, and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files.
These payloads contain no additional context-menu-specific CSS or assets.

Usage and the top specimen need only Context Menu and its listed dependencies.
Beside a row menu also composes Dropdown Menu and Button. Follow
[Dropdown Menu's manual installation](https://cadence.dev/components/dropdown-menu#installation)
and [Button's manual installation](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation),
copying their full [Dropdown Menu payload](https://cadence.dev/r/dropdown-menu.json)
and [Button payload](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json). Beyond the shared files
above, add `@components/cadence/dropdown-menu/index.tsx` and
`@components/cadence/button/index.tsx`. Their only additional npm dependency is:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

Logical sides in RTL uses `DirectionProvider` from the already required
`@base-ui/react`; pair it with the DOM `dir` attribute, as shown.

In Next.js App Router, keep Usage, Beside a row menu, Selection items, Submenus,
Destructive and disabled items, and Controlled open in client modules: they own
state and handlers. Where the panel opens, Pointer alignment, Logical sides in
RTL and Explicit motion scopes are static compositions and can be rendered by
a Server Component with serializable props. Adding event handlers, refs or
function-valued `render`, `className` or `style` props requires a client caller;
synchronous `useId` alone does not. Keep the shipped client directives. The
site's preview shell is not consumer setup. Opening, navigation, selection and
dismissal require hydration; without JavaScript the target and code remain readable.

Compose a root, trigger and content. The trigger renders a `div`; supply a
focusable target with `tabIndex={0}` and a useful name or explanation for
Shift+F10 and the Context Menu key. Base UI handles the native `contextmenu`
event, pointer anchor and touch long press, including movement cancellation.
Keep the same actions available through a visible control for discoverability
and touch use. Content includes its own portal, positioner and popup. Both
Content and SubContent default to right/start, zero side offset and a 4px
alignment offset; do not add another portal around them. Submenus use Sub,
SubTrigger and SubContent. Base UI owns collision handling, roving item focus,
typeahead, submenu navigation and dismissal. Constrain unusually wide caller
content with `max-w-(--available-width)` and check the minimum width and actual
open bounds on narrow screens.

The caller owns commands and their effects, authorization, controlled `open`,
checkbox `checked`, radio-group `value`, persistence and error feedback. Use
`defaultOpen`, `defaultChecked` and `defaultValue` for uncontrolled initial
state. Establish the context anchor through the real target event; setting
`open` from an unrelated button supplies no cursor point. The installed root
omits `modal` and `triggerId`: Tab stays within the open panel, while
Shift+Tab or Escape closes it and restores focus to the target. Outside pointer
interaction is blocked and desktop scrolling is locked while open.

Use `onClick` for commands. Ordinary items close by default;
`closeOnClick={false}` keeps them open, and checkbox/radio items stay open by
default. Disabled items remain keyboard-discoverable but cannot activate;
root `disabled` prevents the context menu opening. Shortcut text registers no
key binding. Labels inside ContextMenuGroup name that group; outside it,
including inside RadioGroup, they are captions. Usage's navigational command
passes an anchor through the item's `render` prop so its `href` and the menu
role, focus and activation behavior share one element. This component supplies
no form-state or validation package; the examples update only local state.

Full mode scales and fades panels and animates the checkbox/radio mark.
Reduced retains opacity at full size; none disables these transitions from
the first mounted frame. A nested provider can restore full inside none,
subject to the system reduced-motion preference. Preserve the primitive's
events and focus behavior when supplying custom render elements or handlers.

## Usage

Right-click the focusable file target, or focus it and press Shift+F10. Open is a real
changelog link. Rename and Open with only update this local file label; application
commands, storage and authorization belong to the caller. Interactive menus need hydration;
the target, explanation and runnable code remain readable without JavaScript.

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuSub, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function FileMenu() {
  const [name, setName] = useState("Roadmap.md");
  return (
    <ContextMenu>
      <ContextMenuTrigger
        tabIndex={0}
        className="flex h-24 w-56 flex-col items-center justify-center gap-1 rounded-lg border border-dashed text-sm"
      >
        <span className="font-medium">{name}</span>
        <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Right-click for actions</span>
      </ContextMenuTrigger>
      <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions">
        <ContextMenuGroup>
          <ContextMenuItem render={<a href="/docs/changelog" />}>Open</ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => setName("Roadmap (renamed).md")}>Rename</ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuSub>
            <ContextMenuSubTrigger>Open with</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
            <ContextMenuSubContent>
              <ContextMenuGroup>
                <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => setName("Editor: Roadmap.md")}>Editor</ContextMenuItem>
                <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => setName("Preview: Roadmap.md")}>Preview</ContextMenuItem>
              </ContextMenuGroup>
            </ContextMenuSubContent>
          </ContextMenuSub>
        </ContextMenuGroup>
      </ContextMenuContent>
    </ContextMenu>
  );
}
```

## Where the panel opens

Right-click each fixed target. The panel is anchored to the cursor point, rather than to the target box. These four physical sides use an 8px gap and zero cross-axis offset so the difference is visible. Collision handling may flip the requested side near an edge; the default is right/start, with sideOffset=0 and alignOffset=4.

<ComponentExample name="sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function PointerSides() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["top", "right", "bottom", "left"] as const).map((side) => (
        <ContextMenu key={side}>
          <ContextMenuTrigger
            tabIndex={0}
            className="grid h-20 w-28 place-content-center rounded-md border border-dashed text-sm"
          >
            {side}
          </ContextMenuTrigger>
          <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions" side={side} sideOffset={8} alignOffset={0}>
            <ContextMenuGroup>
              <ContextMenuItem>Close menu</ContextMenuItem>
            </ContextMenuGroup>
          </ContextMenuContent>
        </ContextMenu>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Pointer alignment

Start, center and end align the panel against the cursor point along the cross axis. These are three separate bottom-side menus, not three configurations of a shared instance. Collision handling still shifts or flips the panel when space is limited.

<ComponentExample name="alignments" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function PointerAlignments() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["start", "center", "end"] as const).map((align) => (
        <ContextMenu key={align}>
          <ContextMenuTrigger
            tabIndex={0}
            className="grid h-20 w-28 place-content-center rounded-md border border-dashed text-sm"
          >
            {align}
          </ContextMenuTrigger>
          <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions" side="bottom" align={align} alignOffset={0} sideOffset={8}>
            <ContextMenuGroup>
              <ContextMenuItem>Close menu</ContextMenuItem>
            </ContextMenuGroup>
          </ContextMenuContent>
        </ContextMenu>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Logical sides in RTL

Logical inline-start and inline-end follow the direction provider. In this RTL example they request right and left respectively. The surrounding dir attribute also gives the native content its text direction. Install @base-ui/react alongside the component; it is already a Context Menu dependency.

<ComponentExample name="logical-sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DirectionProvider } from "@base-ui/react/direction-provider";
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function LogicalPointerSides() {
  return (
    <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">
      <div dir="rtl" className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        {(["inline-start", "inline-end"] as const).map((side) => (
          <ContextMenu key={side}>
            <ContextMenuTrigger
              tabIndex={0}
              className="grid h-20 w-32 place-content-center rounded-md border border-dashed text-sm"
            >
              {side}
            </ContextMenuTrigger>
            <ContextMenuContent
              aria-label="File actions"
              side={side}
              alignOffset={0}
              sideOffset={8}
              className="max-w-(--available-width)"
            >
              <ContextMenuGroup>
                <ContextMenuItem>Close menu</ContextMenuItem>
              </ContextMenuGroup>
            </ContextMenuContent>
          </ContextMenu>
        ))}
      </div>
    </DirectionProvider>
  );
}
```

## Beside a row menu

A visible row menu makes the same actions discoverable for touch and keyboard users. Share action data and callbacks; render ContextMenuItem inside ContextMenu and DropdownMenuItem inside DropdownMenu. Both routes below update the same local result. Also install @cadence/dropdown-menu and @cadence/button for this composition; no file is opened or renamed on a server.

<ComponentExample name="row-menu" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";
import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";

export function RowMenu() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No row action yet");
  const actions = ["Open", "Rename"];
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
        <ContextMenu>
          <ContextMenuTrigger tabIndex={0} className="rounded-md border border-dashed px-6 py-4 text-sm">
            Roadmap.md
          </ContextMenuTrigger>
          <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions">
            <ContextMenuGroup>
              {actions.map((action) => (
                <ContextMenuItem key={action} onClick={() => setResult(`${action} selected locally`)}>
                  {action}
                </ContextMenuItem>
              ))}
            </ContextMenuGroup>
          </ContextMenuContent>
        </ContextMenu>
        <DropdownMenu>
          <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Row actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuContent>
            <DropdownMenuGroup>
              {actions.map((action) => (
                <DropdownMenuItem key={action} onClick={() => setResult(`${action} selected locally`)}>
                  {action}
                </DropdownMenuItem>
              ))}
            </DropdownMenuGroup>
          </DropdownMenuContent>
        </DropdownMenu>
      </div>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        {result}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Selection items

Checkbox and radio items stay open by default. Grid and sort belong to this example; Rulers demonstrates an uncontrolled default. Labels name the Show group and Sort radio group, while separators divide the sections. Inset keeps labels and plain text aligned with the reserved indicator space.

<ComponentExample name="selection" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuRadioGroup, ContextMenuRadioItem, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function SelectionMenu() {
  const [grid, setGrid] = useState(true);
  const [sort, setSort] = useState("name");
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <ContextMenu>
        <ContextMenuTrigger tabIndex={0} className="rounded-md border border-dashed px-6 py-4 text-sm">
          View options
        </ContextMenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions">
          <ContextMenuGroup>
            <ContextMenuLabel inset>Show</ContextMenuLabel>
            <ContextMenuCheckboxItem checked={grid} onCheckedChange={setGrid} inset>
              Grid
            </ContextMenuCheckboxItem>
            <ContextMenuCheckboxItem defaultChecked>Rulers</ContextMenuCheckboxItem>
          </ContextMenuGroup>
          <ContextMenuSeparator />
          <ContextMenuRadioGroup aria-label="Sort" value={sort} onValueChange={setSort}>
            <ContextMenuLabel>Sort</ContextMenuLabel>
            <ContextMenuRadioItem value="name" inset>
              Name
            </ContextMenuRadioItem>
            <ContextMenuRadioItem value="date">Date modified</ContextMenuRadioItem>
          </ContextMenuRadioGroup>
        </ContextMenuContent>
      </ContextMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        Grid: {grid ? "shown" : "hidden"}; sort: {sort}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Submenus

ArrowRight opens Open with; ArrowLeft returns to its parent trigger in LTR. The selected application is recorded locally and closes both panels. Each submenu owns its own portal; it is not a second root menu.

<ComponentExample name="submenus" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuSub, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function Submenu() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("Not opened");
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <ContextMenu>
        <ContextMenuTrigger tabIndex={0} className="rounded-md border border-dashed px-6 py-4 text-sm">
          Open a file
        </ContextMenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions">
          <ContextMenuGroup>
            <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => setResult("Default app")}>Default app</ContextMenuItem>
            <ContextMenuSub>
              <ContextMenuSubTrigger inset>Open with</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
              <ContextMenuSubContent>
                <ContextMenuGroup>
                  {["Editor", "Preview"].map((app) => (
                    <ContextMenuItem key={app} onClick={() => setResult(app)}>
                      {app}
                    </ContextMenuItem>
                  ))}
                </ContextMenuGroup>
              </ContextMenuSubContent>
            </ContextMenuSub>
          </ContextMenuGroup>
        </ContextMenuContent>
      </ContextMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        {result}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Destructive and disabled items

Default and destructive commands are directly present in one menu. Rename and Keep open use inset; Keep open opts out of dismissal. F2 and the delete hint are text only: the component does not bind those shortcuts. Disabled command, checkbox, radio and submenu parts can receive keyboard focus but cannot activate. The second target disables the entire root: neither right-click nor Shift+F10 opens its Cadence menu. aria-disabled announces that state on the focusable div. Delete records a local result; production deletion and any confirmation belong to the caller.

<ComponentExample name="items" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuRadioGroup, ContextMenuRadioItem, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut, ContextMenuSub, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function ItemStates() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No command yet");
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <ContextMenu>
        <ContextMenuTrigger tabIndex={0} className="rounded-md border border-dashed px-6 py-4 text-sm">
          File commands
        </ContextMenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions">
          <ContextMenuGroup>
            <ContextMenuLabel inset>File</ContextMenuLabel>
            <ContextMenuItem inset onClick={() => setResult("Renamed locally")}>
              Rename<ContextMenuShortcut>F2</ContextMenuShortcut>
            </ContextMenuItem>
            <ContextMenuItem inset closeOnClick={false} onClick={() => setResult("Still open")}>
              Keep open
            </ContextMenuItem>
            <ContextMenuItem disabled onClick={() => setResult("Incorrectly activated")}>
              Locked command
            </ContextMenuItem>
            <ContextMenuCheckboxItem disabled defaultChecked>
              Locked visibility
            </ContextMenuCheckboxItem>
          </ContextMenuGroup>
          <ContextMenuRadioGroup defaultValue="locked">
            <ContextMenuRadioItem disabled value="locked">
              Locked sort
            </ContextMenuRadioItem>
          </ContextMenuRadioGroup>
          <ContextMenuGroup>
            <ContextMenuSub>
              <ContextMenuSubTrigger disabled>Unavailable app</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
              <ContextMenuSubContent>
                <ContextMenuGroup>
                  <ContextMenuItem>Never opened</ContextMenuItem>
                </ContextMenuGroup>
              </ContextMenuSubContent>
            </ContextMenuSub>
          </ContextMenuGroup>
          <ContextMenuSeparator />
          <ContextMenuGroup>
            <ContextMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => setResult("Deleted locally")}>
              Delete<ContextMenuShortcut>⌘⌫</ContextMenuShortcut>
            </ContextMenuItem>
          </ContextMenuGroup>
        </ContextMenuContent>
      </ContextMenu>
      <ContextMenu disabled>
        <ContextMenuTrigger
          tabIndex={0}
          aria-disabled="true"
          className="rounded-md border border-dashed px-6 py-4 text-sm opacity-50"
        >
          Disabled target
        </ContextMenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions">
          <ContextMenuGroup>
            <ContextMenuItem>Unavailable</ContextMenuItem>
          </ContextMenuGroup>
        </ContextMenuContent>
      </ContextMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        {result}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled open

The caller owns open and observes Base UI change reasons. Open at the target with a right-click or Shift+F10, then close through a caller-owned action or Escape. ContextMenu has no modal or triggerId prop in this installed API. Use its real target event to establish the cursor anchor; setting open=true from an unrelated button does not supply that point.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function ControlledMenu() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [reason, setReason] = useState("Not opened");
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <ContextMenu
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={(value, details) => {
          setOpen(value);
          setReason(details.reason);
        }}
      >
        <ContextMenuTrigger tabIndex={0} className="rounded-md border border-dashed px-6 py-4 text-sm">
          Controlled target
        </ContextMenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions">
          <ContextMenuGroup>
            <ContextMenuItem
              closeOnClick={false}
              onClick={() => {
                setReason("Caller closed");
                setOpen(false);
              }}
            >
              Close from caller
            </ContextMenuItem>
          </ContextMenuGroup>
        </ContextMenuContent>
      </ContextMenu>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">
        {open ? "Open" : "Closed"}: {reason}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

Ordinary examples inherit the site header. This exception mounts the first menu in none from its first frame and overrides the second back to full. The OS reduced-motion preference still wins over full. Install the cadence-provider dependency to import CadenceProvider from its installed lib/provider path. Right-click each target to compare; neither changes the global mode.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MenuMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <ContextMenu>
          <ContextMenuTrigger tabIndex={0} className="rounded-md border border-dashed px-4 py-4 text-sm">
            Open without motion
          </ContextMenuTrigger>
          <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions" data-testid="initial-none">
            <ContextMenuGroup>
              <ContextMenuCheckboxItem>Grid</ContextMenuCheckboxItem>
            </ContextMenuGroup>
          </ContextMenuContent>
        </ContextMenu>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <ContextMenu>
            <ContextMenuTrigger tabIndex={0} className="rounded-md border border-dashed px-4 py-4 text-sm">
              Open nested full
            </ContextMenuTrigger>
            <ContextMenuContent aria-label="File actions" data-testid="nested-full">
              <ContextMenuGroup>
                <ContextMenuCheckboxItem>Grid</ContextMenuCheckboxItem>
              </ContextMenuGroup>
            </ContextMenuContent>
          </ContextMenu>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A canvas, map, or list of files where the object itself is the target.
- A table row with more actions than fit in a cell.
- A destructive action that should be one gesture away, not one visible button.

## When not to use

- An action a user needs to discover. A context menu is invisible until someone
  right-clicks; put the primary action in the row and keep the menu for the rest.
- A single toggle. Use a `checkbox` or `switch` that is always visible.
- The same list on a touch device only: a long-press competes with scroll and text
  selection. Keep a visible `dropdown-menu` as well.

## API

### `ContextMenu`

`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` and the remaining Base UI Context Menu root props.
The installed API omits `modal` and `triggerId`; it retains the underlying modal menu behavior.
Outside pointer interaction is blocked while open and desktop scrolling is locked.
Tab stays within the open panel. Shift+Tab or Escape closes the root menu and returns
focus to the target; activating an ordinary command also dismisses it.

### `ContextMenuTrigger`

Native div props and `render`. The trigger is the area that listens for `contextmenu` and
long-press; it renders a `div` by default, so give it the box you want to be right-clickable.

### `ContextMenuContent`

| Prop          | Type                                     | Default     | Description                                   |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"right"`   | Requested side from the cursor; collisions may flip it. |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`            | `"start"`   | Alignment along that side.                    |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                 | `0`         | Gap from the pointer.                         |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                 | `4`         | Shift along the alignment axis.               |
| `className`   | string or Base UI state callback                                 | –           | Merged last.                                  |

### `ContextMenuItem`, `ContextMenuCheckboxItem`, `ContextMenuRadioItem`

`ContextMenuItem` (`onClick`, `disabled`, `inset`, `variant`), `ContextMenuCheckboxItem`,
`ContextMenuRadioGroup`, `ContextMenuRadioItem`, `ContextMenuSub`, `ContextMenuSubTrigger`,
`ContextMenuSubContent` — the same parts and props as `dropdown-menu`, with context-menu
slots.

### `ContextMenuGroup`, `ContextMenuLabel`, `ContextMenuSeparator`

`ContextMenuGroup`, `ContextMenuLabel`, `ContextMenuSeparator`, `ContextMenuShortcut`,
`ContextMenuPortal`.

## Motion contract

| Phase         | Properties                                        | Token             | Interruptible |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------- |
| open          | panel `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` from the pointer | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| close         | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.96`               | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| check / radio | mark `opacity` + `scale`                          | `state.morph`     | yes           |
| reduced       | panel fades, no scale; the mark cross-fades at full size | `exit.fade` | yes           |
| none          | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`; the mark jumps | –      | –             |

The panel grows out of the point that was pressed. That is the whole reason the recipe is
anchored rather than centred: a context menu belongs to the place it was summoned, and a
scale from the pointer says so without moving the panel.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The site header changes inherited mode without remounting the target or clearing caller-owned
selection. A real header press may dismiss an open menu through normal outside interaction;
the explicit motion-scope example demonstrates local overrides. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                      | Action                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Shift+F10` / Context Menu key | Opens the menu at the focused element.                   |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp`   | Moves the highlight.                                          |
| Typeahead letters         | Highlights the next item starting with them.                  |
| `Enter` / `Space`         | Runs the highlighted item.                                    |
| `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` | Opens or closes a submenu.                                   |
| `Escape`                  | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.             |
| `Tab`                     | Keeps focus in the open context menu.                         |
| `Shift+Tab`               | Closes the root menu and returns focus to the target.         |

## Accessibility

- The trigger keeps the browser's own `contextmenu` event: the menu opens from the keyboard
  with `Shift+F10` or the dedicated key, which is what a screen reader user presses.
- The panel is `role="menu"` and the items are `menuitem` / `menuitemcheckbox` /
  `menuitemradio`, so "right-click for options" is announced as a menu, not as a tooltip.
- On touch, Base UI opens the menu on a long press and cancels it if the finger moves —
  which is why the same actions must also be reachable from a visible control.
- Escape restores focus to the target. The installed Context Menu uses a modal focus manager
  internally: Tab stays within the open menu, while Shift+Tab closes the root menu and
  returns focus to the target. Unlike Dropdown Menu, it does not expose a modal prop.
  Keep Escape and visible command paths available.

## Responsive behavior

The panel flips to the side with room and shifts along the cross axis to stay inside the
viewport, so a right-click near the bottom-right corner opens up and to the left. On a
narrow screen it caps its height at `--available-height` and scrolls. The caller must
contain unusually wide content; the RTL example caps width at `--available-width`.

## Performance

- One portal per open panel, including an additional portal for a submenu. CSS transitions
  animate `opacity` and `scale`; placement and interaction remain owned by Base UI.
- Base UI owns target and item event handling; the example adds no per-frame positioning loop.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip). The item and submenu parts share their classes with
  `dropdown-menu` but not its file, so the two install independently.

## Notes for AI

- Use `onClick` for the action; there is no `onSelect` on Base UI's menu item.
- Do not hide the only path to an action behind a context menu — pair it with a visible
  control, because a context menu is undiscoverable and unavailable on most touch flows.
- `ContextMenuTrigger` is the right-click area, so its content is what the user aims at;
  avoid making the whole page a trigger.

# Menubar

Application menus along the top of a window.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/menubar
```

The Controlled opening example also composes `@cadence/button`; install that item alongside Menubar when copying it.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/dropdown-menu](https://cadence.dev/r/dropdown-menu.json) — direct registry dependency.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all ten target files, including Dropdown Menu and every shared `lib/` file.
Keep the mirrored `cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives
intact. The provider files and `motion` are required imports; wrapping your
application in `CadenceProvider` is optional. Complete the base theme setup
linked above, including Cadence's easing tokens, and ensure Tailwind scans the
copied files. These payloads contain no additional menubar-specific CSS or assets.

Usage, the top specimen and all examples except Controlled opening need only
Menubar and its listed dependencies. Controlled opening also composes Button.
Follow [Button's manual installation](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation)
and copy its full [payload source](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json), adding
`@components/cadence/button/index.tsx` alongside the shared files already listed.
Its only additional npm dependency is:

```package-manager
npm install class-variance-authority
```

Right-to-left menus uses `DirectionProvider` from the already required
`@base-ui/react`; pair it with DOM `dir`, including portal content, as shown.

In Next.js App Router, keep Usage, Shortcuts and groups, Selection items,
Nested commands, Item variants and closing, and Controlled opening in client
modules: they own state and handlers. Moving between menus, Horizontal and
vertical, Disabled bars and commands, Panel sides, Panel alignment,
Right-to-left menus, Modal and non-modal menus, and Explicit motion scopes are
static compositions and can be rendered by a Server Component with serializable
props. Adding event handlers, refs or function-valued `render`, `className` or
`style` props requires a client caller; synchronous `useId` alone does not. Keep
the shipped client directives. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup.
Opening, navigation, selection and dismissal require hydration; without
JavaScript the bar labels and code remain readable.

Give the bar an accessible name and put each top-level trigger and content in
its own `MenubarMenu`. Content includes its own portal, positioner and popup;
do not wrap it in another portal. Content defaults to bottom/start with an 8px
side offset and -4px alignment offset. Submenus use Sub, SubTrigger and
SubContent; their inherited defaults are right/start, zero side offset and
-3px alignment offset. Base UI owns roving focus, typeahead, sibling traversal,
collision handling and dismissal. Vertical orientation also needs caller layout
classes. Keep trigger labels short and constrain wide panels with
`max-w-(--available-width)`; check their minimum width and actual narrow-screen
bounds. Review the pointer/Escape limitation under Moving between menus.

The caller owns command effects, authorization, controlled `open`, checkbox and
radio values, persistence, loading and errors. Control each menu with
`open`/`onOpenChange`; use a stable trigger `id` and matching `triggerId` when
opening it externally. The bar has no shared `open` prop. Ordinary items close
on activation unless `closeOnClick={false}`; checkbox and radio items stay open
by default. Uncontrolled item state resets when the closed panel unmounts, as
Selection items demonstrates. Disabled items may receive arrow-key focus but
cannot activate. Shortcut text does not register keys, and `inset` changes only
alignment. Use a real anchor through `render` for destinations; a label inside
Group names that group, while an ungrouped label is a caption.

The bar defaults to `modal={true}`: a click-opened menu limits outside pointer
interaction and locks desktop scrolling. Forward Tab leaves the bar and closes
the panel. From a panel item, Shift+Tab returns to the trigger with the panel
still open; another Shift+Tab leaves the bar and closes it. Escape closes and
returns to the trigger. `modal={false}` allows outside interaction. Menubar
reuses Dropdown Menu's popup and selection motion; the bar itself does not
animate. Full mode fades and scales panels and marks, reduced keeps opacity
without scale, and none removes transition time. Optional provider scopes
control mode and speed, subject to the OS reduced-motion preference.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function EditorMenubar() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No command yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Menubar aria-label="Editor">
        <MenubarMenu>
          <MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setResult("New local document")}>New</MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setResult("Saved locally")}>Save</MenubarItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
        <MenubarMenu>
          <MenubarTrigger>Edit</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setResult("Undo selected locally")}>Undo</MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setResult("Redo selected locally")}>Redo</MenubarItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
        <MenubarMenu>
          <MenubarTrigger>Help</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarItem render={<a href="/docs/changelog" />}>Changelog</MenubarItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
      </Menubar>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{result}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Moving between menus

The bar coordinates sibling menus. Use Left/Right to move between horizontal triggers and between open menus. The first fixed bar uses the default looping focus; the second sets `loopFocus={false}` so traversal stops at either end.

Current limitation: after opening menus with the pointer and dismissing them with Escape, moving to a previously dismissed neighbour can focus its trigger while leaving the earlier panel open. Press Enter on the focused trigger to open that menu. This also occurs with unstyled Base UI primitives and with motion set to none. This pointer-history case remains an unresolved keyboard regression; fresh keyboard traversal is shown below.

<ComponentExample name="traversal" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function MenuTraversal() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {[true, false].map((loopFocus) => (
        <Menubar key={String(loopFocus)} loopFocus={loopFocus} aria-label={loopFocus ? "Looping menus" : "Bounded menus"}>
          {["File", "Edit", "View"].map((label) => (
            <MenubarMenu key={label}>
              <MenubarTrigger>{label}</MenubarTrigger>
              <MenubarContent>
                <MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>{label} command</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup>
              </MenubarContent>
            </MenubarMenu>
          ))}
        </Menubar>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Horizontal and vertical

Orientation changes roving-focus keys, not layout classes. The vertical bar supplies `h-auto flex-col items-stretch` and places its panels on the right; the horizontal bar keeps the defaults. Up/Down traverses vertical triggers before a menu opens.

<ComponentExample name="orientation" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function MenuOrientations() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
      {(["horizontal", "vertical"] as const).map((orientation) => (
        <Menubar key={orientation} orientation={orientation} aria-label={`${orientation} menus`}
          className={orientation === "vertical" ? "h-auto flex-col items-stretch" : undefined}>
          {["File", "Edit"].map((label) => (
            <MenubarMenu key={label}>
              <MenubarTrigger>{label}</MenubarTrigger>
              <MenubarContent side={orientation === "vertical" ? "right" : "bottom"}>
                <MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>{label} command</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup>
              </MenubarContent>
            </MenubarMenu>
          ))}
        </Menubar>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Shortcuts and groups

A `MenubarLabel` inside its `MenubarGroup` names that group. `inset` aligns labels and commands with selection marks. `MenubarShortcut` is a text hint only: this local example does not register a global shortcut or export a file. The Changelog item is a real link.

<ComponentExample name="grouping" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarLabel, MenubarMenu, MenubarSeparator, MenubarShortcut, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function GroupedCommands() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No export yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Menubar aria-label="Export commands">
        <MenubarMenu>
          <MenubarTrigger>Export</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarLabel inset>Document</MenubarLabel>
              <MenubarItem inset onClick={() => setResult("PDF selected locally")}>
                PDF<MenubarShortcut>⇧⌘P</MenubarShortcut>
              </MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem inset onClick={() => setResult("PNG selected locally")}>PNG</MenubarItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
            <MenubarSeparator />
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarLabel>Help</MenubarLabel>
              <MenubarItem render={<a href="/docs/changelog" />}>Changelog</MenubarItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
      </Menubar>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">{result}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Selection items

Checkboxes and radios keep the panel open by default. Sidebar and density are caller-owned values; Line numbers demonstrates independent uncontrolled state. Sidebar and density persist across panel lifetimes. Line numbers is an uncontrolled item: closing the panel unmounts it, so reopening restores its default.

<ComponentExample name="selection" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Menubar, MenubarCheckboxItem, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarLabel, MenubarMenu, MenubarRadioGroup, MenubarRadioItem, MenubarSeparator, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function MenuSelection() {
  const [sidebar, setSidebar] = useState(true);
  const [density, setDensity] = useState("comfortable");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Menubar aria-label="View settings">
        <MenubarMenu>
          <MenubarTrigger>View</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarLabel inset>Show</MenubarLabel>
              <MenubarCheckboxItem checked={sidebar} onCheckedChange={setSidebar}>Sidebar</MenubarCheckboxItem>
              <MenubarCheckboxItem defaultChecked inset>Line numbers</MenubarCheckboxItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
            <MenubarSeparator />
            <MenubarRadioGroup aria-label="Density" value={density} onValueChange={setDensity}>
              <MenubarLabel>Density</MenubarLabel>
              <MenubarRadioItem value="compact" inset>Compact</MenubarRadioItem>
              <MenubarRadioItem value="comfortable">Comfortable</MenubarRadioItem>
            </MenubarRadioGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
      </Menubar>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">Sidebar: {sidebar ? "shown" : "hidden"}; density: {density}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Nested commands

A submenu belongs to its trigger, not to a neighbouring top-level menu. Right opens it and Left returns to its trigger in LTR. Selecting a destination updates only this local result and closes the menu tree.

<ComponentExample name="submenus" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarSub, MenubarSubContent, MenubarSubTrigger, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function NestedCommands() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("Not moved");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Menubar aria-label="Organize document">
        <MenubarMenu>
          <MenubarTrigger>Organize</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setResult("Kept here")}>Keep here</MenubarItem>
              <MenubarSub>
                <MenubarSubTrigger inset>Move to</MenubarSubTrigger>
                <MenubarSubContent>
                  <MenubarGroup>
                    {["Backlog", "Review"].map((value) => (
                      <MenubarItem key={value} onClick={() => setResult(value)}>{value}</MenubarItem>
                    ))}
                  </MenubarGroup>
                </MenubarSubContent>
              </MenubarSub>
            </MenubarGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
      </Menubar>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">{result}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Item variants and closing

Default and destructive are item variants. `closeOnClick={false}` keeps the panel open for the middle action; it is separate from the visual `inset` choice. These handlers record local results and do not mutate a server document.

<ComponentExample name="items" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function ItemBehaviors() {
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No item action yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Menubar aria-label="Item commands">
        <MenubarMenu>
          <MenubarTrigger>Actions</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarItem onClick={() => setResult("Renamed locally")}>Rename</MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem inset closeOnClick={false} onClick={() => setResult("Still open")}>Keep open</MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => setResult("Deleted locally")}>Delete</MenubarItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
      </Menubar>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">{result}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled bars and commands

Disable the entire bar, an individual trigger, or each item part independently. Disabled menu items may receive arrow-key focus, but cannot activate or change selection. The disabled submenu cannot open. Do not make disabled commands disappear from the keyboard model.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Menubar, MenubarCheckboxItem, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarRadioGroup, MenubarRadioItem, MenubarSub, MenubarSubContent, MenubarSubTrigger, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function DisabledCommands() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      <Menubar disabled aria-label="Disabled bar">
        <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Disabled bar</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent><MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>Unavailable</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
      </Menubar>
      <Menubar aria-label="Disabled commands">
        <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger disabled>Disabled trigger</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent><MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>Unavailable</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
        <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Unavailable commands</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarItem disabled>Delete locked document</MenubarItem>
              <MenubarCheckboxItem disabled defaultChecked>Locked sidebar</MenubarCheckboxItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
            <MenubarRadioGroup defaultValue="locked">
              <MenubarRadioItem disabled value="locked">Locked density</MenubarRadioItem>
            </MenubarRadioGroup>
            <MenubarGroup>
              <MenubarSub>
                <MenubarSubTrigger disabled>Unavailable destination</MenubarSubTrigger>
                <MenubarSubContent><MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>Never opened</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarSubContent>
              </MenubarSub>
              <MenubarItem>Done</MenubarItem>
            </MenubarGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
      </Menubar>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled opening

Control an individual `MenubarMenu` with `open`/`onOpenChange`. The external action is part of this focused behavior example; `useId` and `triggerId` preserve its real File anchor. The bar itself has no shared `open` prop. Escape and selecting Save close through the same callback.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function ControlledMenu() {
  const id = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No controlled action");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open externally</Button>
      <Menubar aria-label="Controlled menu">
        <MenubarMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} triggerId={id}>
          <MenubarTrigger id={id}>File</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent>
            <MenubarGroup><MenubarItem onClick={() => setResult("Saved locally")}>Save</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup>
          </MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu>
      </Menubar>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm">{result}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Panel sides

These four fixed menus demonstrate physical sides without a placement selector. `sideOffset` defaults to 8px. Base UI may flip or shift to avoid the viewport; a requested side is not a guarantee on a narrow screen.

<ComponentExample name="sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function MenuSides() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["top", "right", "bottom", "left"] as const).map((side) => (
        <Menubar key={side} aria-label={`${side} placement`}>
          <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>{side}</MenubarTrigger>
            <MenubarContent side={side}><MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>Done</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarContent>
          </MenubarMenu>
        </Menubar>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Panel alignment

Start, center and end compare the panel with its trigger on the cross axis. These examples explicitly set `alignOffset={0}` for exact alignment; the component default is -4px. Alignment is independent of side.

<ComponentExample name="alignments" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function MenuAlignments() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {(["start", "center", "end"] as const).map((align) => (
        <Menubar key={align} aria-label={`${align} alignment`}>
          <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>{align}</MenubarTrigger>
            <MenubarContent align={align} alignOffset={0}><MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>Done</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarContent>
          </MenubarMenu>
        </Menubar>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Right-to-left menus

Set both Base UI direction context and DOM direction, including portal content. In RTL, inline-start resolves to the right and inline-end to the left; horizontal trigger traversal reverses. Panels remain constrained to available viewport width.

<ComponentExample name="logical-sides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DirectionProvider } from "@base-ui/react/direction-provider";
import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function RtlMenus() {
  return (
    <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">
      <div dir="rtl" className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        {(["inline-start", "inline-end"] as const).map((side) => (
          <Menubar key={side} aria-label={`${side} RTL`}>
            <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>{side}</MenubarTrigger>
              <MenubarContent side={side} className="min-w-0 w-48 max-w-(--available-width)">
                <MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>Done</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup>
              </MenubarContent>
            </MenubarMenu>
            <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Help</MenubarTrigger>
              <MenubarContent><MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>About</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarContent>
            </MenubarMenu>
          </Menubar>
        ))}
      </div>
    </DirectionProvider>
  );
}
```

## Modal and non-modal menus

The default `modal={true}` limits outside pointer interactions and locks desktop page scrolling while a click-opened menu is present. `false` allows the rest of the document to remain interactive. These are menu semantics: Forward Tab leaves the bar and closes the panel. From a panel item, Shift+Tab first returns to the bar trigger with its panel still open; a second Shift+Tab leaves the bar and closes it. Escape closes directly and returns to the trigger.

<ComponentExample name="modality" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function MenuModality() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {[true, false].map((modal) => (
        <Menubar key={String(modal)} modal={modal} aria-label={`modal ${modal}`}>
          <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>{String(modal)}</MenubarTrigger>
            <MenubarContent><MenubarGroup><MenubarItem>Done</MenubarItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarContent>
          </MenubarMenu>
        </Menubar>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Explicit motion scopes

Only this named example overrides the header. The first panel mounts under `none`, with no animated first frame. The second nests `full` inside `none`; system reduced motion still wins. Ordinary examples inherit header mode and speed.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Menubar, MenubarCheckboxItem, MenubarContent, MenubarGroup, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function MenuMotionScopes() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <Menubar aria-label="Instant menu"><MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Open without motion</MenubarTrigger>
          <MenubarContent data-testid="initial-none"><MenubarGroup><MenubarCheckboxItem>Sidebar</MenubarCheckboxItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarContent>
        </MenubarMenu></Menubar>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Menubar aria-label="Nested full menu"><MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Open nested full</MenubarTrigger>
            <MenubarContent data-testid="nested-full"><MenubarGroup><MenubarCheckboxItem>Sidebar</MenubarCheckboxItem></MenubarGroup></MenubarContent>
          </MenubarMenu></Menubar>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A desktop-style application shell with a menu across the top.
- A documentation tool or editor where File / Edit / View are the mental model.
- A dense toolbar whose commands need names, shortcuts, and grouping.

## When not to use

- A web page's main navigation. Use links or `navigation-menu`: a menu bar hides its
  destinations behind a click.
- One trigger with a list of actions. Use `dropdown-menu`.
- Commands a user reaches for a dozen times a minute. First-class buttons beat two clicks.

## API

`Menubar` takes `modal` (default `true`), `disabled`, and `orientation` (default
`"horizontal"`), and `loopFocus` (default `true`). Vertical orientation needs caller layout classes. Each `MenubarMenu` accepts the menu root state props (`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `triggerId`); these do not belong on the bar. Every other part mirrors `dropdown-menu` under menubar slots:

| Part                                                                                  | Notes                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MenubarMenu`                                                                         | One top-level menu; wraps the trigger and its content.    |
| `MenubarTrigger`                                                                      | The label in the bar. Opens on click, `Enter`, `ArrowDown`. |
| `MenubarContent`                                                                      | The panel: `min-w-[12rem]`, `sideOffset={8}`, `alignOffset={-4}`. |
| `MenubarItem`                                                                         | `onClick`, `inset`, `variant`.                            |
| `MenubarCheckboxItem` / `MenubarRadioGroup` / `MenubarRadioItem`                        | Selection that keeps the panel open.                      |
| `MenubarSub` / `MenubarSubTrigger` / `MenubarSubContent`                                | A nested menu.                                           |
| `MenubarGroup` / `MenubarLabel` / `MenubarSeparator` / `MenubarShortcut` / `MenubarPortal` | Structure.                                            |

## Motion contract

| Phase         | Properties                                     | Token             | Interruptible |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------- |
| open          | panel `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` from the trigger | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| close         | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.96`            | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| check / radio | mark `opacity` + `scale`                       | `state.morph`     | yes           |
| reduced       | panel fades, no scale; the mark cross-fades    | `exit.fade`       | yes           |
| none          | every duration resolves to `0ms`               | –                 | –             |

The bar itself does not animate. Switching from one open menu to the next replaces one panel
with another; there is no shared element between them, and a highlight sliding along the bar
would suggest a continuity the markup does not have.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. Ordinary specimens inherit the header mode and speed; only the explicit
motion-scopes example overrides them. Header pointer interaction may close a menu normally. The
independent runtime fixture verifies live mode changes without an outside press. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                        | Action                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight`  | Traverses horizontal top-level menus (reversed in RTL); while open, opens the neighbour unless entering a submenu; after the pointer/Escape history described above, Enter may be needed. |
| `ArrowDown` / `Enter` / `Space` | Opens a horizontal menu; Up/Down traverses closed vertical triggers. |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`     | Moves the highlight inside an open menu.                       |
| `Home` / `End`              | First and last item.                                           |
| `Escape`                    | Closes the menu and returns focus to its trigger.              |
| `Tab`                       | Leaves the open menu/bar for the next page control and closes the panel. |
| `Shift+Tab`                 | From a panel item, returns to its trigger and keeps the panel open; another Shift+Tab leaves the bar and closes it. |

## Accessibility

- The root is `role="menubar"` with `aria-orientation`; each trigger is `aria-haspopup="menu"`
  and reports `aria-expanded`, so the bar announces its structure rather than a row of
  buttons that happen to open panels.
- Roving focus keeps one tab stop for the whole bar: `Tab` enters it once and leaves it once,
  which is what makes a menu bar usable without forty presses.
- `MenubarLabel` inside a `MenubarGroup` is that group's accessible name.
- Shortcut hints are text. Register the keys yourself, or a screen reader will announce a
  shortcut that does nothing.

## Responsive behavior

A menubar is a desktop pattern. Its default bar is a single fixed-height flex row; it does not
automatically wrap triggers. Keep labels short, constrain panels to the available width, and
supply layout classes if wrapping or vertical presentation is required. For touch, prefer `dropdown-menu` behind a single
trigger, or a `navigation-menu`; long-pressing a menu bar is not a gesture anyone expects.

## Performance

- One portal per open menu; a closed bar mounts only its triggers.
- No motion on the bar itself, and the open panel is the same `opacity` + `scale` transition
  as every other popup in the library.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip). The item parts come from `dropdown-menu` through a
  `registryDependencies` entry, so the two install once and the menu behaviour is one file.

## Notes for AI

- Use `menubar` only for an application shell. For a site's navigation, links are the
  correct element and `navigation-menu` is the right component.
- Wrap each top-level menu in `MenubarMenu`; a bare `MenubarTrigger` has no menu to open.
- Keep the bar to a handful of menus. Each one is a click away from invisible content.

# Code block

Install commands, source snippets, and tool output.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block
```

The block installs `button` for the copy and fold controls, and `code-highlight` — the Shiki adapter — for syntax
colouring. That second item is only downloaded when a block actually asks for a `language`.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority shiki lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/code-highlight](https://cadence.dev/r/code-highlight.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all twelve target files, including Button, both Code Highlight files and
every shared `lib/` file. Keep the mirrored `cadence/` tree, relative imports
and shipped `"use client"` directives intact. The provider files and `motion`
are required imports; wrapping your application in `CadenceProvider` is optional.
Complete the base theme setup linked above, including Cadence's easing tokens,
and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. These payloads contain no additional
code-block-specific CSS or assets. Usage, the top specimen and every example
use only the dependencies listed above, including `lucide-react` and Button;
there are no example-only packages to install.

The CLI installs Code Highlight's files and its `shiki` dependency along with
Code Block. The on-demand download described under Command means the browser's
dynamic highlighter and grammar imports, not an optional installation step.
A string child with `language` loads that client highlighter after hydration;
omitted or unknown languages remain plain text. `CodeBlockContent` can override
the root language. For server highlighting, await `highlightCode` from
`@/components/cadence/code-highlight/highlight` and render its returned lines
through `CodeBlockLine` inside `CodeBlockContent`, retaining the original string
for Copy. Handle its `null` result with plain source. The website's Usage fences
and these Manual source blocks already receive server-highlighted nodes; that
site pipeline is separate from a consumer passing `language`. Folding limits
visible height, not the amount of text tokenized.

In Next.js App Router, Controlled folding, Controlled tabs and Updating text
need client caller modules because they own state and event callbacks. Usage
and the other static compositions can be rendered by a Server Component with
serializable props. Adding handlers, refs or function-valued props requires a
client caller; synchronous `useId` alone does not. Keep each tab's `value`, its
panel's `value` and the `values` copy map aligned. For a server-composed tabbed
block, pass `defaultTab` explicitly as Content tabs does, or supply a controlled
`tab` from a client caller. Do not rely on automatic first-tab discovery across
the server/client boundary: omitting the initial selection leaves no selected
tab and shows every panel, including after hydration. A client caller can use
the automatic fallback. The site's preview shell and package-manager
preference are not consumer setup. Hydration enables Copy, tabs, highlighting
and folding; without JavaScript the complete source remains readable.

The caller owns source text, selected content, stream/network state, errors and
the exact copy string. Pass the full string to `CodeBlockCopyButton` as `value`,
or use `values` for tab-specific text; diff markers and removed rows are excluded
only when the caller excludes them from that string. Clipboard writes require
a secure context and browser permission. A refused or unavailable clipboard
announces failure; readers can select the source manually. Keep stable content
nodes while appending text rather than keying the block by its source.

`CodeBlock` defaults to the `default` variant and size. Folding is opt-in via
`maxLines`; `defaultExpanded` defaults to false, and `expanded` with
`onExpandedChange` makes it controlled. Place `CodeBlockExpandButton` in a
footer; it appears only for overflowing content. This Manual uses the existing
controlled 16-line fold per file, keeps the complete copy string, and retains
fold state when switching installation methods. Ordinary Usage fences remain
fully expanded. Content defaults to unwrapped, unnumbered source starting at
line 1; use `lineNumbers`, `startLine`, or `wrap` deliberately. Constrain the
parent width and use native source scrolling, or `wrap` with a bounded content
height for output. Give tab lists a meaningful `label` and keep native focus,
panel relationships and source scrolling intact.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

const install = `npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block`;

export function Install() {
  return (
    <CodeBlock language="bash">
      <CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockTitle>Terminal</CodeBlockTitle>
        <CodeBlockActions>
          <CodeBlockCopyButton value={install} />
        </CodeBlockActions>
      </CodeBlockHeader>
      <CodeBlockContent>{install}</CodeBlockContent>
    </CodeBlock>
  );
}
```

## Line numbers

`lineNumbers` numbers each line from `startLine`. This excerpt begins at 42 and preserves the blank line. The gutter is generated content, excluded from selection and copied text.

<ComponentExample name="line-numbers" />

```tsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

export function LineNumbersExample() {
  const source = "const response = await fetch(url);\n\nreturn response.json();";
  return (
    <CodeBlock>
      <CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockTitle>Lines 42–44</CodeBlockTitle>
        <CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton value={source} /></CodeBlockActions>
      </CodeBlockHeader>
      <CodeBlockContent lineNumbers startLine={42}>{source}</CodeBlockContent>
    </CodeBlock>
  );
}

```

## Diff

Show `default`, `added`, `removed`, and `highlighted` lines directly. Added and removed rows carry + / − markers as well as colour. Highlighted calls attention without claiming a change. Here Copy deliberately returns the resulting source, excluding the removed row and all diff markers.

<ComponentExample name="diff" />

```tsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockLine,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

export function DiffExample() {
  const result = "for await (const chunk of reader) {\n  controller.enqueue(chunk);\n}";
  return (
    <CodeBlock>
      <CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockTitle>Stream change</CodeBlockTitle>
        <CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton value={result} /></CodeBlockActions>
      </CodeBlockHeader>
      <CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>
        <CodeBlockLine variant="removed">const chunks = await reader.read();</CodeBlockLine>
        <CodeBlockLine variant="added">{"for await (const chunk of reader) {"}</CodeBlockLine>
        <CodeBlockLine variant="highlighted">{"  controller.enqueue(chunk);"}</CodeBlockLine>
        <CodeBlockLine>{"}"}</CodeBlockLine>
      </CodeBlockContent>
    </CodeBlock>
  );
}

```

## Folding a long file

`maxLines` measures and clamps a fold without cropping the string. The footer reserves room for its measured toggle to avoid moving later sections during hydration. The first file starts collapsed, the second uses `defaultExpanded`, and the short file has no dead toggle. Copy still returns the entire source. Use the footer button to expand, collapse, or reverse the fold mid-flight.

<ComponentExample name="folding" />

```tsx
import { FileCode2Icon } from "lucide-react";
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockExpandButton,
  CodeBlockFooter,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

const SOURCE = `export async function stream({ prompt, signal }: StreamOptions) {
  const response = await fetch("/api/chat", {
    method: "POST",
    body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }),
    signal,
  });

  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(await response.text());

  const reader = response.body?.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream());

  for await (const chunk of reader) {
    controller.enqueue(chunk);
    if (signal.aborted) break;
  }
};`;

export function SourceExample() {
  return (
    <CodeBlock maxLines={6} language="tsx">
      <CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockTitle><FileCode2Icon />app/api/chat/route.ts</CodeBlockTitle>
        <CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton value={SOURCE} /></CodeBlockActions>
      </CodeBlockHeader>
      <CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>{SOURCE}</CodeBlockContent>
      <CodeBlockFooter className="min-h-[calc(--spacing(12)+1px)] justify-center"><CodeBlockExpandButton /></CodeBlockFooter>
    </CodeBlock>
  );
}


export function FoldingExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <SourceExample />
      <CodeBlock maxLines={3} defaultExpanded>
        <CodeBlockHeader><CodeBlockTitle>Initially expanded</CodeBlockTitle></CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockContent>{SOURCE}</CodeBlockContent>
        <CodeBlockFooter className="min-h-[calc(--spacing(12)+1px)]"><CodeBlockExpandButton /></CodeBlockFooter>
      </CodeBlock>
      <CodeBlock maxLines={3}>
        <CodeBlockHeader><CodeBlockTitle>A short file needs no toggle</CodeBlockTitle></CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockContent>{"export const ready = true;"}</CodeBlockContent>
        <CodeBlockFooter className="min-h-[calc(--spacing(12)+1px)]"><CodeBlockExpandButton /></CodeBlockFooter>
      </CodeBlock>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Tool output

Output uses `size="sm"`, `wrap`, and a bounded scrolling source. This fixed error uses `variant="destructive"`; the caller supplies the error text. No tokenizer or request is needed for plain tool output.

<ComponentExample name="tool-output" />

```tsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

export function ToolOutputExample() {
  const stderr = "Error: Unable to write the generated report because the destination directory is read-only. Choose a writable destination and run the command again.\n\nNo files were changed.";
  return (
    <CodeBlock variant="destructive" size="sm">
      <CodeBlockHeader><CodeBlockTitle>run_shell · exit 1</CodeBlockTitle></CodeBlockHeader>
      <CodeBlockContent wrap className="max-h-48">{stderr}</CodeBlockContent>
    </CodeBlock>
  );
}

```

## Floating actions

Place `CodeBlockActions` directly inside the block, without a header. Hover or keyboard focus reveals Copy; a device without hover keeps it visible. The invisible action remains in the tab order so it can reveal itself on focus.

<ComponentExample name="floating-actions" />

```tsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

export function FloatingActionsExample() {
  const output = "Build complete.\nGenerated 74 routes.\nNo deployment was requested.";
  return (
    <CodeBlock>
      <CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton value={output} /></CodeBlockActions>
      <CodeBlockContent>{output}</CodeBlockContent>
    </CodeBlock>
  );
}

```

## Content tabs

These are content tabs for the same install command, separate from the block’s visual `variant`. Arrow keys and Home/End select a panel. `values` makes Copy follow the current tab. Inactive panels remain mounted and hidden, retaining their source nodes and scroll position; only the active source is in the tab order.

<ComponentExample name="content-tabs" />

```tsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockPanel,
  CodeBlockTab,
  CodeBlockTabs,

  pnpm: "pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block",
  npm: "npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block",
  yarn: "yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block",
};

export function ContentTabsExample() {
  return (
    <CodeBlock defaultTab="pnpm" language="bash">
      <CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockTabs label="Package manager">
          <CodeBlockTab value="pnpm">pnpm</CodeBlockTab>
          <CodeBlockTab value="npm">npm</CodeBlockTab>
          <CodeBlockTab value="yarn">yarn</CodeBlockTab>
        </CodeBlockTabs>

      </CodeBlockHeader>

      <CodeBlockPanel value="yarn">{INSTALL.yarn}</CodeBlockPanel>
    </CodeBlock>
  );
}

```

## Highlighting

A string child with `language="tsx"` loads the Shiki adapter and its grammar dynamically. The content can override the root language, as the JSON block does. An unknown language stays plain and readable. The initial server output stays visible while highlighting loads; theme token variables recolour it without replacing the code.

<ComponentExample name="highlighting" />

```tsx

```
