## Controlled folding

The caller owns `expanded` and handles `onExpandedChange`. The external buttons demonstrate API updates; the native fold button updates the same state. API updates keep the same source node; normal pointer and keyboard focus behavior still applies.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-fold" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockExpandButton,
  CodeBlockFooter,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

const SOURCE = `export async function stream({ prompt, signal }: StreamOptions) {
  const response = await fetch("/api/chat", {
    method: "POST",
    body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }),
    signal,
  });

  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(await response.text());

  const reader = response.body?.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream());

  for await (const chunk of reader) {
    controller.enqueue(chunk);
    if (signal.aborted) break;
  }
};`;

export function ControlledFoldExample() {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setExpanded(true)}>Expand from outside</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setExpanded(false)}>Collapse from outside</Button>
      </div>
      <CodeBlock maxLines={4} expanded={expanded} onExpandedChange={setExpanded}>
        <CodeBlockHeader><CodeBlockTitle>Caller-owned fold</CodeBlockTitle></CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>{SOURCE}</CodeBlockContent>
        <CodeBlockFooter className="min-h-[calc(--spacing(12)+1px)]"><CodeBlockExpandButton /></CodeBlockFooter>
      </CodeBlock>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Controlled tabs

The caller owns `tab` and handles `onTabChange`. The external action selects the related output, while the tabs still support native keyboard navigation. Copy follows the controlled selection. This state is independent of the package-manager example.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-tabs" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockPanel,
  CodeBlockTab,
  CodeBlockTabs,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

export function ControlledTabsExample() {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState("source");
  const values = { source: "export const ready = true;", output: "ready: true" };
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setTab("output")}>Show output from outside</Button>
      <CodeBlock tab={tab} onTabChange={setTab}>
        <CodeBlockHeader>
          <CodeBlockTabs label="Source or output">
            <CodeBlockTab value="source">Source</CodeBlockTab>
            <CodeBlockTab value="output">Output</CodeBlockTab>
          </CodeBlockTabs>
          <CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton values={values} /></CodeBlockActions>
        </CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockPanel value="source">{values.source}</CodeBlockPanel>
        <CodeBlockPanel value="output">{values.output}</CodeBlockPanel>
      </CodeBlock>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Updating text

Append a local chunk to both a plain output string and highlighted source. These are explicit caller events, not a simulated network stream. Keep the same content nodes: plain output remains one text node, finished highlighted lines retain their identity, and Copy always receives the current complete string. Reset is also caller-owned.

<ComponentExample name="updating-text" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

export function UpdatingTextExample() {
  const [chunks, setChunks] = useState(0);
  const output = `Build started.\n${"Checked another route.\n".repeat(chunks)}`;
  const source = `export const ready = true;\n${"// Checked another route.\n".repeat(chunks)}`;
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setChunks((count) => count + 1)}>Append a local chunk</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setChunks(0)}>Reset text</Button>
      </div>
      <CodeBlock>
        <CodeBlockHeader>
          <CodeBlockTitle>Plain output</CodeBlockTitle>
          <CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton value={output} /></CodeBlockActions>
        </CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockContent className="max-h-48">{output}</CodeBlockContent>
      </CodeBlock>
      <CodeBlock language="tsx">
        <CodeBlockHeader>
          <CodeBlockTitle>Highlighted source</CodeBlockTitle>
          <CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton value={source} /></CodeBlockActions>
        </CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockContent lineNumbers className="max-h-48">{source}</CodeBlockContent>
      </CodeBlock>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Without motion

The first block explicitly uses `mode="none"`: copying and folding resolve immediately. The nested `mode="full"` block opts its content tabs back into full motion; the operating system’s reduced preference still takes precedence. Ordinary examples elsewhere on this page inherit the site header settings.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
import { FileCode2Icon } from "lucide-react";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
```

## When to use

- A source snippet the reader is meant to copy: an install command, a route handler, a config file.
- An answer from an assistant, where the block sits inside a message and the reader may want the code out of it.
- Tool calls and their output — a shell run, a stack trace, a JSON payload — where the reader scans rather than reads.
- A diff or a patch, where added and removed lines have to be distinguishable at a glance and without colour.
- A long file that would dominate the page: cap it with `maxLines` and let the reader unfold it.
- One snippet in several forms — an install per package manager, a source file and its output — where the reader
  should not have to scroll past variants that are not theirs.

## When not to use

- A single value the reader copies — an API key, a URL, an id. Use the copy button on its own; a bordered code
  surface gives a one-line value more weight than it deserves.
- Inline code in a sentence. Use `<code>`, which the page's typeset styles.
- Content that is not code and not output: a quote, a log line with no structure, a terminal transcript with
  interactive prompts. A block that looks like code but is not sets the wrong expectation about copying.
- A whole editor. This is a viewer; it has no caret, no selection model of its own, and no undo.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CodeBlock` | `variant`, `size`, native `div` props | `variant`: `default` \| `destructive`. `size`: `default` \| `sm`. |
| | `maxLines`, `expanded`, `defaultExpanded`, `onExpandedChange` | Additive fold. Uncontrolled unless `expanded` is passed. |
| | `language` | Additive. Highlights a string child; an unknown name renders plainly. |
| | `defaultTab`, `tab`, `onTabChange` | Additive switcher. Holds the selection the tabs, the panels and the copy button share. |
| `CodeBlockHeader` | native `div` props | Sits above the source and draws a full-width rule between the label and the code. |
| `CodeBlockTitle` | native `div` props | Truncates. The selected tab's text style — 12px, medium, foreground, on the same 24px line box — so a header reads the same with or without a switcher. Wrap it in an anchor to link to the file. |
| `CodeBlockTabs` | `label`, native `div` props | Additive. `role="tablist"`, one tab stop, arrow keys move within it. Needs a `CodeBlock` parent. |
| `CodeBlockTab` | `value` (required), native `button` props | Additive. `role="tab"`; only the selected one renders the shared pill. |
| `CodeBlockActions` | native `div` props | In a header it sits at the end; on its own it floats. |
| `CodeBlockCopyButton` | `value` or `values`, all `Button` props | Copies `value`, or `values[tab]` when the block switches variants. `variant` defaults to `ghost`, `size` to `icon-xs`. |
| `CodeBlockContent` | `wrap`, `lineNumbers`, `startLine`, `language`, native `pre` props | Always `dir="ltr"` and focusable (`tabIndex={0}`; pass `-1` to remove it). `language` overrides the block's. |
| `CodeBlockPanel` | `value` (required), all `CodeBlockContent` props | Additive. One variant: renders the content, stays mounted, hidden while another tab is selected. |
| `CodeBlockLine` | `variant`, native `span` props | `default` \| `added` \| `removed` \| `highlighted`. |
| `CodeBlockFooter` | native `div` props | Sits below the source and draws the matching rule above it. |
| `CodeBlockExpandButton` | all `Button` props | Additive. Renders nothing unless the block overflows. |

`CodeBlockContent` takes its `id` from the block, which is what `CodeBlockExpandButton` points
`aria-controls` at. If you pass an `id` of your own for an anchor link, pass the same value to the button's
`aria-controls` as well.

Highlighting is a second item, installed automatically as a dependency of `code-block`:

| `code-highlight` | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `highlightCode` | `(code: string, language: string) => Promise<ReactNode[][] \| null>` | For a Server Component or any await. `null` when the language is not bundled. |
| `useHighlightedCode` | `(code: string, language?: string) => ReactNode[] \| null` | Client hook. `null` until the grammar loads, so the caller keeps its plain text. |
| `loadHighlighter` | `(language: string) => Promise<Highlighter \| null>` | The lower-level form: `highlight(code, state)` returns lines plus the grammar state for the next chunk. |

Every part carries a `data-slot` (`code-block`, `code-block-header`, `code-block-title`, `code-block-tabs`,
`code-block-tab`, `code-block-tab-indicator`, `code-block-actions`, `code-block-copy-button`,
`code-block-panel`, `code-block-content`, `code-block-code`, `code-block-line`, `code-block-line-content`,
`code-block-footer`, plus the additive `code-block-viewport` and `code-block-expand-button`), so a consumer can
restyle without a wrapper.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fold / unfold | viewport `height`, measured and clamped to the content | `geometry.resize` | yes (a second click retargets the spring) |
| floating actions | `opacity 0 → 1` on hover and focus-within | `data.transition` | yes |
| copy | glyph cross-fade + `scale` 0.96 → 1 | `state.morph` | yes |
| fold toggle | chevron `rotate 0 → 180`, label swaps | `state.morph` | yes |
| tab indicator | one pill shared between tabs, `layoutId` | `layout.shared` | yes (a third tab pressed mid-travel retargets it) |
| reduced | opacity stays; the chevron and height jump, the copy glyph swaps without scaling, and the tab pill appears in place instead of travelling | `geometry.resize` resolves to `{ duration: 0 }` | – |
| none | every transition resolves to zero duration; the block is in its end state on the first frame | – | – |

Three notes on the choices:

- The fold animates a **measured** height rather than a `max-height` in a class. A class would need a magic number
  per line count, and it would break the moment a line wraps. The spring is the token's, and the rendered height is
  clamped to the content so it can never settle above or below the real size.
- Under reduced motion the height change is a jump on purpose. Unfolding is information — the reader asked to see
  more lines — and a 200 ms layout tween is exactly the motion the reduced mode exists to remove.
- The tab pill is a shared element only in full mode. Reduced motion drops the `layoutId`, so the pill is painted
  where the selection landed: which tab is current is information, the travel between them is not. A panel change
  never animates its height for the same reason.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the tab list (once), the selected tab, the copy button, the source, and the fold toggle. |
| Arrow Left / Right | Moves between tabs and selects the one it lands on — a tab list is one tab stop, not one stop per tab. |
| Home / End | Jumps to the first or the last tab. |
| Arrow keys / Page Up / Page Down | Scroll the source once it has focus; a long line or a capped block scrolls without moving the page. |
| Enter / Space | Copies, selects the focused tab, or toggles the fold. |
| Cmd/Ctrl + C | Copies the selection — line numbers and diff markers are excluded, blank lines are kept. |

## Accessibility

- The source is a real `pre` > `code` and is focusable, so a keyboard user can scroll a block that overflows. A
  `max-height` on the content keeps that true for capped blocks too.
- Line numbers are drawn with generated content, so they stay out of the text selection and out of the accessibility
  tree; the code is read as code, without a column of digits.
- The copy button's accessible name is `Copy`, then `Copied`; a polite live region repeats the result, so the tick
  is confirmation, not the only signal. A refused clipboard write leaves the glyph on `Copy` rather than claiming
  success.
- Diff lines carry a `+` / `−` marker next to the tint, so the change survives a monochrome display.
- The fold toggle is a real button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the source, and it is not
  rendered at all when there is nothing to unfold.
- The switcher is the ARIA tabs pattern: `role="tablist"` with a name (`label`, "Language" by default), tabs that
  carry `aria-selected` and point `aria-controls` at their panel, one tab stop with a roving `tabindex`, and
  `role="tabpanel"` panels labelled by their tab. Inactive panels are `hidden`, which takes their focusable source
  out of the tab order.
- The block is `dir="ltr"` throughout, because code reads left to right even on an RTL page. The header follows the
  page's direction.

## Responsive behavior

- `size="sm"` tightens the padding and drops the source to `text-xs` — the right weight for output inside a
  message or a tool row.
- Long lines scroll inside the block, never the page: the source owns the overflow, and the wrapper clips it.
  The bar is thin and drawn in the theme's own grey rather than the OS's, because a native scrollbar follows the
  operating system and not the page — a dark page on a light system would otherwise get a white bar down the code.
- `wrap` is for output, not for source. Wrapped source loses its indentation structure, which is the one thing code
  formatting carries.
- On a narrow screen the header's title truncates rather than wrapping, and the actions stay reachable — a touch
  device always shows them, because there is no hover to reveal them with. The tab list scrolls sideways on its
  own when three tabs and a title do not fit, so the copy button keeps its place. That row scrolls without a bar:
  a track in a 24px control strip reads as a second seam under the label, and the arrow keys and a swipe move it
  anyway.

## Performance

The initially folded viewport reserves the built-in line height and padding before hydration, so
measuring a fold does not pull later document anchors upward. With JavaScript disabled the cap is
absent and the complete source stays readable. Custom content line height or padding may change
that estimate; provide a suitable SSR layout if overriding those metrics.

- Without a `language`, a string child is one text node: streaming a chunk does not rebuild a subtree, only the
  changed text is painted. With a `language`, each finished line is one node that is never re-created, and the
  line being written is the only one re-tokenized.
- One `ResizeObserver` per foldable block, and none for a block that cannot fold. The measurement is a read inside
  the observer callback, never during render.
- The fold animates `height` — a layout property, and the one place in this component that touches layout. It is
  scoped to the source viewport and moves following document content, is clamped, and it resolves to zero duration under
  reduced and none.
- Everything else is `opacity` and `scale` on small elements: two glyphs and a chevron.
- Shiki is a dynamic import. A block with no `language` never loads it; a block with one loads the engine and a
  single grammar, both cached for the rest of the session. `getLoadedLanguages()` is checked first, so the second
  `tsx` block on a page does not re-load anything.
- Tokenizing runs on the main thread. Its cost depends on the grammar, source and device;
  a thousand-line file is not free: cap it with `maxLines`, or hand the nodes in from a Server Component with
  `highlightCode`.

## Notes for AI

- Reach for `code-block` for code, terminal output, tool calls, logs, diffs and stack traces. Never hand-roll a
  `<pre>` — the copy affordance, the focus ring, and the fold are the point.
- Give the block a `value` to copy that matches what is displayed. Passing a truncated string is the most common
  bug: the reader copies less than they can see.
- Tool output is not source: `size="sm"` with `wrap` and a `max-h-*` on the content. Errors use
  `variant="destructive"` on `CodeBlock`; do not recolour the text.
- When a stream is still arriving, keep rendering the same `<CodeBlockContent>` and let the string grow. Do not key
  the block by content, and do not remount it — a remount restarts the fold measurement, drops focus, and throws
  away the cached lines, so the whole block is tokenized again on the next chunk.
- Pass `language` for source, and leave it out for tool output, logs and stack traces: a tokenizer that guesses at
  output colours noise, and the plain path is the cheaper one.
- The first paint is plain while the highlighter chunk loads. Do not hide the block until it is coloured; showing
  the text immediately is the point.
- Use `maxLines` for anything longer than a screenful, with `CodeBlockExpandButton` in the footer. Do not cap the
  block by cropping the string.
- When a snippet has more than one right form — an install for pnpm, npm and yarn, a source and its output — use
  `CodeBlockTabs` / `CodeBlockTab` / `CodeBlockPanel`, and give the header's `CodeBlockCopyButton` `values` so it
  copies the variant on screen. Do not stack two blocks with a hand-rolled toggle, and do not put unrelated files
  behind tabs: a tab is the same snippet in another form, not a second snippet.

# Command

Search and run actions from a keyboard-driven command palette.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/command
```

For manual installation copy `command/index.tsx`, install `cmdk` and `lucide-react`, and install the
`dialog`, `input-group`, `cadence-utils`, and `cadence-provider` registry dependencies.

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
```

Copy all fourteen target files, including every shared `lib/` file and the
Button, Dialog, Input, Textarea and Input Group sources. Input Group imports
all three controls even when Command only renders its input. Keep the mirrored
`cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives intact. The
provider files and `motion` are required imports; wrapping your application in
`CadenceProvider` is optional.

Complete the linked base theme setup, including Cadence's easing tokens, and
ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. These payloads contain no additional
Command-specific CSS or assets. Inline commands do not animate. CommandDialog
inherits Dialog's scale and fade in full mode, opacity only in reduced, and
zero-duration transitions in none. Filtering, highlighting and list height
changes remain immediate. The system reduced-motion preference also applies
without a provider and to an explicitly nested full provider.

Usage, the top palette and all eleven body examples use this dependency graph.
Button is already included through Dialog and Input Group; `cmdk` also supplies
the examples' `useCommandState`. No example-only package or file is needed.

Keep Usage and the stateful palette, keyword, shortcut, controlled, caller-owned
result and Without motion compositions in client modules. A custom filter is
a function prop; SearchableList also subscribes to the actual Command store
with `useCommandState`, so A custom filter and Composing the search input need
a client caller too. Refs, event handlers and other function props require
the same boundary. Static compositions such as Keyboard and pointer navigation,
An unavailable input and Persistent help while filtering can be rendered from a Server Component
with serializable props; the examples' client directives remain valid. A
Server Component can also render a client composition with serializable data.
The site's preview shell is not consumer setup. Search, selection and dialog
interaction require hydrated JavaScript.

Compose `CommandInput` and `CommandList` inside `Command`, with items inside
groups. `CommandDialog` supplies the dialog surface, title and description;
it does not create a Command root or an opener. The caller owns open state,
action execution, routing, requests and any global shortcut listener.
`CommandShortcut` is only a visual hint. Root `value` controls the highlight;
input `value` controls the query; item `onSelect` runs the action. Supply stable
item values and optional keywords for cmdk's local filter, or set
`shouldFilter={false}` and manage results in the caller.

Give Command an accessible `label`. Reuse Usage's SearchableList inside that
root when hiding a zero-result list and announcing empty feedback outside it;
its input keeps `aria-controls` pointing to the mounted list and reports
`aria-expanded={false}` while empty. CommandInput retains cmdk's `asChild`
input composition, while the Base UI dialog uses `render`. Disabled items
cannot run and are skipped by arrow navigation. The list scrolls within its
300px maximum height; the parent owns inline width. The inline examples use
an unmatched initial value to avoid cmdk scrolling its default highlighted
item into view on mount; dialog palettes retain the default first highlight.

## Usage

The common palette keeps the caller's action and open state together. Its search and list are inside an explicit Command root.
The local SearchableList composition reads cmdk's result count with useCommandState. A miss collapses the suggestion
list and announces the empty text outside it. The composed input sets aria-expanded accordingly; the same list and
its aria-controls target remain mounted. This avoids presenting an expanded listbox without options.

```tsx
"use client";

import { useCommandState } from "cmdk";
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";
import { Command, CommandDialog, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from "@/components/cadence/command";

function SearchableList({ children, emptyMessage = "No actions found.", ...inputProps }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof CommandInput>, "children" | "asChild"> & { children: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: string }) {
  const empty = useCommandState((state) => state.search.length > 0 && state.filtered.count === 0);
  return (
    <>
      <CommandInput {...inputProps} asChild>
        <InputGroupInput aria-expanded={!empty} />
      </CommandInput>
      {empty && <CommandEmpty><span role="status">{emptyMessage}</span></CommandEmpty>}
      <CommandList hidden={empty}>{children}</CommandList>
    </>
  );
}

export function Palette({
  label = "Open command palette",
  showCloseButton = false,
}: {
  label?: string;
  showCloseButton?: boolean;
}) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [executed, setExecuted] = useState("No action yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-sm flex-col gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        {label}
      </Button>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {executed}
      </p>
      <CommandDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Workspace commands"
        description="Find an action, then press Enter to run it."
        showCloseButton={showCloseButton}
      >
        <Command label="Workspace actions">
          <SearchableList placeholder="Search workspace...">

            <CommandGroup heading="Workspace">
              {["projects", "search", "settings"].map((value) => (
                <CommandItem
                  key={value}
                  value={value}
                  onSelect={(action) => {
                    setExecuted(`Executed: ${action}`);
                    setOpen(false);
                  }}
                >
                  {value}
                </CommandItem>
              ))}
            </CommandGroup>
          </SearchableList>
        </Command>
      </CommandDialog>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Dialog palette

Keep Command explicit inside CommandDialog. This named palette supplies its own title and description, enables the built-in close button, and closes after an action. The top palette uses the default hidden close button; Escape still dismisses it. Each opener owns independent open and executed-action state. Install `@cadence/button` for the buttons in these examples.

## Keywords and disabled actions

Inline examples reserve the unmatched initial `defaultValue="none"` to start without a highlight.
cmdk otherwise scrolls its default highlighted item into view on mount, which can move a long page.
Typing or using arrow keys then selects and scrolls the actual matching item normally.
The controlled example uses the same initial unmatched value; dialog palettes retain the default first item.
SearchableList shows empty feedback only for a nonempty query with zero registered matches. The initial
nonempty result layout stays the same in server markup and after hydration. Filtering and counting stay with cmdk.

Stable item values and optional keywords participate in local fuzzy filtering. Search for user to find Profile or find to find Search files. Disabled items remain visible when they match, but arrows skip them and they cannot run. Groups hide when none of their items match; the default separator hides during a search.

<ComponentExample name="keywords" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useCommandState } from "cmdk";
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, CommandSeparator } from "@/components/cadence/command";

function SearchableList({ children, emptyMessage = "No actions found.", ...inputProps }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof CommandInput>, "children" | "asChild"> & { children: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: string }) {
  const empty = useCommandState((state) => state.search.length > 0 && state.filtered.count === 0);
  return (
    <>
      <CommandInput {...inputProps} asChild>
        <InputGroupInput aria-expanded={!empty} />
      </CommandInput>
      {empty && <CommandEmpty><span role="status">{emptyMessage}</span></CommandEmpty>}
      <CommandList hidden={empty}>{children}</CommandList>
    </>
  );
}

export function Keywords() {
  const [executed, setExecuted] = useState("No action yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-sm flex-col gap-3">
      <Command defaultValue="none" label="Account actions" className="rounded-lg border">
        <SearchableList placeholder="Try user or find...">

          <CommandGroup heading="Workspace">
            <CommandItem value="search" keywords={["find"]} onSelect={setExecuted}>
              Search files
            </CommandItem>
          </CommandGroup>
          <CommandSeparator />
          <CommandGroup heading="Account">
            <CommandItem value="profile" keywords={["account", "user"]} onSelect={setExecuted}>
              Profile
            </CommandItem>
            <CommandItem value="billing" disabled>
              Billing unavailable
            </CommandItem>
          </CommandGroup>
        </SearchableList>
      </Command>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {executed}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Shortcut hints

CommandShortcut displays a hint beside an action. It registers no global shortcut. Click or press Enter here to record the command; an application owns any real routing or keyboard listener and its cleanup.

<ComponentExample name="shortcuts" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useCommandState } from "cmdk";
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, CommandShortcut } from "@/components/cadence/command";

function SearchableList({ children, emptyMessage = "No actions found.", ...inputProps }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof CommandInput>, "children" | "asChild"> & { children: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: string }) {

  return (
    <>
      <CommandInput {...inputProps} asChild>
        <InputGroupInput aria-expanded={!empty} />
      </CommandInput>
      {empty && <CommandEmpty><span role="status">{emptyMessage}</span></CommandEmpty>}
      <CommandList hidden={empty}>{children}</CommandList>
    </>
  );
}

export function Shortcuts() {
  const [executed, setExecuted] = useState("No action yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-sm flex-col gap-3">
      <Command defaultValue="none" label="Navigation actions" className="rounded-lg border">
        <SearchableList placeholder="Search navigation...">

          <CommandGroup heading="Navigation">
            <CommandItem value="settings" onSelect={setExecuted}>
              Settings<CommandShortcut>⌘,</CommandShortcut>
            </CommandItem>
            <CommandItem value="projects" onSelect={setExecuted}>
              Projects<CommandShortcut>⌘P</CommandShortcut>
```

## Controlled highlight and query

The root value is the highlighted command, not a submitted form value or a record that an action ran. CommandInput owns a separate search string. Arrow keys only move the highlight; item onSelect records execution. The external button clears the query and highlights settings without running it.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useCommandState } from "cmdk";
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from "@/components/cadence/command";

function SearchableList({ children, emptyMessage = "No actions found.", ...inputProps }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof CommandInput>, "children" | "asChild"> & { children: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: string }) {
  const empty = useCommandState((state) => state.search.length > 0 && state.filtered.count === 0);
  return (
    <>
      <CommandInput {...inputProps} asChild>
        <InputGroupInput aria-expanded={!empty} />
      </CommandInput>
      {empty && <CommandEmpty><span role="status">{emptyMessage}</span></CommandEmpty>}
      <CommandList hidden={empty}>{children}</CommandList>
    </>
  );
}

export function Controlled() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  const [highlight, setHighlight] = useState("none");
  const [executed, setExecuted] = useState("none");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-sm flex-col gap-3">
      <Command label="Controlled actions" value={highlight} onValueChange={setHighlight} className="rounded-lg border">
        <SearchableList placeholder="Search controlled actions..." value={query} onValueChange={setQuery}>

          <CommandGroup heading="Workspace">
            {["projects", "settings"].map((value) => (
              <CommandItem key={value} value={value} onSelect={setExecuted}>
                {value}
              </CommandItem>
            ))}
          </CommandGroup>
        </SearchableList>
      </Command>
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        onClick={() => {
          setQuery("");
          setHighlight("settings");
        }}
      >
        Highlight settings externally
      </Button>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Query: {query || "empty"}; highlighted: {highlight || "none"}; executed: {executed}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## A custom filter

A custom filter returns a score from 0 to 1. This fixed policy accepts prefixes of stable values or keywords, ignoring case; pref matches Settings through preferences, while ttings does not. Filtering and list height update immediately.

<ComponentExample name="filter" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useCommandState } from "cmdk";
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from "@/components/cadence/command";

function SearchableList({ children, emptyMessage = "No actions found.", ...inputProps }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof CommandInput>, "children" | "asChild"> & { children: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: string }) {
  const empty = useCommandState((state) => state.search.length > 0 && state.filtered.count === 0);
  return (
    <>
      <CommandInput {...inputProps} asChild>
        <InputGroupInput aria-expanded={!empty} />
      </CommandInput>
      {empty && <CommandEmpty><span role="status">{emptyMessage}</span></CommandEmpty>}
      <CommandList hidden={empty}>{children}</CommandList>
    </>
  );
}

export function PrefixFilter() {
  return (
    <Command
      defaultValue="none"
      label="Prefix actions"
      className="w-full max-w-sm rounded-lg border"
      filter={(value, search, keywords = []) =>
        [value, ...keywords].some((text) => text.toLowerCase().startsWith(search.trim().toLowerCase())) ? 1 : 0
      }
    >
      <SearchableList placeholder="Match a prefix, such as pref..." emptyMessage="No prefix matches.">

        <CommandGroup heading="Actions">
          <CommandItem value="settings" keywords={["preferences"]}>
            Settings
          </CommandItem>
          <CommandItem value="projects">Projects</CommandItem>
        </CommandGroup>
      </SearchableList>
    </Command>
  );
}
```

## Caller-owned results

Set shouldFilter=false when the caller supplies the visible result set and its order. This example filters a fixed local city array; it makes no network request. The caller supplies the empty text; SearchableList reads the actual registered result count, collapses the empty list and announces the message outside it. An application owns request cancellation, loading, errors and authorization.

<ComponentExample name="results" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useCommandState } from "cmdk";
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from "@/components/cadence/command";

function SearchableList({ children, emptyMessage = "No actions found.", ...inputProps }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof CommandInput>, "children" | "asChild"> & { children: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: string }) {
  const empty = useCommandState((state) => state.search.length > 0 && state.filtered.count === 0);
  return (
    <>
      <CommandInput {...inputProps} asChild>
        <InputGroupInput aria-expanded={!empty} />
      </CommandInput>
      {empty && <CommandEmpty><span role="status">{emptyMessage}</span></CommandEmpty>}
      <CommandList hidden={empty}>{children}</CommandList>
    </>
  );
}

export function CallerResults() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  const [executed, setExecuted] = useState("No action yet");
  const results = ["Paris", "London", "Tokyo"].filter((city) => city.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()));
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-sm flex-col gap-3">
      <Command defaultValue="none" label="City actions" shouldFilter={false} className="rounded-lg border">
        <SearchableList placeholder="Search local city data..." value={query} onValueChange={setQuery} emptyMessage="No city found.">
          <CommandGroup heading="Cities">
            {results.map((city) => (
              <CommandItem key={city} value={city} onSelect={setExecuted}>
                Open {city}
              </CommandItem>
            ))}
          </CommandGroup>
        </SearchableList>
      </Command>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {executed}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard and pointer navigation

The left list stops at its first and last enabled item and keeps the default Ctrl+N/J/P/K bindings. The right list loops with arrows, disables those optional bindings, and disables pointer-hover highlighting. Clicking an enabled item still activates it. Both lists skip the disabled middle row; neither setting changes native text editing.

<ComponentExample name="navigation" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Command, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from "@/components/cadence/command";

export function Navigation() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
      <Command defaultValue="none" label="Bounded actions" loop={false} className="rounded-lg border">
        <CommandInput placeholder="Bounded; Ctrl+N enabled" />
        <CommandList>
          <CommandGroup heading="Bounded">
            <CommandItem value="first">First</CommandItem>
            <CommandItem value="unavailable" disabled>
              Unavailable
            </CommandItem>
            <CommandItem value="last">Last</CommandItem>
          </CommandGroup>
        </CommandList>
      </Command>
      <Command
        defaultValue="none"
        label="Looping actions"
        loop
        vimBindings={false}
        disablePointerSelection
        className="rounded-lg border"
      >
        <CommandInput placeholder="Looping; arrow keys" />
        <CommandList>
          <CommandGroup heading="Looping">
            <CommandItem value="first">First</CommandItem>
            <CommandItem value="unavailable" disabled>
              Unavailable
            </CommandItem>
            <CommandItem value="last">Last</CommandItem>
          </CommandGroup>
        </CommandList>
      </Command>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## An unavailable input

Disable the input when search is unavailable, and separately disable every unavailable action. Disabling the search field alone does not disable other items. The native disabled input cannot receive keyboard focus.

```tsx
          </CommandItem>

```

## Persistent help while filtering

forceMount on the Help group and its item keeps the help action available for every query. alwaysRender keeps the decorative rule visible. The Workspace group still follows normal filtering and hides on a miss. Persistent actions need their own valid behavior in the application; this specimen only demonstrates visibility.

```tsx
import { Command, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, CommandSeparator } from "@/components/cadence/command";

export function MountedActions() {

        </CommandGroup>

          </CommandItem>

```

## Composing the search input

SearchableList uses CommandInput's cmdk asChild composition API with one ref-forwarding InputGroupInput. The child sets truthful aria-expanded while preserving input-group styling; this example also supplies native inputMode and autoComplete. The Base UI dialog continues to use its own render API.

<ComponentExample name="custom-input" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useCommandState } from "cmdk";
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from "@/components/cadence/command";

function SearchableList({ children, emptyMessage = "No actions found.", ...inputProps }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof CommandInput>, "children" | "asChild"> & { children: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: string }) {
  const empty = useCommandState((state) => state.search.length > 0 && state.filtered.count === 0);
  return (
    <>
      <CommandInput {...inputProps} asChild>
        <InputGroupInput aria-expanded={!empty} />
      </CommandInput>
      {empty && <CommandEmpty><span role="status">{emptyMessage}</span></CommandEmpty>}
      <CommandList hidden={empty}>{children}</CommandList>
    </>
  );
}

export function CustomInput() {
  return (
    <Command defaultValue="none" label="Custom search field" className="w-full max-w-sm rounded-lg border">
      <SearchableList placeholder="Search with a composed input..." inputMode="search" autoComplete="off">

        <CommandGroup heading="Workspace">
          <CommandItem value="projects">Projects</CommandItem>
          <CommandItem value="settings">Settings</CommandItem>
        </CommandGroup>
      </SearchableList>
    </Command>
  );
}
```

## Without motion

The first palette is explicitly inside mode=none from its first mount. The second opts back into full within that subtree; the operating system reduced-motion preference still wins. Ordinary examples inherit the site header mode and speed. Inline filtering and highlighting remain immediate in every mode.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useCommandState } from "cmdk";
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Command, CommandDialog, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from "@/components/cadence/command";

function SearchableList({ children, emptyMessage = "No actions found.", ...inputProps }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof CommandInput>, "children" | "asChild"> & { children: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: string }) {
  const empty = useCommandState((state) => state.search.length > 0 && state.filtered.count === 0);
  return (
    <>
      <CommandInput {...inputProps} asChild>
        <InputGroupInput aria-expanded={!empty} />
      </CommandInput>
      {empty && <CommandEmpty><span role="status">{emptyMessage}</span></CommandEmpty>}
      <CommandList hidden={empty}>{children}</CommandList>
    </>
  );
}

function Palette({
  label = "Open command palette",
  showCloseButton = false,
}: {
  label?: string;
  showCloseButton?: boolean;
}) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [executed, setExecuted] = useState("No action yet");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-sm flex-col gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        {label}
      </Button>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {executed}
      </p>
      <CommandDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Workspace commands"
        description="Find an action, then press Enter to run it."
        showCloseButton={showCloseButton}
      >
        <Command label="Workspace actions">
          <SearchableList placeholder="Search workspace...">

            <CommandGroup heading="Workspace">
              {["projects", "search", "settings"].map((value) => (
                <CommandItem
                  key={value}
                  value={value}
                  onSelect={(action) => {
                    setExecuted(`Executed: ${action}`);
                    setOpen(false);
                  }}
                >
                  {value}
                </CommandItem>
              ))}
            </CommandGroup>
          </SearchableList>
        </Command>
      </CommandDialog>
    </div>
  );
}

export function WithoutMotion() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="flex w-full flex-wrap gap-4">
        <Palette label="Open instant palette" />
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Palette label="Open nested full palette" />
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Search application actions without navigating a menu hierarchy.
- Offer keyboard navigation across grouped commands.
- Present a controlled command palette in a dialog.

## When not to use

- Use `Combobox` to choose a form value.
- Use `DropdownMenu` for a short list without search.
- Use a search page for remote results requiring pagination.

## API

| Part | Props | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Command` | cmdk root props: `label`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `filter`, `shouldFilter`, `loop`, `vimBindings`, `disablePointerSelection` | `shouldFilter=true`, `loop=false`, `vimBindings=true`, `disablePointerSelection=false`; value is the highlighted command |
| `CommandDialog` | Base UI Dialog root props, `title`, `description`, `className`, `showCloseButton`, required `children` | title `"Command Palette"`, description `"Search for a command to run..."`, `showCloseButton=false` |
| `CommandInput` | cmdk input props, `value`, `onValueChange`, `placeholder`, `disabled` | Typing filters locally; the root supplies the accessible label |
| `CommandList` | cmdk list props, `className` | Scrollable, max height 300px; no height tween |
| `CommandEmpty` | cmdk empty props, `className` | Shown when no command matches |
| `CommandGroup` | cmdk group props, `heading`, `value`, `forceMount` | Give a heading or unique value |
| `CommandItem` | cmdk item props, `value`, `keywords`, `disabled`, `onSelect` | Enter or click runs the action; disabled rows are skipped |
| `CommandSeparator` | cmdk separator props, `alwaysRender` | Hidden during search unless always rendered |
| `CommandShortcut` | span props, `className` | Hint only; no keyboard handler |

Parts merge user classes last and forward refs and remaining props. cmdk retains its `asChild` API;
the Base UI dialog uses `render`. The check glyph follows upstream's `data-checked`; the highlight's
`data-selected` is not a committed choice.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | dialog opacity 0 to 1 and scale from `--motion-scale-in`; backdrop opacity 0 to 1 | `popup.anchored` via Dialog, `duration.base` / `duration.fast` | yes, CSS transitions |
| close | dialog and backdrop fade out, panel scales back in full mode | `exit.fade` via Dialog | yes |
| filter / highlight | instant replacement and background feedback, no row motion | none | n/a |
| reduced | opacity only; scale classes absent | mode durations | yes |
| none | dialog and backdrop durations resolve to zero | zero duration | n/a |

The inline command has no animation. `CommandDialog` inherits Dialog's recipes and mode branches;
it adds no transition of its own. Fixed centering translation is layout, not motion.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. Ordinary specimens inherit the site header; the named Without motion example
uses explicit fixed local providers. The Dialog surface retains Base UI callback/render/ref semantics. Command parts use
cmdk’s native string class and object style props; cmdk owns filtering and keyboard selection.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowDown / ArrowUp | Move highlight, skipping disabled rows |
| Home / End | First / last enabled item |
| Ctrl+N / J, Ctrl+P / K | Next / previous item when vimBindings is enabled (default) |
| Enter | Run the highlighted item's `onSelect` |
| Escape | Close the dialog; an inline command has no dismissal behavior |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focus traversal, trapped inside an open dialog |

## Accessibility

cmdk owns combobox/listbox roles, `aria-activedescendant`, and selected/disabled attributes.
Give `Command` a `label` to name its search field. The dialog supplies a title, description and focus trap. The caller opens it from a real button;
dismissal restores focus to the initiating control. In these examples, a zero-result list is hidden, the input reports aria-expanded=false,
and CommandEmpty announces text outside the list. No-result messages are not executable options. SearchableList must stay inside Command
because useCommandState reads that root's actual cmdk store; it adds no second filter.
Separators are decorative (`aria-hidden`) because a listbox permits options and option groups.

## Responsive behavior

The inline palette fills its container. The dialog keeps viewport margins and a desktop max width.
The list scrolls independently so the search input stays reachable on short screens.

## Performance

Filtering and list height changes are instant. No layout animation, row stagger, or application
request orchestration is added. T2 source budget: 10 KB gzip; cmdk is a declared dependency.

## Notes for AI

- Put items inside groups, inside a list, inside `Command`.
- Keep `Command` inside `CommandDialog`; the dialog does not create a cmdk root.
- Use item `onSelect`; the caller owns routing and async work.
- `CommandShortcut` registers no shortcut. Related: `combobox`, `dialog`, `dropdown-menu`.

# Toast

Transient notifications with accessible actions and dismissal.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toast
```

For manual installation copy `toast/index.tsx`, install `@base-ui/react` and `lucide-react`, and install
`button`, `cadence-utils`, and `cadence-provider`.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — transitive registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.
