4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all ten target files, including Button and every shared `lib/` file.
Keep the mirrored `cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"`
directives intact. The provider files and `motion` are required imports;
wrapping your application in `CadenceProvider` is optional. Complete the
linked base theme setup, including Cadence's easing tokens, and ensure
Tailwind scans the copied files. No additional Toast-specific CSS or assets
are required. Usage, the top preview and all eight body examples use this
same dependency graph, with no example-only package or file.

Mount one `Toaster` for the shared `toast` manager in a stable application
location, within any `CadenceProvider` that should control its motion.
`Toaster` supplies the Base UI provider, portal, viewport and notification
list, and can wrap your application children. `CadenceProvider` controls
motion; it does not mount a toaster. For an isolated notification area,
create a stable manager with `useState(createToastManager)` and pass that
same manager to its one provider. Give independently mounted viewports
distinct names through `viewportProps={{ "aria-label": "Export notifications" }}`.
The custom composition instead mounts `ToastProvider`, `ToastPortal`,
`ToastViewport` and a list that reads `useToastManager` under that provider.

Keep Usage and all eight interactive body compositions in client modules.
The shared `toast` export is a client-side manager; call `add`, `update` and
`close` from application events. Custom manager objects, hook calls, refs,
event handlers, `actionProps.onClick` and state callbacks belong in the same
client boundary. A Server Component can render a client notification
composition with serializable props or wrap children in `Toaster` using its
default manager; do not create or pass a manager across the server boundary.
The site's preview shell is not consumer setup. Notification interactions
require hydrated JavaScript.

The caller owns message data, request state, action effects and persistent
results. Keep the id returned by `add` to update or close that notification;
`close()` clears the manager's notifications. An action does not close its
toast automatically: call `close(id)` when that is the intended result.
Toaster's defaults remain Base UI's 5000ms timeout and limit of three;
`timeout={0}` keeps a notification until dismissal. Hover and focus pause
the primitive's timers. The Timers example explicitly uses a limit of two;
older limited notifications remain mounted, hidden and inert.

Full mode uses token-backed opacity and scale; reduced keeps opacity
transitions only, and none removes transitions. Base UI's direct pointer
tracking and swipe dismissal remain available in every mode. Stack positions
and natural content height update immediately. Loading is a static glyph.
`CadenceProvider`'s `timeScale` changes animation clocks, not notification
timeouts, and the system reduced-motion preference still applies to a
nested full provider. Base UI owns swipe recognition and dismissal; custom
composition selects the physical swipe direction. F6 enters the active
viewport, Tab reaches the notification and its controls, and Escape closes
the focused notification. Keep important information in persistent UI and
choose announcement priority for the message's urgency.

## Usage

Mount one toaster within your `CadenceProvider`. Call the shared manager from event handlers.

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { toast, Toaster } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

export function Notifications() {
  return (
    <Toaster>
      <Button onClick={() => toast.add({ title: "Changes saved", description: "Your workspace is up to date.", type: "success" })}>
        Save notification
      </Button>
    </Toaster>
  );
}
```

## Notification types

Types select a glyph, not request handling. Plain, success, info, warning, error and loading are fixed independent commands. Loading is a static glyph in every motion mode.

<ComponentExample name="types" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { createToastManager, Toaster } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

export function Types() {
  const [manager] = useState(createToastManager);
  return <Toaster viewportProps={{ "aria-label": "Types notifications" }} toastManager={manager} timeout={0}>
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      {([undefined, "success", "info", "warning", "error", "loading"] as const).map(type => <Button key={type ?? "plain"} variant="outline" onClick={() => manager.add({ title: `${type ?? "plain"} notification`, type })}>Show {type ?? "plain"}</Button>)}
      <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => manager.close()}>Clear types</Button>
    </div>
  </Toaster>;
}
```

## Actions and dismissal

The caller owns the undo operation and persistent result. This action explicitly closes its notification; action activation alone does not imply dismissal.

<ComponentExample name="actions" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { createToastManager, Toaster } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

export function Actions() {
  const [manager] = useState(createToastManager);
  const [result, setResult] = useState("Item available");
  return <Toaster viewportProps={{ "aria-label": "Archive notifications" }} toastManager={manager} timeout={0}>
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <Button onClick={() => {
        setResult("Item archived");
        const id = manager.add({ title: "Item archived", actionProps: { children: "Restore item", onClick: () => { setResult("Item restored"); manager.close(id); } } });
      }}>Archive item</Button>
      <p role="status">{result}</p>
    </div>
  </Toaster>;
}
```

## Announcement priority

Low priority uses polite announcements. High priority is for urgent information. Neither arrival moves focus; F6 enters the active viewport and Escape dismisses the focused toast.

<ComponentExample name="priority" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { createToastManager, Toaster } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

export function Priority() {
  const [manager] = useState(createToastManager);
  return <Toaster viewportProps={{ "aria-label": "Priority notifications" }} toastManager={manager} timeout={0}>
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => manager.add({ title: "Draft saved", priority: "low" })}>Polite notification</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => manager.add({ title: "Connection unavailable", description: "Your draft remains on this device.", type: "error", priority: "high" })}>Urgent notification</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => manager.close()}>Clear priority</Button>
    </div>
  </Toaster>;
}
```

## Caller-owned progress

Queue, finish and dismiss are explicit application events. This example performs no request and runs no simulated timer. The same manager id updates the existing toast; the persistent result remains after dismissal.

<ComponentExample name="progress" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { createToastManager, Toaster } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

export function Progress() {
  const [manager] = useState(createToastManager);
  const [id, setId] = useState<string>();
  const [result, setResult] = useState("No export queued");
  return <Toaster viewportProps={{ "aria-label": "Export notifications" }} toastManager={manager} timeout={0}>
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button disabled={!!id} onClick={() => { setId(manager.add({ title: "Export queued", type: "loading", onClose: () => setId(undefined) })); setResult("Export queued"); }}>Queue export</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" disabled={!id} onClick={() => { if (id) manager.update(id, { title: "Export ready", description: "Download it from your exports page.", type: "success" }); setResult("Export ready"); }}>Finish export</Button>
        <Button variant="ghost" disabled={!id} onClick={() => { if (id) manager.close(id); setId(undefined); }}>Dismiss export</Button>
      </div>
      <p role="status">{result}</p>
    </div>
  </Toaster>;
}
```

## Timeout and visible limit

The provider uses a 5000ms timeout and shows at most two notifications. Hovering or focusing pauses timers. The pinned primitive marks older notifications as limited rather than immediately removing them. A per-notification timeout of zero keeps a message until dismissed.

<ComponentExample name="timers" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { createToastManager, Toaster } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

export function Timers() {
  const [manager] = useState(createToastManager);
  return <Toaster viewportProps={{ "aria-label": "Timer notifications" }} toastManager={manager} timeout={5000} limit={2}>
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Button onClick={() => manager.add({ title: "Timed notification", description: "Closes after five seconds without hover or focus." })}>Add timed notification</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => manager.add({ title: "Persistent notification", timeout: 0 })}>Add persistent notification</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => manager.close()}>Clear timers</Button>
    </div>
  </Toaster>;
}
```

## Custom composition

Compose the real provider, portal, viewport and parts to customize content. This example omits the type glyph. Each specimen owns one manager and one viewport; applications normally mount one toaster for their shared manager.

<ComponentExample name="composition" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  createToastManager,
  ToastProvider,
  ToastPortal,
  ToastViewport,
  Toast,
  ToastContent,
  ToastTitle,
  ToastDescription,
  ToastAction,
  ToastClose,
  useToastManager,
 } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

function NotificationList({ direction = "right" }: { direction?: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right" }) {
  const { toasts } = useToastManager();
  return toasts.map(item => <Toast key={item.id} toast={item} swipeDirection={direction}>
    <ToastContent>
      <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1"><ToastTitle /><ToastDescription /></div>
      <ToastAction /><ToastClose />
    </ToastContent>
  </Toast>);
}
export function Composition({ direction = "right", label = "Show custom notification" }: { direction?: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right"; label?: string }) {
  const [manager] = useState(createToastManager);
  return <ToastProvider toastManager={manager} timeout={0}>
    <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => manager.add({ title: "Custom notification", description: `Swipe ${direction} or use the close button.` })}>{label}</Button>
    <ToastPortal><ToastViewport aria-label={`${label} notifications`}><NotificationList direction={direction} /></ToastViewport></ToastPortal>
  </ToastProvider>;
}
```

## Swipe directions

Each trigger owns an independent notification with a fixed physical swipe direction. Swipe recognition belongs to Base UI. Reduced and none omit Cadence's swipe-variable transform; Base UI still tracks the pointer directly with no transition in every mode. Swipe dismissal and keyboard controls remain available.

<ComponentExample name="swipe" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  createToastManager,
  ToastProvider,
  ToastPortal,
  ToastViewport,
  Toast,
  ToastContent,
  ToastTitle,
  ToastDescription,
  ToastAction,
  ToastClose,
  useToastManager,
 } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

function NotificationList({ direction = "right" }: { direction?: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right" }) {
  const { toasts } = useToastManager();
  return toasts.map(item => <Toast key={item.id} toast={item} swipeDirection={direction}>
    <ToastContent>
      <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1"><ToastTitle /><ToastDescription /></div>
      <ToastAction /><ToastClose />
    </ToastContent>
  </Toast>);
}
function Composition({ direction = "right", label = "Show custom notification" }: { direction?: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right"; label?: string }) {
  const [manager] = useState(createToastManager);
  return <ToastProvider toastManager={manager} timeout={0}>
    <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => manager.add({ title: "Custom notification", description: `Swipe ${direction} or use the close button.` })}>{label}</Button>
    <ToastPortal><ToastViewport aria-label={`${label} notifications`}><NotificationList direction={direction} /></ToastViewport></ToastPortal>
  </ToastProvider>;
}

export function Swipe() {
  return <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">{(["up", "down", "left", "right"] as const).map(direction => <Composition key={direction} direction={direction} label={`Swipe ${direction}`} />)}</div>;
}
```

## Without motion

These fixed local providers demonstrate none and full nested within none. The operating system reduced-motion preference still takes precedence. Ordinary examples inherit the header mode and speed.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import {
  createToastManager,
  ToastProvider,
  ToastPortal,
  ToastViewport,
  Toast,
  ToastContent,
  ToastTitle,
  ToastDescription,
  ToastAction,
  ToastClose,
  useToastManager,
 } from "@/components/cadence/toast";

function NotificationList({ direction = "right" }: { direction?: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right" }) {
  const { toasts } = useToastManager();
  return toasts.map(item => <Toast key={item.id} toast={item} swipeDirection={direction}>
    <ToastContent>
      <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1"><ToastTitle /><ToastDescription /></div>
      <ToastAction /><ToastClose />
    </ToastContent>
  </Toast>);
}
function Composition({ direction = "right", label = "Show custom notification" }: { direction?: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right"; label?: string }) {
  const [manager] = useState(createToastManager);
  return <ToastProvider toastManager={manager} timeout={0}>
    <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => manager.add({ title: "Custom notification", description: `Swipe ${direction} or use the close button.` })}>{label}</Button>
    <ToastPortal><ToastViewport aria-label={`${label} notifications`}><NotificationList direction={direction} /></ToastViewport></ToastPortal>
  </ToastProvider>;
}

export function WithoutMotion() {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="none"><div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
    <Composition label="Show instant notification" />
    <CadenceProvider mode="full"><Composition label="Show nested full notification" /></CadenceProvider>
  </div></CadenceProvider>;
}
```

## When to use

- Brief, nonblocking confirmation after an application action.
- An optional undo action with a visible close button.
- Caller-owned progress updated from existing application state.

## When not to use

- Inline validation errors: use Field and an error slot.
- Critical decisions requiring acknowledgment: use Alert Dialog.
- Persistent records or long instructions: use page content.

## API

| Part | Props | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Toaster` | Base UI Provider props, `children`, `toastManager`, `viewportProps` | shared `toast` manager; optional `viewportProps` forwards Viewport props except `children`; renders portal, viewport and list |
| `ToastProvider` | `timeout`, `limit`, `toastManager`, `children` | Base UI defaults: 5000ms, limit 3 |
| `ToastPortal` | Base UI Portal props, `container`, `keepMounted` | document portal |
| `ToastViewport` | Base UI Viewport props, `className` | fixed bottom right; F6 hotkey |
| `Toast` | Base UI Root props, required `toast`, `swipeDirection`, `render`, `className` | native swipe directions and dismissal |
| `ToastContent` | Base UI Content props, `render`, `className` | horizontal content layout |
| `ToastTitle` / `ToastDescription` | Base UI title / description props | text from the toast object |
| `ToastAction` | Base UI Action props | outline Button, size sm; actionProps from toast |
| `ToastClose` | Base UI Close props, `children` | ghost Button, icon-sm; label "Close toast", X glyph |
| `toast` / `createToastManager` | Base UI manager exports | add / update / close state supplied by caller |
| `useToastManager` | Base UI hook | provider's toast list and manager methods |

All parts forward upstream props and refs. Classes merge user values last. Button render defaults
match pinned upstream. Each rendered part retains its `toast-*` data slot.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | opacity 0 to 1, scale from `--motion-scale-in` in full | `popup.anchored`, duration.base, ease.out | yes, CSS transition |
| close / limited | opacity to 0; exit scale on close in full | `exit.fade`, duration.base | yes |
| swipe | Base UI pointer tracking in every mode; swipe-variable transform in full | primitive-owned gesture | yes |
| stack / content updates | bottom and natural height update instantly | no layout transition | n/a |
| reduced | opacity transitions only; no animated scale or swipe transform | duration.base × 0.6 | yes |
| none | zero duration; native pointer tracking remains immediate | zero duration | n/a |

Notifications remain expanded in a vertical stack; there is no collapsed height or stack-scale animation.
Base UI owns timeout pausing, lifecycle, swipe recognition and removal. No extra animation scheduler is added.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. Ordinary examples inherit the site header mode on the same component tree. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| F6 | Move focus to the notification viewport |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Traverse action and close controls |
| Escape | Dismiss the focused notification |
| Enter / Space | Activate the focused action or close button |

## Accessibility

Base UI announces notification title and description at the selected priority. Focus is not moved when a
toast arrives. Actions and close controls are named buttons. Important content must also exist in persistent
application UI; a notification should never be its only location. Timers pause during hover or focus. Give each independently mounted viewport a distinct, meaningful name with `Toaster viewportProps={{ "aria-label": "Export notifications" }}` or `ToastViewport aria-label` when composing the parts. The default remains “Notifications”; the manager and live-region behavior are unchanged.

## Responsive behavior

The viewport keeps 1rem margins on small screens and a max-sm width. On desktop it sits at bottom right.
Long descriptions wrap. Keep messages short so stacked notifications do not fill the screen.

## Performance

T2, 10 KB gzip source budget. Only opacity, scale and native swipe transform transition. Stack geometry
and content sizing update instantly; no measurement occurs during render and no height tween runs.

## Notes for AI

- Keep one provider per manager and mount its viewport once.
- Use Base UI `render`, retain each slot, and preserve the three mode branches.
- Caller state drives add/update/close; do not add request or validation orchestration.
- Related: `alert`, `alert-dialog`, `button`, `field`.

# Accordion

Reveal related sections while keeping their headings easy to scan.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/accordion
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| accordion | `@components/cadence/accordion/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/accordion.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: accordion](https://cadence.dev/r/accordion.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, keeping `accordion/index.tsx` and the shared
`lib/` directory in the same `cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and
the sources' `"use client"` directives. Copy every file in the motion,
utilities and provider payloads, including helpers not imported by Accordion
directly. The provider files and `motion` package are required imports even
without the optional `CadenceProvider` wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the
copied files. Include the Cadence duration and easing tokens used by the
disclosure classes. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is
required. Keep the inner measurement wrapper: full mode transitions the
nonnegative measured panel height, while reduced and none update it
immediately. Initially open server-rendered content retains its natural height.
Standalone components follow the system preference; use `CadenceProvider`
to choose a product mode or override an inherited scope.

The basic Usage and the static examples can be composed in a Server Component
with serializable values and children, including the `render={<section />}`
element. Use a client caller for controlled arrays and their change handlers,
the Changing content action, refs, or function-valued `render`, `className`
and `style` props. The Persistent content example retains its client directive;
synchronous `useId` alone does not require a client caller. Keep a meaningful
level-two section heading above the trigger's level-three headings.

The Controlled and Changing content examples additionally use
`@cadence/button`; Persistent content uses `@cadence/input` and
`@cadence/label`. Install those items separately, or copy every target and
recursive dependency from their Manual panels. The caller owns open-value
arrays, content updates and any input data; Accordion provides disclosure UI.

## Usage

The trigger includes a level-three heading. Place the accordion under a meaningful level-two section heading, such as the component questions in the preview.

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Accordion defaultValue={["shipping"]}>
      <AccordionItem value="shipping">
        <AccordionTrigger>When will my order arrive?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>Most orders arrive within five working days.</AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

Base UI uses arrays for both single and multiple selection. The caller owns the value; these external actions open or close the account section without resetting other examples.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function ControlledExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string[]>([]);
  return <div className="grid gap-4">
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setValue(["account"])}>Open account from outside</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setValue([])}>Close from outside</Button>
    </div>
    <Accordion value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
      <AccordionItem value="account">
        <AccordionTrigger>Account settings</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>Your account details stay with the caller.</AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
    <p role="status">Open sections: {value.join(", ") || "none"}</p>
  </div>;
}
```

## Multiple sections

Set multiple to keep several answers open. Both start open here; closing Delivery leaves Returns unchanged.

<ComponentExample name="multiple" />

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function MultipleExample() {
  return <Accordion multiple defaultValue={["delivery", "returns"]}>
    <AccordionItem value="delivery"><AccordionTrigger>Delivery</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Track your delivery from your order history.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    <AccordionItem value="returns"><AccordionTrigger>Returns</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Start a return within thirty days.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
  </Accordion>;
}
```

## Disabled

An item can be unavailable while its neighbours remain usable. Root disabled applies to every trigger. Disabled triggers cannot activate and are skipped by Tab; initially open information can still be read.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function DisabledExample() {
  return <div className="grid gap-4">
    <Accordion defaultValue={["available"]}>
      <AccordionItem value="available"><AccordionTrigger>Available settings</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>You can edit these settings.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
      <AccordionItem value="locked" disabled><AccordionTrigger>Unavailable section</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Not available yet.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
      <AccordionItem value="help"><AccordionTrigger>Settings help</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Contact the workspace owner.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
    <Accordion disabled defaultValue={["readable"]}>
      <AccordionItem value="readable"><AccordionTrigger>Read-only summary</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>The whole group is disabled; this initial summary remains readable.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
      <AccordionItem value="later"><AccordionTrigger>Locked next step</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Unavailable.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
  </div>;
}
```

## Persistent content

Closed panels normally unmount. Root keepMounted preserves the native input and its draft while hidden; the second group applies keepMounted to one panel instead. Each input has an independent label and ID. Hidden controls leave the tab order.

<ComponentExample name="persistent" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function PersistentExample() {
  const rootId = useId();
  const panelId = useId();
  return <div className="grid gap-4">
    <Accordion keepMounted defaultValue={["draft"]}>
      <AccordionItem value="draft"><AccordionTrigger>Workspace draft</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>
        <Label htmlFor={rootId}>Workspace note</Label><Input id={rootId} defaultValue="Keep this draft" />
      </AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
    <Accordion defaultValue={["local"]}>
      <AccordionItem value="local"><AccordionTrigger>Panel draft</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent keepMounted>
        <Label htmlFor={panelId}>Panel note</Label><Input id={panelId} defaultValue="Keep this panel" />
      </AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
  </div>;
}
```

## Searchable content

hiddenUntilFound keeps a closed panel in the DOM with hidden="until-found", overriding keepMounted. In supporting browsers, search for “Cobalt delivery reference” using the browser’s Find command to reveal it. The second group applies the same option to one panel. Browser support and native find behavior remain browser responsibilities.

<ComponentExample name="searchable" />

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function SearchableExample() {
  return <div className="grid gap-4">
    <Accordion hiddenUntilFound>
      <AccordionItem value="reference"><AccordionTrigger>Delivery reference</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Cobalt delivery reference: use your order number when contacting support.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
    <Accordion>
      <AccordionItem value="policy"><AccordionTrigger>Searchable policy</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent hiddenUntilFound>Indigo returns reference: keep your receipt for a return.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
  </div>;
}
```

## Changing content

This caller-owned action inserts real detail into an open answer. Full mode follows the measured height and can reverse while opening or closing; reduced and none update height immediately. The section’s own trigger still controls disclosure.

<ComponentExample name="changing-content" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function ChangingContentExample() {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);
  return <Accordion defaultValue={["motion"]}>
    <AccordionItem value="motion">
      <AccordionTrigger>Can I reduce the motion?</AccordionTrigger>
      <AccordionContent>
        <p>Yes. Your system preference is respected, and the provider can disable motion entirely.</p>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setExpanded(!expanded)} aria-expanded={expanded}>Toggle details</Button>
        {expanded && <p className="mt-4">Disclosure heights update instantly in reduced and none modes. Full mode follows the measured content height and can reverse while moving.</p>}
      </AccordionContent>
    </AccordionItem>
  </Accordion>;
}
```

## Custom panel rendering

Use render to change the panel’s element while preserving the supplied children, props and ref. className styles the inner content; style applies to the outer measured panel. The existing trigger and heading remain native accessible controls.

<ComponentExample name="custom-render" />

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function CustomRenderExample() {
  return <Accordion defaultValue={["support"]}>
    <AccordionItem value="support">
      <AccordionTrigger>Where can I get help?</AccordionTrigger>
      <AccordionContent render={<section />} className="text-muted-foreground" style={{ scrollMarginTop: "6rem" }}>
        <a href="/docs/installation">Read the installation guide</a> before adding your first component.
      </AccordionContent>
    </AccordionItem>
  </Accordion>;
}
```

## Legacy orientation

vertical and horizontal are deprecated Base UI state values, shown separately below. Cadence retains a vertical layout for both; these props and loopFocus do not enable arrow-key roving focus. Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move between triggers.

<ComponentExample name="orientation" />

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function OrientationExample() {
  return <div className="grid gap-4">
    {(["vertical", "horizontal"] as const).map(orientation => <Accordion key={orientation} orientation={orientation} loopFocus defaultValue={["state"]}>
      <AccordionItem value="state"><AccordionTrigger>{orientation} state</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Orientation is retained as state; keyboard navigation follows normal Tab order.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
      <AccordionItem value="next"><AccordionTrigger>Next {orientation} section</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>This is still a vertically stacked section.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>)}
  </div>;
}
```

## Without motion

The first accordion has an explicit none provider from its first render. A nested full provider opts the second accordion back into the normal geometry recipe. The operating system’s reduced-motion preference still takes priority over full.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function WithoutMotionExample() {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="none"><div className="grid gap-4">
    <Accordion defaultValue={["instant"]}><AccordionItem value="instant"><AccordionTrigger>Instant disclosure</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>No height transition runs here.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem></Accordion>
    <CadenceProvider mode="full"><Accordion defaultValue={["nested"]}><AccordionItem value="nested"><AccordionTrigger>Nested full disclosure</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>The operating system can still reduce this transition.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem></Accordion></CadenceProvider>
  </div></CadenceProvider>;
}
```

## When to use

- FAQ answers that readers scan by heading.
- Related settings sections with optional detail.
- Compact reference material with meaningful section titles.

## When not to use

- Use Collapsible for a single disclosure without grouped navigation.
- Use Tabs for peer views occupying one shared panel.
- Keep essential instructions visible rather than hiding them.

## API

### `Accordion`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Value[]` | uncontrolled / `[]` | Expanded item values. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details) => void` | — | Caller-owned controlled state. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Permit several expanded items. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable all items. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" | "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` | Deprecated; retained as state only. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep closed panels in the DOM. |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow browser find-in-page to reveal content. |

### `AccordionItem`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `unknown` | generated | Stable identity for controlled state. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable this item's trigger. |

### `AccordionTrigger`

All Base UI Trigger props pass through, including `render`, `ref`, and `nativeButton`. A heading wraps
the trigger. Two decorative icons swap immediately with `aria-expanded`; no rotation is animated.

### `AccordionContent`

All Base UI Panel props pass through, including `keepMounted`, `hiddenUntilFound`, `render`, `style`,
and `ref`. `className` styles the inner content, matching upstream; `style` applies to the panel.
Root and Item classes merge last.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open / close / content resize | Measured height clamped at zero | `geometry.resize` CSS form: `duration.slow` / `ease.out` | Yes, native CSS reversal from current height |
| Initially open | Natural height, no entrance | — | — |
| Reduced | Instant height, no transform | Zero duration | Yes |
| None | Instant height, no transform or transition | Zero duration | Yes |

The CSS form preserves position on interruption rather than spring velocity. Base UI owns panel
mounting, hidden state, keyboard navigation, and find-in-page behavior. An inner ResizeObserver
retargets changes in content without observing the animated panel itself. The closed size is zero.

## Accessibility

Triggers expose expanded state and control labelled regions. Focus stays on the trigger when a
panel toggles. Give each trigger a meaningful heading; do not place interactive controls inside it.
Disabled items are skipped in tab navigation. Content controls remain in normal tab order.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Toggle the focused trigger. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Follow normal page order through triggers and open content. |

Base UI 1.6 follows the updated APG guidance without arrow-key roving focus. `orientation` and
`loopFocus` are deprecated passthrough props; neither changes keyboard focus behavior.

## Responsive behavior

The root fills its container. Long headings wrap and the icons retain their size. Content is
remeasured when wrapping changes; there is no fixed maximum height or breakpoint-specific state.

## Performance

T3 budget: 12 KB gzip. One observer per mounted content slot; closed panels unmount by default.
Measurements run after commit and on content resize, never during render. No timers drive motion.
Server-rendered initially open content keeps its natural size before hydration.

## Notes for AI

- Use the Base UI array value API, not Radix `type="single"` or `collapsible` props.
- Preserve all four exports and the trigger-icon slot when customising.
- Keep the measurement wrapper and mode branch when editing motion.
- Related: Collapsible for a standalone disclosure; Tabs for alternate views.

# Collapsible

Reveal optional detail with a standalone disclosure.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/collapsible
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.


No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, keeping `collapsible/index.tsx` and the shared
`lib/` directory in the same `cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and
the sources' `"use client"` directives. Copy every file in the motion,
utilities and provider payloads, including helpers not imported by Collapsible
directly. The provider files and `motion` package are required imports even
without the optional `CadenceProvider` wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the
copied files. Include the Cadence duration and easing tokens used by the
disclosure classes. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is
required. Keep the inner measurement wrapper: full mode transitions the
nonnegative measured panel height, while reduced and none update it
immediately. Initially open server-rendered content retains its natural height.
Outer padding and borders remain part of the closing box minimum; put
decoration on a child when the closing endpoint must reach zero.
Standalone components follow the system preference; use `CadenceProvider`
to choose a product mode or override an inherited scope.

The Usage, Controlled and Changing content examples need a client caller for
their local state and event handlers. Use a client caller for refs or
function-valued `render`, `className` and `style` props too. Static
composition with serializable props and children, including element-valued
`render`, can be authored in a Server Component. Persistent content and
Custom render retain their client directives; synchronous `useId` alone
does not require a client caller. A custom Content render must preserve the
supplied props and measurement children.

Usage, Controlled, Custom trigger and Changing content additionally use
`@cadence/button`; Persistent content uses `@cadence/input` and
`@cadence/label`. Install those items separately, or copy every target and
recursive dependency from their Manual panels. The caller owns the boolean
open state, content updates and durable input data. Collapsible provides
disclosure UI; `keepMounted` retains a draft only while mounted, and
`hiddenUntilFound` depends on browser support.

## Usage

A standalone disclosure starts open here. The trigger keeps its expanded state and keyboard semantics; no demo configuration is needed.

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";

export function BasicExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);
  return (
    <Collapsible open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
        <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">Project details</h3>
        <CollapsibleTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" size="sm" />}>
          {open ? "Hide details" : "Show details"}
        </CollapsibleTrigger>
      </div>
      <CollapsibleContent>
        <p className="mt-4 rounded-lg border p-4 text-sm">
          Components are copied into your project so you can make them your own.
        </p>
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

Own the boolean `open` state in the caller. The external buttons update this example only; the trigger reports requests through `onOpenChange`.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";

export function ControlledExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
          Open from outside
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
          Close from outside
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Collapsible open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <CollapsibleTrigger>Account details</CollapsibleTrigger>
        <CollapsibleContent>Your account details stay with the caller.</CollapsibleContent>
      </Collapsible>
      <p role="status">Details: {open ? "open" : "closed"}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Custom trigger

Compose Button through `render` for a styled native trigger. When rendering a non-button element, set `nativeButton={false}` so Base UI supplies button role, focus and Enter/Space handling. The first disclosure starts open; the second starts closed.

<ComponentExample name="custom-trigger" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";

export function CustomTriggerExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <Collapsible defaultOpen>
        <CollapsibleTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Button details</CollapsibleTrigger>
        <CollapsibleContent>Initially visible without an entrance animation.</CollapsibleContent>
      </Collapsible>
      <Collapsible>
        <CollapsibleTrigger
          nativeButton={false}
          render={<div />}
          className="w-fit rounded border p-2 focus-visible:outline-2"
        >
          Non-native details
        </CollapsibleTrigger>
        <CollapsibleContent>A div receives the primitive's role, focus and keyboard handling.</CollapsibleContent>
      </Collapsible>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

Disable the whole root or one trigger. A disabled, initially open summary stays readable; disabled triggers cannot toggle and are skipped by normal Tab navigation. Other disclosures remain independent.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";

export function DisabledExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <Collapsible disabled defaultOpen>
        <CollapsibleTrigger>Locked project</CollapsibleTrigger>
        <CollapsibleContent>
          This initially open summary remains readable while the root is disabled.
        </CollapsibleContent>
      </Collapsible>
      <Collapsible>
        <CollapsibleTrigger disabled>Unavailable details</CollapsibleTrigger>
        <CollapsibleContent>Not available yet.</CollapsibleContent>
      </Collapsible>
      <Collapsible>
        <CollapsibleTrigger>Available details</CollapsibleTrigger>
        <CollapsibleContent>You can still open this independent section.</CollapsibleContent>
      </Collapsible>
      <a href="/docs/installation">Read the installation guide</a>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Persistent content

Put `keepMounted` on Content to retain this native input and its draft when closed. Closed content leaves the focus order. Persistence lasts while the example is mounted; store durable drafts in the caller.

<ComponentExample name="persistent" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function PersistentExample() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <Collapsible defaultOpen>
      <CollapsibleTrigger>Workspace draft</CollapsibleTrigger>
      <CollapsibleContent keepMounted>
        <Label htmlFor={id}>Workspace note</Label>
        <Input id={id} defaultValue="Keep this draft" />
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
```

## Searchable content

Put `hiddenUntilFound` on Content to use `hidden="until-found"` while closed. Supporting browsers can reveal this reference through find-in-page; browser support varies. This option overrides `keepMounted`. It is not a search service or a promise of cross-browser Find UI support.

<ComponentExample name="searchable" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";

export function SearchableExample() {
  return (
    <Collapsible>
      <CollapsibleTrigger>Reference notes</CollapsibleTrigger>
      <CollapsibleContent hiddenUntilFound>
        Cobalt delivery reference: use your order number when contacting support.
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
```

## Changing content

The button adds or removes local detail in this example. The inner natural content is observed and the open panel follows its height, including responsive wrapping. Outer padding and borders remain supported; their box minimum persists during closing. Put decoration on a child when the closing endpoint must reach zero.

<ComponentExample name="changing-content" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";

export function ChangingContentExample() {
  const [details, setDetails] = useState(false);
  return (
    <Collapsible defaultOpen>
      <CollapsibleTrigger>Project information</CollapsibleTrigger>
      <CollapsibleContent className="mt-4 rounded-lg border p-4 text-sm">
        <p className="mb-4">Components are copied into your project so you can make them your own.</p>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" aria-expanded={details} onClick={() => setDetails(!details)}>
          Toggle extra detail
        </Button>
        {details && (
          <p className="mt-4">
            The disclosure follows content changes and responsive wrapping. Reduced and none modes update its height
            instantly.
          </p>
        )}
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
```

## Custom render

Render Root and Content as sections while preserving the supplied props and measurement children. Content has default div semantics; this example explicitly opts into a named region. Caller classes and styles remain applied to the outer panel.

<ComponentExample name="custom-render" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";

export function CustomRenderExample() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <Collapsible defaultOpen render={<section />}>
      <CollapsibleTrigger id={id}>Support resources</CollapsibleTrigger>
      <CollapsibleContent
        render={<section />}
        role="region"
        aria-labelledby={id}
        className="text-muted-foreground"
        style={{ scrollMarginTop: "6rem" }}
      >
        <a href="/docs/installation">Read the installation guide</a> before adding your first component.
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
```

## Without motion

This named example explicitly sets `none` for the first disclosure. The nested `full` provider restores its recipe, while the system reduced-motion preference still wins. Other examples inherit the site header mode and speed.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function WithoutMotionExample() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <div className="grid gap-4">
        <Collapsible defaultOpen>
          <CollapsibleTrigger>Instant disclosure</CollapsibleTrigger>
          <CollapsibleContent>No height transition runs here.</CollapsibleContent>
        </Collapsible>
        <CadenceProvider mode="full">
          <Collapsible defaultOpen>
            <CollapsibleTrigger>Nested full disclosure</CollapsibleTrigger>
            <CollapsibleContent>The operating system can still reduce this transition.</CollapsibleContent>
          </Collapsible>
        </CadenceProvider>
      </div>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Optional details for one independent section.
- Advanced settings beside a visible summary.
- Supporting reference notes that users may reveal on demand.

## When not to use

- Use Accordion for a group of labelled sections.
- Use Tabs for peer views sharing one panel.
- Keep essential instructions visible.

## API

### `Collapsible`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | uncontrolled / `false` | Controlled or initial expanded state. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, details) => void` | — | State change request; details support cancellation. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignore trigger interaction. |
| `className`, `style`, `render`, `ref` | Base UI Root props | — | Forwarded unchanged, including state callbacks. |

### `CollapsibleTrigger`

All Base UI Trigger props pass through, including `disabled`, `nativeButton`, `render`, `ref`, and
state-based classes/styles. Use `render`, not `asChild`, for a custom element. Supply an accessible name.

### `CollapsibleContent`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep closed content in the DOM. |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | `boolean` | `false` | Reveal via browser find-in-page; overrides keepMounted. |
| `className`, `style`, `render`, `ref` | Base UI Panel props | — | Applied to the outer panel; classes merge last. |

All primitive props remain available. A custom render must preserve supplied children and props,
including the natural measurement wrapper. The added `collapsible-content-inner` slot is structural.
Outer padding and borders are supported in both `border-box` and `content-box`; expanded content
retains its natural height. During closing, CSS keeps the outer padding/border minimum until Base UI
hides or unmounts the panel. To reach a visually zero-height endpoint before hiding, put that decoration
on a content child. Caller styles are preserved; padding and borders are never animated.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open / close / content resize | Measured height clamped at zero | `geometry.resize` CSS form: `duration.slow` / `ease.out` | Yes, native reversal from current position |
| Initially open | Natural height without entrance | — | — |
| Reduced | Instant height, no transform | Zero duration | Yes |
| None | Instant height, no transform or transition | Zero duration | Yes |

An inner ResizeObserver watches natural content, never the animated panel. Measurements happen after
commit, on resize and when outer classes/styles change. Border-box targets include outer vertical
padding and borders; content-box targets use the natural inner height. Native CSS reversal preserves
position rather than spring velocity. Base UI owns mounting, hidden state and transition completion. No icon animation or extra recipe is added.

## Accessibility

The trigger exposes `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Content retains Base UI's default div semantics;
add a named region only when the content warrants one. Focus stays on the trigger when toggled.
Disabled controls are skipped in normal tab navigation. Keep interactive content outside the trigger.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Toggle the focused trigger. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Follow normal page order through the trigger and visible content. |

## Responsive behavior

No fixed dimensions or breakpoint-driven state. Natural content is remeasured when wrapping changes.
The root and trigger are unstyled; use caller classes or compose Button for visual feedback.

## Performance

T3 budget: 12 KB gzip. One ResizeObserver per mounted content panel, disconnected on unmount.
Closed content unmounts by default. Initially open server content uses natural height before hydration.
No timers or render-time measurements drive animation.

## Notes for AI

- Use boolean `open`, not Accordion's array value API.
- Keep content lifecycle props on Content and preserve the measurement wrapper.
- Preserve all three exports and the full/reduced/none branch.
- Related: Accordion for grouped sections; Tabs for alternate views.

# Tabs

Switch between peer views with a shared selection indicator.

**Manual**

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, keeping `tabs/index.tsx` and the shared `lib/`
directory in the same `cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and the
sources' `"use client"` directives. Copy every file in the motion, utilities
and provider payloads, including helpers not imported by Tabs directly.
The provider files and `motion` package are required imports even without
the optional `CadenceProvider` wrapper.

Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the
copied files. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is required.
Standalone components follow the system motion preference; use
`CadenceProvider` to choose a product mode or override an inherited scope.
Each list scopes its own shared selection indicator. Full mode moves it
using `layout.shared`; reduced, none and a zero clock place it immediately.
Panels switch without a fade or height animation. The caller chooses list
width, scrolling and orientation; preserve the indicator children and refs
when supplying a custom trigger render.

Controlled and List sizing need a client caller for their state and event
handlers. Refs, event handlers and function-valued `render`, `className`
or `style` props also require a client caller. Usage, Vertical, Line style,
Custom elements and persistent panels, and Disabled use serializable props
and children and can be composed in a Server Component. Element-valued
`render` is supported there; synchronous `useId` inside TabsList does not
itself require a client caller.

Controlled and List sizing additionally use `@cadence/button`. Install it
separately, or copy every target and recursive dependency from its Manual
panel. The caller owns controlled selection and durable panel data. Supply
matching trigger/content values and a list label; `null` selects no panel.
`keepMounted` retains the draft textarea while its panel is hidden, but
does not persist data after the Tabs tree unmounts. Default lists activate
with Enter or Space; `activateOnFocus` opts into selection on arrow focus.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from "@/components/cadence/tabs";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="overview">
      <TabsList aria-label="Project views">
        <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="activity">Activity</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="overview">Project overview</TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="activity">Recent activity</TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

The caller owns `value` and `onValueChange`. Change selection updates this list externally while other examples keep their own selection. Values may be any Base UI tab value; `null` selects nothing. User change requests include cancellable event details.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tabs";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

function ProjectTabs({ orientation = "horizontal", variant = "default", wide = false, disabled = false, value, onValueChange }: {
  orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical";
  variant?: "default" | "line";
  wide?: boolean;
  disabled?: boolean;
  value?: string | null;
  onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="overview" value={value} onValueChange={onValueChange} orientation={orientation} className="w-full max-w-md">
      <TabsList aria-label="Project views" variant={variant} className={wide ? "w-full" : undefined}>
        <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="activity">Activity</TabsTrigger>
        {disabled && <TabsTrigger value="locked" disabled>Locked</TabsTrigger>}
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="overview" className="rounded-lg border p-4 text-sm">Project overview. Peer views share one selection indicator.</TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="activity" className="rounded-lg border p-4 text-sm">Recent activity.</TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  );
}

export function Controlled() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>("overview");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col gap-4">
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" className="self-start" onClick={() => setValue(value === "overview" ? "activity" : "overview")}>Change selection</Button>
      <ProjectTabs value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />
      <output className="text-sm" aria-live="polite">Selected: {value}</output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Vertical

Vertical lists use Up/Down for focus. Both filled and line lists below have fixed vertical orientation and independent selection; the line list opts into activation on focus.

<ComponentExample name="vertical" />

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tabs";

  return (

      <TabsList aria-label="Project views" variant={variant} className={wide ? "w-full" : undefined}>
        <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>

    </Tabs>
  );
}

function SettingsTabs({ vertical = false }: { vertical?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="account" orientation={vertical ? "vertical" : "horizontal"} className="w-full max-w-md">
      <TabsList variant="line" aria-label="Settings views" activateOnFocus>
        <TabsTrigger value="account">Account</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="notifications">Notifications</TabsTrigger>

    </Tabs>
  );
}

export function Vertical() {
  return <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-6"><ProjectTabs orientation="vertical" disabled /><SettingsTabs vertical /></div>;
}
```

## Line style

`variant="line"` moves the shared indicator to the edge. `activateOnFocus` selects on arrow focus; the default is manual activation with Enter or Space.

<ComponentExample name="line-style" />

```tsx
}
```

## Custom elements and persistent panels

`render` preserves the primitive semantics and refs on a custom element. Hidden panels unmount by default; `keepMounted` keeps the draft textarea and its value when History is selected. Render callbacks must spread merged props and retain children, including the indicator.

<ComponentExample name="persistent" />

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tabs";

export function Persistent() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="draft" className="w-full max-w-md">
      <TabsList aria-label="Editor views">
        <TabsTrigger value="draft" render={<button type="button" />}>Draft</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="history">History</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="draft" keepMounted render={<section />}>
        <textarea aria-label="Draft text" className="min-h-24 w-full rounded-md border bg-background p-3 text-sm" defaultValue="Work in progress" />
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="history" className="p-4 text-sm">Previous revisions</TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## List sizing

The caller sets the list width. Resize list switches between content width and full width; the selected indicator follows the same tab without resetting selection. A parent resize is also observed.

<ComponentExample name="list-sizing" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tabs";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

function ProjectTabs({ orientation = "horizontal", variant = "default", wide = false, disabled = false, value, onValueChange }: {
  orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical";
  variant?: "default" | "line";
  wide?: boolean;
  disabled?: boolean;
  value?: string | null;
  onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="overview" value={value} onValueChange={onValueChange} orientation={orientation} className="w-full max-w-md">
      <TabsList aria-label="Project views" variant={variant} className={wide ? "w-full" : undefined}>
        <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="activity">Activity</TabsTrigger>
        {disabled && <TabsTrigger value="locked" disabled>Locked</TabsTrigger>}
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="overview" className="rounded-lg border p-4 text-sm">Project overview. Peer views share one selection indicator.</TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="activity" className="rounded-lg border p-4 text-sm">Recent activity.</TabsContent>

export function ListSizing() {

  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col gap-4">

```

## Disabled

Locked stays visible and cannot be selected. Base UI allows focus on this disabled tab; Enter and Space leave the current selection unchanged.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

