## When to use

- Peer views of the same project.
- Settings categories that share a local context.
- Editors with preview and history panels.

## When not to use

- Use links and Breadcrumb for separate destinations.
- Use Accordion for sections that can remain open together.
- Use ToggleGroup for a set of independent formatting actions.

## API

### `Tabs`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | Base UI tab value | uncontrolled / `0` | Controlled or initial selection; null means none. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details) => void` | — | Change request with reason, activation direction and cancellation. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal` / `vertical` | `horizontal` | Layout and keyboard axis. |
| `className`, `style`, `render`, `ref` | Base UI Root props | — | Forwarded, including state callbacks. |

### `TabsList`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `default` / `line` | `default` | Filled surface or edge indicator. |
| `activateOnFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Select on arrow focus. |
| `loopFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Wrap focus at either end. |

All Base UI List props pass through. `tabsListVariants` is exported for composing styles.

### `TabsTrigger`

`value` identifies the corresponding panel. `disabled` defaults to false. All Base UI Tab props pass
through, including `nativeButton`, `render`, `ref`, events and state-based classes/styles. User classes
merge last. The added `tabs-indicator` slot is decorative and aria-hidden.

### `TabsContent`

`value` links to the corresponding trigger. `keepMounted` defaults to false. All Base UI Panel props,
render/ref and state callbacks remain available. Panels switch immediately without size or entrance motion.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selection | Shared indicator transform via FLIP | `layout.shared`, physics-defined `spring.morph` | Yes, inherits velocity |
| Initial selection | Static indicator at selected trigger | — | — |
| Reduced | Static indicator, no layout/transform | No motion | Instant |
| None | Static indicator, no transform or animation | Zero duration | Instant |

Each list has a unique LayoutGroup. Default and line indicators follow both axes; independent and nested
lists cannot exchange indicators. Shared-layout measurements use list-local coordinates, so panel reflow,
parent recentering and page scrolling do not add a sideways or vertical detour to the selection path.
The primitive owns active state, cancellation, disabled fallback and
mounting. Reduced and none render a plain span with no layoutId. Parent size changes leave the indicator
anchored to the selected trigger. There is no panel fade, height animation or extra recipe.

## Accessibility

Base UI provides tablist/tab/tabpanel roles, linked IDs and roving focus. Supply a list label. Selection
is exposed through aria-selected; focus remains on the operated tab. Disabled tabs remain arrow-focusable for discoverability but cannot activate. A custom
render must preserve supplied semantics, refs and children. Persistent hidden panels leave the focus order.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left / Right | Move horizontal tab focus; direction follows the surrounding DirectionProvider. |
| Up / Down | Move vertical tab focus. |
| Home / End | Focus the first / last tab, including disabled tabs. |
| Enter / Space | Select the focused tab in default manual activation mode. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Leave the list for the panel or surrounding page. |

## Responsive behavior

No breakpoint changes selection or orientation. The caller chooses layout and may constrain or scroll
long lists. The indicator is inset within its active trigger and follows changes in label and parent size.

## Performance

T3 source budget: 12 KB gzip. Only the active indicator participates in shared layout projection;
there are no measurement observers or animation timers in this component. Server output includes the
initial selected indicator; initial=false avoids an entrance replay. Keep large lists and panels small.

## Notes for AI

- Preserve all five exports and the four upstream slots.
- Use value/defaultValue, not the retired animated-tabs items API.
- Keep each list scoped and preserve the explicit reduced/none static branch.
- Related: Accordion, Collapsible, ToggleGroup.

# Table

Invoices, transaction histories, and small collections of structured records.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/table
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| table | `@components/cadence/table/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/table.json) |

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: table](https://cadence.dev/r/table.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

Copy both target files, keeping `table/index.tsx` and `lib/cn.ts` in the
same `cadence/` tree so the relative import resolves. Preserve the source's
`"use client"` directive. Complete the base theme setup linked above and
ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. Table needs no motion runtime,
provider or additional item-specific CSS; all three motion modes keep its
native table parts static. Row colour feedback is CSS state feedback.

Usage, Footer totals, Density and alignment, Horizontal overflow, and Empty
results pass serializable props and children and can be composed in a Server
Component. Selected rows and Row actions require a client caller for their
state and event handlers. Refs and event handlers also require a client
caller. Row actions additionally uses [Button](/components/button): install
it separately, or copy every target and recursive dependency from its Manual
panel, including its motion setup. The other examples and the top preview
need no additional component dependencies.

Keep the native caption, header, body and footer hierarchy, provide a meaningful
caption or accessible name, and set header `scope` as shown below. Table
does not fetch records, calculate totals, sort, filter, paginate or own
selection. The caller supplies stable row keys, data, selected state and
action handlers; `data-state="selected"` only styles a row. Controls inside
cells keep their own keyboard behaviour.

Table's props, classes and ref target the `table`, not its automatic
`overflow-x-auto` wrapper. Constrain the surrounding layout with `min-w-0`
where needed, and choose column widths and wrapping yourself. For a wide
table, supply `tabIndex={0}`, a caption and a visible focus ring as in
Horizontal overflow, then verify native arrow-key scrolling in your target
browsers. Columns remain present; Table adds no grid keyboard model.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCaption,
  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@/components/cadence/table";

export function Invoices() {
  return (
    <Table tabIndex={0} className="focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring">
      <TableCaption>Recent invoices.</TableCaption>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead scope="col">Invoice</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            Amount
          </TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>INV-001</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-right">$250.00</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

## Footer totals

`TableFooter` renders a native `tfoot`. This example keeps a row header, spans the label across two columns and aligns the total with the amounts. The caller supplies both the records and the total; Table does no arithmetic.

<ComponentExample name="footer-totals" />

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCaption,
  TableCell,
  TableFooter,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@/components/cadence/table";

const invoices = [
  { id: "INV-001", status: "Paid", method: "Credit card", amount: "$250.00" },
  { id: "INV-002", status: "Pending", method: "Bank transfer", amount: "$150.00" },
  { id: "INV-003", status: "Unpaid", method: "PayPal", amount: "$350.00" },
];

export function FooterTotalsExample() {
  return (
    <Table>
      <TableCaption>November invoice totals.</TableCaption>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead scope="col">Invoice</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col">Status</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            Amount
          </TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        {invoices.map((invoice) => (
          <TableRow key={invoice.id}>
            <TableHead scope="row">{invoice.id}</TableHead>
            <TableCell>{invoice.status}</TableCell>
            <TableCell className="text-right tabular-nums">{invoice.amount}</TableCell>
          </TableRow>
        ))}
      </TableBody>
      <TableFooter>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead scope="row" colSpan={2}>
            Total
          </TableHead>
          <TableCell className="text-right tabular-nums">$750.00</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableFooter>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

## Selected rows

Selection belongs to the application. These named native checkboxes own their checked state and set `data-state="selected"` on the corresponding rows. The attribute only adds row colour: it does not turn a row into a control, add `aria-selected`, or introduce grid navigation. Space toggles the focused checkbox; the initial selection is independent of every other specimen.

<ComponentExample name="selected-rows" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCaption,
  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@/components/cadence/table";

const invoices = [
  { id: "INV-001", status: "Paid", method: "Credit card", amount: "$250.00" },
  { id: "INV-002", status: "Pending", method: "Bank transfer", amount: "$150.00" },
  { id: "INV-003", status: "Unpaid", method: "PayPal", amount: "$350.00" },
];

export function SelectedRowsExample() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>(["INV-001"]);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <Table>
        <TableCaption>Choose invoices for your report.</TableCaption>
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead scope="col">Include</TableHead>
            <TableHead scope="col">Invoice</TableHead>
            <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
              Amount
            </TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {invoices.map((invoice) => (
            <TableRow key={invoice.id} data-state={selected.includes(invoice.id) ? "selected" : undefined}>
              <TableCell>
                <input
                  type="checkbox"
                  aria-label={`Include ${invoice.id}`}
                  checked={selected.includes(invoice.id)}
                  onChange={(event) =>
                    setSelected((current) =>
                      event.target.checked ? [...current, invoice.id] : current.filter((id) => id !== invoice.id),
                    )
                  }
                  className="size-4 accent-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring"
                />
              </TableCell>
              <TableHead scope="row">{invoice.id}</TableHead>
              <TableCell className="text-right tabular-nums">{invoice.amount}</TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableBody>
      </Table>
      <p role="status">Selected invoices: {selected.length}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Density and alignment

```tsx
          <TableCaption>{compact ? "Compact spacing" : "Default spacing"} with numeric alignment.</TableCaption>

                Seats
```

## Row actions

Links and buttons inside cells keep their own keyboard behaviour. Tab reaches the invoice history link and then the payment action; Enter or Space activates the button. The local handler changes only this example and disables the completed action. In an application, the caller owns persistence, pending state and errors. Install `@cadence/button` alongside Table for this composition; the button inherits the surrounding motion settings.

<ComponentExample name="row-actions" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCaption,
  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@/components/cadence/table";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function RowActionsExample() {
  const [paid, setPaid] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <Table>
        <TableCaption>Invoice actions owned by the application.</TableCaption>
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead scope="col">Invoice</TableHead>
            <TableHead scope="col">Status</TableHead>
            <TableHead scope="col">Action</TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead scope="row">
              <a href="/docs/changelog" className="underline underline-offset-4">
                INV-001 history
              </a>
            </TableHead>
            <TableCell>{paid ? "Paid" : "Pending"}</TableCell>
            <TableCell>
              <Button variant="outline" size="sm" disabled={paid} onClick={() => setPaid(true)}>
                Mark INV-001 paid
              </Button>
            </TableCell>
          </TableRow>
        </TableBody>
      </Table>
      <p role="status">{paid ? "INV-001 marked paid locally." : "No payment action yet."}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Horizontal overflow

The built-in container scrolls when the table needs more room. Constrain the surrounding layout with `min-w-0`; put the minimum width and a visible focus ring on Table itself. In this wide specimen, focus the named table and press horizontal arrow keys to scroll its ancestor. No columns are removed, and there is no grid arrow-key selection model. Check keyboard scrolling in your target browsers.

<ComponentExample name="horizontal-overflow" />

```tsx
import {

  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,

export function HorizontalOverflowExample() {

      tabIndex={0}
      className="min-w-[44rem] focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-ring"
    >
      <TableCaption>Delivery records. Focus the table and use horizontal arrow keys to scroll.</TableCaption>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead scope="col">Invoice</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col">Customer</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col">Delivery reference</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            Amount
          </TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead scope="row">INV-001</TableHead>
          <TableCell>morgan@example.com</TableCell>
          <TableCell>November workspace delivery</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-right tabular-nums">$250.00</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

## Empty results

Keep the header relationships and place the empty message in one cell spanning every column. The caller decides that the result is empty and provides the message; Table does not fetch or filter records. `whitespace-normal` lets this message wrap at narrow widths.

<ComponentExample name="empty-results" />

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCaption,
  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@/components/cadence/table";

export function EmptyResultsExample() {
  return (
    <Table>
      <TableCaption>Invoices matching the application's current query.</TableCaption>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead scope="col">Invoice</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col">Status</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            Amount
          </TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell colSpan={3} className="h-24 text-center whitespace-normal text-muted-foreground">
            No matching invoices. Try another query in your application.
          </TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Invoice summaries with amounts and payment states.
- Transaction histories with a few consistent columns.
- Small record collections where column comparisons matter.

## When not to use

- For page layout: use CSS grid or flex.
- For large collections needing sorting, filtering, pagination, or virtualization:
  compose those behaviours in the application; Table only supplies markup and styles.
- For independent summaries with no column relationships: use cards or a list.

## API

All eight exports accept `React.ComponentProps` for their native element,
including `children`, `className`, `style`, event handlers, ARIA attributes and
React 19 `ref`. Classes merge last. No custom props or defaults are added.

| Export | Element |
| --- | --- |
| `Table` | `table` |
| `TableHeader` | `thead` |
| `TableBody` | `tbody` |
| `TableFooter` | `tfoot` |
| `TableRow` | `tr` |
| `TableHead` | `th` |
| `TableCell` | `td` |
| `TableCaption` | `caption` |

Each part's slot is its kebab-case name: `table`, `table-header`, `table-body`,
`table-footer`, `table-row`, `table-head`, `table-cell`, and `table-caption`.

`Table` also creates a `div` with `data-slot="table-container"` and
`relative w-full overflow-x-auto`. Its props, classes and ref target the **table**,
not that wrapper. Size the surrounding layout to constrain the scrolling region.
`TableHead` and `TableCell` keep upstream's no-wrap and checkbox alignment styles.
Rows retain hover, `data-state="selected"` and descendant `aria-expanded` feedback.

## Motion contract

T0: no motion recipe, hook, provider, or animation runtime. All modes render the
same static table. Row colour feedback is the upstream CSS colour transition;
rows do not enter, reorder, resize, or animate selection.

| Mode | Animated properties |
| --- | --- |
| full | none |
| reduced | none |
| none | none |

No timing token or interruption lifecycle applies.

## Accessibility

- Native table, row, header, cell and caption semantics remain intact. Provide a
  meaningful caption or an accessible name and use `scope` for header relationships.
- Static rows and cells stay out of the tab order. Links, buttons and checkboxes
  inside cells keep their native keyboard interaction; no grid arrow-key model is added.
- The wrapper scrolls horizontally on narrow screens; columns are not removed.
  If keyboard scrolling needs an explicit focus stop across your target browsers,
  pass `tabIndex={0}` to the named table with a visible focus ring, as in Usage.
  This supplies a focusable descendant of the scrolling container; arrow keys
  can scroll that ancestor without adding grid keyboard semantics.
- No layout measurement or data processing runs. Render large datasets through
  application-owned pagination or virtualization; the server markup remains native HTML.

## Responsiveness and performance

The table fills its container, which provides native horizontal scrolling when columns need more
width. The caller owns column sizing, wrapping and any sticky behavior. Rows are all rendered; large
datasets need application pagination or virtualization.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not
imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for
this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Preserve the table hierarchy: caption, header, body and footer belong inside Table.
- Class names and refs on Table address the table; constrain its parent for overflow.
- Table does not fetch data, validate values, sort, filter, paginate or own selection.
- Do not add decorative row entrance or reorder motion to this T0 component.

# Carousel

A swipeable collection with previous and next controls.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/carousel
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority embla-carousel-react@8.6.0 lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all ten target files, including every file from the motion and provider
helpers, into the same `cadence/` tree so their relative imports resolve.
Preserve the sources' `"use client"` directives and the exact
`embla-carousel-react@8.6.0` pin: the motion policy integrates with that
engine's internals. Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure
Tailwind scans the copied files. No additional item-specific CSS is required.
The provider files are required imports; an application wrapper is optional.
Standalone components follow the system motion preference. Use
`CadenceProvider` to control a subtree as shown above.

Usage, Multiple visible slides, Vertical collection, Looping, Right-to-left,
Drag behavior, Alignment and initial position, and Without motion use
serializable props and children and can be composed in a Server Component.
Changing slides needs a client caller for state and handlers. API and plugins
needs a client caller for hooks, `setApi`, plugin lifecycle functions and
external navigation; Custom controls needs one for `useCarousel` and its
handlers. Refs, function-valued options and Button render/state callbacks
also require a client caller. Button and CadenceProvider are already included
in this installation graph; the top preview and examples need no additional
component or example-only npm dependencies.

Keep CarouselContent and CarouselItem inside Carousel; call `useCarousel`
only beneath that root. Supply stable slide keys, a region label, slide labels,
and any current-slide announcement yourself. The root is not focusable by
default: supply `tabIndex={0}` and a visible focus style when needed. Both
orientations use ArrowLeft / ArrowRight; native navigation buttons support
Enter / Space. Interactive slide content must accommodate that root capture
handler. Offscreen slides remain mounted and accessible.

Constrain the parent width, size slides with basis classes, and leave space
for the outboard controls. CarouselContent props, classes and ref address
the inner track, not its fixed overflow-hidden viewport. Horizontal tracks
use `touch-pan-y`; vertical tracks need an explicit height and
`touch-pan-x`. Set `orientation="vertical"` to select that axis; it takes
precedence over `opts.axis`. RTL needs both native `dir="rtl"` and
`opts.direction="rtl"`; the default control positions and icons stay as shown.

SSR renders static markup; Embla initializes its position and options after
hydration. Embla owns track translation, snapping, drag, loop, focus, resize
and slide-mutation handling. Navigate through its API rather than adding a
second transform or CSS transition to the track. Full mode interpolates;
reduced and none keep the correct slide position and direct pointer tracking
while making autonomous engine interpolation immediate. A live downgrade
settles the existing target without resetting selection. Button retains its
own press-feedback policy.

Keep plugin instances stable and clean up API subscriptions. The caller owns
data updates, external selection/status, and independent plugin animation or
autoplay; pause those under reduced/none and provide pause controls. Carousel
does not bundle autoplay, data fetching or virtualization. Caller overrides
of navigation `onClick`, `disabled`, or root `onKeyDownCapture` replace the
corresponding defaults, so preserve the intended navigation yourself.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselNext } from "@/components/cadence/carousel";
export function BasicExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-lg px-12 py-12">
      <Carousel
        aria-label="Project highlights"
        tabIndex={0}
        className="w-full outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
      >
        <CarouselContent className="touch-pan-y">
          {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((slide) => (
            <CarouselItem key={slide} aria-label={`${slide} of 4`}>
              <div className="flex h-36 items-center justify-center rounded-xl border bg-muted text-3xl font-semibold">
                {slide}
              </div>
            </CarouselItem>
          ))}
        </CarouselContent>
        <CarouselPrevious />
        <CarouselNext />
      </Carousel>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Changing slides

These two caller-owned updates are limited to this example. Resize changes the real parent width; Change slides adds/removes the last keyed slide. Embla observes geometry and slide mutations and rebuilds its snaps. Existing slide DOM stays mounted; removing the selected last item clamps to a valid snap.

<ComponentExample name="changing-slides" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselNext } from "@/components/cadence/carousel";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { useState } from "react";

export function ChangingExample() {
  const [narrow, setNarrow] = useState(false);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(4);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-2">
        <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => setNarrow(!narrow)}>
          Resize track
        </Button>
        <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => setCount(count === 4 ? 5 : 4)}>
          Change slides
        </Button>
      </div>
      <div className="px-12 py-12">
        <Carousel
          aria-label="Changing projects"
          tabIndex={0}
          opts={{ align: "start" }}
          className={`${narrow ? "mx-auto w-3/4" : "w-full"} outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring`}
        >
          <CarouselContent className="touch-pan-y">
            {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].slice(0, count).map((slide) => (
              <CarouselItem key={slide} aria-label={`${slide} of ${count}`}>
                <div className="flex h-36 items-center justify-center rounded-xl border bg-muted text-3xl font-semibold">
                  {slide}
                </div>
              </CarouselItem>
            ))}
          </CarouselContent>
          <CarouselPrevious />
          <CarouselNext />
        </Carousel>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## API and plugins

Use the real Embla API for external navigation and subscribe with cleanup. A stable lifecycle-only plugin reports readiness without adding animation. This example also keeps a native narrow-screen duration override; reduced/none clamp its interpolation. Install Button for the external action.

<ComponentExample name="api" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselNext } from "@/components/cadence/carousel";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import type { CarouselApi } from "@/components/cadence/carousel";

export function ApiExample() {
  const [api, setApi] = useState<CarouselApi>();
  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(1);
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
  const plugins = useMemo(
    () => [
      {
        name: "exampleStatus",
        options: {},
        init() {
          setReady(true);
        },
        destroy() {
          setReady(false);
        },
      },
    ],
    [],
  );
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!api) return;
    const update = () => setCurrent(api.selectedScrollSnap() + 1);
    update();
    api.on("select", update).on("reInit", update);
    return () => {
      api.off("select", update).off("reInit", update);
    };
  }, [api]);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-4">
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => api?.scrollTo(3, false)}>
        Go to last slide
      </Button>
      <div className="px-12 py-12">
        <Carousel
          aria-label="API projects"
          tabIndex={0}
          className="w-full outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
          setApi={setApi}
          plugins={plugins}
          opts={{ breakpoints: { "(max-width: 480px)": { duration: 37 } } }}
        >
          <CarouselContent className="touch-pan-y">
            {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((slide) => (
              <CarouselItem key={slide} aria-label={`${slide} of 4`}>
                <div className="flex h-36 items-center justify-center rounded-xl border bg-muted text-3xl font-semibold">
                  {slide}
                </div>
              </CarouselItem>
            ))}
          </CarouselContent>
          <CarouselPrevious />
          <CarouselNext />
        </Carousel>
      </div>
      <p role="status" className="text-center text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Slide {current} of 4{ready ? " · Ready" : ""}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The API is the actual Embla 8.6.0 instance, including events, `reInit`, `plugins`, `scrollTo`, `scrollProgress`, and `destroy`. Keep plugin instances stable. Plugins are not removed by motion mode changes: pause autoplay and independent plugin animation under reduced/none yourself and provide pause controls. Cadence clamps engine interpolation even when an API or plugin requests `jump=false`.

## Alignment and initial position

Compare `start`, `center`, and `end` with a fixed `startIndex: 1`. Each slide is two-thirds width and `containScroll: false` preserves the requested edge alignment instead of trimming the endpoint snaps. Arbitrary Embla options are pass-through configuration, not additional Cadence variants.

<ComponentExample name="alignment" />

```tsx

            aria-label="Align start"

            opts={{ align: "start", containScroll: false, startIndex: 1 }}
            className="w-full outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
          >
            <CarouselContent className="touch-pan-y">
              {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((slide) => (
                <CarouselItem key={slide} aria-label={`${slide} of 4`} className="basis-2/3">
                  <div className="flex h-36 items-center justify-center rounded-xl border bg-muted text-3xl font-semibold">
                    {slide}
                  </div>
                </CarouselItem>
              ))}
            </CarouselContent>
            <CarouselPrevious />
            <CarouselNext />
          </Carousel>
        </div>
        <div className="grid gap-3">
          <p className="text-sm font-medium">Alignment: center</p>
          <Carousel
            aria-label="Align center"
            tabIndex={0}
            opts={{ align: "center", containScroll: false, startIndex: 1 }}
            className="w-full outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
          >
            <CarouselContent className="touch-pan-y">
              {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((slide) => (
                <CarouselItem key={slide} aria-label={`${slide} of 4`} className="basis-2/3">
                  <div className="flex h-36 items-center justify-center rounded-xl border bg-muted text-3xl font-semibold">
                    {slide}
                  </div>
                </CarouselItem>
              ))}
            </CarouselContent>
            <CarouselPrevious />
            <CarouselNext />
          </Carousel>
        </div>
        <div className="grid gap-3">
          <p className="text-sm font-medium">Alignment: end</p>
          <Carousel
            aria-label="Align end"
            tabIndex={0}
            opts={{ align: "end", containScroll: false, startIndex: 1 }}
            className="w-full outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
          >
            <CarouselContent className="touch-pan-y">
              {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((slide) => (
                <CarouselItem key={slide} aria-label={`${slide} of 4`} className="basis-2/3">
                  <div className="flex h-36 items-center justify-center rounded-xl border bg-muted text-3xl font-semibold">
                    {slide}
                  </div>
                </CarouselItem>
              ))}
            </CarouselContent>
            <CarouselPrevious />
            <CarouselNext />
          </Carousel>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Custom controls

Use `useCarousel` inside the root for caller-owned controls with native disabled states. This horizontal row replaces the default outboard buttons; Button retains its own motion contract. The hook throws outside a Carousel.

<ComponentExample name="custom-controls" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselNext } from "@/components/cadence/carousel";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { useCarousel } from "@/components/cadence/carousel";

function ProjectControls() {
  const { scrollPrev, scrollNext, canScrollPrev, canScrollNext } = useCarousel();
  return (
    <div className="mt-4 flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-2">
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" disabled={!canScrollPrev} onClick={scrollPrev}>
        Earlier project
      </Button>
      <Button size="sm" disabled={!canScrollNext} onClick={scrollNext}>
        Later project
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}

export function CustomControlsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-lg px-12 py-12">
      <Carousel
        aria-label="Custom project controls"
        tabIndex={0}
        className="w-full outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
      >
        <CarouselContent className="touch-pan-y">
          {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((slide) => (
            <CarouselItem key={slide} aria-label={`${slide} of 4`}>
              <div className="flex h-36 items-center justify-center rounded-xl border bg-muted text-3xl font-semibold">
                {slide}
              </div>
            </CarouselItem>
          ))}
        </CarouselContent>
        <ProjectControls />
      </Carousel>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Without motion

## When to use

- Browse a short collection of related projects, cards or photos.
- Show one highlighted item with explicit previous/next navigation.
- Allow touch swiping alongside keyboard and button navigation.

## When not to use

- Use Tabs for named views that must remain directly selectable.
- Use Scroll Area for continuous reading or long lists.
- Keep essential content discoverable without relying on automatic advance.

## API

| Part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Root | Native div props/ref; `orientation="horizontal"` (or `vertical`); `opts` and `plugins` use Embla types; `setApi(api)` receives the public instance. |
| Track | Native div props/ref/style/classes target the **inner track**. Its fixed overflow-hidden outer viewport owns the `carousel-content` slot and Embla ref. |
| Slide | Native div props/ref; group/slide semantics. Default full basis; caller classes size each slide. |
| Previous / Next | All Button props, including render, ref, state callback classes/styles and events. Defaults: outline, icon-sm. Caller disabled/onClick override the navigation defaults as upstream does. |
| Context hook | Context with API, viewport ref, original options, orientation, navigation functions and canScroll states. Throws outside Carousel. |
| API type | Exported Embla instance type (possibly undefined before initialization). |

The fixed Base UI API and new-york-v4 visuals are pinned at `96da9cc7f1aa`.
Navigation buttons retain the Base API's icon-sm default with the visual source's round size-8
shape. Orientation controls the axis even if opts.axis differs, as upstream does. Options such
as startIndex, align, loop, dragFree, watchDrag, breakpoints and direction pass to Embla.
For RTL set both native `dir="rtl"` and `opts.direction="rtl"`.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Recipe | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter / exit | — | No authored entrance or removal animation. |
| Interaction | `data.transition` | `data.transition`, engine form: Embla alone translates the track. Default duration.base maps to 22 attraction units via carouselClock; timeScale scales it. Explicit full-mode opts.duration remains native. |
| Interruption | — | Next/previous/drag retarget Embla's existing location and velocity. Release uses the effective base clock, including breakpoint options, instead of a hard-coded release duration. |
| Reduced | — | Track and loop relocation transforms retain the correct state position. Direct dragging remains available. All autonomous engine interpolation is zero; no CSS/Motion transform animation is added. |
| None | — | Same immediate state positioning, with every engine duration zero even for explicit API/plugin duration requests. |
| Buttons | — | Composed Button owns its declared feedback.press recipe; reduced/none remove press scale. Static control placement/vertical rotation are layout. |

A mode downgrade settles the existing target without resetting selection. Engine friction,
geometry and momentum destinations remain Embla-owned. Independent plugin animations remain
caller-owned. Removing the track transform would display the wrong slide and is not reduction.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Reach native controls and any focusable slide content. |
| Enter / Space | Activate a focused navigation button. |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Previous / next from inside the region, on both orientations (pinned upstream behaviour). |

Supply a region label and per-slide labels, and optionally a polite status as in the preview.
The root is not focusable by default; use tabIndex and a visible focus class when desired.
Embla scrolls focused offscreen slide content into view. Caller onKeyDownCapture replaces the
upstream capture handler; caller onClick similarly replaces the navigation action. This is not
a tab widget and does not hide offscreen content from assistive technology. Avoid interactive
content whose arrow handling conflicts with the root capture handler.

## Responsiveness and performance

Size slides with basis utilities and pair inner negative margins with slide padding. Vertical
tracks require an explicit height. Set touch-pan-y on horizontal tracks and touch-pan-x on
vertical tracks to preserve cross-axis page scrolling. Leave room for controls outside the viewport.
Embla observes viewport/slide geometry and slide mutations, reinitializing snaps as needed;
options/plugins reinitialize through the native React adapter. No layout reads happen in render.
SSR renders static first-slide markup, then Embla initializes after hydration. No autoplay,
virtualization or per-slide Motion instances are bundled. Only track transforms animate.

## Notes for AI

- Preserve opts, plugins, setApi, useCarousel and all native part props when adapting examples.
- Use the exposed Embla API for selection rather than applying another transform to the track.
- Keep selected position under reduced/none; assert the lack of interpolation, not transform:none.
- Use Button for individual actions, Tabs for directly named panels, and Scroll Area for long content.

# Scroll Area

Constrained lists and wide content with native scrolling and custom scrollbars.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/scroll-area
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge @base-ui/react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| scroll-area | `@components/cadence/scroll-area/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/scroll-area.json) |

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: scroll-area](https://cadence.dev/r/scroll-area.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

Copy both target files into the same `cadence/` tree so the relative import
of `lib/cn` resolves. Preserve the component's `"use client"` directive.
Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied
files. No motion runtime, provider or additional item-specific CSS is required.

Usage, Vertical scrolling, Horizontal scrolling, Both axes and Without overflow
use serializable props and children and can be composed in a Server Component.
Caller rendering and sizing needs a client caller for its ref, handler and
state callbacks. Changing content needs one for state and handlers. Right-to-left
content also needs a client caller as written because its track uses function
`className` and `style` props. Refs, events and other function-valued
render/state props require a client caller. Custom render components must forward
props, children and ref. The top preview needs no extra dependencies.

Install [Button](/components/button) separately for Caller rendering and sizing
and Changing content. Without the CLI, follow Button's Manual instructions to
copy all its target files and install its complete recursive dependencies.
These example-only files and dependencies are separate from Scroll Area's
two-file installation graph. The CLI is an optional shortcut:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

The RTL example imports DirectionProvider from the already-installed
`@base-ui/react/direction-provider`; it adds no npm dependency. Use both that
provider and native `dir="rtl"` for matching content direction and thumb geometry.

Constrain the root height for vertical overflow and the parent width for wide
content; grid/flex parents may need `min-w-0`. Put content padding on a child,
reserving room for the overlaid tracks. The root creates the viewport, default
vertical track and corner; add `ScrollBar orientation="horizontal"` inside it
for horizontal content. Additional tracks are rendered inside the viewport.
There is no exported Content part or viewport prop/ref API. Root props, classes,
styles and ref address the outer element; ScrollBar props address the track,
whose thumb is internal. Query the viewport slot from the root ref when the
application needs imperative scrolling.

Supply accessible names, content semantics, stable keys and individually labelled
controls. The overflowing viewport uses native Tab, arrows, Page Up/Down and
Home/End; tracks and thumbs provide pointer control. `keepMounted` retains a
track without creating overflow. `overflowEdgeThreshold` only delays edge state
attributes. Neither option hides or removes content.

SSR includes the actual content and bounded overflow viewport, so native scrolling
remains available without JavaScript. Custom track measurement, pointer dragging
and caller update buttons require hydration. Base UI refreshes geometry on native
scrolling and viewport resize; content-only growth can leave the thumb stale until
one of those occurs because this wrapper has no Content part. The caller owns
entries, dimensions, scrolling to new data, pagination and virtualization.

Scroll Area is static in full, reduced and none: native thumb positioning remains
functional and no fade, smoothing or resize interpolation is added. Native wheel,
touch momentum and keyboard scrolling follow the browser/platform policy.
Application-added smooth scrolling or animation remains caller-owned; the optional
Button composition retains Button's separate motion contract.

## Usage

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-area";

export function VerticalExample() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea aria-label="Release notes" className="h-48 w-full rounded-md border">
      <ul className="flex flex-col gap-3 p-4 pr-6 text-sm">
        {Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => (
          <li key={i.toString()}>Release {20 - i}: improved keyboard navigation and component parity.</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </ScrollArea>
  );
}
```

## Vertical scrolling

Constrain the root height and keep padding on a content child. The viewport owns native scrolling; the default vertical track appears only when content overflows. Focus the viewport and use arrows or Page Down, or scroll with a wheel or touch.

<ComponentExample name="vertical" />

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-area";

export function VerticalExample() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea aria-label="Release notes" className="h-48 w-full rounded-md border">
      <ul className="flex flex-col gap-3 p-4 pr-6 text-sm">
        {Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => (
          <li key={i.toString()}>Release {20 - i}: improved keyboard navigation and component parity.</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </ScrollArea>
  );
}
```

## Horizontal scrolling

Add a horizontal ScrollBar and give the content a width larger than its viewport. The root stays within its parent; the timeline scrolls locally without widening the page. All six phases remain in the DOM.

<ComponentExample name="horizontal" />

```tsx
import { ScrollArea, ScrollBar } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-area";

export function HorizontalExample() {

      <ol className="flex w-max gap-4 p-4 pb-6">
        {["Research", "Design", "Build", "Review", "Ship", "Learn"].map((phase) => (
          <li key={phase} className="flex h-24 w-40 items-center justify-center rounded-md bg-muted text-sm">
            {phase}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ol>
      <ScrollBar orientation="horizontal" />
    </ScrollArea>
  );
}
```

## Both axes

A bounded height and wide content create two independent native scroll ranges. The default vertical track and explicit horizontal track follow the same viewport. Reserve content space for both overlaid tracks.

<ComponentExample name="both-axes" />

```tsx
import { ScrollArea, ScrollBar } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-area";

            <span>Delivery {i + 1}: workspace components and documentation</span>
            <span className="shrink-0">Completed</span>
          </li>
        ))}

  );

```

## Without overflow

These short panels have no scroll range. The default track is absent. keepMounted retains the second panel's horizontal track in the DOM even without overflow; it does not create a scroll range or force a useful thumb. Content remains readable.

<ComponentExample name="without-overflow" />

```tsx
import { ScrollArea, ScrollBar } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-area";

export function WithoutOverflowExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <ScrollArea aria-label="Short note" className="h-32 w-full rounded-md border">
        <p className="p-4 text-sm">All changes saved.</p>
      </ScrollArea>
      <ScrollArea aria-label="Reserved track" className="h-32 w-full rounded-md border">
        <p className="p-4 text-sm">A mounted horizontal track has no scroll range.</p>
        <ScrollBar keepMounted orientation="horizontal" />
      </ScrollArea>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Caller rendering and sizing

The custom section explicitly uses `role="region"` with an accessible name instead of inheriting the primitive's presentation role. Root props, ref, classes and styles belong to the outer section, while children render inside its native viewport. State callbacks retain a fixed height and change only the overflow border. overflowEdgeThreshold delays edge attributes by 16px; it changes neither scroll range nor content visibility. The application-owned action queries the viewport slot from its root ref and scrolls instantly. There is no invented viewport prop. Install Button separately for this composition. Custom render components must forward props, children and ref.

<ComponentExample name="caller-rendering" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { ScrollArea } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-area";

export function CallerRenderingExample() {
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  function returnToTop() {
    rootRef.current
      ?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-slot="scroll-area-viewport"]')
      ?.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: "instant" });
  }
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={returnToTop}>
        Return activity to top
      </Button>
      <ScrollArea
        ref={rootRef}
        render={<section />}
        role="region"
        aria-label="Workspace activity"
        overflowEdgeThreshold={{ yStart: 16, yEnd: 16 }}
        className={(state) =>
          state.hasOverflowY ? "h-48 w-full rounded-md border border-primary" : "h-48 w-full rounded-md border"
        }
        style={() => ({ maxWidth: "100%" })}
      >
        <ol className="flex flex-col gap-3 p-4 pr-6 text-sm">
          {Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => (
            <li key={i.toString()}>
              <a href="/docs/changelog" className="underline underline-offset-4">
                Activity {i + 1}: read the changelog
              </a>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ol>
      </ScrollArea>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Right-to-left content

Use native dir for content and Base UI DirectionProvider for the primitive's thumb geometry. At the inline start, the first Arabic phase appears on the right; scrolling reveals the remaining phases without reversing the data array. The custom horizontal track also demonstrates render, callback className and style on the track, rather than on the root or internal thumb.

<ComponentExample name="rtl" />

```tsx
import { DirectionProvider } from "@base-ui/react/direction-provider";

export function RtlExample() {

            {["البحث", "التصميم", "البناء", "المراجعة", "النشر", "التعلم"].map((phase) => (
              <li key={phase} className="flex h-24 w-40 items-center justify-center rounded-md bg-muted text-sm">
                {phase}
              </li>

```

## Changing content

The caller owns entries and panel dimensions. These two actions change actual data and root height independently; the viewport and draft input keep their identities. This pinned wrapper has no Content part: content-only growth can leave thumb geometry stale until a native scroll or viewport resize. Scroll after changing the count, or resize the panel, to refresh it. It does not automatically follow new entries or virtualize them. Install Button separately for this composition.

<ComponentExample name="changing-content" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { ScrollArea } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-area";

export function ChangingContentExample() {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);
  const [tall, setTall] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setExpanded((value) => !value)}>
          Change activity count
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setTall((value) => !value)}>
          Resize activity panel
        </Button>
      </div>
      <p role="status">
        {expanded ? 40 : 20} entries · {tall ? "Tall" : "Compact"} panel
      </p>
      <ScrollArea
        aria-label="Updating activity"
        className={tall ? "h-72 w-full rounded-md border" : "h-48 w-full rounded-md border"}
      >
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 p-4 pr-6 text-sm">
          <input
            aria-label="Activity draft"
            defaultValue="Keep this draft"
            className="w-full min-w-0 rounded-md border p-2 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring"
          />
          <ol className="flex flex-col gap-3">
            {Array.from({ length: expanded ? 40 : 20 }, (_, i) => (
              <li key={i.toString()}>Activity {i + 1}: documentation updated.</li>
            ))}
          </ol>
        </div>
      </ScrollArea>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Long activity feeds constrained by a panel height.
- Horizontal timelines or collections wider than their available space.
- Bounded lists that need custom scrollbars while retaining native scrolling.

## When not to use

- For ordinary page content: allow the document to scroll.
- For paged slides: use Carousel.
- For reading progress or smooth scrolling effects: this component adds neither.

## API

| Export | Props and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `ScrollArea` | Base UI `ScrollArea.Root.Props`; no additional defaults. |
| `ScrollBar` | Base UI `ScrollArea.Scrollbar.Props`; `orientation="vertical"`, `keepMounted=false`. |

Both exports forward native events, ARIA, style, ref and Base UI `render`.
Classes merge last, including state callback classes. Root also forwards
`overflowEdgeThreshold` (Base UI default zero). Scrollbar props target the track;
the thumb is created internally. Root creates the viewport, default vertical track
and corner. ScrollArea's `children` render inside the viewport, including any
additional horizontal track, matching the pinned upstream composition.

Slots: `scroll-area`, `scroll-area-viewport`, `scroll-area-scrollbar`,
`scroll-area-thumb`. The scrollbar includes `data-orientation`.
Root classes, padding, borders and styles remain on the root; content padding
belongs on a child. Root ref does not address the viewport. No viewport prop or
ref API is invented; query its slot from the root for application-owned imperative scrolling.

## Motion contract

T0: empty recipe set, no provider, hook, timing token or authored animation.
Enter, exit and resize are immediate. Full, reduced and none share static markup.
The primitive positions and sizes its thumb from actual native scroll geometry;
those transforms represent user position and remain functional in every mode.
No smoothing, automatic scrolling, entrance or opacity transition is added.

| Mode | Authored motion |
| --- | --- |
| full | none |
| reduced | none |
| none | none |

Upstream focus-ring and colour feedback remain CSS state feedback. Native wheel,
touch momentum and keyboard scrolling follow browser/platform preferences.
Caller-added smooth scrolling and CSS animation are application-owned.

## Accessibility

- Base UI supplies a focusable viewport when overflow exists with a visible keyboard focus ring.
  Tab enters the viewport and its interactive descendants; arrows, Page Up/Down,
  Home/End retain native browser scrolling. No custom keyboard model is added.
- Give the root a meaningful accessible name, as in Usage. Keep list or document
  semantics in the content and label interactive controls individually.
- Tracks and thumbs are pointer controls; keyboard users scroll the native viewport.
- Constrain height for vertical overflow and width for horizontal overflow. The
  viewport retains all content on narrow screens; size a grid parent with `min-w-0`.
- Base UI updates geometry on native scrolling and viewport resize. The pinned
  wrapper has no Content part: content-only growth may leave the thumb stale until
  a scroll or viewport resize occurs. Cadence preserves that upstream behaviour. It adds no
  measurement loop, data processing or virtualization. Paginate or virtualize large
  datasets in the application.

## Responsiveness and performance

Give the root explicit dimensions so its viewport can scroll; horizontal scrolling needs the
corresponding ScrollBar. Parent grids may need min-w-0. Base UI manages custom scrollbar interaction
while content uses native scrolling; it does not virtualize children.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native
HTML behavior remains browser-owned. The server renders the real content and bounded overflow viewport, so native scrolling remains available without JavaScript. Custom track measurement, pointer dragging and caller-owned update buttons require hydration. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Preserve root/viewport ownership, native scrolling and Base UI render/ref support.
- Add ScrollBar with horizontal orientation for wide content; its default stays vertical.
- Do not add decorative fading, smooth scrolling or animation to this T0 component.


2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| chart | `@components/cadence/chart/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/chart.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: chart](https://cadence.dev/r/chart.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, including every shared helper, into the same
`cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and the shipped `"use client"`
directives. Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind
scans these files. No additional Chart-specific CSS is required. Configured
colours such as `--primary` and `--chart-1` must exist in your theme;
ChartStyle scopes the resulting `--color-<key>` variables to each chart.

Put `"use client"` at the top of the caller file for Usage and every chart
example, including static bar, line, area and pie compositions. Recharts
3.10.1 cannot be imported directly in a React Server Component: its context
initialization requires the client boundary. A Server Component may fetch data
and pass serializable rows/configuration into that client wrapper. Define
config icon component references, tooltip/legend formatters, event handlers,
refs and live-data state inside the client boundary. Preserve the wrapper when
copying the examples below, even where their snippets omit the directive.

Import chart types, series and axes from the already-installed `recharts`;
ChartContainer supplies configuration, responsive sizing and the motion clock,
not a data prop. Keep data keys aligned with config keys and series
`dataKey`/`nameKey`; use `var(--color-<key>)` on series. Provide either
`color` or a complete light/dark `theme` map per config entry. Tooltip and
legend content need ChartContainer context. `hideIcon` replaces a config
icon with the colour marker; it does not remove that marker. `type="none"`
payload entries are omitted. Tooltip formatters replace the whole value row,
so include its label and value; `labelFormatter` formats the heading.

Legends and theme colours uses four caller-supplied theme variables. The base
theme above does not define them. For example, add these semantic mappings
to your global stylesheet; choose your own accessible palette as needed:

```css
:root {
  --chart-1: var(--foreground);
  --chart-2: var(--foreground);
  --chart-3: var(--muted-foreground);
  --chart-4: var(--muted-foreground);
}
```

These mappings follow the base foreground tokens when the theme changes.
This example also needs the example-only icons:

```package-manager
npm install lucide-react
```

Live data and motion ownership additionally uses [Button](/components/button).
Without the CLI, follow Button's Manual instructions to copy all its target
files and install its complete recursive dependencies. These example-only
dependencies are separate from Chart's nine-file graph. The optional CLI
shortcut is:

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

The top preview uses only Chart and Recharts. Give the container a nonzero
height/min-height and available width; flex/grid parents may need `min-w-0`.
ResponsiveContainer uses ResizeObserver after hydration; `initialDimension`
defaults to 320 × 200 and is only the initial fallback, not the final layout.
Supply an accessible name, enable Recharts `accessibilityLayer`, and retain
a caption/text summary or data table for exact values. The caller owns data,
loading, filtering, formatting, stable identity and responsive tick density.
Server rendering reserves the chart container; SVG charts appear after
hydration. Responsive measurement, keyboard/pointer tooltips and update actions
require JavaScript. Keep the adjacent text/table usable without it.

The provider files are required imports; wrapping is optional. Standalone
charts respect the system preference. Full animates SVG data geometry through
`data.transition`; reduced and none settle it immediately with no chart fade.
Static SVG coordinate transforms remain. Provider `timeScale` controls the
clock; series `animationDuration`, `animationBegin` and `animationEasing`
cannot bypass it, while `isAnimationActive={false}` opts a series out.
ChartTooltip placement is immediate in every mode. Cadence traverses the
provided chart elements for its installed Recharts series; custom component
boundaries, shapes, nested animation controllers and independent CSS/WAAPI
must implement the same motion policy themselves. Mode changes should keep
the chart, axes, legend and caller state mounted.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Bar, BarChart, XAxis } from "recharts";
import { ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartTooltipContent } from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const config = { visits: { label: "Visits", color: "var(--primary)" } };
const data = [
  { month: "Jan", visits: 186 },
  { month: "Feb", visits: 305 },
];

export function Example() {
  return (
    <ChartContainer role="group" config={config} className="min-h-48 w-full" aria-label="Monthly visits">
      <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
        <XAxis dataKey="month" />
        <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
        <Bar dataKey="visits" fill="var(--color-visits)" />
      </BarChart>
    </ChartContainer>
  );
}
```

## Bar chart

Use bars to compare categories. Each series shares labels and colours with the tooltip and legend; the data table preserves exact values without relying on colour.

<ComponentExample name="bar" />

```tsx
import { Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, XAxis } from "recharts";
import {
  ChartContainer,
  ChartLegend,
  ChartLegendContent,
  ChartTooltip,
  ChartTooltipContent,
} from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const config = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", color: "var(--foreground)" },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" },
};
const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

export function BarExample() {
  const data = baseline;
  return (
    <figure className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-3">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">Monthly visits · bar</figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group" config={config} className="h-64 w-full min-w-0" aria-label="Monthly visits, bar chart">
        <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
          <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
          <XAxis dataKey="month" tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
          <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
          <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent hideIcon={false} />} />
          <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} isAnimationActive />
          <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} isAnimationActive />
        </BarChart>
      </ChartContainer>
      <DataTable data={data} />
    </figure>
  );
}
```

## Legends and theme colours

ChartStyle scopes the config colour variables to each chart. The first legend uses config icons; the second uses `hideIcon` to replace them with colour markers. Light and dark theme mappings apply independently of neighbouring examples.

<ComponentExample name="legends" />

```tsx
import { MonitorIcon, SmartphoneIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, XAxis } from "recharts";
import {
  ChartContainer,
  ChartLegend,
  ChartLegendContent,
  ChartTooltip,
  ChartTooltipContent,
} from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>

        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

const themeConfig = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", icon: MonitorIcon, theme: { light: "var(--chart-1)", dark: "var(--chart-2)" } },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", icon: SmartphoneIcon, theme: { light: "var(--chart-3)", dark: "var(--chart-4)" } },
};
function ThemedChart({ hideLegendIcons = false }: { hideLegendIcons?: boolean }) {
  const data = baseline;
  return (
    <figure className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-3">
```
