## Tooltip indicators and formatting

Compare dot, line, dashed and hidden indicators directly. Each real tooltip starts at February and remains available from the chart keyboard surface. The last chart formats its heading and value rows; `hideLabel` removes the heading in the hidden-indicator example. A config icon takes precedence over a marker, and entries with `type="none"` are omitted.

<ComponentExample name="tooltips" />

```tsx
import { Bar, BarChart, XAxis } from "recharts";
import { ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartTooltipContent } from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const config = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", color: "var(--foreground)" },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" },
};
const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

function TooltipExample({
  indicator = "dot",
  hidden = false,
  formatted = false,
}: {
  indicator?: "dot" | "line" | "dashed";
  hidden?: boolean;
  formatted?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <figure className="grid min-w-0 gap-2">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">
        {formatted ? "Formatted values" : hidden ? "Without an indicator or heading" : `${indicator} indicator`}
      </figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group"
        config={config}
        className="h-48 w-full min-w-0"
        aria-label={`Visits, ${formatted ? "formatted" : hidden ? "no indicator" : indicator} tooltip`}
      >
        <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={baseline}>
          <XAxis dataKey="month" />
          <ChartTooltip
            defaultIndex={1}
            active
            content={
              <ChartTooltipContent
                indicator={indicator}
                hideIndicator={hidden}
                hideLabel={hidden}
                labelFormatter={formatted ? (label) => `Month: ${label}` : undefined}
                formatter={
                  formatted
                    ? (value, name) => (
                        <span>
                          {name}: {Number(value).toLocaleString()} visits
                        </span>
                      )
                    : undefined
                }
              />
            }
          />
          <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" />
        </BarChart>
      </ChartContainer>
    </figure>
  );
}

export function Tooltips() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-6">
      <TooltipExample />
      <TooltipExample indicator="line" />
      <TooltipExample indicator="dashed" />
      <TooltipExample hidden />
      <TooltipExample formatted />
      <DataTable data={baseline} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Live data and motion ownership

Each Update action replaces only its own chart data. Recharts owns interpolation and the data model; Cadence owns the `data.transition` clock. The deliberately explicit series timing below cannot override the inherited clock. `isAnimationActive={false}` opts a series out. Reduced and none settle geometry immediately, including a running transition when the header mode changes. Custom shapes, nested controllers and independent CSS/WAAPI must honour the same modes. Tooltip position changes stay immediate.

<ComponentExample name="live-data" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Area, AreaChart, Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, Line, LineChart, Pie, PieChart, XAxis } from "recharts";
import {
  type ChartConfig,
  ChartContainer,
  ChartLegend,
  ChartLegendContent,
  ChartTooltip,
  ChartTooltipContent,
} from "@/components/cadence/chart";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

type ChartKind = "bar" | "line" | "area" | "pie";
const config = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", color: "var(--foreground)" },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" },
};
const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

function VisitChart({
  kind = "bar",
  data = baseline,
  chartConfig = config,
  hideLegendIcons = false,
}: {
  kind?: ChartKind;
  data?: typeof baseline;
  chartConfig?: ChartConfig;
  hideLegendIcons?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <figure className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-3">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">Monthly visits · {kind}</figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group" config={chartConfig} className="h-64 w-full min-w-0" aria-label={`Monthly visits, ${kind} chart`}>
        {kind === "bar" ? (
          <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
            <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
            <XAxis dataKey="month" tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
            <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
            <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent hideIcon={hideLegendIcons} />} />
            <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} isAnimationActive animationDuration={5000} />
            <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} isAnimationActive animationBegin={5000} />
          </BarChart>
        ) : kind === "line" ? (
          <LineChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
            <XAxis dataKey="month" />
            <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
            <Line dataKey="desktop" stroke="var(--color-desktop)" isAnimationActive animationDuration={5000} />
          </LineChart>
        ) : kind === "area" ? (
          <AreaChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
            <XAxis dataKey="month" />
            <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
            <Area dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-mobile)" stroke="var(--color-desktop)" isAnimationActive />
          </AreaChart>
        ) : (
          <PieChart accessibilityLayer>
            <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent nameKey="month" />} />
            <Pie data={data} dataKey="desktop" nameKey="month" fill="var(--color-desktop)" isAnimationActive />
          </PieChart>
        )}
      </ChartContainer>
      <DataTable data={data} />
    </figure>
  );
}

function UpdatingChart({ kind }: { kind: ChartKind }) {
  const [updated, setUpdated] = useState(false);
  const data = updated
    ? baseline.map((row) => ({ ...row, desktop: 350 - row.desktop, mobile: row.mobile + 40 }))
    : baseline;
  return (
    <div className="grid min-w-0 gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" className="justify-self-start" onClick={() => setUpdated((value) => !value)}>
        Update {kind} data
      </Button>
      <output className="text-sm" aria-live="polite">
        {updated ? "Updated" : "Baseline"}
      </output>
      <VisitChart kind={kind} data={data} />
    </div>
  );
}

export function LiveData() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-8">
      <UpdatingChart kind="bar" />
      <UpdatingChart kind="line" />
      <UpdatingChart kind="area" />
      <UpdatingChart kind="pie" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Comparing categories with a bar chart.
- Showing trends with Recharts Line/Area series.
- Sharing labels, colours and formatting between series, tooltip and legend.

## When not to use

- Exact values without a visual comparison: use Table.
- A single completion value: use Progress.
- Large datasets requiring canvas/WebGL: choose a dedicated rendering engine.

## API

### `ChartContainer`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| config | ChartConfig | required | Per-series label, icon, color or light/dark theme. |
| children | ResponsiveContainer children | required | Recharts chart composition. |
| initialDimension | `{ width: number; height: number }` | 320 × 200 | Initial SSR/responsive fallback. |
| id | string | React useId | Scoped data-chart suffix; upstream does not forward id as a DOM id. |
| className / style / ref | div props | — | Applied to outer div; classes merged last. |

### `ChartTooltip` and `ChartTooltipContent`

ChartTooltip accepts Recharts Tooltip props; positional CSS animation is always disabled.
ChartTooltipContent retains upstream Recharts Tooltip, default content and div prop types.
Native div attributes, styles, events and refs apply to the content root. Engine placement and
animation metadata is not emitted as DOM attributes.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| indicator | dot / line / dashed | dot | Series marker. |
| hideLabel / hideIndicator | boolean | false | Suppress heading / marker. |
| nameKey / labelKey | string | — | Resolve config keys from payload. |
| formatter / labelFormatter | Recharts callbacks | — | Custom row / heading. |
| color / labelClassName / className | string | — | Marker / heading / root styles. |
| active / payload / label | Recharts content props | — | Usually injected by Tooltip. |

### `ChartLegend`, `ChartLegendContent`, `ChartStyle`, `ChartConfig`

ChartLegend is Recharts Legend. ChartLegendContent accepts default legend content + div prop
types; consumes className, payload, nameKey, hideIcon=false, verticalAlign="bottom". Top alignment
adds bottom padding. Native div attributes, styles, events and refs apply to the content root.
Legend formatter receives the resolved label, entry and index; onClick/onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave
receive entry, index and event. Clickable entries support Tab, Enter and Space. Engine placement
and animation options belong on ChartLegend/ChartTooltip. ChartStyle accepts id
and config and emits nothing without configured colours. ChartConfig is a record of label/icon
plus either color or a complete light/dark theme map. Helpers require ChartContainer context.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Series enter / data update | SVG data geometry (T4 engine form) | `data.transition` | Recharts retargets from its series state |
| Tooltip / legend | Immediate placement; no wrapper reveal | — | Immediate |
| Reduced | Geometry jumps to final data; no transform/scale tween | `data.transition` | Running controller completes |
| None | Zero animation duration; final data | `data.transition` | Running controller completes |

The full clock is duration.base / ease.out, scaled by provider timeScale. Reduced adds no fade
because comparison must remain legible. Static SVG coordinate transforms are retained in all
modes. This is not a DOM layout animation. Mode changes do not remount the chart.

## Accessibility

Give the chart an accessible name, keep Recharts accessibilityLayer enabled, and provide a
text summary or data table for exact values. Tooltips are supplemental. Labels and values must
convey meaning independently of colour. Use a visible focus ring on the chart surface when needed.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Enter / leave the Recharts chart surface. |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Move the active data point and tooltip in Cartesian charts. |

Legend content is descriptive, not a toggle control. Add native buttons for series filtering.

## Responsive behavior

Give ChartContainer a nonzero height or min-height. ResponsiveContainer measures available
space through ResizeObserver; the initialDimension fallback is 320 × 200. Use fewer ticks and
short labels on narrow screens; a caption and data table remain available without pointer input.

## Performance

Recharts is an explicit dependency, loaded only on chart pages in this site. Limit plotted data
and series rather than animating thousands of marks. Cadence uses one rAF per active series,
cancels on cleanup, and completes immediately in reduced/none. No render-time DOM measurement
or wrapper entrance is added. Browser evidence covers data updates, resize and mode downgrade.

## Notes for AI

Keep the upstream composition: ChartContainer wraps a Recharts chart; it does not accept data.
Import series and axes from Recharts. Never erase SVG coordinate transforms to satisfy a motion
assertion. Related: Table for values, Progress for one completion value, Calendar for dates.

# Calendar

Select dates, multiple days, and ranges with accessible month navigation.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/calendar
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority react-day-picker@9.13.2 date-fns@4.1.0 lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |

| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all ten target files, including Button and every shared helper, into the
same `cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and shipped `"use client"`
directives. Button is already a recursive dependency, including its full npm
dependencies and source; the Controlled month and date example needs no
additional installation. All other examples use packages and provider files
already listed above.

Complete the base theme setup and ensure Tailwind CSS v4 scans the copied
files. Calendar supplies its own DayPicker class names; no additional
Calendar-specific stylesheet or `react-day-picker/style.css` import is
required. Keep DayPicker's optional `animate` CSS clock off when using
Cadence month motion.

Keep `"use client"` on the caller files shown in Usage and all examples.
Declare selection/month state, event handlers, refs, function matchers,
`labels`, `formatters` and custom `components` inside that client boundary.
date-fns locale objects such as `enUS`, `fr` and `arSA` contain functions:
import and pass them inside the client caller as well. A Server Component can
render Calendar with serializable props, including Date values and plain
date/range/weekday matchers, or pass those values to a client wrapper; Date
objects alone do not require a client caller. Controlled values need their
matching client callbacks. Omitting `mode` browses dates without selection.

The caller owns selected dates/ranges, visible month when controlled,
timezone, form serialization and application validation. Pass consistent
`defaultMonth`, `today` and, when needed, `timeZone` across server and
browser. For native dropdown captions, supply an explicit locale within the
client wrapper to avoid environment-dependent month formatting. Locale does
not translate the pinned DayPicker's default previous/next labels: provide
`labels` for those controls and distinct `aria-label`/`labels.labelNav`
names for multiple calendars. The examples compose visible day numerals with
localized accessible dates; preserve that composition when changing formatters.

Keep the complete DayPicker props on a custom day component, including its
events, disabled state, children and focus modifiers. The Custom day example
wraps `CalendarDayButton` and passes its locale explicitly. Replacing
`Month` or `MonthGrid` also replaces the default month motion owner;
caller-provided grid opacity/transform styles take precedence over the
corresponding animation property.

Provider imports are required; wrapping is optional. Standalone Calendar
respects the system preference. Month changes fade and translate the existing
grid in full mode, fade only in reduced, and update immediately in none.
First paint and selection/range styles are static, and week-count height
changes immediately. A fixed `CadenceProvider mode="none"` also disables
month animation under a full-mode parent. Do not key/remount Calendar by month
to animate it; keep focus and caller drafts in the existing tree.

Cells default to 32px; allow space for larger cells, week numbers and multiple
months. Months stack below `md` and form a row at `md`. Server-rendered
dates, initial selection, native caption options and source files remain
readable without JavaScript; navigation, selection, focus management and
caller actions require hydration. Calendar is inline and creates no hidden
form field or popup. Follow [Usage](#usage) for the client selection example.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";
import { useState } from "react";
import { formatDay, labelDayButton, labelGridcell } from "react-day-picker";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function SingleSelectionExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date(2026, 10, 12));
  return (
    <Calendar
      {...stable}
      aria-label="Appointment date"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Appointment date navigation" }}
      mode="single"
      selected={date}
      onSelect={setDate}
      footer={date ? `Selected: ${date.toDateString()}` : "Choose a date"}
    />
  );
}
```

## Multiple dates

Choose one to three independent workshop days with `required`, `min` and `max`. In pinned DayPicker 9.13.2, selecting a fourth date resets the selection to that new date; it does not keep the previous three or disable all other dates.

<ComponentExample name="multiple-dates" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";
import { useState } from "react";
import { formatDay, labelDayButton, labelGridcell } from "react-day-picker";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function MultipleDatesExample() {
  const [days, setDays] = useState<Date[]>([new Date(2026, 10, 12)]);
  return (
    <Calendar
      {...stable}
      aria-label="Workshop days"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Workshop days navigation" }}
      mode="multiple"
      required
      min={1}
      max={3}
      selected={days}
      onSelect={setDays}
      footer={`${days.length} ${days.length === 1 ? "date" : "dates"}`}
    />
  );
}
```

## Date ranges

Choose a weekday trip of at least two nights. `min` counts nights, not inclusive dates. Weekends are disabled; with `excludeDisabled`, clicking an end across a disabled day resets the start to the clicked date. The caller owns the partial and completed range.

<ComponentExample name="date-ranges" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";
import { useState } from "react";
import { formatDay, labelDayButton, labelGridcell } from "react-day-picker";
import type { DateRange } from "react-day-picker";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function DateRangesExample() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | undefined>();
  return (
    <Calendar
      {...stable}
      aria-label="Weekday trip"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Weekday trip navigation" }}
      mode="range"
      selected={range}
      onSelect={setRange}
      min={2}
      disabled={{ dayOfWeek: [0, 6] }}
      excludeDisabled
      footer={
        range?.from ? `${range.from.toDateString()} – ${range.to?.toDateString() ?? "Choose an end"}` : "Choose a start"
      }
    />
  );
}
```

## Multiple months

A two-month range stays visible across November and December. `pagedNavigation` advances by two months. The real months stack below md and sit side by side at md; `fixedWeeks` reserves six rows in each month. Selection remains one range across both grids.

<ComponentExample name="multiple-months" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";

import type { DateRange } from "react-day-picker";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function MultipleMonthsExample() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | undefined>({
    from: new Date(2026, 10, 28),
    to: new Date(2026, 11, 3),
  });
  return (
    <Calendar
      {...stable}
      aria-label="Two-month stay"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Two-month stay navigation" }}

```

## Navigation button variants

All six `buttonVariant` values apply to previous/next navigation buttons. Day buttons keep their selection styling. Each calendar navigates independently; the labels identify the comparison rather than changing any prop.

```tsx
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,

export function NavigationButtonVariantsExample() {
  return (
```

## Localized navigation

The French calendar starts weeks on Monday and offers native dropdowns. The Arabic calendar has an explicit RTL direction and narrow visible weekday labels; its accessible weekday names remain complete. A date-fns locale localizes dates, but pinned DayPicker keeps default previous/next labels in English: provide `labels` for those controls as well. Each calendar has its own accessible name and language.

<ComponentExample name="localized-navigation" />

```tsx

      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function LocalizedNavigationExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-6">
      <Calendar
        {...stable}
        aria-label="Calendrier français"
        lang="fr"
        locale={fr}
        weekStartsOn={1}
        captionLayout="dropdown"
        startMonth={new Date(2025, 0)}

        labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Navigation du calendrier français", labelNext: () => "Mois suivant", labelPrevious: () => "Mois précédent" }}
      />
```

## Controlled month and date

Both the visible month and selected date belong to this example. “Set November 20” updates them together; “Clear appointment” clears only the selection. Navigation and keyboard changes still call `onMonthChange`. The note is an independent draft that should survive month changes, site motion changes and source expansion. Install Button as well for these caller-owned actions.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-month-and-date" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";
import { useState } from "react";
import { formatDay, labelDayButton, labelGridcell } from "react-day-picker";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function ControlledMonthAndDateExample() {
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(november);
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date(2026, 10, 12));
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-2">
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          onClick={() => {
            setMonth(november);
            setDate(new Date(2026, 10, 20));
          }}
        >
          Set November 20
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setDate(undefined)}>
          Clear appointment
        </Button>
      </div>
      <input
        aria-label="Appointment note"
        defaultValue="Keep this draft"
        className="w-full min-w-0 rounded-md border p-2 text-sm"
      />
      <Calendar
        {...stable}
        aria-label="Controlled appointment"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Controlled appointment navigation" }}
        mode="single"
        month={month}
        onMonthChange={setMonth}
        selected={date}
        onSelect={setDate}
        weekStartsOn={1}
        fixedWeeks
        footer={date ? `Selected: ${date.toDateString()}` : "No appointment"}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled dates

Compose exact-date, before-date and weekday matchers. November 5 is unavailable and November 11 is hidden. Disabled dates remain visible but cannot be selected; hidden dates leave their grid position empty. These are presentation and selection constraints, not application validation or server authorization.

<ComponentExample name="disabled-dates" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";
import { useState } from "react";
import { formatDay, labelDayButton, labelGridcell } from "react-day-picker";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function DisabledDatesExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
  return (
    <Calendar
      {...stable}
      aria-label="Available appointment"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Available appointment navigation" }}
      mode="single"
      selected={date}
      onSelect={setDate}
      disabled={[new Date(2026, 10, 5), { before: new Date(2026, 10, 4) }, { dayOfWeek: [0, 6] }]}
      hidden={new Date(2026, 10, 11)}
      footer={date ? `Selected: ${date.toDateString()}` : "Weekdays from November 4; November 5 unavailable"}
    />
  );
}
```

## Grid layout

Compare a six-row grid with week numbers and Monday starts against a larger-cell calendar hiding outside-month dates. `showOutsideDays` defaults to true; `fixedWeeks` and `showWeekNumber` default to false. `--cell-size` belongs to the caller, not a Calendar size enum.

<ComponentExample name="grid-layout" />

```tsx

    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function GridLayoutExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-6">
      <Calendar
        {...stable}
        aria-label="Fixed six-week grid"
```

## Custom day button

Compose the exported `CalendarDayButton` to preserve native events, disabled state, focus and modifiers while adding a decorative availability dot on Tuesdays. The caption formatter and today class are caller overrides. A static `styles.month_grid.opacity: 1` keeps text at full contrast and takes precedence over the opacity animation; the grid can still translate in full mode. Replacing Month or MonthGrid entirely also takes ownership of month motion.

<ComponentExample name="custom-day" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";
import { useState } from "react";
import { formatDay, labelDayButton, labelGridcell } from "react-day-picker";
import type { DayButtonProps } from "react-day-picker";
import { Calendar, CalendarDayButton } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

function BookingDay(props: DayButtonProps) {
  return (
    <CalendarDayButton {...props} locale={enUS}>
      {props.children}
      <span aria-hidden="true">{props.day.date.getDay() === 2 ? "•" : ""}</span>
    </CalendarDayButton>
  );
}

export function CustomDayExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
  return (
    <Calendar
      {...stable}
      aria-label="Booking availability"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Booking availability navigation" }}
      mode="single"
      selected={date}
      onSelect={setDate}
      components={{ DayButton: BookingDay }}
      formatters={{
        formatCaption: (date) => `Bookings · ${date.toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "long", year: "numeric" })}`,
      }}
      styles={{ month_grid: { opacity: 1 } }}
      classNames={{ today: "rounded-md underline" }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Browse without selection

Omitting `mode` displays dates without selectable day buttons. The first calendar can browse only November–December; `disableNavigation` keeps disabled navigation buttons, while `hideNavigation` removes them. These fixed calendars have independent navigation and no invented selected value.

<ComponentExample name="browse-only" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { formatDay, labelDayButton, labelGridcell } from "react-day-picker";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function BrowseOnlyExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-6">
      <Calendar
        {...stable}
        aria-label="Browse months without selecting"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Browse months without selecting navigation" }}
        startMonth={november}
        endMonth={new Date(2026, 11, 1)}
      />
      <Calendar {...stable} aria-label="Navigation disabled"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Disabled calendar navigation" }} disableNavigation />
      <Calendar {...stable} aria-label="Navigation hidden"

    </div>
  );
}
```

## Without motion

This named example intentionally overrides the header with a fixed `CadenceProvider mode="none"`. Its first paint and later month changes are immediate. Ordinary examples inherit the header, including the system reduced-motion preference; reduced mode fades the grid without translating it.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { enUS } from "date-fns/locale";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";
import { formatDay, labelDayButton, labelGridcell } from "react-day-picker";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

const november = new Date(2026, 10, 1);
const today = new Date(2026, 10, 4);
const stable = {
  defaultMonth: november, today, locale: enUS, className: "min-w-64 rounded-md border",
  labels: {
    // Include the visible numeral while retaining the localized date and today/selected context.
    labelDayButton: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelDayButton>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelDayButton(...args)}`,
    labelGridcell: (...args: Parameters<typeof labelGridcell>) =>
      `${formatDay(args[0], args[2], args[3])}, ${labelGridcell(...args)}`,
  },
};

export function WithoutMotionExample() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <Calendar {...stable} aria-label="Instant month navigation"
      labels={{ ...stable.labels, labelNav: () => "Instant calendar navigation" }} mode="single" />
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Pick a date in a booking or scheduling interface.
- Select several independent days or a contiguous range.
- Browse adjacent months with keyboard and localized captions.

## When not to use

Use an Input for free-form date text. Compose a Popover for a date-picker field;
Calendar itself is an inline calendar, without field serialization or popup orchestration.

## API

### `Calendar`

All DayPicker 9.13.2 props and discriminated selection types are preserved.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode | single / multiple / range | undefined | No selection when omitted. |
| selected / onSelect | DayPicker selection type / handler | — | Caller owns selected values. |
| month / onMonthChange | Date / handler | — | Controlled navigation. Otherwise use defaultMonth. |
| showOutsideDays | boolean | true | Show days from adjacent months. |
| captionLayout | DayPicker caption layout | label | Label or native month/year dropdowns. |
| buttonVariant | Button variant | ghost | Navigation button appearance. |
| locale / weekStartsOn | Partial Locale / 0–6 | DayPicker locale | Labels, formatting and week boundary. |
| disabled / hidden | Matcher or Matcher[] | — | DayPicker matching rules. |
| numberOfMonths / fixedWeeks / showWeekNumber | number / boolean / boolean | 1 / false / false | Grid layout options. |
| className / classNames / style / styles | DayPicker styles | — | Caller overrides win. |
| formatters / labels / components | DayPicker overrides | — | Override individual formatters, accessible labels or entire parts. |
| animate | boolean | false | Forwarded upstream API; external DayPicker animation CSS is caller-owned. Do not combine a second CSS clock with Cadence motion. |

### `CalendarDayButton`

Accepts DayPicker's DayButton props (`day`, `modifiers`, native button attributes) plus
`locale?: Partial<Locale>`. Preserves native events, disabled state, classes, styles and
focus management. Selection and range modifiers have the upstream data attributes.
Custom components replace default parts completely and must maintain the same accessibility
and motion contract. A custom Month or MonthGrid also takes ownership of month motion.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Month changes | opacity and signed horizontal transform on the actual grid | `data.transition`, distance.sm | Yes; latest month replaces the target, without remounting the month tree. |
| Reduced | opacity only | `data.transition` reduced | Mode changes settle running motion. |
| None | Immediate grid update | zero duration | No animation is started. |
| Selection / enter / exit | Static selection and range styles | none | No decoration on mount. |

The same grid responds to buttons, native dropdowns, keyboard navigation and external controlled
month updates. Week-count height changes immediately. Caller transform/opacity styles take
precedence over the corresponding animation property. No outgoing duplicate steals focus.

## Accessibility

DayPicker owns grid labels, selected/disabled semantics and roving focus. Native month/year
selects stay keyboard reachable. Pass a meaningful `aria-label` when several calendars appear, and a distinct `labels.labelNav` for each navigation landmark. These examples prepend the visible day numeral to DayPicker’s existing `labelDayButton` and browse-only `labelGridcell`, preserving its localized full date and today/selected context for speech input. These are caller-owned label overrides; Calendar retains DayPicker’s defaults. If you customize `formatDay` or locale-provided day labels, compose those same values into the accessible name.
DayPicker 9.13.2 keeps its default navigation labels in English even with a date-fns locale;
provide `labels` to localize those strings. Use the `footer` live region or a separate status for selected values. Do not replace a day
with a non-interactive element in a selectable calendar.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Previous/next day or week; crosses month boundaries. |
| Home / End | Start/end of week. |
| Page Up / Page Down | Previous/next month. |
| Shift + Page Up / Page Down | Previous/next year. |
| Enter / Space | Select focused day using the active selection mode. |
| Tab | Move between navigation, caption controls and the roving day target. |

## Validation and data ownership

Calendar renders the caller's selection and disabled matchers. The caller owns business rules,
validation, timezone, serialization and form state. No hidden field or schema is created.
DayPicker's required/min/max/excludeDisabled selection behavior is forwarded unchanged.
In 9.13.2, selecting another date at the multiple-mode max resets selection to that date.
With excludeDisabled, a range crossing a disabled date resets its start to the clicked date.

## Responsive behavior

Cells default to 32px and can be enlarged with `className="[--cell-size:--spacing(10)]"`.
Multiple months stack vertically below md and become a row at md. Provide enough space when
customizing cells, week numbers or month counts. The preview is checked at 390px and 1280px.

## Performance

No layout measurements, duplicate month DOM or animation timers. Only the changing month grid
animates; dates and keyboard focus remain managed by DayPicker. The dependency is pinned to
9.13.2 with date-fns 4.1.0. Pass an explicit defaultMonth/today/timeZone when server and client
must agree across timezone or date boundaries. For SSR dropdown captions, pass an explicit locale
(e.g. enUS from date-fns/locale): the pinned upstream formatter uses the environment locale
when locale is omitted, which can differ between server and browser.

## Notes for AI

Keep the discriminated DayPicker selection props together. Do not introduce validation or
remount with a month key to animate. Prefer Calendar inside Popover for a field, and preserve
custom labels, locale and disabled matchers when composing it.

# Navigation Menu

Site navigation with shared popup content and interruptible sizing.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/navigation-menu
```

The action examples also use `@cadence/button`; Retained content uses `@cadence/input`.
Add those registry items when copying the corresponding compositions.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.
- [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) |
| navigation-menu | `@components/cadence/navigation-menu/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/navigation-menu.json) |

[Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json)

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json)

[Source files: navigation-menu](https://cadence.dev/r/navigation-menu.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all nine target files, including every shared helper, into the same
`cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and shipped `"use client"`
directives. Complete the base theme setup and ensure Tailwind CSS v4 scans
the copied files. No additional Navigation Menu stylesheet is required.

For the action examples, also follow [Button manual installation](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation),
copying every target and installing its recursive dependencies. Retained
content additionally needs [Input manual installation](https://cadence.dev/components/input#installation).
Both pages provide complete files and npm commands without the shadcn CLI;
merge shared targets once. The RTL example's `DirectionProvider` comes from
the already listed `@base-ui/react` package. The fixed-motion example uses
the provider files above.

Usage can compose these client components from a Server Component with its
string props and children. Keep state, refs, `actionsRef`, event handlers,
callback classes/styles and function-based `render` composition inside a
`"use client"` caller. `navigationMenuTriggerStyle()` is also exported from
a client module: call it inside that client boundary, as the examples do.
Do not invoke it from a Server Component. Preserve the client boundaries shown in the
examples when copying their compositions.

Compose Root, List, Item, Trigger, Content and real Link destinations as in
[Usage](#usage). Give navigation landmarks distinct accessible labels and
items stable values. Root already appends one portaled positioner, popup and
viewport; do not append another `NavigationMenuPositioner`. Root forwards
`align` to that positioner; orientation changes keyboard traversal, not its
bottom placement. Size each content panel responsively within the available
viewport; the shared viewport scrolls overflowing content. For RTL, preserve
`DirectionProvider`, the native wrapper's `dir`/`lang`, and those native
attributes on the portaled content.

The caller owns route destinations, active-route state and router integration.
Custom link components must forward native link props and refs. `active`
marks the current page; `closeOnClick` opts into closing on link activation.
Controlled `value` needs a matching client `onValueChange`; `null` closes
the menu. Base UI owns hover intent, click/touch, focus guards, keyboard
traversal and outside/Escape dismissal. Keep its native focus handlers and
portal lifecycle. Intent delays are not animation durations.

Provider imports are required; wrapping is optional. Standalone menus respect
the system preference. Full mode scales/fades the popup and resizes its
measured width/height; reduced keeps opacity and applies geometry instantly;
none removes every authored transition. Keep the same popup through updates
and mode changes. `keepMounted` retains inactive panels while the portal is
open, but a complete close unmounts the default portal and resets uncontrolled
input drafts on reopening. Store persistent drafts in caller state.

Without JavaScript, server-rendered top-level labels and standalone anchors
remain available, and both installation methods expose complete source.
Popup content is portaled and requires hydration: provide another accessible
route to essential destinations instead of relying on hover-only access.
Navigation Menu does not create a mobile drawer or manage application data.

## Usage

```tsx
import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuTrigger, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuLink } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function SiteNavigation() {
  return (
    <NavigationMenu aria-label="Main navigation">
      <NavigationMenuList>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="learn">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Learn</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent className="w-64">
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs">Documentation</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}
```

## Grouped links

Use native destinations inside independently sized panels. Learn has a compact list; Build uses a two-column grid. A standalone News link stays in the top-level list.

<ComponentExample name="grouped-links" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger, navigationMenuTriggerStyle } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function GroupedLinksExample({ label = "Learning resources" }: { label?: string } = {}) {
  return (
    <NavigationMenu aria-label={label}>
      <NavigationMenuList>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="learn">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Learn</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent className="w-60">
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/installation">Installation</NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/motion">Motion guide</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="build">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Build</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent className="grid w-80 max-w-full grid-cols-2 gap-2">
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/components">Components</NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/registry">Registry</NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/theming">Themes</NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/accessibility">Accessibility</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
        <NavigationMenuItem>
          <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/changelog" className={navigationMenuTriggerStyle()}>News</NavigationMenuLink>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}
```

## Controlled navigation

The caller owns the open item value. External actions set stable item values; `null` closes the popup.
The in-panel Close navigation action uses `actionsRef.close()`, and `onValueChange` reports its reason.
External value-only switches may adopt natural geometry immediately. Pressing an outside action can
first invoke normal outside dismissal; keep a command inside the panel when demonstrating its own
imperative close reason.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-navigation" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function ControlledNavigationExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [reason, setReason] = useState("No interaction yet");
  const actions = useRef<{ close: () => void; unmount: () => void } | null>(null);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setValue("learn")}>
          Open Learn
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setValue("build")}>
          Open Build
        </Button>
      </div>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {value ?? "Closed"} · {reason}
      </p>
      <NavigationMenu
        aria-label="Controlled resources"
        value={value}
        actionsRef={actions}
        onValueChange={(next, details) => {
          setValue(next);
          setReason(details.reason);
        }}
      >
        <NavigationMenuList>
          <NavigationMenuItem value="learn">
            <NavigationMenuTrigger>Learn</NavigationMenuTrigger>
            <NavigationMenuContent className="w-56">
              <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/installation">Installation</NavigationMenuLink>
            </NavigationMenuContent>
          </NavigationMenuItem>
          <NavigationMenuItem value="build">
            <NavigationMenuTrigger>Build</NavigationMenuTrigger>
            <NavigationMenuContent className="w-72">
              <NavigationMenuLink href="/components">Browse components</NavigationMenuLink>
              <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/registry">Registry integration</NavigationMenuLink>
              <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => actions.current?.close()}>Close navigation</Button>
            </NavigationMenuContent>
          </NavigationMenuItem>
        </NavigationMenuList>
      </NavigationMenu>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Active links and custom rendering

Mark the current route with `active`; Base UI supplies `aria-current="page"`. `render` preserves a native nav, button and anchor here. A router component must forward link props and refs. Callback classes/styles receive primitive state and merge last. `navigationMenuTriggerStyle()` styles standalone links; `NavigationMenuIndicator` is a static trigger icon, alongside the built-in chevron. The ref action focuses the actual current-page anchor.

<ComponentExample name="active-links" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuIndicator, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger, navigationMenuTriggerStyle } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function ActiveLinksExample() {
  const link = useRef<HTMLAnchorElement>(null);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
      <NavigationMenu aria-label="Current page resources" render={<nav data-custom-root="resources" />}>
        <NavigationMenuList>
          <NavigationMenuItem>
            <NavigationMenuLink active href="/components/navigation-menu" ref={link}
              render={<a href="/components/navigation-menu" />} className={navigationMenuTriggerStyle()}>Navigation Menu</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuItem>
          <NavigationMenuItem value="resources">
            <NavigationMenuTrigger render={<button type="button" />}
              className={(state) => state.open ? "bg-accent" : ""}>
              Resources<NavigationMenuIndicator aria-hidden="true" />
            </NavigationMenuTrigger>
            <NavigationMenuContent className="w-60" style={(state) => ({ padding: state.open ? 12 : 8 })}>
              <NavigationMenuLink render={<a href="/docs/installation" />}>Installation</NavigationMenuLink>
              <NavigationMenuLink render={<a href="/docs/changelog" />}>Changelog</NavigationMenuLink>
            </NavigationMenuContent>
          </NavigationMenuItem>
        </NavigationMenuList>
      </NavigationMenu>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => link.current?.focus()}>Focus current page</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Retained content

Type a resource note, switch to Guides, and return to Notes. `keepMounted` retains the same input while another panel is active; inactive content is hidden after its exit. During exit, Base UI marks an outgoing panel inert when focus has left it; focus still inside the panel is handed off by the primitive. A complete close unmounts the default portal, so reopening starts a new input with its default draft. It is not persistent application storage.

<ComponentExample name="retained-content" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function RetainedContentExample() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <NavigationMenu aria-label="Retained resource draft">
      <NavigationMenuList>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="notes">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Notes</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent keepMounted className="grid w-64 gap-2">
            <label htmlFor={id} className="text-sm font-medium">Resource note</label>
            <Input id={id} defaultValue="Read the install guide" />
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/installation">Installation</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="guides">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Guides</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent keepMounted className="w-72">
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/motion">Motion guide</NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/theming">Theming guide</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}
```

## Changing panel content

The in-panel action reveals actual additional destinations and changes the content width. Base UI measures the same shared popup after the update. Full mode interpolates measured width/height; reduced and none apply geometry immediately. The action belongs to this example and does not configure other instances.

<ComponentExample name="changing-content" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function ChangingContentExample() {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);
  return (
    <NavigationMenu aria-label="Growing resource list">
      <NavigationMenuList>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="resources">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Resources</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent className={expanded ? "w-80" : "w-60"}>
            <Button variant="outline" aria-expanded={expanded} onClick={() => setExpanded((current) => !current)}>
              {expanded ? "Show fewer guides" : "Show more guides"}
            </Button>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/installation">Installation</NavigationMenuLink>
            {expanded && <>
              <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/motion">Motion guide</NavigationMenuLink>
              <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/theming">Theming guide</NavigationMenuLink>
              <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/accessibility">Accessibility guide</NavigationMenuLink>
            </>}
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}
```

## Popup alignment

The root forwards start (default), center and end alignment to its one built-in positioner. Each trigger below belongs to a separate menu. Collision handling may shift the panel on a narrow screen. Root does not forward side/offset props; do not append another positioner to change placement.

<ComponentExample name="alignment" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function AlignmentExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-6">
      {(["start", "center", "end"] as const).map((align) => (
        <NavigationMenu key={align} align={align} aria-label={`${align} aligned resources`}>
          <NavigationMenuList><NavigationMenuItem value="resources">
            <NavigationMenuTrigger>{align}</NavigationMenuTrigger>
            <NavigationMenuContent className="w-64"><NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/installation">Installation</NavigationMenuLink></NavigationMenuContent>
          </NavigationMenuItem></NavigationMenuList>
        </NavigationMenu>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled triggers

A disabled trigger cannot activate the popup. Base UI keeps it in the native Tab sequence while arrow traversal skips it. Enter and Space leave it closed. Keep the available destination as a real standalone link. Disabling a trigger does not provide access to the content behind it.

<ComponentExample name="disabled-triggers" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger, navigationMenuTriggerStyle } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

          <NavigationMenuContent className="w-60"><NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/installation">Installation</NavigationMenuLink></NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="upcoming"><NavigationMenuTrigger disabled>Upcoming</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent><NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/changelog">Changelog</NavigationMenuLink></NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
        <NavigationMenuItem><NavigationMenuLink className={navigationMenuTriggerStyle()} href="/docs/changelog">News</NavigationMenuLink></NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}
```

## Following links

Both native anchors follow this example's own summary target. `closeOnClick={false}` is the default and keeps the popup open; `closeOnClick` closes it when followed. Enter activates a focused link; Space retains browser scrolling behavior. Application routing still owns the destination.

<ComponentExample name="link-behavior" />

```tsx

```

## Pointer delay

This menu waits 300 ms before hover opens and 200 ms before pointer leave closes. These are Base UI intent delays, not animation clocks. Click and keyboard activation remain immediate. The finite interaction policy is fixed here, with no delay selector.

## Without motion

This fixed local provider demonstrates `mode="none"` from the first popup insertion. Navigation, focus, links and measurements still work; opacity, scale and geometry transitions have zero duration. Every other example inherits the site header mode/speed and the system preference.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
      </NavigationMenu>

  );
```
