
## When to use

- Primary site navigation with grouped destinations.
- Desktop resource menus with differently sized panels.
- Navigation that needs pointer, touch and keyboard access to the same links.

## When not to use

- Application commands: use `menubar` or `dropdown-menu`.
- Persistent mobile navigation: use `sidebar` or a `sheet` composition.
- Switching local page content: use `tabs`.

## API

| Part | Props | Defaults and behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NavigationMenu` | Base UI Root props, `align` | `align="start"`; `value`/`defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `onOpenChangeComplete`, `actionsRef`, `delay`, `closeDelay`, `orientation`, `render`, ref and native nav props pass through. Automatically appends one positioner. |
| `NavigationMenuList` | Base UI List props | List semantics and keyboard navigation. |
| `NavigationMenuItem` | Base UI Item props | Stable `value` associates trigger and content. |
| `NavigationMenuTrigger` | Base UI Trigger props | Native button, supports disabled, render, refs, callback classes/styles. |
| `NavigationMenuContent` | Base UI Content props | Portaled content, `keepMounted=false`; caller classes/styles merge with primitive state. |
| `NavigationMenuLink` | Base UI Link props | Native anchor; `active`, `closeOnClick`, render, refs supported. |
| `NavigationMenuIndicator` | Base UI Icon props | Static arrow within a trigger; no extra animation. |
| `NavigationMenuPositioner` | Base UI Positioner props | `side="bottom"`, `sideOffset=8`, `align="start"`, `alignOffset=0`; anchor, collision, render, refs and state callbacks pass through. |
| `navigationMenuTriggerStyle` | CVA function | Trigger classes for standalone navigation links. |

The pinned Base UI API exports Positioner, rather than Radix's Viewport export or `viewport` root prop.
Positioner contains the popup and viewport. Root already appends it; do not add a second one. Popup and
viewport have additive `data-slot` hooks. Positioner props still follow upstream composition.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Recipe / tokens | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | Popup opacity and anchor scale; content opacity | `popup.anchored`, fast clock, scale.in | Native CSS reversal |
| Close / outgoing content | Opacity to zero; popup returns to anchor scale | `exit.fade`, fast clock | Base UI retains exit nodes until completion |
| Switch / update | Shared popup width/height, clamped to available space | `geometry.resize`, slow clock / ease.out | Base UI measures current size before retargeting |
| Reduced | Opacity only; no scale or geometry transition | Fast clock at 0.6×; geometry instant | Live downgrade keeps nodes and focus |
| None | All durations zero, geometry instant | Zeroed CSS tokens | Running transitions finish immediately |

Content switches cross-fade; they do not slide. The positioner follows the active trigger instantly.
Sizing uses Base UI's measured popup variables, not render-time reads or a second animation engine. Trigger activation and in-panel content mutation retarget the resize clock; a value-only controlled switch can adopt the new natural geometry immediately.
Popup and content own token-derived CSS clocks so explicit nested modes and the preview speed work across portals. Caller custom motion must obey the same mode contract.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Enter and leave the navigation without a modal focus trap. |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Move between top-level items in horizontal orientation; logical direction follows RTL. |
| ArrowUp / ArrowDown in a vertical list | Move between top-level triggers. |
| ArrowDown / Enter / Space | Open a trigger; Tab enters its content. |
| Escape | Close and return focus to the active trigger. |
| Enter on a link | Follow the native link destination. |

## Accessibility

Root is a navigation landmark; give multiple navigation regions distinct accessible labels. Triggers
expose expanded state and content association. Base UI owns pointer hover, click/touch activation,
focus guards and outside/Escape dismissal. Disabled triggers stay focusable but cannot open a panel. Base UI owns the normal portal lifecycle; Cadence does not replace a node to reset a running transition. Cadence removes aria-hidden from Base UI 1.6’s tabbable focus sentinels within this menu; they remain empty generic spans with their original Tab redirection handlers. Keep link text meaningful and keyboard focus rings visible.

## Responsive behavior

Popup width and height are limited by Base UI's available viewport dimensions. Its viewport scrolls
when content exceeds that space. Supply responsive widths/grids for your destinations; the component
does not replace your information architecture with a mobile drawer. Resize updates anchor geometry
immediately in all modes. Reduced and none never tween width/height.

## Performance

T3: one shared popup, native CSS transitions, and Base UI's existing post-commit measurements and
mutation/resize tracking. No additional geometry observer, timer, layout animation loop or persistent
will-change. Two scoped child-list observers repair newly inserted focus sentinels; they disconnect on unmount. Geometry transitions are limited to the popup; nothing transitions top/left. Inactive
content unmounts by default; keepMounted deliberately retains caller state and its DOM cost.

## Notes for AI

Match the Base UI surface, including render, refs and state callback classes/styles. Do not add Radix
asChild or substitute a command menu. Keep stable item values; do not key the viewport on selection.
Use real links, label the landmark, and keep mobile content within available space.

# Resizable

Adjustable split panels with pointer and keyboard resizing.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/resizable
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge react-resizable-panels@4.16.0 lucide-react
```

2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers.

- [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency.

3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines.

| Item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) |
| resizable | `@components/cadence/resizable/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/resizable.json) |

[Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json)

[Source files: resizable](https://cadence.dev/r/resizable.json)

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

Copy both target files into the same `cadence/` tree, keeping the relative
`../lib/cn` import and the shipped `"use client"` directive. Complete the
base theme setup and ensure Tailwind CSS v4 scans the copied files. Keep
`react-resizable-panels` pinned to `4.16.0`: these wrappers use its v4
Group, Panel and Separator APIs. No Resizable stylesheet or Provider is required.

External updates, Container resizing and Custom parts additionally use
[Button manual installation](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation).
Copy all of Button's targets and install its recursive npm dependencies from
that page; merge shared files once. This supplies the action buttons without
the shadcn CLI. Button retains its own motion contract.

Compose `ResizablePanelGroup`, panels and labelled handles as in [Usage](#usage).
The declarative Usage can be composed from a Server Component with its string
props, style objects and children. Keep state, DOM/imperative refs, event
handlers, layout/resize callbacks and the engine's ref or persistence hooks
inside a `"use client"` caller, as the interactive examples do. Import
`useGroupRef` and `usePanelRef` from the pinned engine package when needed.

Give vertical groups a definite height; constrain parent width and allow
inner content to scroll. Orientation and mobile breakpoints belong to the
caller. Numeric sizes are pixels; use explicit strings such as `"40%"`
for percentages. Group `defaultLayout` maps matching panel ids to numeric
percentages and supplies an initial layout, not a controlled value. Use
`groupRef.current?.setLayout()` or `panelRef.current` methods for subsequent updates.
At least one panel per group must preserve relative size; min/max and
collapse constraints can change the applied result.

The engine owns pointer resizing, separator keyboard/ARIA behavior, resize
observation and deferred separator previews. Label each handle and keep
essential controls reachable outside collapsed panels. `elementRef` addresses
the DOM; `groupRef` and `panelRef` expose imperative APIs. Panel classes and
styles target inner content; the engine retains its flex geometry. Handle
children are the wrapper's optional grip; `preview` customizes the deferred
overlay. This API does not use Base UI `render` or `asChild`.

The caller owns persistence and draft data. Use stable panel ids and a
consistent initial layout across server rendering and hydration. Restore
browser storage after mount through the imperative API, or pass a serialized
server-loaded layout. If using the engine's `useDefaultLayout` during SSR,
provide server-safe storage with a consistent initial value: its default
reads `localStorage` during rendering, even in a `"use client"` caller.
`onLayoutChange` reports live pointer updates; prefer
`onLayoutChanged` for persistence after release, using
`meta.isUserInteraction` and `meta.requestedLayout` when appropriate.
Initial mount and imperative updates can also report completed changes;
an unchanged applied layout may emit no new completed callback.

Resizable adds no authored animation: full, reduced and none keep direct
layout updates immediate. Separator preview defers pointer commitment until
release; it does not tween geometry. Avoid adding width/flex transitions.
No motion Provider is needed for Resizable itself. Static panel content and
initial drafts render without JavaScript, while pointer/keyboard resizing
and public refs require hydration. Percentage-based initial sizes may be
adjusted after the engine measures the container. Both installation panels expose
complete source without JavaScript.

## Usage

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function Horizontal() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="horizontal" className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 240 }}>
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="40%" minSize="20%" maxSize="70%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Explorer</ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize explorer" />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="60%" minSize="30%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Editor</ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## Horizontal layout

A horizontal group places panels side by side. Percentage defaults and constraints leave the editor at least 30% wide; inner content scrolls instead of forcing the page wider. Drag the divider or focus it and use Left/Right. The divider itself has vertical ARIA orientation.

<ComponentExample name="horizontal" />

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function Horizontal() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="horizontal" className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 240 }}>
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="40%" minSize="20%" maxSize="70%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Explorer</ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize explorer" />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="60%" minSize="30%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Editor</ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## Vertical layout

Set `orientation="vertical"` and give the group a definite height. Up/Down resize this stack; the divider has horizontal ARIA orientation. Parent height and inner overflow are application responsibilities.

<ComponentExample name="vertical" />

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function Vertical() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="vertical" className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 300 }}>
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="55%" minSize="25%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Preview</ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize preview" />
      <ResizablePanel minSize="25%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Output</ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## Handle styles

`withHandle` adds a decorative grip. Both fixed examples retain the same focusable, labelled separator and keyboard/pointer target; the plain divider is the default. The grip adds no animation and does not change the resize API.

<ComponentExample name="handle-styles" />

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function HandleStyles() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-4">
      {[false, true].map((grip) => (
        <ResizablePanelGroup key={String(grip)} className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 140 }}>
          <ResizablePanel defaultSize="50%" minSize="20%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">{grip ? "Grip" : "Plain"}</ResizablePanel>
          <ResizableHandle withHandle={grip} aria-label={grip ? "Resize with grip" : "Resize plain divider"} />
          <ResizablePanel minSize="20%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Content</ResizablePanel>
        </ResizablePanelGroup>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Collapsible panels

This fixed example leaves an 8% rail when collapsed, with a 25% minimum, 60% maximum and a 5% collapse threshold. Enter toggles the preceding panel; Home/End reach its permitted bounds. Dragging below the threshold collapses it. Keep essential actions outside collapsed content; a nonzero rail does not guarantee room for every control.

<ComponentExample name="collapsible-panels" />

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function CollapsiblePanels() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 240 }}>
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="35%" minSize="25%" maxSize="60%" collapsible collapsedSize="8%" collapsedThreshold="5%" className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">
        <span className="whitespace-nowrap">Files</span>
      </ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize collapsible files" />
      <ResizablePanel minSize="40%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Focus the divider and press Enter to collapse or restore Files.</ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## Locked layouts

These three groups demonstrate distinct disabled levels. A disabled group locks all resizing. A disabled panel stays fixed even when another divider moves. A disabled separator only locks that boundary: the enabled second divider can still resize other panels, including indirectly across the locked boundary. Group locking keeps separators in the Tab order without adding `aria-disabled` to each one; setting `disabled` on a separator itself adds that attribute and removes its tab stop. Disabled boundaries do not hide panel content.

<ComponentExample name="locked-layouts" />

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function LockedLayouts() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-4">
      {(["group", "panel", "separator"] as const).map((lock) => (
        <ResizablePanelGroup key={lock} disabled={lock === "group"} className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 150 }}>
          <ResizablePanel defaultSize="30%" minSize="15%" disabled={lock === "panel"} className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">Locked {lock}</ResizablePanel>
          <ResizableHandle disabled={lock === "separator"} aria-label={`Resize ${lock} first divider`} />
          <ResizablePanel defaultSize="35%" minSize="15%" className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">Middle</ResizablePanel>
          <ResizableHandle aria-label={`Resize ${lock} second divider`} />
          <ResizablePanel minSize="15%" className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">End</ResizablePanel>
        </ResizablePanelGroup>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## External updates

Install `@cadence/button` for the external actions. Each mounted example owns unique IDs and a draft. The public panel ref collapses to zero, expands, resizes and inspects size/collapse state; the group ref reads or applies a percentage layout. `defaultLayout` supplies an initial layout, not a controlled value. The live callback reports every pointer move; the completed callback waits for release and distinguishes user input from imperative updates. Persist `meta.requestedLayout` when retaining an unconstrained request. `onResize` supplies pixels, percentages and the previous size. Resizing, header changes and source expansion preserve the actual input node and draft; actions intentionally move focus to their button.

<ComponentExample name="external-updates" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { useGroupRef, usePanelRef } from "react-resizable-panels";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function ExternalUpdates() {
  const id = useId();
  const files = `${id}-files`;
  const editor = `${id}-editor`;
  const group = useGroupRef();
  const panel = usePanelRef();
  const [size, setSize] = useState(40);
  const [previous, setPrevious] = useState<number>();
  const [pixels, setPixels] = useState(0);
  const [live, setLive] = useState(40);
  const [origin, setOrigin] = useState("initial");
  const [requested, setRequested] = useState(40);
  const [inspection, setInspection] = useState("Not inspected");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => panel.current?.collapse()}>Collapse</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => panel.current?.expand()}>Expand</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => panel.current?.resize("55%")}>Resize to 55%</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => group.current?.setLayout({ [files]: 40, [editor]: 60 })}>Reset layout</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => {
          const current = panel.current?.getSize();
          setInspection(`${Math.round(current?.asPercentage ?? 0)}% / ${Math.round(current?.inPixels ?? 0)}px · ${panel.current?.isCollapsed() ? "collapsed" : "expanded"} · layout ${Math.round(group.current?.getLayout()[files] ?? 0)}%`);
        }}>Inspect layout</Button>
      </div>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Files {Math.round(size)}% · {origin} · live {Math.round(live)}% · requested {Math.round(requested)}% · previous {previous === undefined ? "initial" : `${Math.round(previous)}%`} · {Math.round(pixels)}px</p>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" data-inspection>{inspection}</p>
      <ResizablePanelGroup groupRef={group} defaultLayout={{ [files]: 40, [editor]: 60 }} className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 260 }}
        onLayoutChange={(layout) => setLive(layout[files] ?? 0)}
        onLayoutChanged={(layout, meta) => { setOrigin(meta.isUserInteraction ? "user" : "external"); setRequested((meta.requestedLayout ?? layout)[files] ?? 0); }}>
        <ResizablePanel id={files} panelRef={panel} defaultSize="40%" minSize="20%" maxSize="60%" collapsible className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm"
          onResize={(next, _, prev) => { setSize(next.asPercentage); setPixels(next.inPixels); setPrevious(prev?.asPercentage); }}>
          <label className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-2" htmlFor={`${id}-draft`}>Draft
            <input id={`${id}-draft`} className="w-full min-w-0 rounded border bg-background px-2 py-1" defaultValue="Keep this note" />
          </label>
        </ResizablePanel>
        <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize files externally" />
        <ResizablePanel id={editor} defaultSize="60%" minSize="40%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Editor</ResizablePanel>
      </ResizablePanelGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Resize previews

`resizePreviewMode="panel"` applies each drag immediately. The fixed `"separator"` example moves an overlay while panels keep their current sizes, then applies the layout on release. Its `preview` node customizes the overlay; keyboard updates remain immediate. These are interaction strategies, not motion modes or timed interpolation.

<ComponentExample name="resize-previews" />

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function ResizePreviews() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-4">
      {(["panel", "separator"] as const).map((mode) => (
        <ResizablePanelGroup key={mode} resizePreviewMode={mode} className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 180 }}>
          <ResizablePanel defaultSize="40%" minSize="20%" maxSize="70%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">{mode === "panel" ? "Live panels" : "Release to apply"}</ResizablePanel>
          <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label={`Resize ${mode} preview`} preview={<div className="h-full w-1 bg-primary" />} />
          <ResizablePanel minSize="30%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Editor</ResizablePanel>
        </ResizablePanelGroup>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Container resizing

Install `@cadence/button` for the caller-owned width change. The upper panel preserves its 40% share; the lower preserves 100 pixels as its parent narrows. Numeric sizes are pixels, explicit `"40%"` strings are percentages; other CSS size units are continuous inputs, not variants. At least one panel per group must preserve relative size, and constraints can limit the requested result. The button changes real parent geometry without a width transition.

<ComponentExample name="container-resize" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function ContainerResize() {
  const [compact, setCompact] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col items-start gap-4">
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setCompact((value) => !value)}>{compact ? "Restore container" : "Narrow container"}</Button>
      <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-4" style={{ width: compact ? "80%" : "100%" }}>
        {(["preserve-relative-size", "preserve-pixel-size"] as const).map((behavior) => (
          <ResizablePanelGroup key={behavior} className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 180 }}>
            <ResizablePanel defaultSize={behavior === "preserve-pixel-size" ? 100 : "40%"} groupResizeBehavior={behavior} className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">
              {behavior === "preserve-pixel-size" ? "100px" : "40%"}
            </ResizablePanel>
            <ResizableHandle aria-label={`Resize ${behavior}`} />
            <ResizablePanel className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">Flexible remainder</ResizablePanel>
          </ResizablePanelGroup>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Nested panels

A vertical group can live inside a horizontal panel. Each labelled divider owns its axis. F6 and Shift+F6 cycle enabled separators within the focused divider’s group; Tab follows the document order into the nested group. Give the outer group a height so the nested stack can fill its panel.

<ComponentExample name="nested-panels" />

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function NestedPanels() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 300 }}>
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="30%" minSize="15%" className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">Files</ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize nested files" />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="45%" minSize="20%">
        <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="vertical">
          <ResizablePanel minSize="25%" className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">Preview</ResizablePanel>
          <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize nested preview" />
          <ResizablePanel minSize="25%" className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">Console</ResizablePanel>
        </ResizablePanelGroup>
      </ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize nested inspector" />
      <ResizablePanel minSize="15%" className="overflow-auto p-3 text-sm">Details</ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## Custom parts

Install `@cadence/button` for the focus action. `elementRef` addresses the actual separator DOM node; `panelRef` and `groupRef` address imperative APIs. Caller classes/styles target the panel’s inner content, while library flex geometry retains precedence. This thicker divider disables double-click reset, keeps native click callbacks, increases hit targets and leaves cursor styling to the caller with `disableCursor`. Handle children remain the wrapper’s optional grip; use `preview` for deferred-drag overlays.

<ComponentExample name="custom-parts" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function CustomParts() {
  const handle = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [clicks, setClicks] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-4">
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => handle.current?.focus()}>Focus divider</Button>
      <ResizablePanelGroup disableCursor resizeTargetMinimumSize={{ coarse: 32, fine: 16 }} className="rounded-md border" style={{ height: 200 }}>
        <ResizablePanel defaultSize="40%" minSize="20%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm" style={{ fontWeight: 600 }}>Files</ResizablePanel>
        <ResizableHandle elementRef={handle} disableDoubleClick withHandle className="w-2 bg-muted" aria-label="Resize custom divider" onClick={() => setClicks((count) => count + 1)} />
        <ResizablePanel minSize="30%" className="overflow-auto p-4 text-sm">Editor</ResizablePanel>
      </ResizablePanelGroup>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Divider clicks: {clicks}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Editor panes whose widths users adjust.
- Preview/output workspaces with vertical splits.
- Collapsible tool panels with persistent application-owned layouts.

## When not to use

- Static columns: use CSS grid.
- Hidden disclosure content: use Collapsible or Accordion.
- Mobile navigation: use Sheet or Sidebar.

## API

| Export | Props and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `ResizablePanelGroup` | `react-resizable-panels` `GroupProps`; orientation horizontal, resizing enabled, immediate panel preview. |
| `ResizablePanel` | `PanelProps`; min 0%, max 100%, collapsible false, collapsed size 0%, relative resize behavior. |
| `ResizableHandle` | `SeparatorProps` plus optional `withHandle` (unset by default). |

All native attributes/events, string classes, style objects, `elementRef`, `groupRef`,
`panelRef`, constraints, callbacks, disabled state and preview props pass through. This primitive
has no Base UI `render`, `asChild`, or callback class/style API. Group and handle classes merge
caller last. Panel classes and caller styles target the library's inner content element; `elementRef` addresses
its root. Managed flex/display geometry retains library precedence; other caller styles pass through.
Handle children follow upstream: the wrapper renders its optional grip instead of caller children.

Numeric sizes are **pixels**; use strings such as `"40%"` for percentages. Group layouts map
stable panel ids to numeric percentages. Slots: `resizable-panel-group`, `resizable-panel`,
`resizable-handle`. Use `elementRef` for DOM access rather than a generic React ref.

## Motion contract

T0: declared, implemented and documented recipe sets are empty. Direct manipulation is functional
layout, not an authored animation. The default panel preview, keyboard, collapse/expand and imperative updates apply
immediately in full, reduced and none. Separator preview defers pointer commitment until release without interpolation. No spring, timer, geometry tween, opacity reveal, provider,
`data-motion` or motion hook is shipped. Mode changes preserve the same panel nodes and input state.

| Mode | Authored motion |
| --- | --- |
| full | none; immediate layout |
| reduced | none; immediate layout |
| none | none; immediate layout |

Caller-added animation is application-owned. Do not transition flex or width/height on these panels:
it makes the divider lag behind input and bypasses the geometry recipe budget.

## Accessibility

The primitive supplies focusable separators, `aria-controls`, orientation and value bounds/current
value. Label each handle. Tab focuses the separator; axis arrows resize by 5 percentage points,
Home/End reach permitted limits, Enter toggles the preceding collapsible panel, and F6/Shift+F6
cycle enabled separators within the same group. Double-click restores the associated panel's default size unless disabled.
A locked group disables resizing; disabling only a separator still permits indirect panel resizing.
Group-level locking retains separator Tab stops without adding `aria-disabled`; a separator’s own `disabled` prop sets `aria-disabled` and removes its tab stop. Keep critical controls outside a collapsible panel so they remain reachable when it is zero-sized.

## Responsive behavior

Constrain the group's height for vertical layouts. Use `min-w-0` on grid parents, percentage constraints
for narrow screens and scrollable inner content for long lines. Orientation changes are caller-owned;
there is no automatic mobile breakpoint. The preview supports both axes at desktop and 390px.
The library adjusts constraints on container resize; at least one panel must preserve relative size.

## Performance

No Cadence animation or extra measurement engine is added. The library owns resize observation and
pointer/keyboard handling. Keep expensive persistence work in `onLayoutChanged`, not every live update.
Percentage defaults can shift slightly during SSR hydration; provide stable ids and consistent initial
layout. Static panel text and the initial draft render without JavaScript; pointer/keyboard resizing and public refs require hydration. This T0 source budget excludes the declared third-party dependency; it is not a total bundle claim.

## Notes for AI

- Use v4 Group/Panel/Separator props and public refs; v3 direction/PanelGroup APIs do not apply.
- Preserve constraints and immediate resizing in all modes.
- Use stable ids when persisting layouts and explicit units for panel sizes.

# Sidebar

Workspace navigation for dashboards and application shells.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/sidebar
```

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority lucide-react
```

4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition.

No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme.

The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once:

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="full">{children}</CadenceProvider>;
}
```

Copy all 16 target files, including `lib/hooks/use-mobile.ts` and every
`cadence-motion` and `cadence-provider` helper. Keep their relative imports,
the `cadence/` directory structure and the shipped `"use client"` directives.
Complete the linked manual base setup, including Cadence theme CSS, and ensure
Tailwind CSS v4 scans the copied files. Its `--color-sidebar*` mappings supply
the sidebar utilities with semantic colour fallbacks; set matching
`--sidebar*` light/dark variables to customize them. No separate Sidebar
stylesheet is required. Apply `bg-background text-foreground` to your application
root so the main content inherits the active theme's text colour.
The registry graph already includes Button, Input,
Separator, Sheet, Skeleton, Tooltip and `lucide-react` used by these examples;
they require no additional example-only installation.

Keep `SidebarProvider`, navigation and `SidebarInset` together as in
[Usage](#usage). `SidebarProvider` is required for sidebar state and
`useSidebar`; it is separate from the optional `CadenceProvider` motion wrapper.
No `TooltipProvider` is required; add one only to share tooltip delay settings.
Use the default main element for application content, or
`SidebarInset render={<section />}` with a unique accessible name for an
embedded shell inside an existing main.

Serializable props, children and native elements such as `render={<a href="/" />}`
can be composed from a Server Component. Keep search state, controlled
`open`/`onOpenChange`, handlers, refs, `useSidebar` and function-valued
`render`/class/style props inside a `"use client"` caller, as the interactive
examples do. Supply real destinations or your router's link element through
`render`, not `asChild`; the caller owns routing, filtering and active state.
Set `aria-current="page"` on the current link as well as `isActive` for styling.

Desktop starts expanded unless `defaultOpen` or controlled `open` says otherwise.
Controlled callers must apply requested `onOpenChange` values themselves.
Desktop `open` does not control `openMobile`, which starts false. Below 768px,
collapsible sidebars switch to an 18rem modal Sheet after hydration; server
rendering initially uses the desktop tree. `collapsible="none"` remains static.
Desktop collapse retains children, while breakpoint changes and mobile closing
can unmount them: keep persistent drafts above Sidebar. Include a visible mobile
close control when needed; Sheet also provides Escape, outside dismissal and
focus management. Its built-in close button is hidden by Sidebar.

The desktop setter writes `sidebar_state=true` or `false` for seven days at
path `/`; it never reads the cookie. To restore it, read the request cookie on
the server and pass a boolean `defaultOpen`, using a consistent server/client
initial value. Otherwise a reload uses the default again. This cookie records
desktop state only. Ctrl+B or Cmd+B also toggles inside inputs and broadcasts
to every mounted provider; prefer one application provider. The rail is not
in Tab order, so retain the labelled trigger.

Desktop widths default to 16rem and 3rem for the icon rail; override
`--sidebar-width` and `--sidebar-width-icon` through provider style. Mobile
uses its own 18rem width; customize Sidebar style when needed. The 12rem widths,
containing transform and absolute desktop panels in these embedded examples
are local layout choices. Caller `style.transform` on Sidebar takes ownership
of desktop positioning and suppresses its offcanvas motion.

Sidebar animates only desktop offcanvas translation with `layout.move` in full;
reduced and none update position immediately. Gaps and icon widths always
change immediately. Mobile Sheet, buttons, tooltips and loading skeletons keep
their own inherited motion contracts; install their helpers even if you only
use desktop navigation.

## Usage

A minimal embedded application shell with real search and links. At the application root, use the default main semantics of SidebarInset. For an embedded shell, use Cadence's additive `render` prop to render a uniquely named section. The default element remains main.

```tsx
"use client";

import { Home, Inbox, Settings } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useId, useState } from "react";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupContent, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarHeader, SidebarInput, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarRail, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function Navigation({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const target = useId();
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  return (
    <>
      <SidebarHeader>
        <strong className="truncate text-sm group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden">Acme workspace</strong>
        <SidebarInput
          className="group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden" aria-label={`Search ${label}`}
          placeholder="Search workspace"
          value={query}
          onValueChange={setQuery}
        />
      </SidebarHeader>
      <SidebarContent>
        <nav aria-label={label}>
          <SidebarGroup>
            <SidebarGroupLabel>Workspace</SidebarGroupLabel>
            <SidebarGroupContent>
              <SidebarMenu>
                {(
                  [
                    [Home, "Overview"],
                    [Inbox, "Inbox"],
                    [Settings, "Settings"],
                  ] as const
                )
                  .filter(([, text]) => text.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()))
                  .map(([Icon, text]) => (
                    <SidebarMenuItem key={text}>
                      <SidebarMenuButton
                        render={<a href={`#${target}`} aria-current={text === "Overview" ? "page" : undefined} />}
                        isActive={text === "Overview"}
                        tooltip={text}
                      >
                        <Icon aria-hidden="true" />
                        <span>{text}</span>
                      </SidebarMenuButton>
                    </SidebarMenuItem>
                  ))}
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroupContent>
            <p id={target} className="sr-only">
              Workspace navigation destination
            </p>
          </SidebarGroup>
        </nav>
      </SidebarContent>
      <SidebarFooter>
        <span className="truncate text-xs group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden">Acme team</span>
      </SidebarFooter>
      <SidebarRail />
    </>
  );
}

function Workspace({
  label,
  side = "left",
  variant = "sidebar",
  collapsible = "offcanvas",
  defaultOpen = true,
}: {
  label: string;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  variant?: "sidebar" | "floating" | "inset";
  collapsible?: "offcanvas" | "icon" | "none";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <Frame label={label} side={side} defaultOpen={defaultOpen}>
      <Sidebar side={side} variant={variant} collapsible={collapsible} className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <Navigation label={label} />
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <Workspace label="Workspace navigation" />;
}
```

## Icon navigation

The fixed icon rail starts collapsed on desktop. Keep icon and text in each button; the text still names the link, and the string tooltip appears on focus or hover. Rail widths and labels change immediately; only offcanvas travel uses the Sidebar recipe. Search remains a real filter when expanded; the compact rail hides its header text, search and footer text.

<ComponentExample name="icon-navigation" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useId, useState } from "react";

function Frame({

  content,

  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,

  open?: boolean;

      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}

              Workspace navigation destination
```

## Controlled navigation

The caller owns desktop open and observes every requested change. Only this behavior example adds external controls. useSidebar exposes state, open, setOpen, openMobile, setOpenMobile, isMobile and toggleSidebar. Desktop open does not control the mobile Sheet; opening mobile while on desktop only records that separate state. The setter writes sidebar_state for seven days at path / but never reads it. Read a cookie on the server and supply defaultOpen to restore an uncontrolled shell.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-navigation" />

```tsx

                        <span>{text}</span>
                      </SidebarMenuButton>
                    </SidebarMenuItem>
                  ))}
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroupContent>
            <p id={target} className="sr-only">
              Workspace navigation destination
            </p>
          </SidebarGroup>
        </nav>
      </SidebarContent>
      <SidebarFooter>
        <span className="truncate text-xs group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden">Acme team</span>
      </SidebarFooter>
      <SidebarRail />

function Workspace({
  label,
  side = "left",
  variant = "sidebar",
  collapsible = "offcanvas",
  defaultOpen = true,
}: {
  label: string;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  variant?: "sidebar" | "floating" | "inset";
  collapsible?: "offcanvas" | "icon" | "none";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <Frame label={label} side={side} defaultOpen={defaultOpen}>
      <Sidebar side={side} variant={variant} collapsible={collapsible} className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <Navigation label={label} />
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

function HookControls() {
  const { state, openMobile, isMobile, setOpen, setOpenMobile, toggleSidebar } = useSidebar();
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-2 text-xs">
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Expand desktop
      </Button>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
        Collapse desktop
      </Button>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={toggleSidebar}>
        Toggle navigation
      </Button>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpenMobile(true)}>
        Open mobile
      </Button>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpenMobile(false)}>
        Close mobile
      </Button>
      <output data-sidebar-state>
        {state} / {openMobile ? "mobile open" : "mobile closed"} / {isMobile ? "mobile" : "desktop"}
      </output>
    </div>
  );
}

function ControlledNavigation() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);
  const [changes, setChanges] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Frame
      label="Controlled navigation"
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={(next) => {
        setOpen(next);
        setChanges((n) => n + 1);
      }}
      content={
        <>
          <HookControls />
          <output aria-label="Desktop changes">Desktop changes: {changes}</output>
        </>
      }
    >
      <Sidebar className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <Navigation label="Controlled navigation" />
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <ControlledNavigation />;
}
```

## Variants

These fixed shells compare sidebar, floating and inset separately. Floating adds a padded rounded panel; inset styles its sibling SidebarInset. In this embedded documentation each inset uses `render={<section />}` with a unique accessible name because the page already has a main; use its default main landmark at your application root. The containing transform and absolute panel keep each desktop specimen inside its own card. The local 12rem desktop width is an embedding choice, not a library default.

## Collapse modes

The three shells start with desktop defaultOpen=false. Offcanvas removes its gap and makes hidden navigation inert; icon retains a compact rail; none stays static and visible on every viewport. A none sidebar still receives provider state, but its trigger cannot visually hide it. On small screens offcanvas and icon both become a Sheet; none remains in the document.

## Mobile behavior

Below 768px the real trigger opens a right-edge Sheet. The explicit close control calls setOpenMobile(false); Escape and backdrop dismissal also close it. Desktop and mobile trees can remount, and closing the default Sheet unmounts its children. Keep a draft above Sidebar, as here, to survive close/reopen and viewport changes. Search inside Navigation is intentionally local and resets when its tree remounts.

<ComponentExample name="mobile-behavior" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Home, Inbox, Settings, X } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupContent, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarHeader, SidebarInput, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarRail, SidebarTrigger, useSidebar } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function Navigation({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const target = useId();
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  return (
    <>
      <SidebarHeader>
        <strong className="truncate text-sm group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden">Acme workspace</strong>
        <SidebarInput
          className="group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden" aria-label={`Search ${label}`}
          placeholder="Search workspace"
          value={query}
          onValueChange={setQuery}
        />
      </SidebarHeader>
      <SidebarContent>
        <nav aria-label={label}>
          <SidebarGroup>
            <SidebarGroupLabel>Workspace</SidebarGroupLabel>
            <SidebarGroupContent>
              <SidebarMenu>
                {(
                  [
                    [Home, "Overview"],
                    [Inbox, "Inbox"],
                    [Settings, "Settings"],
                  ] as const
                )
                  .filter(([, text]) => text.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()))
                  .map(([Icon, text]) => (
                    <SidebarMenuItem key={text}>
                      <SidebarMenuButton
                        render={<a href={`#${target}`} aria-current={text === "Overview" ? "page" : undefined} />}
                        isActive={text === "Overview"}
                        tooltip={text}
                      >
                        <Icon aria-hidden="true" />
                        <span>{text}</span>
                      </SidebarMenuButton>
                    </SidebarMenuItem>
                  ))}
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroupContent>
            <p id={target} className="sr-only">
              Workspace navigation destination
            </p>
          </SidebarGroup>
        </nav>
      </SidebarContent>
      <SidebarFooter>
        <span className="truncate text-xs group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden">Acme team</span>
      </SidebarFooter>
      <SidebarRail />
    </>
  );
}

function Workspace({
  label,
  side = "left",
  variant = "sidebar",
  collapsible = "offcanvas",
  defaultOpen = true,
}: {
  label: string;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  variant?: "sidebar" | "floating" | "inset";
  collapsible?: "offcanvas" | "icon" | "none";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <Frame label={label} side={side} defaultOpen={defaultOpen}>
      <Sidebar side={side} variant={variant} collapsible={collapsible} className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <Navigation label={label} />
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

function MobileClose() {
  const { isMobile, setOpenMobile } = useSidebar();
  return isMobile ? (
    <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => setOpenMobile(false)}>
      <X aria-hidden="true" />
      Close navigation
    </Button>
  ) : null;
}

function MobileBehavior() {
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
  return (
    <Frame label="Mobile workspace" side="right" content={<p className="text-xs">Navigation becomes a Sheet below 768px.</p>}>
      <Sidebar side="right" className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <SidebarHeader>
          <MobileClose />
          <SidebarInput
            aria-label="Persistent mobile draft"
            placeholder="Caller-owned draft"
            value={draft}
            onValueChange={setDraft}
          />
        </SidebarHeader>
        <SidebarContent>
          <Navigation label="Mobile workspace" />
        </SidebarContent>
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <MobileBehavior />;
}
```

## Menu styles

Compare the default and outline menu-button variants and the sm/default/lg size axis without multiplying every combination. isActive controls styling; aria-pressed belongs to the caller for a command. Use aria-current on a real navigation link. Native disabled prevents command activation. These are ordinary controls and links, with normal Tab order rather than menu arrow navigation.

<ComponentExample name="menu-styles" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Home, Inbox } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function MenuStyles() {
  return (
    <Frame label="Menu styles">
      <Sidebar collapsible="none" className="h-full">
        <SidebarContent>
          <nav aria-label="Menu styles">
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarGroupLabel>Commands</SidebarGroupLabel>
              <SidebarMenu>
                {(["sm", "default", "lg"] as const).map((size) => (
                  <SidebarMenuItem key={size}>
                    <SidebarMenuButton size={size}>
                      <Home aria-hidden="true" />
                      <span>{size} command</span>
                    </SidebarMenuButton>
                  </SidebarMenuItem>
                ))}
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton variant="outline">

        </SidebarContent>

export function Example() {

}
```
