## Groups and actions

Header, footer, separator, group label and group content organize navigation. Add project is a real caller-owned action; each new stable name receives its own menu action. The badge is a non-interactive count. The fixed footer action is always visible, while showOnHover reveals row actions on hover or keyboard focus. Icon collapse hides group labels, badges and actions. A group label may render as a heading.

<ComponentExample name="groups-and-actions" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Home, MoreHorizontal, Plus, Settings } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupAction, SidebarGroupContent, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarHeader, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuAction, SidebarMenuBadge, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarRail, SidebarSeparator, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function GroupsAndActions() {
  const [projects, setProjects] = useState(["Website"]);
  const [action, setAction] = useState("No project action");
  return (
    <Frame label="Project actions" content={<output>{action}</output>}>
      <Sidebar className="md:absolute md:h-full" collapsible="icon">
        <SidebarHeader>
          <span className="truncate text-sm font-medium">Acme projects</span>
        </SidebarHeader>
        <SidebarSeparator />
        <SidebarContent>
          <nav aria-label="Project actions">
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarGroupLabel render={<h3 aria-label="Projects" />}>Projects</SidebarGroupLabel>
              <SidebarGroupAction
                aria-label="Add project"
                onClick={() => setProjects((rows) => [...rows, `Project ${rows.length + 1}`])}
              >
                <Plus aria-hidden="true" />
              </SidebarGroupAction>
              <SidebarGroupContent>
                <SidebarMenu>
                  {projects.map((name, i) => (
                    <SidebarMenuItem key={name}>
                      <SidebarMenuButton onClick={() => setAction(`Opened ${name}`)}>
                        <Home aria-hidden="true" />
                        <span>{name}</span>
                      </SidebarMenuButton>
                      {i === 0 ? (
                        <SidebarMenuBadge aria-label="3 updates">3</SidebarMenuBadge>
                      ) : (
                        <SidebarMenuAction
                          showOnHover
                          aria-label={`Options for ${name}`}
                          onClick={() => setAction(`Options for ${name}`)}
                        >
                          <MoreHorizontal aria-hidden="true" />
                        </SidebarMenuAction>
                      )}
                    </SidebarMenuItem>
                  ))}
                </SidebarMenu>
              </SidebarGroupContent>
            </SidebarGroup>
          </nav>
        </SidebarContent>
        <SidebarSeparator />
        <SidebarFooter>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuButton onClick={() => setAction("Opened settings")}>
                <Settings aria-hidden="true" />
                <span>Settings</span>
              </SidebarMenuButton>
              <SidebarMenuAction aria-label="Settings options" onClick={() => setAction("Settings options")}>
                <MoreHorizontal aria-hidden="true" />
              </SidebarMenuAction>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarFooter>
        <SidebarRail />
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <GroupsAndActions />;
}
```

## Sub-navigation

Sub lists remain semantic ul/li navigation. Compare md and sm sub-buttons; the active link supplies aria-current. The unavailable link has no href and leaves the Tab order. Icon collapse hides the sublist immediately. Compose Collapsible separately when disclosure behavior is needed; this list does not invent a disclosure or animate its height.

<ComponentExample name="sub-navigation" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Home } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useId } from "react";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuSub, SidebarMenuSubButton, SidebarMenuSubItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarRail, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function SubNavigation() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <Frame label="Nested navigation">
      <Sidebar collapsible="icon" className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <SidebarContent>
          <nav aria-label="Nested navigation">
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarMenu>
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton>
                    <Home aria-hidden="true" />
                    <span>Projects</span>
                  </SidebarMenuButton>
                  <SidebarMenuSub>
                    {(["md", "sm"] as const).map((size) => (
                      <SidebarMenuSubItem key={size}>
                        <SidebarMenuSubButton
                          size={size}
                          href={`#${id}`}
                          isActive={size === "md"}
                          aria-current={size === "md" ? "page" : undefined}
                        >
                          {size} project
                        </SidebarMenuSubButton>
                      </SidebarMenuSubItem>
                    ))}
                    <SidebarMenuSubItem>
                      <SidebarMenuSubButton aria-disabled="true" tabIndex={-1}>
                        Unavailable project
                      </SidebarMenuSubButton>
                    </SidebarMenuSubItem>
                  </SidebarMenuSub>
                </SidebarMenuItem>
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroup>
          </nav>
          <span id={id} className="sr-only">
            Project destination
          </span>
        </SidebarContent>
        <SidebarRail />
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <SubNavigation />;
}
```

## Loading navigation

The caller swaps two deterministic skeleton rows for a real navigation row. showIcon adds a skeleton glyph. The loading status supplies an accessible label; skeleton widths are stable between server and client. Pulse follows Skeleton's own inherited motion contract and stops in none.

<ComponentExample name="loading-navigation" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuSkeleton, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function LoadingNavigation() {
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
  return (
    <Frame
      label="Loading navigation"
      content={
        <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => setReady((value) => !value)}>
          {ready ? "Reload navigation" : "Show navigation"}
        </Button>
      }
    >
      <Sidebar className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <SidebarContent>
          <SidebarGroup>
            {ready ? (
              <nav aria-label="Loaded projects">
                <SidebarMenu>
                  <SidebarMenuItem>
                    <SidebarMenuButton>Website</SidebarMenuButton>
                  </SidebarMenuItem>
                </SidebarMenu>
              </nav>
            ) : (
              <div role="status" aria-label="Loading projects">
                <SidebarMenuSkeleton />
                <SidebarMenuSkeleton showIcon />
              </div>
            )}
          </SidebarGroup>
        </SidebarContent>
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <LoadingNavigation />;
}
```

## Caller updates

Only this named behavior example adds and removes application data. Stable keys preserve surviving menu nodes. The input value lives above Sidebar and survives desktop toggles, header mode changes and mobile remounts. Sidebar does not fetch data, own permissions, validate the draft or animate row insertion.

<ComponentExample name="caller-updates" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarHeader, SidebarInput, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarRail, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function CallerUpdates() {
  const [projects, setProjects] = useState(["Website", "Mobile app"]);
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
  return (
    <Frame
      label="Caller updates"
      content={
        <Button
          size="sm"
          variant="outline"
          onClick={() => setProjects((rows) => (rows.length === 2 ? [...rows, "Desktop app"] : rows.slice(0, 2)))}
        >
          {projects.length === 2 ? "Add project" : "Remove project"}
        </Button>
      }
    >
      <Sidebar className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <SidebarHeader>
          <SidebarInput
            aria-label="Project draft"
            value={draft}
            onValueChange={setDraft}
            placeholder="Caller-owned draft"
          />
        </SidebarHeader>
        <SidebarContent>
          <nav aria-label="Caller updates">
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarMenu>
                {projects.map((name) => (
                  <SidebarMenuItem key={name}>
                    <SidebarMenuButton>{name}</SidebarMenuButton>
                  </SidebarMenuItem>
                ))}
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroup>
          </nav>
        </SidebarContent>
        <SidebarRail />
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <CallerUpdates />;
}
```

## Custom parts

Base UI render accepts a native element; the anchor ref, native event and hash destination stay usable. The external focus action is desktop-only, where the link stays mounted. dir="rtl" follows the panel through its mobile portal. A tooltip props object configures the collapsed tooltip. This example deliberately supplies style.transform="none": caller ownership suppresses desktop offcanvas travel, so collapsing makes content inert without moving that caller-positioned surface. Manage its position yourself or omit transform for standard offcanvas behavior.

<ComponentExample name="custom-parts" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Home } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useId, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function CustomParts() {
  const link = useRef<HTMLAnchorElement>(null);
  const id = useId();
  const [clicks, setClicks] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Frame
      label="Custom parts"
      side="right"
      content={
        <>
          <Button className="hidden md:inline-flex" size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => link.current?.focus()}>
            Focus project link
          </Button>
          <output>Native clicks: {clicks}</output>
        </>
      }
    >
      <Sidebar side="right" dir="rtl" style={{ transform: "none" }} className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <SidebarContent>
          <nav aria-label="Custom parts">
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarGroupLabel render={<h3 aria-label="Projects" />}>المشاريع</SidebarGroupLabel>
              <SidebarMenu>
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton
                    render={<a ref={link} href={`#${id}`} lang="ar" />}
                    onClick={() => setClicks((n) => n + 1)}
                    tooltip={{ children: "Website", side: "left" }}
                  >
                    <Home aria-hidden="true" />
                    <span>الموقع</span>
                  </SidebarMenuButton>
                </SidebarMenuItem>
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroup>
          </nav>
          <span id={id} className="sr-only">
            Custom project destination
          </span>
        </SidebarContent>
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <CustomParts />;
}
```

## Without motion

This explicit local provider is fixed to none from the first render. Desktop positions and gaps update immediately; mobile Sheet, composed buttons and tooltips also inherit none. Other examples inherit the site header and system preference. This override does not configure neighboring examples.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { Home, Inbox, Settings } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, type ReactNode, useId, useState } from "react";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";
import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupContent, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarHeader, SidebarInput, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarRail, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

function Frame({
  label,
  children,
  content,
  side = "left",
  defaultOpen = true,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
}: {
  label: string;
  children: ReactNode;
  content?: ReactNode;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      style={{ "--sidebar-width": "12rem" } as CSSProperties}
      className={`relative isolate h-96 min-h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border [transform:translateZ(0)] ${side === "right" ? "flex-row-reverse" : ""}`}
    >
      {children}
      <SidebarInset render={<section />} aria-label={`${label} content`} className="min-w-0 gap-3 p-3">
        <SidebarTrigger aria-label={`Toggle ${label}`} />
        <p className="text-sm font-medium">Project overview</p>
        {content ?? <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Your workspace content.</p>}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

function Navigation({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const target = useId();
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  return (
    <>
      <SidebarHeader>
        <strong className="truncate text-sm group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden">Acme workspace</strong>
        <SidebarInput
          className="group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden" aria-label={`Search ${label}`}
          placeholder="Search workspace"
          value={query}
          onValueChange={setQuery}
        />
      </SidebarHeader>
      <SidebarContent>
        <nav aria-label={label}>
          <SidebarGroup>
            <SidebarGroupLabel>Workspace</SidebarGroupLabel>
            <SidebarGroupContent>
              <SidebarMenu>
                {(
                  [
                    [Home, "Overview"],
                    [Inbox, "Inbox"],
                    [Settings, "Settings"],
                  ] as const
                )
                  .filter(([, text]) => text.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()))
                  .map(([Icon, text]) => (
                    <SidebarMenuItem key={text}>
                      <SidebarMenuButton
                        render={<a href={`#${target}`} aria-current={text === "Overview" ? "page" : undefined} />}
                        isActive={text === "Overview"}
                        tooltip={text}
                      >
                        <Icon aria-hidden="true" />
                        <span>{text}</span>
                      </SidebarMenuButton>
                    </SidebarMenuItem>
                  ))}
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroupContent>
            <p id={target} className="sr-only">
              Workspace navigation destination
            </p>
          </SidebarGroup>
        </nav>
      </SidebarContent>
      <SidebarFooter>
        <span className="truncate text-xs group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden">Acme team</span>
      </SidebarFooter>
      <SidebarRail />
    </>
  );
}

function Workspace({
  label,
  side = "left",
  variant = "sidebar",
  collapsible = "offcanvas",
  defaultOpen = true,
}: {
  label: string;
  side?: "left" | "right";
  variant?: "sidebar" | "floating" | "inset";
  collapsible?: "offcanvas" | "icon" | "none";
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <Frame label={label} side={side} defaultOpen={defaultOpen}>
      <Sidebar side={side} variant={variant} collapsible={collapsible} className="md:absolute md:h-full">
        <Navigation label={label} />
      </Sidebar>
    </Frame>
  );
}

export function Example() {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="none"><Workspace label="Instant navigation" /></CadenceProvider>;
}
```

## When to use

- Persistent workspace navigation in dashboards.
- Application shells with a compact icon rail.
- Navigation that becomes a modal panel on narrow screens.

## When not to use

Use Navigation Menu for short top-level menus and Sheet for a task panel. This component does not
provide routing, permissions, or application state.

## API

### `SidebarProvider`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| defaultOpen | boolean | true | Initial desktop state. |
| open / onOpenChange | boolean / callback | — | Controlled desktop state. |
| style | CSSProperties | — | Overrides `--sidebar-width` (16rem) and `--sidebar-width-icon` (3rem). |
| native div props / ref | native | — | Forwarded to wrapper. |

### `Sidebar`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| side | left / right | left | Physical panel edge. |
| variant | sidebar / floating / inset | sidebar | Surface treatment. |
| collapsible | offcanvas / icon / none | offcanvas | Hide, compact, or remain visible. |
| dir | string | — | Native panel direction in desktop, static and mobile layouts. |
| className / style / ref | native | — | Desktop container; static sidebar or mobile popup respectively. |

`SidebarTrigger` accepts Button props and calls caller `onClick` before toggling. `SidebarRail`
accepts native button props and is excluded from Tab order; the trigger is the keyboard control.
`SidebarInset` defaults to a main landmark and accepts native main props/ref. Cadence adds the Base UI `render` prop (an element or render function) so embedded shells can use a uniquely named section, as above. This preserves the sidebar-inset slot and peer-dependent styling without nesting main landmarks or overriding a main element's role.
`SidebarInput` and `SidebarSeparator` accept their corresponding component props.

`SidebarHeader`, `SidebarFooter`, `SidebarContent`, `SidebarGroup`, `SidebarGroupContent`,
`SidebarMenuBadge`, and `SidebarMenuSkeleton` accept div props. Skeleton supports `showIcon=false`;
its deterministic text width avoids hydration mismatch. `SidebarMenu`/`SidebarMenuSub` render ul;
`SidebarMenuItem`/`SidebarMenuSubItem` render li.

`SidebarGroupLabel`, `SidebarGroupAction`, `SidebarMenuAction`, `SidebarMenuButton`, and
`SidebarMenuSubButton` accept Base UI `render` (element or state callback), native props and refs.
MenuButton supports `isActive=false`, `variant="default"|"outline"`, `size="default"|"sm"|"lg"`,
and `tooltip` (string or TooltipContent props). MenuAction supports `showOnHover=false`.
SubButton supports `size="md"|"sm"` and `isActive=false`. Classes merge caller last; native events
and useRender event merging remain available. `useSidebar` requires a provider.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop offcanvas toggle | transform, own-width translation | `layout.move` | Yes, current position and velocity retarget. |

Full springs between the edge and off-edge position; no mounting reveal. Reduced and none update
position immediately, with no animated transform. Gap, icon widths, label margins and visibility
update immediately in every mode. No layout or height tween is authored. Caller `style.transform`
owns that property and suppresses desktop motion. System reduced motion overrides full; live mode
downgrades stop the running spring without replacing the panel.

Mobile delegates `popup.anchored` / `exit.fade` to Sheet. Button press, tooltip popup and Skeleton pulse
are owned by those dependencies, not extra Sidebar recipes. Their effective mode follows the provider.

## Accessibility

Wrap navigation links in a named nav landmark. `isActive` styles the item; add `aria-current="page"`
to the active link yourself. Offcanvas desktop contents are inert while closed. The mobile Sheet
has a hidden title and description, traps focus, dismisses with Escape/outside click and restores
focus. Place a visible close control inside long mobile navigation when needed. Each example here has a separate provider and unique targets. The window shortcut broadcasts to every mounted provider, so use the individual triggers when comparing several shells on one page.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Ctrl+B / Cmd+B | Toggle desktop state or mobile sheet. Also applies inside inputs, matching upstream. Every mounted provider listens on window; multiple independent shells all respond. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Normal links and controls; no menu-style arrow navigation. |
| Enter / Space | Activate the trigger. |
| Escape | Dismiss the mobile sheet. |

## Responsive behavior

Below 768px, collapsible navigation uses an 18rem Sheet. `collapsible="none"` remains static on all
widths. Left/right and all three variants remain supported. Desktop toggles retain child state;
switching between desktop and mobile uses upstream's separate trees and can remount children.
Default mobile closing unmounts content. Store drafts outside Sidebar if they must survive that.

## Performance

Only the desktop offcanvas transform animates. There is no measurement loop, persistent will-change,
timer, width interpolation or validation dependency. Child input values survive desktop state and
motion-mode updates. Render only the navigation items the application needs.

## Notes for AI

Keep the provider, navigation landmark and main content together. Use `render`, never `asChild`.
Do not assume the cookie is read or desktop `open` controls the mobile sheet. Do not animate icon
widths or disclosure height without a separately reviewed measured geometry contract.

# Data Table

An editable payments table with sorting, filtering, selection, visibility, and pagination.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/data-table
```

The block installs TanStack Table **9.3.1** and the Cadence Table, Input, Button,
Checkbox and Dropdown Menu items. Manual installation: copy
`registry/cadence/data-table/index.tsx` to `components/cadence/data-table/index.tsx`,
install those registry dependencies, then install `@tanstack/react-table@9.3.1`.
Keep the relative imports and sibling install tree.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.

1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed.

```package-manager
npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority lucide-react @tanstack/react-table@9.3.1
```

```tsx
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {

```

Copy all 14 target files, including every `cadence-motion` and
`cadence-provider` helper. Keep the relative imports, sibling `cadence/`
directories and shipped `"use client"` directives. Complete the linked manual
base setup with Cadence theme CSS and ensure Tailwind CSS v4 scans the copied
files. No additional Data Table stylesheet is required. Apply
`bg-background text-foreground` to your application root. `CadenceProvider` is
optional: without it, the controls follow the system motion preference; use it
to choose a local mode or clock. All imports in Usage and the examples, including
Button and the provider, are already covered by this installation graph.

Keep the exact `@tanstack/react-table@9.3.1` dependency. This file uses v9's
`useTable`, explicit feature and row-model registration, and `table.FlexRender`;
v8's `useReactTable` setup is not interchangeable. `DataTableDemo` is the payments
composition shown below. Its exported `Payment` type and `columns` describe
that composition; to change columns or record shape, edit the copied file
rather than passing a generic `columns` prop.

The minimal [Usage](#usage) can remain a Server Component. Pass serializable
`Payment[]` data and initial read-only state from the server; the installed
client component creates its own column header/cell functions and event handlers.
Keep state hooks, change callbacks, native event handlers and refs in a
`"use client"` caller, as the controlled examples do. Customize the exported
`columns` and their header/cell functions in the copied client module.

Supply unique stable `id` values, numeric USD amounts, emails and one of the four
documented statuses. Omitted `data` shows five sample payments; `data={[]}` shows
the empty state. The top site specimen supplies 23 records separately. Sorting,
filtering, visibility, selection and pagination each have independent state:
omit both props for internal state, or pair the state prop with its
`on…Change` callback and apply TanStack's value-or-updater requests. A state prop
alone is read-only; a callback alone replaces the internal setter.

Selection is keyed by payment ID. Select all affects the current page; the live
count includes selected rows matching the current filter. Keep selection cleanup
for removed records in your caller. The composition processes the supplied
collection on the client; fetching, persistence, server pagination,
virtualization and cell editing require application code or adaptation of the
copied composition. Copy payment ID uses the browser clipboard and its original
ID; the host owns clipboard permissions and errors. Email customer uses `mailto:`.

Keep the named native table and its horizontal scroll container inside a
shrinkable parent (`min-w-0`). Columns remain available at narrow widths; the
toolbar lets the filter input shrink beside Columns, and the footer can wrap.
The caller-owned minimum height in Usage reserves room
for ten rows, so filtering does not move the footer; retune or omit it for your
page size and typography. This is layout space, not a height animation. Table
data, row order and geometry update immediately in every mode. The installed
Button, Checkbox and Dropdown Menu retain their own press, indicator and popup
recipes: full uses their authored motion, reduced drops scale and retains fades,
and none settles immediately.

## Usage

```tsx
import { DataTableDemo } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

export function Payments() {
  return <DataTableDemo className="[&_[data-slot=table-container]]:min-h-112.5" />;
}
```

The top specimen reserves room for the default header and ten rows with a caller-owned
minimum height on the scroll container. Filtering, including updates without recent
keyboard or pointer input, keeps the pagination controls and following content still.
This is a minimum, so taller content can grow and horizontal scrolling remains available.
Retune the reserve when changing page size, row typography or cell padding; omit it when
the surrounding layout should follow the number of visible rows.

This is an editable payments **composition**, not a universal table primitive.
It starts from the [pinned Base example](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/examples/base/data-table-demo.tsx)
and [guide](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/content/docs/components/base/data-table.mdx).
`Payment`, `columns`, and `DataTableDemo` retain that example's exports.
Edit the column definitions and feature registration for your application.
The current [TanStack React documentation](https://tanstack.com/table/latest/docs/framework/react/overview)
describes v9; v8's `useReactTable` and `get*RowModel` options do not apply.

## Application data

The caller supplies all four payment statuses, USD amounts, and unique stable IDs. Copy payment ID writes the original ID to the browser clipboard; Email customer is a real `mailto:` link. Clipboard permission and errors belong to the host.

<ComponentExample name="application-data" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const applicationPayments: Payment[] = [
  { id: "invoice-1", email: "lee@example.com", amount: 42, status: "pending" },
  { id: "invoice-2", email: "sam@example.com", amount: 125, status: "processing" },
  { id: "invoice-3", email: "ada@example.com", amount: 316, status: "success" },
  { id: "invoice-4", email: "max@example.com", amount: 88, status: "failed" },
];

export function ApplicationData() {
  return <DataTableDemo data={applicationPayments} className="max-w-4xl" />;
}

```

## Controlled sorting and pagination

Pair each state prop with its change callback. TanStack value-or-updater callbacks accept React setters directly. The page-size select belongs to this pagination UI and resets the page index. Email toggles ascending/descending case-insensitively; filtering automatically resets the page. Previous and Next are the installed table controls. Reset affects only sorting and pagination here.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-sorting-and-pagination" />

```tsx
"use client";

import type { PaginationState, SortingState } from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const payments: Payment[] = Array.from({ length: 23 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: `payment-${i + 1}`,
  email: `person${String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0")}@example.com`,
  amount: (i + 1) * 23,
  status: i % 3 === 0 ? "processing" : "success",
}));

export function ControlledPayments() {
  const [sorting, setSorting] = useState<SortingState>([]);
  const [pagination, setPagination] = useState<PaginationState>({ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 5 });
  const pageSizeId = useId();
  return (
    <div className="w-full min-w-0">
      <DataTableDemo data={payments} sorting={sorting} onSortingChange={setSorting}
        pagination={pagination} onPaginationChange={setPagination} />
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 text-sm">
        <label htmlFor={pageSizeId}>Rows per page</label>
        <select id={pageSizeId} value={pagination.pageSize}
          className="rounded border bg-background p-1"
          onChange={(event) => setPagination({ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: Number(event.target.value) })}>
          <option value="5">5</option><option value="10">10</option><option value="20">20</option>
        </select>
        <output>Page {pagination.pageIndex + 1}; email sort: {sorting[0] ? sorting[0].desc ? "descending" : "ascending" : "unsorted"}</output>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => {
          setSorting([]);
          setPagination({ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 5 });
        }}>Reset sorting and page</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Controlled filtering

The email filter is a case-insensitive substring. This caller starts with a filter, owns subsequent drafts, and can clear it. Updating the value does not replace the filter input or table. A state prop without its callback is read-only; a callback without state takes over updating that slice. Leave both absent for internal state.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-filter" />

```tsx
"use client";

import type { ColumnFiltersState } from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const payments: Payment[] = Array.from({ length: 23 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: `payment-${i + 1}`,
  email: `person${String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0")}@example.com`,
  amount: (i + 1) * 23,
  status: i % 3 === 0 ? "processing" : "success",
}));

export function ControlledFilter() {
  const [filters, setFilters] = useState<ColumnFiltersState>([{ id: "email", value: "person01" }]);
  return (
    <div className="w-full min-w-0">
      <DataTableDemo data={payments} columnFilters={filters} onColumnFiltersChange={setFilters} />
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setFilters([])}>Clear email filter</Button>
      <output className="ml-3 text-sm">Filter: {String(filters[0]?.value ?? "(empty)")}</output>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Column visibility

Status starts hidden; use Columns to show it or hide Email and Amount. Selection and Actions cannot be hidden. Hiding Email keeps its filter state. This instance owns visibility independently from the other tables.

<ComponentExample name="column-visibility" />

```tsx
"use client";

import type { ColumnVisibilityState } from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { useState } from "react";
import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const applicationPayments: Payment[] = [
  { id: "invoice-1", email: "lee@example.com", amount: 42, status: "pending" },
  { id: "invoice-2", email: "sam@example.com", amount: 125, status: "processing" },
  { id: "invoice-3", email: "ada@example.com", amount: 316, status: "success" },
  { id: "invoice-4", email: "max@example.com", amount: 88, status: "failed" },
];

export function ColumnVisibility() {
  const [visibility, setVisibility] = useState<ColumnVisibilityState>({ status: false });
  return <DataTableDemo data={applicationPayments} columnVisibility={visibility} onColumnVisibilityChange={setVisibility} />;
}

```

## Empty results

A fixed unmatched filter and an empty application collection both render No results. The first filter and visibility state are intentionally read-only; typing and menu changes cannot override supplied values without their matching callbacks. The empty cell spans four visible columns in the first table and all five in the second.

<ComponentExample name="empty-results" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const applicationPayments: Payment[] = [
  { id: "invoice-1", email: "lee@example.com", amount: 42, status: "pending" },
  { id: "invoice-2", email: "sam@example.com", amount: 125, status: "processing" },
  { id: "invoice-3", email: "ada@example.com", amount: 316, status: "success" },
  { id: "invoice-4", email: "max@example.com", amount: 88, status: "failed" },
];

export function EmptyResults() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-5">
      <section aria-label="No matching emails" className="min-w-0">
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Read-only filter; Status hidden</p>
        <DataTableDemo data={applicationPayments} columnVisibility={{ status: false }}
          columnFilters={[{ id: "email", value: "no-match" }]} />
      </section>
      <section aria-label="Empty collection" className="min-w-0">
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">No application records</p>
        <DataTableDemo data={[]} />
      </section>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Row selection

The header selects the current page, not all 23 rows. A partial page shows an indeterminate checkbox. Selection is keyed by stable application ID and survives sorting, filtering, and pagination; the installed live status counts the filtered selection only. The caller-owned output includes selected IDs outside the current filter. Clear selected IDs explicitly clears all pages.

<ComponentExample name="row-selection" />

```tsx
"use client";

import type { RowSelectionState } from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const payments: Payment[] = Array.from({ length: 23 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: `payment-${i + 1}`,
  email: `person${String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0")}@example.com`,
  amount: (i + 1) * 23,
  status: i % 3 === 0 ? "processing" : "success",
}));

export function RowSelection() {
  const [selection, setSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({ "payment-1": true });
  return (
    <div className="w-full min-w-0">
      <DataTableDemo data={payments} rowSelection={selection} onRowSelectionChange={setSelection} />
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setSelection({})}>Clear selected IDs</Button>
        <output className="text-sm">Selected IDs: {Object.keys(selection).filter((id) => selection[id]).join(", ") || "none"}</output>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Updating rows

The caller updates the first amount, reverses record order, removes that record, or restores the collection. Surviving rows keep stable keys and selection; filter drafts and the table node survive updates. Removing a record also removes its stale selection in this caller. These operations demonstrate data ownership, not a built-in editing or fetching API. Updates and row reordering are immediate in every motion mode.

<ComponentExample name="updating-rows" />

```tsx
"use client";

import type { RowSelectionState } from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const applicationPayments: Payment[] = [
  { id: "invoice-1", email: "lee@example.com", amount: 42, status: "pending" },
  { id: "invoice-2", email: "sam@example.com", amount: 125, status: "processing" },
  { id: "invoice-3", email: "ada@example.com", amount: 316, status: "success" },
  { id: "invoice-4", email: "max@example.com", amount: 88, status: "failed" },
];

export function UpdatingRows() {
  const [data, setData] = useState(applicationPayments);
  const [selection, setSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({ "invoice-1": true });
  return (
    <div className="w-full min-w-0">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setData((rows) => rows.map((row) =>
          row.id === "invoice-1" ? { ...row, amount: row.amount === 999 ? 42 : 999 } : row))}>Update first payment</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setData((rows) => [...rows].reverse())}>Reverse records</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" disabled={!data.some((row) => row.id === "invoice-1")}
          onClick={() => {
            setData((rows) => rows.filter((row) => row.id !== "invoice-1"));
            setSelection((current) => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(current).filter(([id]) => id !== "invoice-1")));
          }}>Remove first payment</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => {
          setData(applicationPayments);
          setSelection({ "invoice-1": true });
        }}>Restore records</Button>
      </div>
      <DataTableDemo data={data} rowSelection={selection} onRowSelectionChange={setSelection} />
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Native container props

Native div props, React 19 ref, events, style, and classes pass to the outer data-table container. This example adds a separately named region and an explicit focus action. The inner Payments table keeps native table semantics, column scopes, and keyboard scrolling; it does not become an editable grid. The click count receives real bubbling events.

<ComponentExample name="native-container" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const applicationPayments: Payment[] = [
  { id: "invoice-1", email: "lee@example.com", amount: 42, status: "pending" },
  { id: "invoice-2", email: "sam@example.com", amount: 125, status: "processing" },
  { id: "invoice-3", email: "ada@example.com", amount: 316, status: "success" },
  { id: "invoice-4", email: "max@example.com", amount: 88, status: "failed" },
];

export function NativeContainer() {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const titleId = useId();
  const [clicks, setClicks] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="w-full min-w-0">
      <h3 id={titleId} className="text-sm font-medium">Regional payments</h3>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => root.current?.focus()}>Focus payment region</Button>
      <DataTableDemo ref={root} data={applicationPayments} role="region" aria-labelledby={titleId}
        tabIndex={-1} className="rounded-lg border p-2 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring"
        style={{ borderStyle: "dashed" }} onClick={() => setClicks((count) => count + 1)} />
      <output className="text-sm">Region clicks: {clicks}</output>
    </div>
  );
}

```

## Without motion

This explicit local provider fixes only this specimen to none. Open Columns, select rows, and sort normally: menus appear on their first visible frame with zero motion duration, checkmarks switch immediately, and buttons do not scale. Other examples inherit the page header and system preference.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

const applicationPayments: Payment[] = [
  { id: "invoice-1", email: "lee@example.com", amount: 42, status: "pending" },
  { id: "invoice-2", email: "sam@example.com", amount: 125, status: "processing" },
  { id: "invoice-3", email: "ada@example.com", amount: 316, status: "success" },
  { id: "invoice-4", email: "max@example.com", amount: 88, status: "failed" },
];

export function WithoutMotion() {
  return <CadenceProvider mode="none"><DataTableDemo data={applicationPayments} /></CadenceProvider>;
}

```

## When to use

- Payment lists with sortable emails and small client-side collections.
- A starting point for an application-specific TanStack v9 composition.
- A native table with page-level selection and column visibility controls.

## When not to use

- Static records: use [Table](/components/table).
- Very large datasets: build caller-owned server pagination or virtualization.
- Spreadsheet navigation or cell editing: this example has native table semantics.

## API

`DataTableDemo` accepts native `div` props (including React 19 ref, events, style,
and classes merged last) on `data-slot="data-table"`. Table parts retain their
existing slots. The native table is named Payments and has a visible focus ring.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Payment[]` | five sample payments |
| `sorting` | `SortingState` | internal `[]` |
| `columnFilters` | `ColumnFiltersState` | internal `[]` |
| `columnVisibility` | `ColumnVisibilityState` | internal `{}` |
| `rowSelection` | `RowSelectionState` | internal `{}` |
| `pagination` | `PaginationState` | internal `{ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 10 }` |
| `onSortingChange` | `OnChangeFn<SortingState>` | internal setter |
| `onColumnFiltersChange` | `OnChangeFn<ColumnFiltersState>` | internal setter |
| `onColumnVisibilityChange` | `OnChangeFn<ColumnVisibilityState>` | internal setter |
| `onRowSelectionChange` | `OnChangeFn<RowSelectionState>` | internal setter |
| `onPaginationChange` | `OnChangeFn<PaginationState>` | internal setter |

The exported `columns` are the payment-specific TanStack v9 definitions, not an
additional generic public table API. Customize this file rather than passing
arbitrary columns to `DataTableDemo`.

## Motion contract

No row entrance, reorder, resize or layout motion. Sorting, filtering, pagination
and visibility update native markup immediately without keying the table or input
by state. Surviving rows use stable IDs; off-page rows unmount normally.
T2 describes the composed controls; there is no separate table animation runtime.

| Recipe / cause | full | reduced | none |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feedback.press` / Button press | token spring scale | no scale | immediate |
| `state.morph` / checkbox or menu check | opacity and scale | opacity only | zero duration |
| `popup.anchored` / Columns or Actions opens | opacity and scale | opacity only | visible on first frame |
| `exit.fade` / menu closes | opacity and scale exit | opacity only | immediate |

Recipes and timing tokens belong to the installed controls. Dropdown Menu uses
its local `duration.fast` clock, including timeScale and reducedDurationScale,
even through a portal inside a differently configured provider. Live downgrade
drops transforms and `none` removes all motion transitions. No measured geometry,
loop, timer, stagger, or permanent `will-change` is introduced by this block.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Native table headers use `scope="col"`; the sorted header exposes `aria-sort`.
Tab reaches the named filter, column trigger, checkboxes, row actions and page
buttons. Space toggles a focused checkbox; Enter activates buttons. Arrow keys
navigate open menus, Escape dismisses and returns focus. No grid arrow-key model
is added to static cells. Each row checkbox includes its email in the accessible
name; the header is Select all. The filtered selection count is a live status.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller fetches records, decides validity, removes stale selections, and owns
persistence. This block has no validation, submission, request orchestration, or
schema API. All processing is client-side; server pagination, virtualization,
cell editing, resizing, and additional filter controls require adapting the copied
composition. Stable unique IDs must identify the same record across updates.

## Responsiveness and performance

The toolbar and footer wrap. The native Table wrapper scrolls horizontally at
narrow widths; no data columns disappear automatically. Focus the named table
and use arrow keys to scroll, or use touch/pointer scrolling. The composition is
SSR-compatible with deterministic example data. Keep caller arrays stable where
possible; TanStack recomputes client row models when data/state change. This
block is intended for paginated collections, not an unbounded dataset benchmark.

Without a caller-owned minimum, the result region follows the visible row count. Filtering or changing application
data can therefore move content below the table, even with motion set to none.
Updates without recent user input can contribute to CLS; the absence of row
animation does not guarantee layout stability. Reserve space in the surrounding
application layout when background updates must keep neighbouring content still.

## Notes for AI

- Keep Base UI `render`, Dropdown Menu groups, native table markup and stable row IDs.
- Register v9 features, row models, sorting and filtering functions explicitly.
- Keep data fetching, validation, stale selection cleanup and URL state caller-owned.
- Preserve all three modes of the composed controls; do not animate table geometry.
- Related: [Table](/components/table), [Checkbox](/components/checkbox),
  [Dropdown Menu](/components/dropdown-menu), [Pagination](/components/pagination).

# Date Picker

Choose a single date or date range from an anchored calendar.

## Installation

**Command**

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/date-picker
```

The block installs Button, Calendar, Popover, their shared libraries and date-fns
4.1.0. The Date input and Time compositions additionally use Input and Field;
install them with `npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input @cadence/field` before
copying those examples. For manual installation copy `registry/cadence/date-picker/index.tsx` to
`components/cadence/date-picker/index.tsx`, install those registry items and
`date-fns@4.1.0` plus `lucide-react`. Keep the sibling tree and relative imports.

**Manual**

Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI.



Copy all 12 target files, including every `cadence-motion` and

no DayPicker stylesheet: its appearance comes from the copied Tailwind classes.

CSS or validation package is required.

| Additional item | Target file | Full source |
| --- | --- | --- |

| [@cadence/separator](https://cadence.dev/r/separator.json) | `@components/cadence/separator/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/separator.json) |
| [@cadence/field](https://cadence.dev/r/field.json) | `@components/cadence/field/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/field.json) |

Input directly depends on `cadence-utils`; Field directly depends on
`cadence-utils`, Label and Separator. Label and Separator each depend on
`cadence-utils`. The [Input Manual](/components/input#installation) and
[Field Manual](/components/field#installation) expose these complete source
blocks. All other imports in Usage and the examples, including Button and the
provider, are covered by the base graph above.

The minimal [Usage](#usage) can remain a Server Component. The installed client
composition creates its own state and event handlers. Serializable `Date`
values, date ranges and plain `calendarProps` such as `defaultMonth`, `today`
and date matchers can cross that boundary. A serialized Date preserves an
instant, so server and browser time zones must agree on its civil fields for
matching trigger text. When they differ, pass civil year/month/day data to a
client wrapper and construct the local Date there; a server-created local
midnight is not a portable date-only value. Keep state hooks, change callbacks,
native event handlers, refs, render/component functions, custom formatters and
labels in a `"use client"` caller. Imported date-fns locale objects contain
functions: construct and pass them inside that client boundary, as the Locale
example does. Hooks and function-valued props in the controlled and custom-parts
examples belong to the caller.

`DatePickerDemo` is an editable composition. Omit `value` for internal state,
optionally seeded by `defaultValue`; a present `value`, including `undefined`,
is controlled. Pair it with `onValueChange` for editable controlled selection;
without that callback it is read-only. Keep the ownership model stable.
For controlled empty state, create the explicit `value={undefined}` inside a
client caller. The current RSC transport omits that own property, so a
server-passed undefined value becomes uncontrolled; serializable
nonempty Dates do not have that property-presence issue.
Use `mode="range"` with `DateRange` values; it defaults to two displayed months,
which `calendarProps.numberOfMonths` can override. Selection and deselection
leave the popup open. The composition owns `mode`, `selected`, `onSelect` and
`required`; use Calendar directly for multiple or required selection. Pair
`open` with `onOpenChange`, and `calendarProps.month` with `onMonthChange`, when
the application owns those states. `defaultOpen` initializes uncontrolled open
state. Calendar props also own disabled-date matchers, navigation limits and
range constraints; `disabled` on the composition disables its trigger.

Use local civil dates such as `new Date(year, monthIndex, day)`. A date-only ISO
string parses as UTC; it can display the previous local day. Pass deterministic
`defaultMonth` and `today` when the calendar must not depend on the host clock.
If setting DayPicker's `timeZone`, supply dates with matching civil fields and
keep trigger formatting consistent. The caller owns parsing, persistence,
submission, time-zone conversion and DST policy. The Date input example owns
its native ISO civil-date draft; Time owns a separate time string. This block
adds no hidden form value or validation. Render application errors through
`triggerProps` with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`.

Keep the trigger in a shrinkable parent: its date text truncates, while the
available-size constrained popup scrolls. Range months stack at narrow widths
and sit beside each other at the Calendar's desktop breakpoint. Preserve a
focusable button and supplied props when customizing the trigger render, and
retain the popup title and Calendar keyboard semantics. Button owns the press
recipe, Popover owns its anchored open/close recipes, and Calendar owns month
transitions. Full plays their authored transforms and fades; reduced keeps
fades and drops transforms; none settles immediately. Date labels, selection
and calendar geometry update immediately in every mode.

## Usage

```tsx
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

export function Appointment() {
  return <DatePickerDemo label="Appointment date" />;
}
```

An editable composition, using the [pinned Base example](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/examples/base/date-picker-demo.tsx)
and [guide](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/content/docs/components/base/date-picker.mdx),
with new-york-v4's calendar-icon treatment. There is no new date primitive.
The named `DatePickerDemo` export and initially empty single selection remain.
Selection leaves the popup open, including deselection of the selected day.

## Initial values

An omitted value starts empty. defaultValue seeds independent internal state; selecting the chosen day deselects it. A present value without onValueChange is read-only, so interacting with that calendar never changes its selection.

<ComponentExample name="initial-values" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function InitialValues() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      <DatePickerDemo label="Optional date" placeholder="Choose an optional date" calendarProps={calendar} />
      <DatePickerDemo label="Initial date" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 10, 12)} calendarProps={calendar} />
      <DatePickerDemo label="Read-only date" value={new Date(2026, 10, 20)} calendarProps={calendar} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled date and clearing

A present value prop, including undefined, is controlled. Clear and Set November 20 update only this specimen. While the popup is open an external selection update preserves the displayed month and focus tree; selected dates do not key or replace the Calendar. Keep the ownership model stable.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-date-and-clearing" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function ControlledDate() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date(2026, 10, 12));
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <DatePickerDemo label="Controlled appointment" value={date} onValueChange={setDate} calendarProps={calendar} />
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setDate(undefined)}>
          Clear date
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setDate(new Date(2026, 10, 20))}>
          Set November 20
        </Button>
      </div>
      <output className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {date ? `Selected day: ${date.getDate()}` : "No date selected"}
      </output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Range and presets

Range mode shows two months. Select a start and an end date, or apply the caller-owned preset. This example requires two to seven nights and excludes November 5; DayPicker owns the range rules, including incomplete ranges. Clear passes a controlled undefined value. The trigger stays open after selection.

<ComponentExample name="range-and-presets" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import type { DateRange } from "react-day-picker";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function RangePresets() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | undefined>();
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <DatePickerDemo
        mode="range"
        label="Travel dates"
        value={range}
        onValueChange={setRange}
        calendarProps={{ ...calendar, min: 2, max: 7, excludeDisabled: true, disabled: new Date(2026, 10, 5) }}
      />
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          onClick={() => setRange({ from: new Date(2026, 10, 10), to: new Date(2026, 10, 15) })}
        >
          Apply travel preset
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setRange(undefined)}>
          Clear travel dates
        </Button>
      </div>
      <output className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {range?.to ? "Range complete" : range?.from ? "Choose an end date" : "No travel dates"}
      </output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled dates

disabled disables the entire trigger. calendarProps.disabled instead uses DayPicker matchers: this enabled calendar excludes weekends and November 5. Application rules decide acceptable dates; disabling UI does not validate submitted data.

<ComponentExample name="disabled-dates" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function DisabledDates() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      <DatePickerDemo label="Unavailable" disabled calendarProps={calendar} />
      <DatePickerDemo
        label="Weekday appointment"
        calendarProps={{ ...calendar, disabled: [{ dayOfWeek: [0, 6] }, new Date(2026, 10, 5)] }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Birth dates

Dropdown captions provide a month and year route back to 1920. The final navigation year remains 2026, while days after November 1 are unavailable. The fixed today and defaultMonth keep the specimen deterministic without consulting the server clock.

<ComponentExample name="birth-dates" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function BirthDates() {
  return (
    <DatePickerDemo
      label="Birth date"
      calendarProps={{
        ...calendar,
        captionLayout: "dropdown",
        startMonth: new Date(1920, 0),
        endMonth: new Date(2026, 11),
        disabled: { after: new Date(2026, 10, 1) },
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Locale

This fixed French locale changes both the date-fns PPP trigger text and the Calendar labels; weeks start on Monday. Locale does not imply direction. For right-to-left applications, set dir on the host and calendarProps.dir on the calendar. Dates remain Date objects.

<ComponentExample name="locale" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { fr } from "date-fns/locale";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function LocalizedDate() {
  return (
    <DatePickerDemo
      label="Rendez-vous"
      defaultValue={new Date(2026, 10, 12)}
      calendarProps={{ ...calendar, locale: fr, weekStartsOn: 1 }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Date input

Compose a labelled native date Input with the real picker. The caller owns the ISO civil-date draft, local year/month/day construction, empty state and synchronization. This example parses the complete value supplied by a native date input; it is not a free-text parser or a natural-language input.

<ComponentExample name="date-input" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useId } from "react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function DateInput() {
  const id = useId();
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("2026-11-12");
  // The native date input supplies a complete ISO civil date or an empty value.
  const [year = 0, month = 1, day = 1] = draft.split("-").map(Number);
  const date = draft ? new Date(year, month - 1, day) : undefined;
  return (
    <FieldGroup className="w-full max-w-xs">
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>Appointment date input</FieldLabel>
        <Input id={id} type="date" value={draft} onChange={(event) => setDraft(event.target.value)} />
        <FieldDescription>Local calendar date; clearing the input clears the picker.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <DatePickerDemo
        label="Date input calendar"
        value={date}
        onValueChange={(next) =>
          setDraft(
            next
              ? [
                  next.getFullYear(),
                  String(next.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0"),
                  String(next.getDate()).padStart(2, "0"),
                ].join("-")
              : "",
          )
        }
        calendarProps={calendar}
      />
    </FieldGroup>
  );
}
```

## Time

A labelled native time Input owns a separate time string. Changing the day preserves the time. The application decides how to combine these values with a time zone, handle DST and serialize them. This block supplies no time picker primitive or automatic conversion.

<ComponentExample name="time" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useId } from "react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function DateAndTime() {
  const id = useId();
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date(2026, 10, 12));
  const [time, setTime] = useState("09:30");
  return (
    <FieldGroup className="w-full max-w-xs">
      <DatePickerDemo label="Meeting day" value={date} onValueChange={setDate} calendarProps={calendar} />
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>Meeting time</FieldLabel>
        <Input id={id} type="time" value={time} onChange={(event) => setTime(event.target.value)} />
        <FieldDescription>Time is a separate caller-owned value; no zone conversion is applied.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
    </FieldGroup>
  );
}
```

## Controlled month and open state

Control month and onMonthChange together when navigation belongs to the application. Open December changes this specimen's month and open state; its own navigation remains usable. Close calendar demonstrates caller-owned dismissal. open/onOpenChange follow Base UI Popover semantics; defaultOpen initializes an uncontrolled popup when needed.

<ComponentExample name="controlled-month-and-open" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function ControlledMonthAndOpen() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(new Date(2026, 10, 1));
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date(2026, 10, 12));
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <DatePickerDemo
        label="Controlled calendar"
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        value={date}
        onValueChange={setDate}
        calendarProps={{ ...calendar, month, onMonthChange: setMonth }}
      />
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          onClick={() => {
            setMonth(new Date(2026, 11, 1));
            setOpen(true);
          }}
        >
          Open December
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
          Close calendar
        </Button>
      </div>
      <output className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {open ? "Open" : "Closed"}; displayed month: {month.getMonth() + 1}
      </output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Caller-owned errors

A caller-supplied error reaches the real trigger through aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Its unique description belongs to this specimen. This read-only empty value represents an error already determined by the application; no validation callback or schema is introduced.

<ComponentExample name="caller-errors" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useId } from "react";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function CallerErrors() {

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <DatePickerDemo
        label="Required appointment"
        value={undefined}
        triggerProps={{ "aria-invalid": true, "aria-describedby": id }}
        calendarProps={calendar}
      />
      <p id={id} className="text-sm text-destructive">
        Choose an appointment before submitting.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Custom parts and native props

Native div props, styles and React 19 refs pass to the root. triggerProps customizes the actual Button and preserves its click handler and focus ref; contentProps aligns and styles the real popup. The focus action demonstrates that ref and the count observes actual trigger activations. Custom render elements must remain focusable buttons and retain supplied props.

<ComponentExample name="custom-parts" />

```tsx
"use client";
import { useRef } from "react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function CustomParts() {
  const trigger = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const [presses, setPresses] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <DatePickerDemo
        label="Custom appointment"
        className="rounded-md border border-dashed p-2"
        style={{ maxWidth: "100%" }}
        triggerProps={{ ref: trigger, variant: "secondary", onClick: () => setPresses((value) => value + 1) }}
        contentProps={{ align: "end", className: "border-dashed" }}
        calendarProps={calendar}
      />
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => trigger.current?.focus()}>
        Focus date trigger
      </Button>
      <output className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Trigger activations: {presses}</output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Without motion

This named specimen explicitly overrides the header with a fixed none provider. Trigger, popup and month navigation have zero animation from their first insertion. All other specimens inherit the header's motion, speed and theme.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

