```tsx
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

const calendar = { defaultMonth: new Date(2026, 10, 1), today: new Date(2026, 10, 1) };

export function WithoutMotion() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <DatePickerDemo label="Static appointment" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 10, 12)} calendarProps={calendar} />
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Appointment dates and optional calendar selection.
- Travel ranges, with application-owned presets and constraints.
- A starting composition to edit for your application's form.

## When not to use

- An always-visible date grid: use [Calendar](/components/calendar).
- Time-only entry: use a labelled [Input](/components/input) with `type="time"`.
- Free-form language parsing: supply your application's parser and draft state.

## API

`DatePickerDemoProps` is a discriminated union; range values require `mode="range"`.
Native div props, React 19 ref/cleanup, classes and styles go to `data-slot="date-picker"`.

| Prop | Type | Default / behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `"single" \| "range"` | `"single"` |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Date` or `DateRange` | initially empty; present value is controlled |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: Date \| undefined) => void`, range equivalent | observes selection/deselection |
| `label` | `string` | `"Choose date"`; accessible trigger prefix and popup title |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Pick a date"` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false`, disables trigger |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | Popover props | Base UI ownership and event details |
| `calendarProps` | corresponding optional-selection Calendar props | autoFocus, selected default month; range two months |
| `triggerProps` | `ButtonProps` | outline button; caller classes/styles/callbacks last |
| `contentProps` | `PopoverContent` props | start-aligned, available-size constrained, scrollable |

Selection props (`mode`, `selected`, `onSelect`, `required`) are owned by the
composition. Use Calendar directly for required/multiple selection. Other
calendar overrides remain caller-owned, including month, locale, focus and
components. A custom render must retain a focusable button and the supplied props.

## Motion contract

T2 describes existing control motion. No date label animation, layout tween,
selection-keyed remount, new recipe or runtime is added.

| Recipe / cause | full | reduced | none |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feedback.press` / trigger press | token spring scale | no scale | immediate |
| `popup.anchored` / open | opacity and token scale | opacity only | visible first frame |
| `exit.fade` / close | opacity and scale | opacity only | immediate |
| `data.transition` / calendar month | token horizontal translation and opacity | opacity only | immediate |

Popover resolves its own `duration.fast` clock with timeScale and reducedDurationScale
inside the portal. Nested full can recover under outer none; OS reduce still wins.
Live reduced drops scale and live none cancels transitions immediately. Calendar
cancels its WAAPI effect on mode changes without replacing the grid or focused day.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Tab reaches the named trigger; Space/Enter opens the dialog. Calendar focuses the
selected enabled day or its initial focus target. Arrow keys move days, Home/End
move within the week, PageUp/PageDown navigate months. Escape dismisses and returns
focus to the trigger. Selecting a day keeps the popup open. Screen readers hear
the popup title, grid month, day labels and selected states. Range selection retains
DayPicker's grid model. Button names include the label and formatted selection.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller owns validation, parsing, submission, storage, fetching and time-zone
policy. Use `triggerProps` for `aria-invalid` or `aria-describedby`. No schema,
resolver, validation callback or hidden form input is added. Serialize selected
values explicitly in the application.

## Responsiveness and performance

The trigger truncates long labels within the available width. The popup is bounded
by Base UI's available width/height and scrolls; range months stack on small screens
and sit side by side on desktop. No document overflow is required. Deterministic
example dates are SSR-compatible; empty uncontrolled selection renders without
reading the clock. DayPicker's current-month fallback depends on the host clock;
pass `defaultMonth` and `today` for deterministic server/client calendars.

Use local civil dates such as new Date(year, monthIndex, day). A date-only ISO string parses as UTC and can display the previous local day. For DayPicker timeZone, construct dates for that zone (for example TZDate) so trigger and calendar share civil fields. The caller owns persistence, UTC conversion and DST policy. These examples deliberately use fixed local dates.

## Notes for AI

- Keep this a registry block with namespaced dependencies and relative imports.
- Keep value presence semantics so controlled undefined clears correctly.
- Preserve stable Calendar identities and Base UI focus/render/event semantics.
- Keep locale and civil-date/time-zone policy explicit in the caller.
- Related: [Calendar](/components/calendar), [Popover](/components/popover), [Button](/components/button).

# Attachment

Displays file media, metadata, caller-owned upload state, and actions.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/attachment
```

The examples use lucide-react icons; run `pnpm add lucide-react` if needed. The file-selection example also installs Input; Button and the provider are Attachment dependencies.

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input
```

## Usage

This ready file has a native download link and an independent remove action. The caller chooses the removal focus destination.

```tsx
"use client";

import { FileTextIcon, XIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Attachment, AttachmentAction, AttachmentActions, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";

const noteUrl = "data:text/plain;charset=utf-8,Project%20notes%0AReview%20the%20attachment%20examples.";

export function ReadyFile() {
  const [removed, setRemoved] = useState(false);
  const region = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  return (
    <div ref={region} tabIndex={-1} className="max-w-full outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring">
      {removed ? (
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">No attached files.</p>
      ) : (
        <Attachment>
          <AttachmentMedia aria-hidden="true">
            <FileTextIcon />
          </AttachmentMedia>
          <AttachmentContent>
            <AttachmentTitle>project-notes.txt</AttachmentTitle>
            <AttachmentDescription>Text file · 45 B</AttachmentDescription>
          </AttachmentContent>
          <AttachmentTrigger
            render={<a href={noteUrl} download="project-notes.txt" aria-label="Download project notes" />}
          />
          <AttachmentActions>
            <AttachmentAction
              aria-label="Remove project notes"
              onClick={() => {
                setRemoved(true);
                region.current?.focus();
              }}
            >
              <XIcon />
            </AttachmentAction>
          </AttachmentActions>
        </Attachment>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Upload state

Pass all five caller-owned states directly: idle, uploading, processing, error and done. Uploading and processing pulse the filename; readable status remains when motion is disabled. These fixed cards do not upload anything. A busy region uses aria-busy; announce meaningful milestones in a separate polite status, rather than each percentage.

<ComponentExample name="upload-state" />

```tsx
import { FileTextIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { type ComponentProps } from "react";
import { Attachment, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";

function FileTile({
  name = "project-notes.txt",
  description = "Text file · 45 B",
  ...props
}: ComponentProps<typeof Attachment> & { name?: string; description?: string }) {
  return (
    <Attachment {...props}>
      <AttachmentMedia aria-hidden="true">
        <FileTextIcon />
      </AttachmentMedia>
      <AttachmentContent>
        <AttachmentTitle title={name}>{name}</AttachmentTitle>
        <AttachmentDescription>{description}</AttachmentDescription>
      </AttachmentContent>
    </Attachment>
  );
}

export function UploadState() {
  const states = ["idle", "uploading", "processing", "error", "done"] as const;
  const descriptions = {
    idle: "Ready to upload",
    uploading: "Uploading · 64%",
    processing: "Processing file",
    error: "Upload failed · connection lost",
    done: "Upload complete",
  };
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full min-w-0 flex-wrap justify-center gap-3">
      {states.map((state) => (
        <FileTile
          key={state}
          state={state}
          name={`${state}.pdf`}
          description={descriptions[state]}
          aria-busy={state === "uploading" || state === "processing"}
        />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Images

Use AttachmentMedia variant="image" with a native image and meaningful alt text. These vertical cards compare a ready image with a dimmed processing preview. Supply the URL yourself; Attachment never creates or revokes object URLs. This static inline SVG has no object URL lifecycle. Horizontal cards remain the default, as shown in Sizes.

<ComponentExample name="images" />

```tsx
import { Attachment, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";

const imageUrl =
  "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 80 80'%3E%3Crect width='80' height='80' fill='%23d4d4d8'/%3E%3Crect x='10' y='10' width='60' height='60' rx='6' fill='%23fafafa'/%3E%3Cpath d='M20 28h40M20 40h24M20 52h32' stroke='%2352525b' stroke-width='4'/%3E%3C/svg%3E";

export function Images() {
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-full flex-wrap items-start justify-center gap-4">
      {(["done", "processing"] as const).map((state) => (
        <Attachment key={state} state={state} orientation="vertical" aria-busy={state === "processing"}>
          <AttachmentMedia variant="image">
            {/* biome-ignore lint/performance/noImgElement: Native images are the public AttachmentMedia composition. */}
            <img src={imageUrl} width={80} height={80} alt="Interface diagram" />
          </AttachmentMedia>
          <AttachmentContent>
            <AttachmentTitle title={`${state}-diagram.svg`}>{state}-diagram.svg</AttachmentTitle>
            <AttachmentDescription>{state === "done" ? "SVG · 250 B" : "Processing preview"}</AttachmentDescription>
          </AttachmentContent>
        </Attachment>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

The default, sm and xs sizes change spacing, text and icon media. Compare them independently of state and orientation; filenames remain in the DOM and truncate within the available width.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
import { FileTextIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { type ComponentProps } from "react";
import { Attachment, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";

function FileTile({
  name = "project-notes.txt",
  description = "Text file · 45 B",
  ...props
}: ComponentProps<typeof Attachment> & { name?: string; description?: string }) {
  return (
    <Attachment {...props}>
      <AttachmentMedia aria-hidden="true">
        <FileTextIcon />
      </AttachmentMedia>
      <AttachmentContent>
        <AttachmentTitle title={name}>{name}</AttachmentTitle>
        <AttachmentDescription>{description}</AttachmentDescription>
      </AttachmentContent>
    </Attachment>
  );
}

export function Sizes() {
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-full flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-4">
      {(["default", "sm", "xs"] as const).map((size) => (
        <FileTile key={size} size={size} name={`${size}-notes.txt`} description={`Size: ${size}`} />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Trigger and independent actions

AttachmentTrigger fills the card behind AttachmentActions. The native download link has an accessible name; Save toggles its own state without requesting a download. The disabled delete button stays disabled. This local text download uses a fixed data URL; an application supplies its own file URL and authorization. Default triggers are non-submitting buttons, and actions default to ghost Button with icon-xs size.

<ComponentExample name="trigger-and-actions" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { XIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Attachment, AttachmentAction, AttachmentActions, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";

const noteUrl = "data:text/plain;charset=utf-8,Project%20notes%0AReview%20the%20attachment%20examples.";

export function TriggerAndActions() {
  const [opened, setOpened] = useState(0);
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="flex min-w-0 max-w-full flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <Attachment>
        <AttachmentContent>
          <AttachmentTitle>review-notes.txt</AttachmentTitle>
          <AttachmentDescription>Download or save independently</AttachmentDescription>
        </AttachmentContent>
        <AttachmentTrigger
          aria-label="Download review notes"
          onClick={() => setOpened((n) => n + 1)}
          render={<a href={noteUrl} download="review-notes.txt" />}
        />
        <AttachmentActions>
          <AttachmentAction size="sm" onClick={() => setSaved((v) => !v)} aria-pressed={saved}>
            {saved ? "Saved" : "Save"}
          </AttachmentAction>
          <AttachmentAction aria-label="Delete locked review notes" disabled>
            <XIcon />
          </AttachmentAction>
        </AttachmentActions>
      </Attachment>
      <output className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Downloads requested: {opened}; {saved ? "saved" : "not saved"}.
      </output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Scrollable groups

AttachmentGroup is always a horizontal snapping scroller. The first row contains horizontal cards and the second contains vertical cards; orientation belongs to each Attachment, not the group. Tab reaches each download link and reveals off-screen cards. A named, focusable group also supports native arrow-key scrolling. Keep min-width: 0 on its parent.

<ComponentExample name="scrollable-groups" />

```tsx
import { FileTextIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { Attachment, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentGroup, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";

const noteUrl = "data:text/plain;charset=utf-8,Project%20notes%0AReview%20the%20attachment%20examples.";

export function ScrollableGroups() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col gap-4">
      {(["horizontal", "vertical"] as const).map((orientation) => (
        <AttachmentGroup
          key={orientation}
          tabIndex={0}
          role="group"
          aria-label={`${orientation} reference files`}
          className="w-full focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring"
        >
          {[
            "research-notes-with-a-very-long-name.txt",
            "project-roadmap.txt",
            "interface-reference.txt",
            "meeting-notes.txt",
          ].map((name) => (
            <Attachment key={name} orientation={orientation} size="sm">
              <AttachmentMedia aria-hidden="true">
                <FileTextIcon />
              </AttachmentMedia>
              <AttachmentContent>
                <AttachmentTitle title={name}>{name}</AttachmentTitle>
                <AttachmentDescription>Reference · text file</AttachmentDescription>
              </AttachmentContent>
              <AttachmentTrigger render={<a href={noteUrl} download={name} aria-label={`Download ${name}`} />} />
            </Attachment>
          ))}
        </AttachmentGroup>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Caller-owned file selection

The native Input owns its FileList, name and browser file selection. This example stores a File locally and exposes explicit simulation actions for progress, processing, completion, failure and retry; it never starts a request or validates the file. Inspect reads the selected metadata. Selection, reset and removal remain independent of the other examples. Reset clears the native input, and removal returns focus to that same input. A real application owns requests, errors, cancellation and cleanup.

<ComponentExample name="caller-owned-file-selection" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { FileTextIcon, XIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { type ComponentProps, useId, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Attachment, AttachmentAction, AttachmentActions, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";

export function CallerOwnedFileSelection() {
  const id = useId();
  const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const form = useRef<HTMLFormElement>(null);
  const [file, setFile] = useState<File | null>(null);
  const [state, setState] = useState<NonNullable<ComponentProps<typeof Attachment>["state"]>>("idle");
  const [notice, setNotice] = useState("No file selected. This example makes no requests.");
  const descriptions = {
    idle: "Selected locally · no upload started",
    uploading: "Local simulation · 64%",
    processing: "Local simulation · processing",
    error: "Caller supplied: connection lost",
    done: "Local simulation complete",
  };
  function update(next: typeof state) {
    setState(next);
    setNotice(descriptions[next]);
  }
  return (
    <form
      ref={form}
      onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
      className="flex w-full min-w-0 max-w-lg flex-col items-start gap-3"
    >
      <label htmlFor={`${id}-file`} className="text-sm font-medium">
        Choose a local file (name only)
      </label>
      <Input
        ref={input}
        id={`${id}-file`}
        name="attachment"
        type="file"
        aria-describedby={`${id}-notice`}
        onChange={(event) => {
          const selected = event.target.files?.[0] ?? null;
          setFile(selected);
          setState("idle");
          setNotice(selected ? `Selected ${selected.name}; no request started.` : "No file selected.");
        }}
      />
      {file && (
        <Attachment
          state={state}
          aria-busy={state === "uploading" || state === "processing"}
          aria-invalid={state === "error" || undefined}
          aria-describedby={state === "error" ? `${id}-error` : undefined}
        >
          <AttachmentMedia aria-hidden="true">
            <FileTextIcon />
          </AttachmentMedia>
          <AttachmentContent>
            <AttachmentTitle title={file.name}>{file.name}</AttachmentTitle>
            <AttachmentDescription>{descriptions[state]}</AttachmentDescription>
          </AttachmentContent>
          <AttachmentTrigger
            aria-label={`Inspect ${file.name}`}
            onClick={() => setNotice(`${file.name} · ${file.size} bytes · ${file.type || "unknown type"}`)}
          />
          <AttachmentActions>
            <AttachmentAction
              aria-label={`Remove ${file.name}`}
              onClick={() => {
                setFile(null);
                setState("idle");
                form.current?.reset();
                setNotice(`Removed ${file.name}`);
                input.current?.focus();
              }}
            >
              <XIcon />
            </AttachmentAction>
          </AttachmentActions>
        </Attachment>
      )}
      {state === "error" && file && (
        <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-destructive">
          Connection lost. Retry when your application is ready.
        </p>
      )}
      <div className="flex max-w-full flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button type="button" variant="outline" size="sm" disabled={!file} onClick={() => update("uploading")}>
          Start local simulation
        </Button>
        <Button
          type="button"
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          disabled={!file || state !== "uploading"}
          onClick={() => update("processing")}
        >
          Process locally
        </Button>
        <Button
          type="button"
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          disabled={!file || state !== "processing"}
          onClick={() => update("done")}
        >
          Finish locally
        </Button>
        <Button type="button" variant="outline" size="sm" disabled={!file} onClick={() => update("error")}>
          Supply failure
        </Button>
        <Button
          type="button"
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          disabled={!file || state !== "error"}
          onClick={() => update("uploading")}
        >
          Retry locally
        </Button>
        <Button
          type="button"
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          onClick={() => {
            form.current?.reset();
            setFile(null);
            setState("idle");
            setNotice("Local selection reset.");
            input.current?.focus();
          }}
        >
          Reset selection
        </Button>
      </div>
      <p id={`${id}-notice`} role="status" className="max-w-full break-all text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {notice}
      </p>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Custom parts

Native root classes, styles and keyboard events pass through. Focus inspect uses a caller ref, and F2 inside the card focuses the same rendered button. The trigger uses Base UI render-function props; the independent download action demonstrates an anchor with Button callback classes and styles. Keep controls as siblings in the action layer rather than nesting them inside a trigger.

<ComponentExample name="custom-parts" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Attachment, AttachmentAction, AttachmentActions, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

const noteUrl = "data:text/plain;charset=utf-8,Project%20notes%0AReview%20the%20attachment%20examples.";

export function CustomParts() {
  const trigger = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="flex min-w-0 max-w-full flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <Attachment
        className="rounded-none"
        style={{ borderStyle: "dashed" }}
        onKeyDown={(event) => {
          if (event.key === "F2") trigger.current?.focus();
        }}
      >
        <AttachmentContent>
          <AttachmentTitle>custom-notes.txt</AttachmentTitle>
          <AttachmentDescription>F2 focuses the inspect button</AttachmentDescription>
        </AttachmentContent>
        <AttachmentTrigger
          ref={trigger}
          aria-label="Inspect custom notes"
          onClick={() => setCount((n) => n + 1)}
          render={(props) => <button {...props} type="button" data-caller-trigger="yes" />}
        />
        <AttachmentActions>
          <AttachmentAction
            render={<a href={noteUrl} download="custom-notes.txt" />}
            size="sm"
            className={(s) => (s.disabled ? "opacity-50" : "underline")}
            style={(s) => ({ fontWeight: s.disabled ? 400 : 600 })}
          >
            Download
          </AttachmentAction>
        </AttachmentActions>
      </Attachment>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => trigger.current?.focus()}>
        Focus inspect
      </Button>
      <output className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Inspections: {count}</output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Without motion

This named example explicitly uses CadenceProvider mode="none". Its uploading title is fully opaque and has no loop from its first insertion. The other specimens inherit the site header mode and speed; reduced keeps the opacity loop, while none cancels it. State, file selection and geometry remain immediate in every mode.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
import { FileTextIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { type ComponentProps } from "react";
import { Attachment, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle } from "@/components/cadence/attachment";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

function FileTile({
  name = "project-notes.txt",
  description = "Text file · 45 B",
  ...props
}: ComponentProps<typeof Attachment> & { name?: string; description?: string }) {
  return (
    <Attachment {...props}>
      <AttachmentMedia aria-hidden="true">
        <FileTextIcon />
      </AttachmentMedia>
      <AttachmentContent>
        <AttachmentTitle title={name}>{name}</AttachmentTitle>
        <AttachmentDescription>{description}</AttachmentDescription>
      </AttachmentContent>
    </Attachment>
  );
}

export function WithoutMotion() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <FileTile state="uploading" name="quiet-report.pdf" description="Uploading · 64%" aria-busy="true" />
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

File previews in composers, upload lists, or message attachments with caller-owned
metadata and optional open/remove/retry actions.

## When not to use

Use Input for native file selection, Progress for a standalone percentage, and
Item for generic content that does not represent a file. Attachment does not
implement an uploader, drop zone, file parser or streaming message runtime.

## API

| Part | Props and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `Attachment` | Native div props; state `done`, size `default`, orientation `horizontal` |
| `AttachmentMedia` | Native div props; variant `icon` or `image`, default `icon` |
| `AttachmentContent` | Native div props; wraps metadata |
| `AttachmentTitle` | Native span props; filename, busy opacity loop |
| `AttachmentDescription` | Native span props; metadata/status text |
| `AttachmentActions` | Native div props; independent action layer |
| `AttachmentAction` | All Button props; size `icon-xs`, variant falls back to `ghost` |
| `AttachmentTrigger` | Base UI useRender button props; type `button` without render; render element/function |
| `AttachmentGroup` | Native div props; horizontal scroll and snap |

Every part preserves its upstream `attachment-*` data-slot (root: `attachment`).
Native refs, styles and events pass through; classes merge last. Root also exposes
`data-state`, `data-size`, `data-orientation`; media exposes `data-variant`.
No File or request state is stored internally. There is no default upload action.

## Motion contract

| Cause | Recipe | Full | Reduced | None |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Uploading/processing title | `data.transition` | Opacity pulse via theme `animate-pulse` | Same opacity loop, no transform | `animate-none`, opacity 1 |
| Default action pressed | `feedback.press` | Button token spring/press scale | No scale | Instant, no scale |

Continuous timing comes from the project's `--animate-pulse` theme token. This
replaces upstream's travelling shimmer with opacity to stay in the motion budget.
Root/title and default actions expose `data-motion`; live none cancels the loop
without replacing nodes. State, removal, size, orientation and media updates are
immediate. No entry, exit, layout or geometry recipe is implied. Custom render
controls can own their own feedback as with Button.

## Keyboard interactions

Tab reaches triggers and actions separately. Enter/Space activate default buttons;
a rendered link uses native link behaviour. Disabled actions retain Button's native
semantics. A focusable group scrolls with arrow keys; Tab also reveals off-screen
interactive cards. Removal focus policy belongs to the caller.

## Accessibility

Name every icon-only action and overlay trigger, retain meaningful image alt text,
and describe failures in text. The trigger has a visible focus ring. Avoid nested
interactive elements inside triggers. Provide a polite live region for upload
milestones outside a busy region. Truncated filenames remain in the DOM; a title
attribute or your own details view can expose their full visual text.

## Validation and data ownership

The application owns native file input `name`, `accept`, `multiple`, `required`,
File objects, form submission, validation, upload progress, requests, cancel/retry,
URLs and URL cleanup. Attachment forwards `aria-invalid`/`data-invalid` when given;
`state="error"` only styles a supplied failure. It never decides which file is valid.
The Caller-owned file selection example reports a local filename and simulates milestones without requests. Its fixed failure is supplied by the caller, not inferred from the selected File.

## Responsiveness and performance

Cards cap at their parent's width; long names truncate. Groups scroll horizontally
with no document overflow when their parent can shrink. Large lists should be
paginated or virtualized by the application. The busy opacity loop uses CSS with
no per-frame JavaScript or layout reads; none stops it on the next style update.
No @shadcn/react dependency or streaming runtime is needed for this pinned API.

## AI usage notes

Compose these nine parts; keep upload state and file lifecycle in your application.
Do not infer a network operation from the visual `state` value. Prefer stable file
IDs as keys so a progress update preserves focus and the native input. There is no
message streaming dependency and no reason to remount a composer when a file changes.

## Related components

[Button](/components/button) supplies actions, [Input](/components/input) supplies
native file selection, [Progress](/components/progress) displays known progress,
and [Code Block](/components/code-block) displays textual file contents.

# Bubble

Displays conversational content with variants, grouping, reactions, and polymorphic surfaces.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/bubble
```

These examples also use Button for caller-owned actions. Install it separately when copying those examples.

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";

export function Conversation() {
  return (
    <BubbleGroup>
      <Bubble variant="muted"><BubbleContent>The registry is ready.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
      <Bubble align="end"><BubbleContent>Ready for review.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
    </BubbleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Variants

Choose one of seven surfaces. Destructive content includes a readable failure message, so color is not the only signal. Bubbles cap at 80% of the container; ghost permits the full width.

<ComponentExample name="variants" />

```tsx
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";

export function Variants() {
  const variants = ["default", "secondary", "muted", "tinted", "outline", "ghost", "destructive"] as const;
  return (
    <BubbleGroup role="group" aria-label="Bubble variants" className="w-full max-w-lg gap-3">
      {variants.map((variant) => (
        <Bubble key={variant} variant={variant}>
          <BubbleContent>{variant === "destructive" ? "destructive: Message delivery failed." : variant}</BubbleContent>
        </Bubble>
      ))}
    </BubbleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Alignment

Start is the default. Set end on each outgoing Bubble; BubbleGroup supplies the column, without choosing a sender or message role.

<ComponentExample name="alignment" />

```tsx
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";

export function Alignment() {
  return (
    <BubbleGroup role="group" aria-label="Message alignment" className="w-full max-w-lg gap-4">
      <Bubble variant="muted" align="start"><BubbleContent>Incoming: aligned to the start.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
      <Bubble align="end"><BubbleContent>Outgoing: aligned to the end.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
    </BubbleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Consecutive messages

Group consecutive messages from the same sender. Keep sender names and conversation semantics in your surrounding UI. Long unbroken text wraps within the shrinking surface.

<ComponentExample name="consecutive-messages" />

```tsx
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";

export function ConsecutiveMessages() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-lg flex-col gap-4">
      <BubbleGroup role="group" aria-label="Alex's messages">
        <Bubble variant="muted"><BubbleContent>Alex: First thought.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
        <Bubble variant="muted"><BubbleContent>Long content wraps: extremely-long-continuous-conversation-content-that-must-fit-within-a-small-mobile-viewport-without-overflow.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
      </BubbleGroup>
      <BubbleGroup role="group" aria-label="Your reply">
        <Bubble align="end"><BubbleContent>You: I'll check both points.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
      </BubbleGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Links and buttons

BubbleContent accepts a Base UI render element. Use a real anchor with href or a button with an explicit type. The local link has its own useId target; the independent pressed reply keeps its native focus and keyboard behavior. Avoid nesting another interactive control inside these surfaces.

<ComponentExample name="links-and-buttons" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";

export function LinksAndButtons() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(false);
  const detailsId = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-lg flex-col gap-4">
      <BubbleGroup className="gap-4">
        <Bubble variant="outline"><BubbleContent render={<a href={`#${detailsId}`} />}>Read local message details</BubbleContent></Bubble>
        <Bubble>
          <BubbleContent render={<button type="button" />} aria-pressed={selected} onClick={() => setSelected((value) => !value)}>
            {selected ? "Review reply selected" : "Select review reply"}
          </BubbleContent>
        </Bubble>
      </BubbleGroup>
      <p id={detailsId} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Message details stay in this local example.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Reactions

Side defaults to bottom and align to end. These four fixed positions use static transforms, with enough space for the overlapping row. Label decorative emoji rows as an image; interactive reactions use named buttons and caller-owned pressed state. Position changes do not animate.

<ComponentExample name="reactions" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup, BubbleReactions } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";

export function Reactions() {
  const [liked, setLiked] = useState(false);
  const positions = [{ side: "top", align: "start" }, { side: "top", align: "end" }, { side: "bottom", align: "start" }, { side: "bottom", align: "end" }] as const;
  return (
    <BubbleGroup role="group" aria-label="Reaction positions" className="w-full max-w-lg gap-10 py-6">
      {positions.map(({ side, align }) => (
        <Bubble key={`${side}-${align}`} variant="muted">
          <BubbleContent>Reactions at {side} / {align}.</BubbleContent>
          <BubbleReactions side={side} align={align} role="img" aria-label="Reaction: fire">🔥</BubbleReactions>
        </Bubble>
      ))}
      <Bubble variant="outline">
        <BubbleContent>Was this answer helpful?</BubbleContent>
        <BubbleReactions>
          <button type="button" className="rounded-full px-2 py-1 outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring" aria-pressed={liked} aria-label={`👍 ${liked ? 1 : 0} thumbs up`} onClick={() => setLiked((value) => !value)}>👍 {liked ? 1 : 0}</button>
        </BubbleReactions>
      </Bubble>
    </BubbleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Updating text

Keep stable message IDs when adding text. Add reply inserts a new Bubble; Append text updates the first existing node without replaying entry or animating height. The first message also handles F2 so you can append while preserving its focus. Updates and announcements are local to this example; no transport or streaming runtime runs. The application owns chunking, IDs, cancellation, retry, history limits and scroll anchoring.

<ComponentExample name="updating-text" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function UpdatingText() {
  const [messages, setMessages] = useState([{ id: "initial", text: "The registry is ready." }]);
  const [notice, setNotice] = useState("Local message updates only.");
  const helpId = useId();
  const append = () => setMessages((items) => items.map((item, index) => index === 0 ? { ...item, text: `${item.text} Another local chunk.` } : item));
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-lg flex-col gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => {
          setMessages((items) => [...items, { id: `reply-${items.length}`, text: `Reply ${items.length + 1}: ready for review.` }]);
          setNotice("A local reply was added.");
        }}>Add reply</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={append}>Append text</Button>
      </div>
      <p id={helpId} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Focus the first message and press F2 to append without moving focus.</p>
      <BubbleGroup role="group" aria-label="Updating conversation" className="gap-4">
        {messages.map((message, index) => (
          <Bubble key={message.id} variant="muted" data-message-id={message.id}>
            <BubbleContent render={<button type="button" />} aria-describedby={index === 0 ? helpId : undefined} onClick={() => setNotice(`Selected ${message.id}.`)} onKeyDown={(event) => {
              if (index === 0 && event.key === "F2") { event.preventDefault(); append(); }
            }}>{message.text}</BubbleContent>
          </Bubble>
        ))}
      </BubbleGroup>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{notice}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Custom parts

BubbleGroup and Bubble forward native props. BubbleContent forwards its ref and merges native handlers, className and style with a render function. Focus custom reply uses the real button ref. Enter/Space update its count; F2 bubbles to the root and changes alignment without replacing the button or moving focus. The render function receives the bubble-content slot. React 19 callback refs may return cleanup functions.

<ComponentExample name="custom-parts" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function CustomParts() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  const [align, setAlign] = useState<"start" | "end">("start");
  const content = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  const helpId = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-lg flex-col gap-4">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => content.current?.focus()}>Focus custom reply</Button>
      <BubbleGroup role="group" aria-label="Custom reply" className="gap-4">
        <Bubble variant="outline" align={align} className="max-w-full" style={{ borderRadius: "var(--radius)" }} onKeyDown={(event) => {
          if (event.key === "F2") { event.preventDefault(); setAlign((value) => value === "start" ? "end" : "start"); }
        }}>
          <BubbleContent ref={(node) => { content.current = node; }} className="px-4" style={{ fontWeight: 500 }} aria-describedby={helpId} onClick={() => setCount((value) => value + 1)} render={(props, state) => <button {...props} type="button" data-render-slot={(state as { slot?: string }).slot} />}>Custom reply · {count}</BubbleContent>
        </Bubble>
      </BubbleGroup>
      <p id={helpId} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Enter or Space counts an activation. F2 changes alignment on the same node.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Without motion

This example explicitly sets a local CadenceProvider to none. Its Bubble has opacity 1 on its first frame and zero duration under every header and system setting. All other examples inherit the header mode, speed and theme; none is not a shortened reduced fade.

<ComponentExample name="without-motion" />

```tsx
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";
import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider";

export function WithoutMotion() {
  return (
    <CadenceProvider mode="none">
      <BubbleGroup className="w-full max-w-lg">
        <Bubble variant="muted"><BubbleContent>This message is visible immediately.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
      </BubbleGroup>
    </CadenceProvider>
  );
}
```

## When to use

Use for conversational text, quoted replies, suggestion buttons and short
structured output; combine surfaces into a caller-owned conversation layout.

## When not to use

Use Attachment for file metadata, Code Block for syntax-highlighted source, and
Alert for a page-level notice. Bubble supplies a surface rather than a complete
chat, message scroller, composer or streaming runtime.

## API

| Part | Props and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `Bubble` | Native div props; variant default/secondary/muted/tinted/outline/ghost/destructive (default: default), align start/end (default: start) |
| `BubbleGroup` | Native div props; groups consecutive bubbles |
| `BubbleContent` | Base UI useRender div props; render element or function |
| `BubbleReactions` | Native div props; side top/bottom (default: bottom), align start/end (default: end) |

All four parts retain upstream bubble-* slots (root: bubble), native styles,
refs and events. Classes merge last; Bubble styles merge after its local clock.
Bubble exposes data-variant, data-align and data-motion; reactions expose data-side
and data-align. No additional message-state or validation API is introduced.

## Motion contract

| Cause | Recipe | Full | Reduced | None |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New Bubble enters | `data.transition` | Opacity 0→1, duration.base / ease.out | Opacity only, duration ×0.6 | Opacity 1 on first frame, zero duration |

CSS @starting-style performs a one-shot entry. The duration resolves locally through
cm.transition("data.transition"), including provider timeScale, so an inner full
scope restores its clock inside outer none. Reduced drops animated transforms;
this recipe uses opacity in full too. Live none cancels entry on the same node.
Existing text, variants, alignment, reactions and resize update immediately. Removal
is immediate; there is no exit or layout animation. Caller-provided motion is caller-owned.

## Keyboard interactions

Presentational surfaces add no tab stops. Tab reaches rendered buttons, links and
reaction buttons. Enter activates buttons/links; Space activates buttons. Interactive
BubbleContent has a visible focus ring. Appending text preserves the same focused
node. The application owns focus after removing a message.

## Accessibility

Keep conversation-level semantics on a surrounding labelled region. Supply readable
sender/error context and label reactions. Avoid nested interactive content inside
button/link bubbles. Announce meaningful completed updates in a separate polite
status region when needed; announcing every chunk can overwhelm assistive technology.

## Responsiveness and performance

Long words wrap within a shrinking container. Reactions overlap vertically; give
rows sufficient space and keep reaction collections compact. Rich content can use
ghost with its own overflow treatment. Entry changes only opacity; no layout reads,
per-frame JavaScript, timers or forced remounts. Application pagination or virtualization
owns very large histories. No @shadcn/react dependency is needed for this pinned API.

## AI usage notes

Compose the four parts with stable message IDs. Text and reaction state remain in
your application. Use Collapsible for optional show-more UI and Tooltip/Popover for
metadata; those components keep their own motion contracts. Do not invent streaming,
validation or networking props on Bubble.

## Related components

[Attachment](/components/attachment), [Code Block](/components/code-block),
[Collapsible](/components/collapsible), [Tooltip](/components/tooltip),
[Popover](/components/popover).

## Nested sections

Pass `depth: 3` for a subsection. Entries stay in document order and indent one level. The caller supplies unique heading ids and readable labels; Toc does not parse Markdown. Each card uses its own id prefix so its links cannot target the surrounding documentation.

<ComponentExample name="nested" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";

export function Nested() {

        </section>

  );
}
```

## Controlled active section

Supply `activeId` when a router or your observer owns the current section; an empty string clears the highlight. This disables automatic window tracking. The external Mark actions update only this instance, while its delegated link handler keeps caller state in sync with link activation.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Toc } from "@/components/cadence/toc";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Controlled() {
  const id = useId();
  const items = [
    { id: `${id}-overview`, title: "Overview" },
    { id: `${id}-details`, title: "Details" },
  ] as const;
  const [activeId, setActiveId] = useState<string>(items[0].id);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full gap-5">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setActiveId(items[0].id)}>
          Mark Overview
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setActiveId(items[1].id)}>
          Mark Details
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setActiveId("")}>
          Clear highlight
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Toc
        items={items}
        activeId={activeId}
        label="Controlled sections"
        onClick={(event) => {
          const link =
            event.target instanceof Element ? event.target.closest<HTMLAnchorElement>("a[data-toc-id]") : null;
          if (link) setActiveId(link.dataset.tocId ?? "");
        }}
      />
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-6 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {items.map((item) => (
          <h3 key={item.id} id={item.id} className="scroll-mt-24 font-normal">
            {item.title}
          </h3>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Scroll tracking

Without `activeId`, Toc follows headings on window scroll, resize and initial layout. For a bounded article, the caller tracks that scrolling host and supplies `activeId`, as in this example. Scroll the complete article or activate its links: navigation uses the real scroll container and the wrapped label determines the indicator height. The caller keeps entries and heading ids aligned; it does not add another smooth-scroll clock.

<ComponentExample name="scroll-tracking" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Toc } from "@/components/cadence/toc";

export function ScrollTracking() {
  const id = useId();
  const items = [
    { id: `${id}-overview`, title: "Overview" },
    { id: `${id}-installation`, title: "Installation" },
    { id: `${id}-usage`, title: "Usage with longer section titles that wrap across lines" },
    { id: `${id}-api`, title: "API" },
  ] as const;
  const [activeId, setActiveId] = useState<string>(items[0].id);
  const paragraphs = [
    "Choose a section link or scroll this article. Its reading indicator follows the section nearest the top of this scrolling region.",
    "Install the component, then supply the same stable heading ids to both the article and the navigation. Each example here owns a separate id prefix.",
    "Long section titles wrap without widening the navigation rail. The indicator follows the full label height. The article keeps its native keyboard and pointer scrolling.",
    "The caller owns the entries, labels and scroll container. Toc supplies the links, current-section semantics and motion-aware navigation to their real targets.",
  ] as const;
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-5 sm:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_10rem]">
      <section
        aria-label="Example article"
        tabIndex={0}
        className="h-80 min-w-0 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain rounded-md border p-4 text-sm outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring"
        onScroll={(event) => {
          const host = event.currentTarget;
          const top =
            host.getBoundingClientRect().top + host.clientTop + Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(host).paddingTop);
          let current: string = items[0].id;
          for (const item of items) {
            const heading = document.getElementById(item.id);
            if (heading && heading.getBoundingClientRect().top <= top + 1) current = item.id;
          }
          if (host.scrollTop + host.clientHeight >= host.scrollHeight - 1) current = items.at(-1)?.id ?? items[0].id;
          setActiveId(current);
        }}
      >
        {items.map((item, index) => (
          <section key={item.id} className="min-h-64 pb-6">
            <h3 id={item.id} className="scroll-mt-4 font-medium">
              {item.title}
            </h3>
            <p className="mt-3 leading-relaxed text-muted-foreground">{paragraphs[index]}</p>
          </section>
        ))}
      </section>
      <Toc items={items} activeId={activeId} label="Article sections" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Component reference pages with installation, usage, and API sections.
- Long guides whose sections need direct links.
- Articles with nested headings and a reading position indicator.

## When not to use

- Page hierarchy: use Breadcrumb.
- Navigation between different pages: use Sidebar or Navigation Menu.
- Switching panels that hide other content: use Tabs.

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly TocEntry[]` | required | Entries in document order; empty arrays render nothing. |
| `label` | `string` | `"On this page"` | Visible title and accessible navigation label. |
| `activeId` | `string` | automatic | Controlled current heading id; disables automatic tracking. |
| `scrollOffset` | `number` | `96` | Pixels below the viewport top for automatic tracking. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. |
| native nav props | `ComponentProps<"nav">` | – | Includes ref, style, aria attributes, and event handlers. |

`TocEntry` has `id: string`, `title: string`, and optional `depth: 2 | 3` (default `2`).
Slots are `toc`, `toc-title`, `toc-track`, `toc-rail`, `toc-indicator`, `toc-list`, `toc-item`, and `toc-link`.

## Motion contract

One persistent indicator follows the active entry. Its top and bottom edges use the shared physics
spring, then render as translation and vertical scale on a one-pixel base. Wrapped labels determine
the destination's length. Edges stay inside the rail, and interrupted movement preserves velocity.
Text and `aria-current` follow the current section immediately. Activating a link smoothly scrolls
the actual scrolling host to its heading in full mode. The destination respects the heading's scroll
margin and the host's scroll padding; movement stays within the host's scroll bounds.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active section or label size changes | Indicator translateY / scaleY | `layout.shared` / `spring.morph` | Yes; the existing indicator follows the latest target. |
| Section link activation | Native scroll offset | `scroll.navigate` / `duration.page` / `ease.inOut` | Yes; another link retargets from the current position. |
| Initial measurement / restored selection | Instant placement, no entrance | — | — |
| reduced | Instant indicator placement and section navigation | — | Stops springs; completes an active navigation before paint. |
| none | Instant placement and navigation, no animation clock | — | Stops springs; completes an active navigation before paint. |

Zero provider timeScale also places the indicator immediately. Restoring full motion keeps the
settled position until the next section or size change. A ResizeObserver supplies geometry; no
layout is read during render. Navigation uses one token-backed tween, with no separate CSS/native
smooth-scroll clock. Wheel, touch, pointer input, scrolling keys, resizing, history traversal and
external hash changes cancel it at the current position. Positive clock changes retime the current
trip; reduced/none or zero clock complete it immediately. No interrupted trip restarts later.
The site's mobile disclosure stays instant. Initial hashes, reload, history traversal and no-JS
links keep native behavior; only an explicit unmodified section link activation starts the recipe.

## Accessibility

- A labelled `nav` contains an ordered list of native links.
- Tab and Shift+Tab move between links; Enter activates the same navigation as a primary click.
- The active link has `aria-current="location"` and a stronger text weight. The decorative indicator is hidden from assistive technology.
- Heading targets need matching, unique ids. Offset their scroll margin to account for sticky headers.
- Native anchors remain usable before hydration and without JavaScript. Automatic tracking requires JavaScript.
- Navigation preserves unrelated URL parameters and history state, pushes the new fragment and notifies hashchange listeners. Back/forward use native scroll restoration.
- Completion focuses the heading without scrolling a second time. A temporary `tabindex="-1"` is removed on blur/unmount; caller-supplied tabindex is preserved. Interrupted navigation never steals focus.
- Modified/new-tab clicks and caller-cancelled clicks retain native behavior.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move between native section links. |
| Enter | Scroll to the focused link's heading, update the fragment and focus the heading on completion. |
| Scrolling keys / Tab / Escape | Interrupt an ongoing smooth navigation. |

The indicator never receives focus or replaces a link when its destination changes.

## Responsiveness and performance

The component fills its parent and wraps long labels. The caller owns placement, sticky position,
height limits, and overflow. For documentation layouts, place it in a sticky right column with an
independently scrollable list. Smaller viewports can use a native disclosure near the title; a
floating disclosure list avoids moving the article when opened.

Automatic tracking uses passive window scroll events,
resize events, and a ResizeObserver, with cleanup on unmount. It reads heading positions in those callbacks,
updates state only when the active id changes, and selects the final heading at the page bottom.
It tracks headings present when mounted; remount after dynamically replacing the document or pass new items.
The server renders the first entry as current; hydration corrects it for a deep link or restored scroll position.
Before measurement, a static border marks the current link, including without JavaScript. The first
measured position is immediate. The indicator remains mounted through selection and mode changes.
The indicator's two edge values animate; the list's layout does not interpolate. Section navigation
measures its destination once on activation, then writes native offsets without per-frame layout reads.
A ResizeObserver tracks
wrapped labels, font changes, and a mobile disclosure becoming visible. Motion and the shared
Cadence provider/runtime are installed dependencies; a provider is optional and system reduced
motion is respected standalone. The T3 source budget is 12 KB gzip; dependency and page budgets
are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Build the list from the same heading tree that renders the article so links and ids cannot drift.
- Use this Cadence original for document navigation; it has no pinned shadcn counterpart.
- Do not use a component instance to generate heading ids or to own application routing.
